entry.summary: NeuroPB scales neural decoding for brain-computer interfaces by first pretraining a motor encoder on abundant behavioral data from humans, animals, simulations and robots, then aligning scarce neural recordings to that behavioral representation space. This shifts the data bottleneck from neural recordings to easily collected behavior.

entry.title: Discretization and Statistical Consistency of Functional Flow Matching

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman

entry.summary: The paper provides discretization and statistical consistency theory for functional flow matching, proving strong L2 convergence of finite conditional velocity targets under any strongly consistent finite-rank reconstruction, including non-nested adaptive or scattered sensors where martingale arguments fail. It also derives an end-to-end Wasserstein bound for learned flows without assuming uniqueness of the finite-dimensional ODE.

entry.title: Differentiating Through Dual Prices: End-to-End Policy Learning Under Capacity Constraints

author.name: Mohammadsaeed Haghi, Mahdi Salmani, Nima Kelidari

entry.summary: For sequential allocation of scarce social services under capacity constraints, this paper trains outcome models end to end by differentiating an off-policy value estimate through the dual prices that enforce capacities, rather than fitting decision-blind regressions first. Two formulations are studied, an exact and a relaxed version of the pricing problem.

entry.title: The Sample Complexity of Distributionally Robust PAC Learning under Cressie--Read Divergences

author.name: Elad Aigner-Horev, Daniel Rosenberg, Roi Weiss

entry.summary: This paper establishes sample-complexity bounds for distributionally robust PAC learning under Cressie-Read divergence balls, tight up to constant factors in the realizable case and logarithmic factors in the agnostic case, and shows ordinary empirical risk minimization nearly attains both rates. The bounds make explicit how the robustness radius and divergence order enter the rates.

entry.title: Variational Bounds for Perceptron Learning from Structured Data

author.name: Francesco Camilli, Pierluigi Contucci, Federica Gerace, Emanuele Mingione

entry.summary: Using statistical-physics interpolation methods with log-concavity and concentration estimates, the authors derive matching-form minimax variational bounds for the quenched pressure of a finite-temperature continuous-spin perceptron trained on Gaussian mixture data. The upper and lower bounds differ only in the order of optimizing two variational parameters, and coincide when those optimizations commute.

entry.title: MoEGen: Mixture-of-Experts for Instance-Adaptive LoRA Generation

author.name: Yiming Zeng, Lei Lu, Zexin Li, Zhuochun Li, Shuoqiu Li, Shuyi Liao, Xidong Wu, Zeyu Zhang, Minmei Wang, Yu Zhao, Tingting Yu, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: Reframes mixture-of-experts parameter-efficient tuning from selecting stored LoRA adapters to generating instance-specific adapters from small learnable expert codes. This removes the linear growth of adapter storage with expert count and allows adaptation outside a fixed expert pool.

entry.title: Don't Let Me Ask for It: LLMs Show Deficiencies in Active Multi-Turn Information Acquisition for Abductive Inference

author.name: Shahrukh Mohiuddin, Chalamalasetti Kranti, Sherzod Hakimov, David Schlangen

entry.summary: Introduces an interactive game to study how models actively acquire evidence, revise hypotheses and decide when to stop during abductive reasoning, varying whether evidence arrives upfront or must be queried. Finds models do substantially worse when they must drive multi-turn information gathering themselves.

entry.title: DUD: Decoupled Update Dynamics for Reliable Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models

author.name: Yixin Bu, Runze Xia, Guanyun Zou, Yupeng Ji, Haodong Liu, Piji Li

entry.summary: Argues that mechanistic uncertainty estimators lose signal by aggregating residual stream updates, and instead separates feed-forward (parametric memory) from attention (contextual) contributions to detect memory-context conflict. Uses these decoupled dynamics as an uncertainty signal for hallucination-prone generations.

entry.title: ConlangBench: Exploring Language Knowledge and Learning in LLMs through Diverse Constructed Languages

author.name: Jinhong Jeong, Seungyeop Yi, Sangah Lee, Youngjae Yu

entry.summary: Builds a large benchmark of 21 constructed languages with over 21 million parallel sentence pairs and 321k vocabulary entries to study how models translate and learn languages with controlled design properties. Finds models handle a posteriori conlangs, whose vocabularies derive from natural languages, far better than a priori invented ones.

entry.title: Hi-TTRL: Regulating Consensus with Hints for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kunbin Xu, Xingzuo Li, Xuefeng Bai, Kehai Chen

entry.summary: Improves test-time reinforcement learning, where pseudo-labels come from majority voting on unlabeled inputs, by regulating the dual role of consensus strength that otherwise causes either large updates from unreliable labels or vanishing gradients under strong agreement. Uses hints to modulate rollout consensus during training.

entry.title: GPTKB 2.0: Direct Construction of Disambiguated Knowledge Bases from Large Language Models

author.name: Yujia Hu, Tuan-Phong Nguyen, Simon Razniewski

entry.summary: Builds knowledge bases directly from an LLM's parametric knowledge while performing on-the-fly disambiguation of entities, relations and classes to avoid the duplicates and conflations that plague naive extraction. Reports design trade-offs among accuracy, scale and cost and materializes a large KB at scale.

entry.title: Beyond Representational Similarity: Source-Conditioned Description-Length Gain for Generative Plagiarism Detection and Candidate Source Reranking

author.name: Peijia Guo, Wenxuan Xie, ZiGuang Li, Ming Li

entry.summary: Detects generative plagiarism, meaning reuse of a specific source rather than mere AI involvement, by comparing a frozen model's description length for a suspicious document with and without the candidate source in context. The training-free directional score also reranks candidate sources and survives heavy rewriting where similarity methods fail.

entry.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution

author.name: Zhenran Wang, Zhonghan Bian, Jinsong Li, Zhangyang Qi

entry.summary: Builds an end-to-end pipeline that turns a one-line event topic into a date-indexed timeline from news and social media, separating factual events from a public-opinion layer, and converts each cutoff date into audited forecasting questions. Scores models on probability calibration and reasoning quality for how real social events unfold.

entry.title: Sphere Retraction Normalizations

author.name: Jie Zhang, Cheng-Fang Su, Yi-Jui Huang, Min-Te Sun

entry.summary: Generalizes a Riemannian reformulation of residual connections that keeps hidden states on a hypersphere, showing that the whole family of retraction maps collapses on the sphere to a single scalar choice governing how update magnitude becomes rotation angle. This reduces an apparently rich geometric design space to one tunable knob.

entry.title: Exact Model-Free Policy Iteration for Co-safe LTL Planning

author.name: Zetong Xuan, Yu Wang

entry.summary: A theoretical reinforcement learning paper on satisfying co-safe linear temporal logic objectives in finite MDPs, where standard TD or Q-learning can fail because the relevant Bellman operator is not a contraction and its fixed point is not unique. The authors propose a two-stage method that uses a discounted surrogate to identify a clamp set resolving the ambiguity, then runs undiscounted evaluation and greedy improvement with optimality guarantees. Relevant to safe and specification-driven control where reward shaping alone is insufficient.

entry.title: Incremental Aggregation on the Grassmannian for Asynchronous Eigenspace Computation

author.name: Xiaolu Wang, Jiang Hu, Hoi-To Wai

entry.summary: An asynchronous distributed algorithm for finite-sum eigenspace computation that operates directly on the Grassmannian manifold, refreshing only newly arrived components while reusing cached gradients and using an extrinsic polar retraction so stale tangent vectors need no parallel transport. The analysis provides an angle-dependent gradient-dominance characterization supporting convergence under staleness. Relevant to large distributed PCA and subspace tracking without global synchronization barriers.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation

author.name: Teng Lin, Zhiyang Zhang, Yuyu Luo, Nan Tang

entry.summary: MCTS-Report formulates generation of multimodal analytical reports from tables as a tree search over atomic actions such as chapter planning, chart creation, and insight extraction, rather than a fixed linear pipeline. This allows joint optimization of factual accuracy, chart quality, and narrative coherence.

entry.title: Adversarially Robust Abductive Fusion of Pre-trained Transformer-based Perception Models

author.name: Mario Leiva, Yue Ma, Qinru Qiu, Gerardo Simari, Paulo Shakarian

entry.summary: Shows that a metacognitive error-detection layer over frozen perception models can be learned without hand-authored domain knowledge by exploiting embedding geometry, via per-model label vector pools derived from each model's own training embeddings. The resulting abductive fusion recovers accuracy under distribution shift better than voting-style combiners.

entry.title: NeuMoSync: End-to-End Neuromodulatory Control for Plasticity and Adaptability in Continual Learning

author.name: Seyed Roozbeh Razavi Rohani, Khashayar Khajavi, Wesley Chung, Mandana Samiei, Mo Chen

entry.summary: NeuMoSync adds learnable per-neuron feature vectors that track network-wide history plus a higher-level module that synthesizes neuron-specific modulatory signals, loosely inspired by brain neuromodulation. The goal is to counter plasticity loss and improve transfer in sequential continual learning.

entry.title: A/B Agent: A Self-Evolving Agent for Strategy Iteration in Industrial A/B Testing

author.name: Zhuohang Jiang, Yuxin Chen, Yongsen Pan, Zheng Hu, Wenqi Fan, Qing Li, Hongyang Wang, Jun Wang, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: A/B Agent automates industrial recommendation strategy iteration by organizing historical experiment knowledge hierarchically across business scenarios, recommendation stages, objectives, and experimental contexts, instead of flat retrieval. The self-evolving agent designs strategies, configures experiments, and reuses prior outcomes to reduce expert labor.

entry.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zikun Qu, Min Zhang, Mingze Kong, Zhiwei Shang, Yikun Ban, Shuang Qiu, Zhongxiang Dai

entry.summary: SPOT improves on-policy distillation by deciding both where to probe the teacher and what target to distill, using a position-level acquisition score that combines teacher uncertainty structure with whether the student already covers the plausible continuations, and calibrating targets against downstream outcome success. It addresses reverse-KL mode collapse onto a single continuation.

entry.title: When does training on downscaled images yield the same gradients?

author.name: Seunghyun Ji

entry.summary: Analyzes when training a diffusion transformer on downscaled images preserves the native-resolution gradient signal, decomposing the discrepancy into a noise-dependent term that vanishes at high noise and a resolution-dependent floor set by token count that no noise level removes. This challenges the spectral argument used to justify low-resolution training shortcuts.

entry.title: PhysMind: From Video to Executable Worlds for Training-Free Physical Reasoning

author.name: Chen Yang, Shenxiang Zeng, Haoyang Zhao, Zhouyuan Xu, Youquan He, Haoyu Li, Mingyi Deng, Jiansheng Fan, Chen Wang

entry.summary: PhysMind builds a reusable, question-agnostic executable world from a video by segmenting objects, reconstructing meshes, tracking 6D poses and fitting analytic continuous-time dynamics with latent physical parameters, then answers physical, predictive and counterfactual questions by querying or editing that world. It requires no training.

entry.title: Elbow-Based MoE Routing: A Training-Free Inference Time Plugin for Expert Selection

author.name: Robin Pan, Raymond Liu, Daniel Fang, Adelina Andrei, Rosa Wu

entry.summary: Elbow-based routing is a training-free inference-time modification for mixture-of-experts models that varies the number of activated experts per token by locating an inflection point in the sorted router probabilities. The authors argue most router distributions have a clear elbow, letting compute follow token difficulty instead of a fixed top-k.

entry.title: When Modalities Fail to Tango: Conformal Backdoor Detection in Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Yiming Chen, Kemou Li, Haiwei Wu, Jiantao Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that CLIPScore-based backdoor detection in multimodal contrastive learning fails because benign and poisoned similarity distributions overlap heavily and fixed thresholds give no statistical guarantee. The authors integrate conformal prediction to obtain calibrated, guarantee-bearing detection of poisoned image-text pairs.

entry.title: Dynamical Lie Algebras Cannot Describe Shallow QAOA: Cragged Terrains, Barren Plateaus, and Empirical Hardness Models

author.name: Harrison Copp, Charlton Li, An\v{z}ej Margeta-Cacace, Amy Qiao

entry.summary: A large numerical study across roughly 23,000 QAOA instances for maximum independent set finds that dynamical Lie algebra theory badly mispredicts shallow-circuit behavior: barren plateaus are rare and variances often grow polynomially with system size, a regime the authors call cragged terrains. It also builds empirical hardness models for these landscapes.

entry.title: PriDyG: Privacy-preserving Dynamic Graph Inference with LLM-GNN Collaboration

author.name: Yuyang Xia, Ruixuan Liu, Li Xiong

entry.summary: Formulates edge-level differentially private inference over dynamic graphs and proposes PriDyG, which pairs GNN structural learning with LLM semantic reasoning and buffers new edges so each is processed exactly once. Parallel composition makes total privacy cost equal to a single static release regardless of how many model updates occur.

entry.title: Beyond Global Routing Aggregation: Phase-Aware Expert Merging for MoE Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hongyu Zhang, Cheng Yan, Xiang Xia, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Points out that mixture-of-experts vision-language inference is phase-structured, with image-context, question, and answer tokens routing differently, so merging experts using globally aggregated routing statistics is dominated by the numerous image tokens. The proposed phase-aware merging preserves phase-conditioned expert roles while shrinking the stored expert pool without retraining.

entry.title: DIVE: Dynamic Iterative Visual Evidence Construction for Efficient Vision-Language Models

author.name: Chen Zhong, Xiao An, Zijie Wang, Jiepan Li, Guangyi Yang, Wei He

entry.summary: DIVE is a training-free visual token pruning method that recasts pruning as iterative evidence construction, repeatedly selecting the token with the highest residual-conditioned score and updating residuals rather than scoring all tokens once. The insight is that a token's usefulness depends on what evidence has already been retained.

entry.title: Intrinsic-Hybrid Latent Diffusion Models for Generative Modeling on Unknown Manifolds

author.name: Yizhu Wang, Mu Niu, Xiaochen Yang

entry.summary: ILDM couples probabilistic dimensionality reduction with geometry-aware diffusion, treating the latent space as a chart of an unknown Riemannian manifold so the generative process respects intrinsic geometry. This targets data-sparse regimes where standard latent diffusion imposing Euclidean latent structure performs poorly.

entry.title: The Neural Echo: A Signal Processing Perspective for Understanding Neural Networks

author.name: Chongbiao Wang, Daniel Gaa, Joachim Weickert, Karl Schrader

entry.summary: Introduces neural echoes, generalizing impulse responses and diffusion echoes from classical signal processing to neural networks so that local, input-dependent, space-adaptive filter kernels can be visualized via an affine mapping. The tool applies to convolutional, fully connected, recurrent, and transformer-style image and classification networks.

entry.title: MemArena: An Ego-Centric Benchmark for On-Device Agentic Personal Memory Assistants at Scale

author.name: Jiadong Zhang, Xiaosong Ma

entry.summary: MemArena is a simulated single-world benchmark for on-device personal memory assistants, generating 15 days of activity-dense ego-centric interactions among 50 agents with about 10.3M dialog tokens and co-generated ground truth across six recall, reasoning, and trustworthiness dimensions. It compares open-weight readers with vanilla context, BM25 retrieval, oracle retrieval, and two memory backends.

entry.title: Crayotter: Learning Long-Horizon Video Editing Agents via Group-Relative Preference Backpropagation

author.name: Lecheng Yan, Jianze Lin, Yichong Zhang, Ben Pan, Wenxi Li, Chenyang Lyu, Liting Zhou, Cathal Gurrin

entry.summary: Crayotter trains long-horizon video editing agents with group-relative preference backpropagation, converting rankings among alternatives for the same request into zero-sum advantages and redistributing them as bounded credit across semantic editing segments. This sidesteps the ill-posedness of a global scalar reward for subjective, multi-solution editing tasks.

entry.title: SeqLLM: Augmenting LLMs with Behavioral-Sequence Modeling for High-Stakes Decisions at WeChat Pay

author.name: Guilin Li, Jiaxing Zhang, Matthias Hwai Yong Tan, Bo Wang, Weiran Huang

entry.summary: Adds behavioral-sequence modeling to a pretrained LLM for merchant risk screening at a large payment platform by tokenizing behavioral events into a compact discrete vocabulary and aligning them via a lightweight projector in two stages. Designed to avoid catastrophic forgetting of language ability while fusing text profiles with long event sequences.

entry.title: Activation-Guided Neuron Intervention to Induce Alzheimer's-Related Computational Language Phenotypes in a Large Language Model

author.name: Rui He, Ercong Nie, Hong Jiang, Iris E. Sommer, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen

entry.summary: Identifies feed-forward neurons in an 8B model that activate more for Alzheimer-associated transcripts and scales their down-projection weights to create edited model variants. Runs original and edited models through a neuropsychological battery to test whether those representations functionally drive clinically relevant language phenotypes.

entry.title: PDD-RRG: Posterior Diagnostic Decision for Study-level Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Yang Yu, Yiming Ji, Bin Dai, Dong Zhang, Zhiyong Zhou, Shoushan Li, Yakang Dai

entry.summary: PDD-RRG adds a decision-making stage after radiology report generation, producing reports from several different subsets of available inputs (views, priors) and then reconciling conflicting diagnoses into a final study-level report. This targets cases where adding multi-view or historical context actually introduces errors.

entry.title: Convex-Hull-Neighborhood Smooth Dual Generalization: Controlling Local Correction Propagation in Offline RL

author.name: Yi Yang, Zhennan Chen, Mingfeng Lv, Hanlei Li, Zhengsen Ruan, Lvqing Yang

entry.summary: CSDG reformulates the offline RL Bellman backup as an in-sample value target plus an explicit local correction over a convex-hull neighborhood, so the contribution from out-of-distribution actions is separated and smoothed rather than implicitly regularized. The goal is to gain from nearby OOD actions without bootstrapped error amplification.

entry.title: When Outputs Disperse, Does Epistemic Revision Follow? A Black-Box Diagnostic for Machine Collectives

author.name: Molood Arman

entry.summary: Introduces a black-box diagnostic for whether increased output diversity in multi-agent LLM collectives actually reflects revised epistemic stances or merely premise-preserving rephrasing. It measures dispersion in embedding space separately from genuine conclusion revision, challenging the assumption that disagreement implies epistemic diversity.

entry.title: BanglaWild: An In-the-Wild Bengali Scene Text Recognition Benchmark for OCR and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sadab Shiper, Tawsif Tashwar Dipto, Mir Md Inzamam, Eshat Tanzeem

entry.summary: BanglaWild is an in-the-wild Bengali scene text benchmark of 2,535 images with verbatim transcriptions, diagnostic attributes, and standardized spellings, evaluating fifteen vision-language models and three conventional OCR systems side by side. Six open models are also LoRA fine-tuned as baselines.

entry.title: PADFormer: Pose-agnostic Anomaly Detection from Sparse View Images

author.name: Ruiqi Wang, Yiming Qian, Fenggen Yu, Yuxuan Lu, Dakuo Wang, Hao Zhang, Jing Huang

entry.summary: PADFormer performs pose-agnostic anomaly detection entirely in image space by using a vision transformer to reconstruct an anomaly-free version of a query image while preserving pose, trained only on normal data with dynamic patch selection and spatial alignment from sparse reference views. This avoids the expensive 3D reconstruction pipelines prior methods rely on.

entry.title: Free-Lunch Augmentation by Revisiting Diffusion-Based Data Generation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Object Detection

author.name: Zijian Zhuang, Yixiong Zou, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: Revisits diffusion-based synthetic data augmentation for cross-domain few-shot object detection, finding that naive generation performs worse than using the original scarce images. The authors separate visual from semantic domain gaps and address each independently to make synthetic augmentation actually helpful.

entry.title: Season: Spectrum-Aware Orthogonal Gradient Refinement for Transfer-Based Adversarial Attacks

author.name: Tianyi Wang, Zhenghao Gao, Shengjie Xu

entry.summary: Season improves transfer of adversarial examples between CNNs and vision transformers by splitting each gradient update into low-frequency structural and high-frequency textural branches, pushing high-frequency energy into background regions and projecting the textural update orthogonally to the structural direction. This preserves the global shape cues that transformers rely on.

entry.title: REZE: Recognition-Based Zero-Shot Extraction for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Boyang Li, Chenhui Gou, Jianfei Cai

entry.summary: REZE performs zero-shot video temporal grounding without asking the model to emit timestamps: it splits video into short clips, queries the model for per-clip confidence, and applies a deterministic algorithm to convert the score curve into an interval. This removes dependence on each model's idiosyncratic timestamp formatting ability.

entry.title: Coupled Continuous-Discrete Generation for Scene Text Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Axi Niu, Knag Zhang, Qingsen Yan, Hao Jin, Jinqiu Sun, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: DualTSR treats scene text image super-resolution as coupled continuous-discrete generation, using conditional flow matching for the image latents and absorbing-state discrete diffusion for text tokens over a shared multimodal transformer. This removes the need for an external OCR prior at inference and the associated error propagation.

entry.title: VoxStruct3D: Structure-Leading Flow Matching for Voxel-Space 3D MRI Synthesis

author.name: Fang Li, Yang Gao, Shihao Zou, Weixin Si, Hongyu Wu, Qing Xia, Shuai Li, Aimin Hao

entry.summary: VoxStruct3D generates full-resolution 3D MRI volumes directly in voxel space with flow matching and a clean-data prediction objective, avoiding the reconstruction bottleneck imposed by latent diffusion autoencoders. Its generator uses factorized 3D patch embedding with overlapping upsampling and time-modulated residual refinement to suppress patch-boundary artifacts.

entry.title: OutLangSplat: 3D Language Gaussian Splatting for UAV Outdoor Scenes

author.name: Xia Yan, He Wu, Yanghui Xu, Zizhao Wu, Jiazhou Chen

entry.summary: OutLangSplat adapts open-vocabulary 3D language Gaussian splatting to UAV outdoor scenes, where severe occlusion and long-distance viewpoints cause incorrect semantic activation and missing targets in existing indoor-oriented methods. It uses a dual-branch 2D-3D representation with region-based alignment and fusion to improve feature reliability.

entry.title: Overcoming Statistical Bias in Action-Controllable World Models

author.name: Yuhong Shi, Zhenhao Chu, Jie Wei, Jun Hao, Jianyi Liu, Jingwen Fu

entry.summary: Argues that action-conditioned world models often ignore the action because future frames are largely predictable from visual inertia, so they learn statistical shortcuts. Proposes enforcing consistency under counterfactual changes to actions and observations so that predicted dynamics genuinely depend on the control input.

entry.title: Rethinking Pixel Mean Flows via Interval Denoiser

author.name: Alexander Zaytsev, Dmitry Baranchuk, Alexander Korotin, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: Derives an interval-denoising formulation directly from the flow matching ODE that gives an exact analytical target for intermediate trajectory states, enabling few-step generation directly in pixel space without an external autoencoder. Argues the prediction target lies on a low-dimensional manifold, making pixel-space regression tractable.

entry.title: ContextMaster: Interactive Multi-Shot Video Creation via Fixed-Budget Sparse Context Routing

author.name: Xu Guo, Zhengxuan Wei, Xinghui Li, Hanzhuo Huang, Xinyu Liu, Xiangyang Luo, Min Wei, Yiran Zhu, Qiulin Wang, Yulong Xu, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wan, Qi Fan, Xiangwang Hou

entry.summary: Formalizes interactive multi-shot video creation where one model must generate from text, follow references, and edit footage while retaining an expanding shared history, and proposes a role-aware context representation with reusable clean context states and fixed-budget sparse context routing. This keeps per-denoising-step context cost constant as the session grows.

entry.title: CoCo-IR: Contextual Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Shengcao Cao, Tanmaya Shekhar Dabral, Zhongli Ding, Madhuri Shanbhogue, Kaifeng Chen, Zhe Li, Mojtaba Seyedhosseini, Yu-Xiong Wang, Liang-Yan Gui

entry.summary: Defines multi-turn composed image retrieval where users iteratively refine a search, and proposes a large multimodal model that reads the whole interaction history to produce embeddings that evolve across turns. Includes an autonomous data engine to generate training interactions without human annotation.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks for Good: A Survey of Proactive Protection across the Visual Content Lifecycle

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Boyang Chen, Zherui Li, Fuyao Zhang, Xinyu Yan, Hong Xi Tae, Wenwen He, Xuan Wang, Siqi Guo, Junhao Dong, Kun Wang, Hanxun Huang, Yige Li, Xingjun Ma, Yang Cao, Lingjuan Lyu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: Surveys the inversion in which adversarial perturbations and structured signals are deployed by creators, platforms, and auditors to protect visual content across its lifecycle, from release to unauthorized model use to later accountability. Unifies five research communities that converged on this protective paradigm independently.

entry.title: Emergence of Reputation-Based Cooperation in LLM Agents

author.name: Kazuya Horibe, Kenji Itao, Wataru Toyokawa

entry.summary: Studies whether cooperation among language-model agents survives free-rider invasion in an indirect reciprocity donation game where prompt-encoded strategies evolve culturally across generations. Finds robustness varies by over an order of magnitude across four model backends, best predicted by how strongly agents discriminate cooperative from uncooperative partners rather than by adherence to classical norm rules.

entry.title: DreamWAM: Beyond RGB Future Prediction for World Action Models

author.name: Shanglin Yuan, Weiheng Zhao, Xin Shi, Haoyi Jiang, Xianda Guo, Liu Liu, Wenyu Liu, Wei Sui, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Argues world action models should predict action-relevant future state instead of raw RGB frames, where task dynamics are entangled with texture, lighting, and viewpoint nuisances. Jointly denoises RGB and motion latents while adding lightweight gated branches for geometry and semantics as complementary prediction targets.

entry.title: SpikingNav: Robust Embodied Navigation with Spiking Neural Policies

author.name: Jiahong Zhang, Sijun Shen, Dehua Wu, Yifan Lin, Xuechen Xia, Xu Chu, Youhui Zhang, GuoqiLi

entry.summary: SpikingNav applies spiking neural networks to indoor embodied navigation, using event-driven spiking sensing and spiking policy dynamics instead of dense conventional network computation. The claimed benefit is robustness to visual corruption plus lower compute suited to resource-constrained robots. It probes an open question of whether neuromorphic computation actually helps in visually rich sequential decision-making rather than just saving energy.

entry.title: 34 Amazon Research Awards Build on Trainium recipients announced

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon announced 34 recipients of its Build on Trainium research awards, part of a 110 million dollar compute credit program for academic AI research on AWS Trainium silicon, with this cycle focused on responsible AI topics including safety and alignment, multilingual models, representation engineering, sustainable small language models, and synthetic data generation. Recipients get credits, dataset access and an Amazon research contact. Signals continued vendor competition to seed academic ecosystems around non-NVIDIA accelerators.

entry.title: MultiPathFormer: Towards a Foundation Model for Multipath Wireless Propagation

author.name: Blessed Guda, Kayley Sze, Carlee Joe-Wong

entry.summary: MultiPathFormer proposes multipath propagation, rather than raw channel tensors, as the pretraining object for wireless foundation models, representing each link as an ordered sequence of continuous path tokens trained with next-path prediction. It adds environment-aware retrieval augmentation to condition predictions on deployment geometry.

entry.title: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains

author.name: Ayoub Kirouane, Christos Petrocheilos

entry.summary: This work builds an end-to-end Modern Greek retrieval-augmented generation stack on top of NVIDIA Nemotron retrieval models, covering corpus mining, synthetic supervision, embedder and reranker training, reader fine-tuning and a new HERA benchmark. Notably, BM25 beats several off-the-shelf multilingual dense retrievers on specialist Greek corpora, while fine-tuning lifts a 1B embedder from 0.362 to 0.835 nDCG@10.

entry.title: From Non-Convex Self-Concordant Regularization to Scalable Quasi-Newton Training of PINNs

author.name: Chenhao Si, Kang An, Shiqian Ma, Ming Yan

entry.summary: SCORE is a quasi-Newton optimizer for physics-informed neural networks that couples a self-concordance-inspired decrement from the learned inverse metric to both step selection and secant shifting, addressing the indefinite and badly scaled curvature of PDE residual objectives. It targets scalable high-accuracy refinement of PINN solutions.

entry.title: Robustness Emerges Early in Training Dynamics, but Is Not Preserved

author.name: Jiangang Yang, Wenhui Shi, Lu Hu, Jing Xing, Jian Liu

entry.summary: The authors report a robustness fading phenomenon in which shallow layers spontaneously acquire corruption-robust representations and flat loss landscapes early in training but lose them by convergence. They propose two parameter-free interventions, early-phase stabilization and asymmetric weight reversion, to retain or recover those early robust configurations.

entry.title: Robust Control under Stationary Ambiguity

author.name: Konrad J. Mueller, Amira Akkari, Ben Wood, Lukas Gonon

entry.summary: This work addresses a subtle failure of domain randomization: as a policy gradually infers the true simulator parameters during an episode, it specializes and loses robustness, which is undesirable in high-stakes control. The authors formulate robust control under stationary ambiguity so robustness is maintained rather than eroded by online identification.

entry.title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation

author.name: Bhavin Jawade, Cameron R. Wolfe

entry.summary: Benchmarks small, large and reasoning models on MQM-style translation quality evaluation and then distills jury judgments from multiple LLMs into a small model for real-time scoring. Aims to retain reasoning-model evaluation quality at deployable cost.

entry.title: On the Non-Specificity of Statistical Measures Used in Script Decipherment

author.name: Nikhil Raghavendra

entry.summary: Builds a synthetic emblem corpus with compositional but non-phonological meanings and shows it reproduces the same statistical signatures cited as evidence that the Indus script encodes language. Argues that most published decipherment statistics lack specificity because structured non-languages pass the same tests.

entry.title: CVPO: Enhancing LLM Reinforcement Learning Reasoning via Value-Variance Adaptation and Dynamic Curriculum Learning

author.name: Ziqi Jia, Yalu Ouyang, Bo Pang, Panpan Li, Hangfei Xu, Shengzhao Wen, Shiyong Li, Yanpeng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an RL algorithm for reasoning that uses token-level value-variance as a proxy for exploration intensity to adjust advantages, combined with a dynamic curriculum that counters problem difficulty drift during training. Provides a theoretical bound linking variance to policy update magnitude.

entry.title: What Language Does and What the Evidence Supports: A Functional Role Taxonomy and Evidence Audit of Language Grounding in Embodied Agents

author.name: Yifan Guo, Chenghao Li, Zhu Wang, Wei Xu, Yu Li, Yulong Zhu, Zhuo Sun, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu

entry.summary: Survey that separates what language is claimed to do in embodied agents from what evidence supports those claims, defining five functional roles from task specification to execution coupling. Audits the literature and finds a persistent gap where linguistic intermediates are interpretable but not demonstrably causal for behavior.

entry.title: Relational Priors as Convergence Pressure in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Ming Shen, Chao Shang, Sadat Shahriar, Devang Kulshreshtha, Yi Zhang, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi

entry.summary: Injects explicit relational priors, expressed as signed-network relationships rendered in natural language, into multi-agent system prompts while holding protocols fixed. Finds that more positive relational framing mainly acts as convergence pressure, speeding agreement in ways that can help or cause premature consensus.

entry.title: Predicting Multilingual Classification and Translation Performance of LLMs with Cross-Lingual Alignment $\unicode{x2013}$ Is English Enough?

author.name: Adnan Al Ali, Kathy H\"ammerl, Jind\v{r}ich Libovick\'y, Alexander Fraser

entry.summary: Compares 27 variants of cross-lingual alignment scores and different embedding extraction methods to see how well internal alignment to English predicts downstream multilingual performance. Extends the analysis beyond classification to generative machine translation, where prior work had not tested predictiveness.

entry.title: Language-Specialized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR

author.name: Yuan Xie, Jiaqi Song, Xianliang Wang, Ming Lei, Jie Gao, Jie Wu

entry.summary: Decouples multilingual speech recognition training by first optimizing language-specialized teachers with reinforcement learning, then merging their expertise into one multilingual student through on-policy distillation. Aims to avoid the optimization conflicts that arise from jointly modeling acoustically and phonologically heterogeneous languages.

entry.title: Predicting Deep Neural Network Training Outcomes from Early Training Telemetry

author.name: Ranjita Naik, Anh D. Nguyen, Pankaj Kumar Singh

entry.summary: Tests whether a single run's early-epoch telemetry, including loss curves, gradient signal-to-noise ratio, weight-norm growth and activation saturation, can predict its final accuracy and detect doomed or diverging configurations. Uses gradient-boosted trees over 23,788 runs across six architecture and dataset combinations.

entry.title: M-GATE: Multilingual Grammar, Accuracy in Translation, and Efficiency Benchmark for Large Language Models

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Burkert, Angelika Peljak-{\L}api\'nska, David Zelen\'y

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of linguistic proficiency, as distinct from task performance in a language, across 30 typologically diverse languages using adversarially selected grammatical error detection and round-trip translation judged by a validated three-provider panel. Argues most multilingual benchmarks conflate fluency with genuine command of a language.

entry.title: MultiGlobeQA: A Multilingual and Globally Diverse Benchmark for Geospatial Reasoning

author.name: Martin B\"ockling, Elizaveta Nosova, Heiko Paulheim, Andreea Iana

entry.summary: Releases a multilingual geospatial reasoning benchmark of 46,060 questions across 14 spatial-function families with execution-based ground truth from knowledge graphs, covering 201 countries with stratified sampling. Targets the gap between models storing geographic facts and actually computing distances, containment and topological relations.

entry.title: AI-based single-shot structured-light depth reconstruction for real-time laparoscopic surgical guidance

author.name: Wayne Wonseok Rodgers, Xiangyi Le, Seonghoon Jang, Shuwen Wei, Justin Opfermann, Michael Kam, Axel Krieger, Jin U. Kang

entry.summary: A single-shot depth-sensing system for laparoscopic surgery that pairs a passive LED-illuminated binary mask projector with a learned reconstruction stack combining a VQ-VAE prior and a U-Net depth head, avoiding the multi-shot capture and projector-camera synchronization required by conventional fringe projection. Ground truth came from a commercial 3D camera. Useful for real-time intraoperative perception in semi-autonomous surgical robotics.

entry.title: An adaptive split-combine Gaussian mixture filter for nonlinear and multimodal state estimation

author.name: San Kim (Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Won Chang (Department of Statistics, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea, The Institute for Data Innovation in Science, Seoul National University, Seoul, Republic of Korea), Daniel B. Forger (Department of Mathematics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA, Department of Computational Medicine and Bioinformatics, University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, MI, USA), Dae Wook Kim (Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea, KI for Human Augmentation Convergence, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea)

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive Gaussian mixture filter that dynamically splits and merges mixture components to track asymmetric and multimodal state distributions in nonlinear, oscillatory or chaotic systems where Kalman-style single-Gaussian assumptions break down. The adaptive component management targets the long-standing challenge of controlling mixture size and weights during propagation. Applicable to computational biology and other nonlinear dynamical state estimation problems.

entry.title: Agreement Before Diversity: Verification-First Complementarity for Heterogeneous Language-Model Coordination

author.name: Ruitong Li, Binjie Guo, Aisheng Mo, Guowei Su, Jie Li, Ru Zhang

entry.summary: Agreement-Before-Diversity is a label-free rule for heterogeneous LLM ensembles: an anchor answer is kept if two additional trusted samples corroborate it under a fixed equivalence relation, otherwise it is replaced by a synthesis across models. The authors prove exact identities relating the accuracy gap to agreement coverage and conditional correctness.

entry.title: A Trust-region Framework for Moment Estimation

author.name: Oluwasegun A. Somefun

entry.summary: Develops a trust-region interpretation of adaptive moment methods in which each weight update is constrained by a moment condition of order between two and four, yielding a family of learning-rate mechanisms including a kurtosis-like variant. The framework unifies moment normalization, learning-rate scheduling, and spectral filtering views of optimizers.

entry.title: COMPAS: Difficulty-Aware Joint Search for Optimizing Code Generation

author.name: Jingzhi Gong, Jie M. Zhang, Gunel Jahangirova, Dong Huang, Mohammad Reza Mousavi, Mark Harman

entry.summary: COMPAS jointly searches over model choice, prompt, and decoding settings for code generation, and conditions the chosen configuration on task difficulty rather than fixing one global configuration. The empirical analysis shows prompts and decoding parameters interact and that optimal settings vary by model and by task hardness.

entry.title: FinReportBench: Measuring and Improving Institution-Grade Financial Report Generation

author.name: Yinghao Tang, Tan Zhenwei, Yiyao Wang, Wanli Gu, Xiaolu Zhang, Jun Zhou, Wei Chen

entry.summary: FinReportBench is an expert-grounded bilingual benchmark of 244 tasks for institution-grade financial research reports, with a 35-item rubric derived from expert partial orders covering report identity, source discipline, institutional completeness and visual delivery. It measures whether output is actually deliverable rather than merely fluent.

entry.title: When Absence Is Evidence: Evaluating Completeness-Sensitive Negative Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Byoungjae Min, Kennedy Edemacu, Sae-Hong Cho, Yoonhyuk Choi, Beakcheol Jang, Jong Wook Kim

entry.summary: Introduces the notion of completeness-sensitive negative reasoning, where an LLM should answer that something is absent only if the evidence provably covers the query scope, and otherwise say unknown. Paired synthetic and real-document evaluations vary only coverage and show models over-close, conflating justified negatives with unjustified ones.

entry.title: InsightEmb: Learning Action-Intent Embeddings for Agentic Insight Retrieval

author.name: Tsz Ting Chung, Jiangnan Li, Jie Zhou, Mo Yu

entry.summary: InsightEmb is a contrastive embedding model for retrieving prior experiential insights that actually resolve an agent's current decision bottleneck, rather than ones that merely look semantically similar. It learns transferable progress-oriented retrieval geometry using only mathematical reasoning trajectories.

entry.title: Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Observation-Calibrated Self-Distillation

author.name: Yi Yang, Cong Qin, Xiaodan Liu, Chishui Chen, Qing Dong, Yan Zhang, Cao Liu, Zhao Yang, Lu Pan, Jiaye Lin, Yi Feng

entry.summary: Improves agentic RL by refining on-policy self-distillation, where tokens are rescored under a privileged replay view to get dense supervision from sparse trajectory rewards. The paper isolates a confound in which the apparent benefit mixes true privileged information with artifacts of the replay scaffold, and proposes observation-calibrated correction.

entry.title: A-SR: Self-Evolving Agentic LLMs for Symbolic Regression via Hierarchical Coordination

author.name: Wenxiao Zhao, Dong Liu, Kaiyi Xu, Feng Liu, Zhen Zhao, Fei Ben, Shu Wang, Wenhao Li, Yingnian Wu, Fenghua Ling, Haobo Li, Lei Bai

entry.summary: A-SR is a self-evolving multi-agent framework for symbolic regression that replaces the usual single-prompt, scalar-score proposal loop with role-conditioned evidence views, routing elite motifs, failure traces and validity diagnostics to different agents and updating role utilities online. It self-evolves at both the protocol and role-policy level.

entry.title: Physics-informed reduced-order modelling with equivariant spectral submanifolds

author.name: Georg Maierhofer

entry.summary: This paper introduces equivariant spectral submanifold reduction, proving that spectral submanifolds inherit the symmetries of the full-order system and exploiting this to cut the cost of computing nonlinear reduced-order models for high-dimensional dynamical systems. It extends a principled alternative to linear methods such as dynamic mode decomposition.

entry.title: Optimal Training-Time Scaling in Gradual Adaptation

author.name: Zonghuan Xu, Krishna Harish

entry.summary: For gradual domain adaptation with overparameterized linear regression, the paper shows learning progress converges to a continuum curve and is small for both very short and very long per-task training, implying optimal per-task training time scales inversely with the number of intermediate tasks. Experiments on rotated MNIST and a natural year-shift dataset support the prediction.

entry.title: Aligning Large Vision-Language Models at Test Time: A Trajectory-Guided Structured Sampling Approach

author.name: Tianbao Jiang, Weicong Ni, Gerard de Melo, Linlin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes test-time alignment for vision-language models using a memory bank of learned reasoning trajectories to guide structured sampling at inference, avoiding costly post-training RL. Intended to improve visual grounding and logical consistency while sidestepping train-inference distribution mismatch.

entry.title: Interoceptive Attention as Dynamic Homeostatic Prioritization in a Foraging Agent

author.name: St John Grimbly, Nicolas Kuske, Evert A. Boonstra, Bruce A. Bassett, Charel van Hoof, Rowan Hodson, Benjamin Rosman, Ryan Smith, Mark Solms, Jonathan P. Shock

entry.summary: Studies an active-inference foraging agent that must satisfy multiple bodily needs under a fixed perceptual precision budget, dynamically reallocating interoceptive precision toward whichever internal channel is most in deficit. In a four-channel gridworld this selective allocation more than doubles survival during learning at equal budget.

entry.title: MESH: Memory-Efficient Sinkhorn Optimization for Mixture-of-Experts Training

author.name: Masato Fujitake

entry.summary: Diagnoses why memory-efficient Sinkhorn-style optimizers fail on mixture-of-experts pretraining, identifying routed expert matrices with conditional, time-varying gradients as the culprit, and proposes a hidden-momentum Sinkhorn update to fix it. Experiments are on a 110M-parameter DeepSeek-style MoE.

entry.title: Consistency-Driven Co-Evolution for Self-Supervised Cross-Representation Learning

author.name: Xuehang Guo, Pengyuan Li, Tom Hope, Tirthankar Ghosal, Manling Li, Qingyun Wang

entry.summary: CoCoEvolve tackles consistency across chart images, tables and visualization code by replacing ambiguous one-to-many supervision with explicit one-to-one correspondences and optimizing agreement between representations as a self-supervised signal. The goal is a training objective that generalizes beyond task-specific chart or code benchmarks.

entry.title: SVI-DAG: A Structured Variational Inference Approach to Bayesian Causal Discovery

author.name: Shrenik Zinage

entry.summary: SVI-DAG proposes a structured variational inference method for Bayesian causal discovery that models dependencies between graph edges and allows domain knowledge to be injected as inductive bias over DAG posteriors. It aims to give better-calibrated epistemic uncertainty over causal structures than prior factorized approximations.

entry.title: Unscented KalmanNet: a hybrid deep learning filter with calibrated posterior covariance for nonlinear state estimation

author.name: Minhyeok Ko, Abdollah Shafieezadeh

entry.summary: Unscented KalmanNet augments the unscented Kalman filter with two learned components while preserving the sigma-point structure, aiming to correct model mismatch and gain bias while still reporting a calibrated posterior covariance. Prior learned filters typically extend the EKF and either drop explicit covariance or leave mismatch-induced bias uncorrected.

entry.title: DASyR-LLM: Domain-Aware Symbolic Regression with LLMs for Kinetic Model Discovery

author.name: Roberto Aliaga Medina, Paulina Quintanilla, Antonio del Rio Chanona

entry.summary: Embeds an LLM inside an iterative symbolic regression loop for chemical kinetics, using it to critique candidate rate expressions on physicochemical plausibility and to steer the search. The aim is interpretable kinetic models that respect domain constraints instead of merely fitting data.

entry.title: Multimodal Alignment Through Joint Kernel Entropic Gromov--Wasserstein Optimal Transport

author.name: Yixuan Florence Wu, Yilun Zhu, Naichen Shi

entry.summary: Proposes JK-EGW, a Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport framework that aligns multiple modalities into a shared latent space using kernel-based within- and cross-modal affinities rather than raw feature distances. It targets the practical setting of strong unimodal encoders with scarce paired data and provides theoretical control over latent geometry.

entry.title: The Price of Isolation: Estimating the Ecosystem Cost of Symmetric Two-Sided A/B Testing

author.name: Yuanyuan Shen, Yiren Yan, Wenjie Li, Chunhui Zhu

entry.summary: Analyzes when symmetric two-sided isolation in marketplace A/B tests imposes lasting engagement costs, showing via extreme-value theory that the answer depends on the upper tail of match quality. Light or bounded tails make the isolation loss vanish as the catalog grows, while heavier tails leave a persistent cost, contradicting the intuition that scale washes out isolation effects.

entry.title: Nonparametric Goodness-of-fit Testing under Covariate Shift

author.name: Zhen Hou, Dong Xia

entry.summary: Develops nonparametric goodness-of-fit tests valid when labeled data come from a source population but the hypothesis concerns a target population, combining truncated importance-weighted kernel ridge regression with a multiplier bootstrap. Truncation stabilizes estimation and bootstrap calibration even when the density ratio is heavy-tailed.

entry.title: Knowing the Form, Not the Function: Automatically Auditing Answer--Authority Decoupling in Legal Benchmarks

author.name: Hsien-Jyh Liao

entry.summary: Audits whether answer correctness proxies for legal authority grounding using 238 Taiwan bar exam items where the governing statutory provision is known, finding that the two dimensions dissociate in both directions. In criminal law, 24 to 42 percent of valid responses were correct but cited the wrong authority, while 15 to 22 percent were wrong yet cited the right provision.

entry.title: ARCHead: Activation-Metric Residual Correction for Large Language Model Output Heads

author.name: \c{S}uayp Talha Kocabay, Talha R\"uzgar Akku\c{s}, Kamer Ali Yuksel

entry.summary: BBOWP-Bench evaluates whether LLMs can turn natural-language descriptions into well-posed black-box optimization problems, where only objective values are observable and no closed-form objective exists. Unlike prior benchmarks it scores search-space design and algorithm selection, not just translation into explicit mathematical expressions.

entry.title: PAMT: Process-Aligned Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Domain Machine Translation

author.name: Yongshi Ye, Biao Fu, Chongxuan Huang, Yidong Chen, Xiaodong Shi

entry.summary: Analyzes reasoning-model translation across 15 domains and four directions, finding explicit intermediate reasoning helps long or hard inputs but drifts on terminology-heavy and style-constrained text. Proposes process-aligned RL that assigns credit to individual translation reasoning steps rather than only final outputs.

entry.title: ArtECulture: Benchmarking Culture-Conditioned Visual Emotion Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaolin Chen, Xuemeng Song, Wenhao Shi, Xianjing Han, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 6,792 artworks labeled with culture-specific emotion perceptions and rationales across English, Chinese and Arabic cultural contexts, with balanced Western and non-Western content. Evaluates 16 multimodal models on predicting culture-conditioned emotional responses and explaining them.

entry.title: Beyond the Hivemind: Escaping LLM Homogeneity via Meta-Persona Anchoring and Sequential Temperature Scaling

author.name: Tairan Fu, Javier Conde, Carlos Arriaga, Gonzalo Mart\'inez, Pedro Reviriego, Javier Coronado-Bl\'azquez

entry.summary: Attacks output homogenization, where models converge on near-identical answers even at high sampling temperature, using a two-stage scheme in which the model first self-selects an idiosyncratic persona and then generates under filtered temperature scaling. Reports reduced inter-response similarity while preserving grammaticality through top-p filtering.

entry.title: Adaptive Modality Reliability Diagnosis and Restoration for Robust Multimodal Intent Recognition

author.name: Suraj Kumar, Mohnish Raj, Soumi Chattopadhayay, Chandranath Adak, Ayan Dutta

entry.summary: PRIME diagnoses per-sample modality reliability via a contextual log-variance estimate, then attempts to restore degraded modalities and reassess them in a closed loop, rather than simply down-weighting unreliable inputs. It targets multimodal intent recognition with noisy, missing, or conflicting linguistic, acoustic, and visual signals.

entry.title: CLIP-CC-Bench: Evaluating Paragraph-Level Video Descriptions in Video-Language Models

author.name: Mukhtiar Ali, Harsh Dubey, Sugam Mishra, Chulwoo Pack

entry.summary: CLIP-CC-Bench evaluates paragraph-level long-form video description using 90-second movie clips with expert-written reference paragraphs, scored by an ensemble of five LLM-based embedding models under coarse and fine-grained semantic matching. It targets the gap left by short-clip, single-sentence captioning benchmarks.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Action Recognition: Taxonomy, Methods, and Privacy-Utility Trade-offs

author.name: Sareer Ul Amin, Muhammad Ayaz, Muhammad Munsif, Sanghyun Seo

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided survey of 32 peer-reviewed privacy-preserving action recognition papers screened from 885 records, organizing mechanism families into a taxonomy and analyzing privacy-utility trade-offs. It highlights that the field suffers from incompatible threat models, inconsistent metrics, and no shared evaluation standard.

entry.title: ColorFD: A Finite-Difference Guided Black-Box Physical Adversarial Attack for Remote Sensing Object Detection

author.name: Tiannuo Guo, Guhang Qiu, Yuzhen Xie, Rui Feng, Ligang Li, Deliang Xiang

entry.summary: ColorFD is a black-box physical adversarial attack on remote sensing object detectors that places multiple pure-color patches whose positions and colors are optimized jointly with differential evolution and a target-wise fitness function. It targets the underexplored intersection of black-box and physically realizable attacks.

entry.title: MetaVideoAgent: Automated Video-Agent Evolution for Long-Form Video Understanding

author.name: Benlei Cui, Ruize Wang, Junjie Li, Jinhao Chen, Longtao Huang, Yinghao Chen, Yuwen Zhai, Jingqun Tang, Ruijian Jia, Weiwei Wu, Pengfei Sun, Haiwen Hong

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that automatically evolves the design of a video-understanding agent (preprocessing, perception tools, evidence localization) for a target long-video distribution, rather than using a fixed hand-built pipeline. It tackles the practical obstacles of extending automated agent search from text to video, where validating candidates on full long videos is expensive.

entry.title: HelloWorld: Enabling Socially Interactive Characters in Video World Models

author.name: Liangyang Ouyang, Ruicong Liu, Xuangeng Chu, Kaipeng Zhang, Yoichi Sato

entry.summary: Adds user-triggered social interaction to a video world model, so a button press makes an on-screen character turn, wave, nod, or greet the viewer. Uses a self-distillation pipeline that finetunes the generator on clips it synthesizes itself, jointly teaching camera-pose conditioning and interactive response.

entry.title: SAFECAST: Robust Failure Detection for VLA Policies with Contrast-Set Training and Calibration

author.name: Harshitha Rajaprakash, Aditeya Prajapati, Rong Xue, Abrar Anwar, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: Improves failure detection for vision-language-action robot policies by training and calibrating hidden-state risk probes on deliberately perturbed contrast sets, so detection holds under deployment shifts like clutter, lighting, and reworded instructions. Reports statistically significant gains over a strong baseline in both real-robot and simulated suites.

entry.title: Universal Function Approximation via Diffractive Optical Processors: Physical Limits, Error Bounds, and Learnability

author.name: Md Sadman Sakib Rahman, Che-Yung Shen, Aydogan Ozcan

entry.summary: Provides a unified theory showing that phase-encoded diffractive optical processors implement finite Fourier-feature expansions, with completeness following from classical approximation arguments and realizability limited by point-spread-function synthesis. Derives error bounds decomposing truncation, hardware, readout, and noise contributions, and links approximation complexity to optical degrees of freedom.

entry.title: NSF-HRPT: Neural Semantic Field meets Hierarchical Risk Perception Tree for Safety-Critical Scenario Assessment

author.name: Yu Zhao, Jiangyu Pan, Tao Hu, Ming Yin, Fan Yang, Jiangfan Liu, Xiubo Liang

entry.summary: NSF-HRPT combines a learned neural semantic field that predicts scene semantics, trajectories, and probabilistic time-to-collision distributions with a hierarchical risk perception tree providing structured reasoning for quantitative driving-risk assessment from monocular vision. It targets safety-critical scenario evaluation for autonomous driving.

entry.title: CheckOne: Lightweight Fault Detection and Mitigation for Vision Transformers

author.name: Mohammad Hasan Ahmadilivani, Sven-Markus Loorits, Jaan Raik

entry.summary: Evaluates the reliability of vision transformers under hardware faults and proposes CheckOne, a low-cost algorithm-based fault detection and mitigation scheme tailored to the heavy computation of ViTs. It mitigates critical faults at substantially lower overhead than conventional fault-tolerance methods.

entry.title: TwinIR: Coordinated Invisible Dual-Point Attacks on Online HD Map Construction

author.name: Haibo Hu, Jianghuai Deng, Chen Tang, Yang Lou, Qian Xu, Jianping Wang

entry.summary: TwinIR is a physical adversarial attack on online HD map construction for autonomous driving that identifies and jointly suppresses redundant geometric cues from neighboring road boundaries, which otherwise let the model recover the true road layout after a single-point perturbation. It optimizes for minimal, low-perceptibility attack points.

entry.title: GUARD: Grounding Uncertainty and Ablation-Based Risk Detection for Diffusion-Based VLAs

author.name: Suhas Hegde, Jitendra Yasaswi Bharadwaj Katta

entry.summary: GUARD detects at test time when a diffusion-based vision-language-action policy is producing plausible actions that are not actually grounded in the visual and language input, by ablating salient key-value cache entries and comparing denoising responses. It yields diagnostic signals like modality bias and grounding efficiency without retraining the policy.

entry.title: A Model Merging Approach for Continual MLLM Unlearning

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Linlin Zhang, Haoxuan Ji, Xianmin Ye, Zhenxing Niu, Haichang Gao

entry.summary: Addresses continual unlearning in multimodal LLMs, where repeatedly applying one-shot forgetting operations causes cumulative utility loss, rebound of supposedly forgotten content, and drift in retained knowledge. The method merges per-request unlearning adapters into a single adapter, informed by a leave-one-out analysis showing strong cross-task dependencies among them.

entry.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO

author.name: Xuzheng Yang, Jun Ling, Tao Huang, Caiyan Qin, Peng Wang

entry.summary: Targets generalized referring expression comprehension where a model must localize a described object if present and refuse if absent, a setting where MLLMs typically hallucinate bounding boxes. A refusal-calibrated GRPO variant improves rejection of nonexistent referents without the localization degradation seen with plain supervised fine-tuning or RL.

entry.title: RepoProbe: Benchmarking Architecture-Aware Repository Comprehension with Checklists

author.name: Yuexi Yang, Alyssa Wu, Ji Luo, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao Hu, Yuhong Liu, Zhen Qin

entry.summary: RepoProbe evaluates repository-level architectural comprehension with open-ended questions scored against checklists, arguing that GitHub-issue-based benchmarks let models pattern-match error logs instead of understanding code. It also names edit bias, the tendency to propose modifications prematurely instead of understanding existing architecture.

entry.title: SpecDrop: Parameter-Free Category-Conditioned Routing for Modular Specialization

author.name: Boyao Wang, Zhihan Lei

entry.summary: SpecDrop replaces learned mixture-of-experts routers with a fixed parameter-free scheme that assigns each branch a high weight for its designated category and small leakage otherwise, requiring category labels at inference. The experiments probe whether MoE specialization bottlenecks come from routing algorithms or from mismatch between training-signal granularity and target categories.

entry.title: Random features for Grassmannian kernel approximation with bounded rank-one projections

author.name: R\'emi Delogne, Laurent Jacques

entry.summary: This work develops random feature maps that approximate Grassmannian kernels using rank-one projections of subspace projection matrices followed by bounded periodic or binary nonlinearities. This avoids the full Gram matrices required by projection and Binet-Cauchy kernels, enabling scalable kernel methods over subspace-valued data.

entry.title: Diverse and Plausible Algorithmic Recourse via Tractable Recourse Distributions

author.name: Anagha Sabu, Hrithik Suresh, Narayanan C. Krishnan

entry.summary: Tractable Recourse Distributions models the whole space of feasible recourse actions probabilistically instead of optimizing for one or a few counterfactuals, so systems can offer multiple realistic routes to a favorable decision. The framework aims to satisfy diversity, plausibility and feasibility simultaneously rather than trading them off.

entry.title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuanhao Shen, Daniel Xavier de Sousa, Caio C\'esar Sifuentes Barcelos, Hongyu Guo, Xiaodan Zhu

entry.summary: Evaluates the diversity, not just the quality, of analogies produced by ten open and closed models and documents strong domain homogeneity where analogies cluster into a narrow set of source domains. Argues this constrains the use of LLMs for cross-domain ideation and scientific creativity.

entry.title: Calibrating Artificial Guilt: Neurally Grounded Reward Shaping for Prosocial Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Aaditya Mehta, Arya Shah

entry.summary: Derives a guilt weight from a public responsibility fMRI dataset by regressing momentary happiness changes on outcome types, then transplants that empirically calibrated weight into reward shaping for two PPO agents in a social lottery game. It compares neurally calibrated shaping against uniform and other shaping regimes for prosocial behavior.

entry.title: AI-driven Multimodal Representation Learning for Latent Mediation Structure Discovery of Socioeconomic Disadvantage, Psychosocial Factors, and Cardiometabolic Multimorbidity: Insights from the All of Us Research Program

author.name: Cong Cao, Shuangge Ma

entry.summary: Uses modality-specific variational autoencoders to embed socioeconomic, psychosocial, clinical, laboratory, behavioral, and genomic data from a large biobank cohort, then performs mediation analysis in latent space across hundreds of exposure-mediator-outcome combinations. The goal is to uncover pathways linking social disadvantage to cardiometabolic multimorbidity in about 20,000 participants.

entry.title: EASy: Towards Efficient LLM-Based Agentic System

author.name: Junnan Liu, Linhao Luo, Thuy-Trang Vu, Gholamreza Haffari

entry.summary: EASy trains an LLM orchestrator with reinforcement learning to jointly optimize task success and computational cost, giving it explicit knowledge of executor capabilities and intermediate execution feedback rather than routing from the task description alone. It targets generalization to unseen executors.

entry.title: Masked diffusion enables coherent beat tracking

author.name: Francesco Foscarin, Filip Korzeniowski, Richard Vogl

entry.summary: Attributes invalid beat-tracking outputs such as consecutive downbeats to models averaging over multiple plausible beat grids, and applies masked discrete diffusion with independent masking and other modifications so that predictions are built coherently through iterative inference. This removes the need for heavy post-processing.

entry.title: A General Sufficient Condition for Rewriting Horn-ALCHI Atomic Queries into GQL

author.name: David Carral, Calixte Gruson, Quentin Mani\`ere

entry.summary: This work studies when atomic ontology-mediated queries over the description logic Horn-ALCHI can be rewritten into the new ISO standard graph query language GQL. It introduces DL automata as a formalism and identifies a stratified automata class rewritable into two-way regular path query unions, a core GQL fragment.

entry.title: ORACLE: A Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning-Based Analog Circuit Design Optimizer with Large Language Models-Guided Exploration

author.name: Osei Brempong, Mohammed Ayman Habib, Vivan Poddar, Morteza Fayazi

entry.summary: ORACLE is an open-source multi-objective reinforcement learning framework for analog circuit sizing that preserves Pareto trade-offs instead of collapsing specifications into a single scalar reward, with LLM-guided exploration and reuse across changing specifications. It targets the retraining burden of prior RL circuit optimizers.

entry.title: Local Violation Certification for Linear Predict-Then-Optimize Pipelines

author.name: \c{S}. \.Ilker Birbil, Wenhao Chi

entry.summary: This framework certifies constraint violations in linear predict-then-optimize decision pipelines by exploiting structure instead of random scenario sampling, which becomes prohibitive when failures are rare. It shows analytically why sampling is inefficient for rare violations and provides local certificates that also explain why failures occur.

entry.title: Statistical learning theory and Occam's razor: Regularization

author.name: Tom F. Sterkenburg

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science argument that statistical learning theory supplies a genuine, non-pragmatic justification for regularization as a preference for simplicity over fit. The claim is a means-ends justification: reliability and worst-case guarantees require implementing such a preference.

entry.title: Learning Sexism Detection Using Multi-Agent Perspectivist Preference Optimization

author.name: Hadi Mohammadi, Tina Shahedi, Robert A. Bagheri, Mehdi Dastani, Masoume M. Raeissi

entry.summary: Proposes MAP-PO, which preserves annotator disagreement in sexism detection by clustering annotators on labeling behavior, fine-tuning one LLM agent per cluster, and coordinating agents with preference optimization mixing individual and team rewards. It is evaluated on the bilingual EXIST 2024 tweet dataset.

entry.title: Right Reset: Chunking by Prefix Removal

author.name: Mike Vegeto

entry.summary: Observes that deleting the left context of a causal language model barely changes processing of right-hand tokens at true document boundaries, and turns this into an unsupervised chunking signal with a dynamic program producing variable-length chunks. On flattened concatenated records it recovers about 48 percent of original records as clean units versus about 26 percent for a strong embedding-based boundary baseline.

entry.title: Helping Music Co-Creation Agents 'Listen' Well: Hierarchical Self-Supervised World Models for Understanding and Generation

author.name: Scott H. Hawley

entry.summary: Trains a 2.55M-parameter Swin V2 encoder on MIDI piano-roll images with JEPA-style self-supervised objectives to build a hierarchical world model for symbolic music, using no labels or music-theory vocabulary. Probing shows the level at which a musical property becomes decodable tracks its natural time scale, from phrase boundaries at coarse levels to harmonic detail at fine levels.

entry.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

author.name: Javier Rodriguez-Juan, Hiba Arnaout, Jose Garcia-Rodriguez, David Tom\'as, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: ODRA synthesizes cognitive behavioral therapy dialogues using a structured chain-of-thought grounded in clinical CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that prevents simulated patients from being unrealistically compliant. It targets the twin failures of script-based rigidity and multi-agent structural drift in existing synthetic therapy data.

entry.title: VIVID: A Culturally Grounded Benchmark Exposing the Figurative Language Gap in Vietnamese NLP

author.name: Tu Tran Do, Nhat Ngoc Nguyen, Khanh-Tung Tran, Hoang D. Nguyen, Tu Minh Phuong, Long Hoang Dang

entry.summary: Releases a Vietnamese benchmark of 1,636 idioms and proverbs annotated with complexity traits and semantic themes, with generative and discriminative tasks scored by a validated LLM judge. Finds Vietnamese-specialized models underperform general multilingual systems on culturally grounded figurative language.

entry.title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction

author.name: Shufan Ming, Yikun Han, Gibong Hong, Rui Zhang, Halil Kilicoglu

entry.summary: Combines ontology-guided reasoning, external knowledge grounding and data-driven verification rules with LLM inference for biomedical relation extraction, targeting the false-positive problem of pure LLM approaches. Evaluated on three benchmarks plus an out-of-benchmark generalization check.

entry.title: FACTWASH: Catching AI Rewrites That Wash Hearsay into Fact

author.name: Alex Kwon

entry.summary: Defines factwashing as AI rewrites that preserve a claim while stripping attribution, hedging and temporal qualifiers that made it checkable, and releases a deterministic rule-based gate to flag it at write time. Argues cheap lexical checks suffice when the surface cue inventory is bounded, as with negation, while hedging and attribution need model-based detection.

entry.title: CIGTSurv: Clinical Information Guided Tri-modal Survival Prediction with Local Prototype Association and Global Feature Alignment

author.name: Jing Dai, Qibin Zhang, Weiwei Zhou, Mingde Xu, Jingsong Liu, Jingdong Zhang, Hongming Xu

entry.summary: CIGTSurv integrates clinical tabular data with pathology images and genomics for survival prediction by templating clinical records into text and embedding them with pretrained foundation models, then using clinical information as the anchor for cross-modal prototype association and alignment. It targets the underuse of sparse low-dimensional clinical variables in multimodal survival models.

entry.title: UniWorld-View: Large-Baseline View Synthesis via Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Haiyang Zhou, Wangbo Yu, Chaoran Feng, Xunyu Zhou, Yonghong Tian, Li Yuan

entry.summary: Uses video diffusion models to synthesize novel views far from the input viewpoint given only sparse monocular observations, where reconstruction methods such as NeRF and Gaussian splatting break down. Focuses on injecting stronger geometric guidance to keep large-baseline views consistent and camera control precise.

entry.title: Segmentation Pre-training for Label-Efficient Lumbar Spine Degeneration Grading

author.name: Monzon Maria, Zisserman Andrew, Jutzeler Catherine R., Jamaludin Amir

entry.summary: Tests whether pretraining a 3D encoder on cheap automatically generated segmentation pseudo-labels can substitute for expensive radiologist grading labels when classifying lumbar spine degeneration. Fine-tunes lightweight grading heads across label budgets from ten to one hundred percent on a multicentre cohort of roughly two thousand subjects.

entry.title: OmniEdit-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Instruction-based Video Editing

author.name: Chenxuan Miao, Yutong Feng, Yi Lu, Yunfeng Yan, Donglian Qi, Shiwei Zhang, Yu Liu, Xi Chen, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces a structured benchmark for instruction-based video editing that covers spatial, temporal, audio, and reference-based dimensions and adds metrics designed to catch edits that look plausible but ignore the instruction. Argues existing benchmarks inherit image-editing biases and reward visual priors from the source video.

entry.title: IRIS: A Visual Cortex-Inspired Framework for Analyzing Orientation Selectivity in Vision Transformers

author.name: Vaishnavi B Mohan, Vijayakrishna Naganoor, Yashas Annadani, Shashank Hegde

entry.summary: Analyzes whether vision transformers develop orientation-selective units analogous to those in primary visual cortex, despite lacking locality inductive biases, using a neuroscience-inspired probing framework. Aims to clarify mechanistically how ViTs encode low-level features shared across tasks.

entry.title: Objects as Audio-Visual Modal Sound Fields

author.name: Zisen Shao, Zihao Wei, Derong Jin, Ruohan Gao

entry.summary: Builds an object-level acoustic representation reconstructed from multi-view images plus only a handful of impact sound recordings, combining Gaussian splatting geometry priors with modal sound modeling. Enables predicting how an object sounds when struck at unseen locations without heavy physics simulation or large datasets.

entry.title: Algorithm-Driven SVARs: Navigating the Wilderness of Big Data

author.name: Yucheng Yang, Tao Zha

entry.summary: An econometrics contribution arguing that structural VAR conclusions depend not only on identifying restrictions, which the literature disciplines, but also on the hand-picked variable set, and proposing a Bayesian procedure that constructs information sets using an out-of-sample criterion and keeps the largest admissible system. Applications revise conclusions about housing versus household credit and strengthen the credit spread channel of monetary policy. Machine-learning-style model selection applied to macroeconomic identification.

entry.title: CoPlan: A Trustworthy Co-Intelligence Interface for Care Planning through Role-Based Contestable Argument Graphs

author.name: Hung Truong Thanh Nguyen, H\'el\`ene Fournier, Piper Jackson, Makoto Itoh, Shannon Freeman, Rene Richard, Hung Cao

entry.summary: CoPlan is a care-planning interface where specialized AI agents propose interventions along with supporting and challenging arguments, and human planners can accept, reject, modify, or add arguments before the final plan is produced. The design targets contestability rather than fixed AI recommendations.

entry.title: Temporal Context Awareness: A Defense Framework Against Multi-turn Manipulation Attacks on Large Language Models

author.name: Prashant Kulkarni, Assaf Namer

entry.summary: Proposes a defense framework against multi-turn manipulation attacks that build harmful context gradually across benign-looking conversational turns, by continuously tracking semantic drift, cross-turn intention consistency, and evolving conversational patterns. It targets a class of jailbreaks that single-turn detectors miss.

entry.title: C$^2$MOE: Consistency and Complementarity-guided Mixture of Experts for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Learning

author.name: Yuntao Shou, Tao Meng, Wei Ai, Keqin Li

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts framework for conversational emotion recognition when some modalities are missing, unifying representation learning and imputation under an information-theoretic objective that models both cross-modal consistency and complementarity. The claim is that consistency-only approaches produce biased reconstructions.

entry.title: Modality Agreement- and Conflict-Aware Prototype Hypergraph Learning for Multimodal Intent Understanding

author.name: Mohnish Raj, Suraj Kumar, Soumi Chattopadhayay, Chandranath Adak, Ayan Dutta

entry.summary: MACH models multimodal intent recognition by treating disagreement between text, audio, and visual channels as class-informative structure rather than noise, using a hierarchical prototype hypergraph that composes unimodal into bimodal and trimodal abstractions. Conflicting cues such as positive words with incongruent tone can then signal sarcasm or taunting.

entry.title: Combating Knowledge Corruption in Agent Systems: A Byzantine-Tolerant Secure Collaborative RAG Framework

author.name: Zhaoqi Wang, Daqing He, Zijian Zhang, Ye Liu, Jiamou Liu, Zhirui Zeng, Zhan Qin, Zhen Li, Xin Li, Hongwei Yao, Jincheng An, Yong Liu, Yi Li, Qi Sun, Xiulei Liu, Liehuang Zhu

entry.summary: SecureCollaRAG defends multi-agent retrieval-augmented systems against document poisoning by validating knowledge across multiple sources and scoring document provenance credibility with a graph neural network, framed as Byzantine tolerance. Formal analysis and empirical evaluation of stealthy corruption attacks are reported.

entry.title: NodeJEPA: Structure-Conditioned Latent Prediction for Node-Level Graph Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Tinghe Zhang, Jian Xu, Jiaheng Chen, Jiaxing Li, Yucheng Xiao, Qiang Wang

entry.summary: NodeJEPA extends joint-embedding predictive architectures to node-level graph self-supervised learning, predicting latent targets conditioned on structural signals instead of reconstructing node attributes or relying on hand-designed augmentations. It investigates which structural cues the predictor should be conditioned on.

entry.title: Approximate Multi-Objective Search Under Rulebooks

author.name: Omar Muhammetkulyyev, Oren Salzman, Tichakorn Wongpiromsarn

entry.summary: Introduces an approximate notion of dominance for robotic planning under rulebooks, which encode partially ordered priorities like safety before efficiency, and a best-first search algorithm that returns a compact epsilon-approximate optimal set. This makes rulebook-optimal planning computationally tractable.

entry.title: Guideline-as-Oracle: Zero-Annotation Training of an Ophthalmic Telephone Triage Agent

author.name: Chenyu Wang, Yi Liu, Baoqing Li, Min Tu, Diping Song
