entry.summary: Compiles ophthalmology guidelines into a 70-row rule table and uses it as the sole instance-level supervision signal for 3,000 synthetic training dialogues for a telephone triage agent, reserving human labels for evaluation only. The paper catalogs eight strategies for converting rules into dialogues and characterizes the evidential status of each.

entry.title: Towards a satellite image manipulation and deepfake localization benchmark dataset

author.name: Jacob Arndt, Debvrat Varshney, Philipe Dias, Nivedita Nukavarapu

entry.summary: Presents a satellite imagery manipulation and deepfake localization benchmark with fine-grained ground-truth masks, addressing the fact that existing remote sensing forensics datasets either lack localization labels or contain only wholly synthetic images. It supports training and evaluating detection and forensics algorithms.

entry.title: TS2TabPFN: Time Series Classification and Extrinsic Regression through Feature Extraction and a Tabular Foundation Model

author.name: Gabriel da Costa Merlin, Diego Furtado Silva

entry.summary: TS2TabPFN converts time series into engineered feature vectors and feeds them to the TabPFN 2.5 tabular foundation model for classification and extrinsic regression, aiming to combine controllable feature engineering with in-context tabular prediction. It positions tabular foundation models as a general backbone for temporal tasks.

entry.title: Transferable Dual-Stream Representations for Mesoscale-Preserving Sea Surface Temperature Downscaling

author.name: Parth Doshi, Priyanka Aravindan, Vaishnav Vaidheeswaran, Md Mahbub Alam, Gabriel Spadon

entry.summary: EddyFlow is a dual-stream representation learning framework for kilometer-scale sea surface temperature downscaling designed to preserve mesoscale eddy structure rather than only minimizing pixel-wise error, which tends to produce oversmoothed fields. It also targets transferability across ocean regions.

entry.title: Training Crossroads for Recurrent Vision Transformers: Recurrence, Neural ODEs, and Deep Supervision

author.name: Grzegorz Gruszczynski, Pawel Olszowiec, Michal Byra, Grzegorz Stefanski, Alberto Presta

entry.summary: A controlled empirical study of single-block recurrent vision transformers on CIFAR-100 asks when weight-shared recurrence beats independently parameterized depth at matched FLOPs versus matched parameter memory, whether training through an ODE solver acts as numerical refinement or architectural bias, and how deep supervision affects robustness. It deliberately fixes the architecture and varies training and inference regimes.

entry.title: Internalizing Academic Writing Workflows for Introduction Generation via Struct-Aware Policy Learning

author.name: Meicong Zhang, Tiancheng Su, Jiahao Cheng, Guoxiu He, Xinqi Tao, Dejia Song

entry.summary: Proposes internalizing a multi-stage academic writing workflow into a single-pass policy using explicit stage tokens, with credit assignment that separates per-stage quality from global coherence and a refinement-guided objective. Targets paper introduction generation without expensive agent pipelines.

entry.title: Probing Character-level Transformers for the Spanish L-shaped Morphome

author.name: Akhilesh Kakolu Ramarao, Kevin Tang, Wiebke Petersen, Dinah Baer-Henney

entry.summary: Probes character-level transformers to test whether they merely reproduce the Spanish L-shaped stem alternation or actually represent the abstract morphomic class that has no phonological or semantic definition. Under lemma-disjoint cross-validation with surface baselines, finds the class itself is decodable from internal representations.

entry.title: Traceable LLM-Generated Hazard Scenarios for Operational Safety Analysis of Aviation Systems Using ASRS Reports

author.name: Cristian Mascia, Roberto Pietrantuono, Daniel Rodriguez, Stefano Russo

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to generate candidate operational hazard scenarios for aviation from NASA incident reports, producing structured categorical hypotheses plus narrative event sequences, each scored for plausibility from historical co-occurrence and traced back to similar held-out reports. A hybrid validation approach checks the generated scenarios.

entry.title: AutoProteinEngine: A Large Language Model Driven Agent Framework for Multimodal AutoML in Protein Engineering

author.name: Yungeng Liu, Zan Chen, Yu Guang Wang, Yiqing Shen

entry.summary: AutoProteinEngine is an LLM-driven agent framework that lets biologists without deep-learning expertise run multimodal automated machine learning for protein engineering through natural language, handling both sequence and structure modalities. It is an older cross-listed submission rather than new work.

entry.title: Patients-like-me: A Variational LM--GNN Framework for Explainable Clinical Prediction

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Yixuan Li, Hanwei Wu, Qincheng Lu, Chi-Kuang Yeh, Xiao-Wen Chang, Ziyang Song

entry.summary: Combines a language model encoder over electronic health record text with a graph neural network capturing similarity between patients, trained jointly via a variational EM procedure. The design supports reference-patient attribution so clinicians can see which similar cases drove a prediction, evaluated on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.

entry.title: Strategic Evaluation of Planning Strategies for LLM Agents in Cyber-Physical Systems

author.name: J. de Curt\`o, I. de Zarz\`a

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-grounded benchmark where LLM planners issue typed directives in a simulated smart-grid demand-response setting with 40 autonomous prosumers and a simulated feeder. It compares predefined, sequential, hierarchical and search-based execution architectures to ask whether a planning architecture stays appropriate once other agents react and physical constraints bind.

entry.title: ExeCRE: Execution-Consistency Guided Reliability Estimation for Self-Correcting Code Generation

author.name: Yiru Dong, Richong Zhang, Fanshuang Kong, Si Chen

entry.summary: ExeCRE estimates whether generated code is reliable by measuring statistical consistency of execution behavior across candidates, instead of trusting test outcomes or LLM feedback, and uses that estimate to decide when self-correction feedback should be acted upon. The goal is to avoid misleading revisions in self-correcting code pipelines.

entry.title: Tropical Algebraic Geometry for Neuronal Representations: An Arakelov-Green Measure Based Descriptor for Graph Learning

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Weihan Xu, Xuehai Zhou, Shucheng Cao, Qihuang Zhang

entry.summary: Uses tropical algebraic geometry, specifically the tropical Abel-Jacobi transform and polarization distances, to build a training-free geometric descriptor for 3D neuronal morphologies that captures spatial cycles beyond the expressiveness limit of standard message-passing GNNs. A pipeline converts spatial trees into cyclic metric graphs suitable for tropical Jacobian embedding.

entry.title: CARVE: Cross-Slice Anisotropic Reallocation of Visual Evidence for Efficient 3D Medical Volume Understanding

author.name: Zhenyu Yi, Qiang Hu, Zhenhao Li, Jiaxuan Zhao, Yusong Sun, Lichi Zhang

entry.summary: Shows through scaling analyses that adding more slices to 3D medical volume MLLMs yields diminishing returns while cost keeps rising, and that in-plane resolution is a better use of budget. CARVE reallocates the visual token budget across slices using anisotropy-aware compression designed for volumetric rather than 2D or video data.

entry.title: Breaking the Curse ofMultilinguality inMany-to-Many Speech-to-Text Translation via a Resource-AwareMixture of Speech Encoders

author.name: Yexing Du, Kaiyuan Liu, Youcheng Pan, Bo Yang, Chengpeng Fu, Yu Wang, Ming Liu

entry.summary: Tackles the curse of multilinguality in many-to-many speech translation by routing each utterance to one of several expert speech encoders based on language resource level, keeping a frozen expert for high-resource languages and adapting others for low-resource ones. This preserves high-resource quality while lifting low-resource performance.

entry.title: Explicit Language Memory for Long-Horizon Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Houze Xu, Jizhong Li, Ziyi Ye

entry.summary: Proposes a hierarchical vision-language-action architecture with an explicit natural-language memory of progress so that long-horizon robot policies retain temporal consistency, correct errors in closed loop, and avoid degrading the VLM backbone's semantic representations during action fine-tuning. It targets the non-Markovian nature of extended manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Reward Structure Shapes the Interaction Between Episodic Exploration and Neural Memory in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jai Malegaonkar, Rohan Patil, Henrik I. Christensen

entry.summary: A controlled study crossing episodic exploration bonuses with several neural memory architectures in partially observable RL, showing that the same bonus produces qualitatively different effects depending on what the reward actually supervises. It argues that the common notion of sparse reward conflates temporal signal density with the content the reward teaches.

entry.title: Relational Response Fields: A General Theory of Black-Box LLM Response Consistency and Recovery

author.name: Song Zichen

entry.summary: Proposes relational response fields, a theory asking when a set of black-box LLM responses to systematically transformed versions of a query is recoverable at all, given transport constraints under paraphrase or decomposition and independently trusted anchors such as execution results. It identifies an intrinsic difficulty parameter governing recovery under a bounded number of corrupted responses.

entry.title: Stable Density Ridges: Consistency and Convergence of Subspace Constrained Mean Shift

author.name: Wanli Qiao

entry.summary: Shows that the widely assumed convergence of subspace constrained mean shift trajectories to the classical static density ridge is false in general because the static definition ignores rotation of the trailing eigenspace along the algorithm's flow. It introduces the stable ridge as a corrected target and proves consistency and convergence results.

entry.title: VetScore: Risk-Weighted Fact Verification for Veterinary Long-Form QA with Citations

author.name: Ivan Kart\'a\v{c}, Jan Tovarys, Mateusz Lango, Ond\v{r}ej Du\v{s}ek

entry.summary: Proposes an evaluation method for veterinary long-form question answering that decomposes outputs into claims, scores each claim for faithfulness to cited excerpts, and weights the result by the claim's potential for harm. Targets the gap where citations are present but generated claims still are not supported by them.

entry.title: Foreseeing the Invisible: Amodal Reconstruction of Leaf Fossil Images

author.name: Liuxiang Yue, Ailin Zhang, Ziyue Zhao, Yikun Duan

entry.summary: AmodalDINO reconstructs the complete shape of fossil leaves from partially preserved specimens, jointly predicting visible leaf, complete leaf, main vein, and fine vein masks from a single image without needing an upstream instance segmenter. It fine-tunes a DINOv3 ViT-L backbone with task-specific adaptations.

entry.title: A Multi-Sensor Dataset for Monitoring the Operational Environment of Rail Vehicles

author.name: Claudio Diotallevi, Rodrigo Gudi\~no, Zaharia Pachalieva, Philipp Neumaier, Patrick Naumann, Erik Bochinski, Volker Eiselein, Martin K\"oppel

entry.summary: Describes a large multi-sensor railway perception dataset with over seven million annotations, built by German rail infrastructure and annotation partners for automated train operation across automation grades. Intended to support training and validation of safety-critical obstacle and object detection.

entry.title: Dense Metric Depth Completion from Sparse Direct Time-of-Flight Sensors

author.name: Hakyeong Kim, Ruicheng Wang, Chengtang Yao, Jiaolong Yang, Min H. Kim

entry.summary: A generalizable framework for turning extremely sparse, noisy direct time-of-flight depth samples into dense metric depth maps, explicitly handling the sampling patterns and hardware artifacts of low-cost dToF modules. Aimed at XR, robotics, and 3D perception on commodity sensors.

entry.title: Trace, Verify, and Correct: A Training-Free Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Yang Yang, Jiawei Chen, Tairan Chen, Zhaoxia Yin

entry.summary: A training-free pipeline that builds a spatial evidence graph from the image and uses it to verify and correct intermediate steps of a multimodal model's spatial reasoning chain. Shows that unfaithful intermediate judgments materially reduce final answer accuracy.

entry.title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Robustness of Vision-Language Models Under Visual and Textual Perturbations

author.name: Ali Khoramfar, Mohammad Javad Dousti, Alireza Mohamadian, Heshaam Faili

entry.summary: Stress-tests four families of vision-language models on a histopathology-validated brain MRI diagnostic task using perturbations that preserve the clinical evidence, such as reversing slice order or swapping answer-option positions. Finds prediction flips in up to roughly half of cases and strong textual selection bias, showing accuracy alone hides reliability failures.

entry.title: Unleashing the Potential of Vision-Language Models for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Weihan Cai, Hao Tan, Zichang Tan, Jun Wan, Xinping Gao

entry.summary: Shows that a language-aligned perception encoder retains provenance-relevant semantics that make it a stronger frozen backbone for detecting AI-generated images than the widely used self-supervised baseline, provided probing exploits its semantic structure. Proposes a probing scheme beyond semantic-agnostic linear probes.

entry.title: Retrieve in Time, Correct in Frequency

author.name: Yuze Fan, Yue Cao, Pengjie Gao, Haojia Gao, Guangqiu Guo, Ziyue Zhang, Junbo Tan, Bokui Chen, Zhuo Zou, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: A training-free test-time correction method for frozen vision-language-action policies that retrieves progress-aligned successful experience in the time domain but transfers only selected frequency components of its actions. This avoids overwriting the policy's reactive structure while still correcting accumulated long-horizon drift.

entry.title: Mind-VLA: Instruction-Aware Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xingyu Ding, Yuzhong Zhao, Yang Wu, Chaoyang Zhao, Chunhai Zhao, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: Argues that existing 3D-aligned vision-language-action models align the whole scene uniformly and therefore ignore the geometry of the specific object named in the instruction. Proposes instruction-aware spatial alignment that first identifies the target object and then aligns its 3D representation, aiming at fine-grained and occluded manipulation.

entry.title: On Hamming-Lipschitz Type Stability of the Subdominant (Minmax) Ultrametric: Theory and Simple Proofs

author.name: Alokendu Mazumder, Arnab Roy, Punit Rathore

entry.summary: Develops a sparse-perturbation stability theory for the subdominant ultrametric induced by single-linkage clustering, showing that edits propagate only through the minimum spanning tree so a pairwise value can change only if its tree path crosses an edited edge or a newly exposed cut. This yields per-edit and global bounds better suited to sparse changes than classical worst-case metrics.

entry.title: EvtGraph: Event-Adaptive Compression for Sparse Temporal Graph Learning in Multimodal Time Series

author.name: Ziqian Wang, Tingxiong Xiao, Yuxiao Cheng, Jinli Suo

entry.summary: EvtGraph converts irregular multimodal time series into event-level tokens, selects a compact salient subset under an explicit node budget, and performs temporally constrained sparse graph reasoning. The aim is to allocate computation according to temporal information density instead of uniform discretization.

entry.title: Learning Compression Rules for Network Traffic

author.name: Quentin Lampin (Orange Research), \'Eloi Sainte-Beuve (Orange Research, Universit\'e Grenoble Alpes), Louis-Adrien Dufr\`ene (Orange Research), Guillaume Larue (Orange Research), Massih-Reza Amini (Universit\'e Grenoble Alpes)

entry.summary: This work learns compact rule-based compressors for structured network packet headers by first discovering structure with an entropy-ratio partitioning criterion and then selecting a rule subset via dynamic programming under a hard budget on installable rules. It is instantiated for a standardized header-compression scheme used in constrained IoT networks.

entry.title: Mapping the City Through the Lens of Language Models

author.name: Wanqi Liu, Rong Zhao, Zhizhou Sha, Qinyu Cui, Yecheng Zhang

entry.summary: Probes ten open-weight models for implicit assumptions about cities by having them rate anonymized morphological urban profiles across 40 indicators, avoiding place names to isolate priors from memorized facts. Finds a shared preference for larger, faster-growing, infrastructure-dense and less residential urban forms.

entry.title: VIBE: A VAD-Informed Benchmark for Entity-Centered Affective Profiling of Large Language Model Outputs

author.name: Andrei Chetvergov, Alexander Evseev, Timofei Sivoraksha, Stepan Ukolov, Mikhail Solovev, Danil Sazanakov, Sergey Bolovtsov

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark that profiles how models affectively frame socially salient targets such as political figures, countries and religions along valence, arousal and dominance dimensions. Emphasizes a measurement contract separating generation from external scoring plus a standardized reporting format.

entry.title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load

author.name: Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: Reports a 41-day live forecasting challenge on aggregated German grid load using an open-source pipeline engineered for determinism, reproducibility, and auditability in line with EU AI Act obligations for critical infrastructure. It reframes short-term load forecasting as a software-engineering and compliance problem rather than purely an accuracy problem.

entry.title: Lindblad-Inspired Multi-Timescale Reservoir Computing with Separable Rotation and Dissipation

author.name: Jyotiranjan Beuria, Amit Shukla

entry.summary: Introduces a reservoir computing architecture whose recurrent operator is assembled from exactly discretized damped rotational modes, separating reversible signal mixing from irreversible forgetting and giving a direct global stability guarantee. The design draws an analogy to open quantum system dynamics while remaining classical.

entry.title: AgentForge: An Immersive Role-Playing Platform for Learning Agentic Software Engineering

author.name: Zihan Fang, Yueke Zhang, Yu Huang

entry.summary: AgentForge is an immersive role-playing learning environment in which novices adopt one of four software engineering roles inside a multi-agent code-repair workflow, so they learn simultaneously how agentic AI operates, how to steer it, and how to critique its outputs. It targets the transparency and oversight-competence gap for beginners using agentic coding tools.

entry.title: ATLAS: Adaptive Topological Learning with Abstract Successors for Continual Learning

author.name: R. Blake Lawlor, Daniel S. Brown

entry.summary: ATLAS pairs a growing self-organizing topological map with successor features to give a reinforcement learner high sample efficiency while resisting catastrophic forgetting when the environment changes. It is evaluated on spatial navigation tasks against standard on-policy and off-policy baselines.

entry.title: Equitable System-Prompt Selection via Constrained Mixed-Strategy GroupDRO

author.name: Mengyu Xu, Qiaoxin Yang, Zhihan Liu, Ruiyao Xu, Zachary Liu, Kezhen Chen, Chongyang Gao

entry.summary: Formulates system-prompt choice as a constrained group distributionally robust optimization over a pool of existing prompts, assigning mixture weights to minimize worst-case answer-quality loss across paraphrase groups while keeping average loss near optimal. It targets the fact that semantically equivalent questions can receive very different answer quality.

entry.title: D$^2$F-ReAG: Dynamic Decomposition and Filtering for Multi-Hop Reasoning-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiaoyang Li, Junhao Ruan, Shengwei Tang, Kaiyan Chang, Zhengtao Yu, Tong Xiao, Jingbo Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes an adaptive multi-hop RAG pipeline that decides how deeply to decompose a question based on reliability judgments of the root query and filters retrieved evidence at each hop. It targets efficiency and accuracy losses in fixed graph-structured or static decomposition approaches.

entry.title: Q-CueGraph: Query-Conditioned Visual Evidence Graphs for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Pengcheng Pan, Xinfang Zhang

entry.summary: Q-CueGraph gives multimodal models an explicit, budgeted policy for deciding where to zoom in an image, building query-conditioned evidence graphs from OCR and layout for text-rich images or from visual candidate nodes for natural images, feeding a frozen reader. Optional refinement learns which crops help without region-box supervision.

entry.title: Eigenius: A Typed Knowledge-Graph DBMS with Epistemic Stratification and Institution-Mediated Reasoning

author.name: Hans-Martin Will, Allen L. Brown Jr., Matthew Fuchs

entry.summary: Eigenius is an open-source typed knowledge-graph database designed for AI-scientist workflows over the Model Context Protocol, using dependent types, epistemic stratification and institution-mediated reasoning so that provenance is a structural invariant rather than something reconstructed after the fact. It aims to answer what a system knows and on what warrant.

entry.title: AudioScape-TTA: A Structured Soundscape Benchmark for Fine-Grained Text-to-Audio Evaluation

author.name: Jinting Wang, Yuguang Yang, Shengyu Li, Yan Rong, Shan Yang, Xiaoda Yang, Li Liu

entry.summary: AudioScape-TTA is a benchmark for text-to-audio generation that annotates soundscapes with structured semantics and complexity measures such as event density, then scores generations with a rubric rather than a single global similarity metric. It aims to expose fine-grained instruction-following failures invisible to aggregate scores.

entry.title: The Order Is the Guarantee: Verifier-Budgeted Code Deletion with Static-First Learned Proposals

author.name: Ruitong Li, Binjie Guo, Aisheng Mo, Guowei Su, Han Wang, Jie Li, Ru Zhang

entry.summary: Frames removal of redundant code as a scheduling problem where a ranker orders single-statement deletion candidates, a test suite accepts the first that passes, and a finite verification budget bounds attempts. The central claim is that candidate ordering, not model confidence, is the control surface deployments should reason about.

entry.title: FUSEP: A Multi-Center Benchmark for Diverse Tasks in Early Pregnancy Fetal Ultrasound Screening

author.name: Bin Pu, Jiewen Yang, Liwen Wang, Ying Tan, Guannan He, Xingbo Dong, Qika Lin, Jiarong Guo, Lixian Yang, Zuozhu Liu, Shengli Li, Kenli Li

entry.summary: FUSEP is a multi-center benchmark dataset for early-pregnancy fetal ultrasound screening covering guideline-recommended views such as crown-rump length, supporting multiple downstream tasks for automated anomaly detection. It addresses the lack of early-gestation ultrasound data holding back assisted diagnosis.

entry.title: VQ-VAD: Vector-quantized Motion Representation Learning for Human-centric Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Narges Rashvand, Ghazal Alinezhad Noghre, Shanle Yao, Gabriel Maldonado, Hamed Tabkhi

entry.summary: VQ-VAD applies vector-quantized representation learning to pose-based video anomaly detection, learning discrete motion tokens instead of continuous latent trajectories to capture compact recurring behavior patterns. The pose-only input also reduces privacy exposure relative to raw surveillance video.

entry.title: CAMP: A Cycle-Aware Multi-Scale Patch Mixer for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jung Min Choi, Vijaya Krishna yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: CAMP is a time-series forecasting architecture that selects dominant periods per input window instead of per dataset, and treats patch positions non-uniformly so distant patches get broader contextual refinement while recent patches are preserved. Residual dynamics after cycle removal are modeled at multiple temporal resolutions.

entry.title: Active Learning Guided Design Space Refinement for Scalable Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery

author.name: Alexandros Ntagiantas, Panagiotis Tsilimidos, George Giannakopoulos, Christoforos Rekatsinas, Panagiotis Krokidas

entry.summary: The authors combine active learning with adaptive shrinking of the candidate search space to make multi-objective Bayesian optimization tractable over very large discrete materials design spaces. They demonstrate the approach on methane-nitrogen separation in covalent-organic frameworks and on pressure-vessel design.

entry.title: Continual-Learning Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Parameterized Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Xujia Chen, Xinyue Hu, Letian Chen, Yi Liu, Wenhui Fan

entry.summary: CL-PINN treats different parameter values of a parameterized PDE as a sequence of related tasks and trains a physics-informed network with continual learning to avoid uneven accuracy and overfitting to sampled parameters. The aim is better generalization to parameter values never seen during training.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Multidimensional Evaluation of Statistical Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Monnie McGee, Mateo Langston Smith, Julian Cabrera

entry.summary: Evaluates 15 models on 90 statistics exam questions using accuracy plus structural topic modeling and lexical similarity of the generated explanations. Finds accuracy ranges widely while explanation structure is highly convergent across models.

entry.title: HalluTruthQA-4K: A Fine-Grained Corpus and Annotation Process for Arabic Hallucination Detection and Truth Verification

author.name: Salah Eddine Bekhouche, Abdessalam Bouchekif, Hichem Telli, Mohammed-En-Nadhir Zighem, Abdenour Hadid

entry.summary: Expands an Arabic hallucination resource to 4,000 expert-curated question-answer instances across Islamic knowledge, history, science and geography, adding fine-grained annotation of the erroneous span, the reason for the error and the correct answer. Serves as the official dataset for a shared task track.

entry.title: Cooking beyond Frames: A Stereo Event Camera Dataset in the Kitchen

author.name: Chengming Feng, Hesam Araghi, Liming Zheng, Julien Dupeyroux, Xucong Zhang, Jan van Gemert, Nergis T\"omen

entry.summary: Introduces a large stereo event-camera benchmark of unscripted human cooking activity, filling a gap in neuromorphic vision datasets that have focused on driving and drones with scripted actions. Intended for developing and benchmarking event-based perception of everyday human behavior.

entry.title: Persistent Object Narratives for Token-Efficient Video Language Models

author.name: Junzhe Chen, Siyuan Meng, Xiaojie Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a slot-based visual interface for video language models that first groups features into object-like slots and then links recurring observations into persistent per-object narratives via a parameter-free memory. This reduces token counts while making cross-time object evidence explicit.

entry.title: Structured LLM Reasoning for Zero-Shot Human--Robot Coordination Under Hidden Goals

author.name: Dong Hae Mangalindan, Anand Gokhale, Francesco Bullo, Vaibhav Srivastava

entry.summary: Builds a structured language-model architecture for zero-shot human-robot coordination when goals are private, decomposing decisions into theory-of-mind inference, hierarchical planning, dialogue interpretation, action verification, and replanning. Human-participant experiments show fewer interaction steps and higher trust than an ablation without theory-of-mind and an offline multi-agent RL policy.

entry.title: PRIMAL3: Pathfinding via Reinforcement and Imitation Multi-Agent Learning - Leveraging LaCAM3

author.name: Chengyang He, Tanishq Duhan, Gadiel Sznaier Camps, Fangyuan Wang, Yuhong Cao, Jiankai Sun, Ge Sun, Mac Schwager, Guillaume Sartoretti

entry.summary: An ultra-large-scale multi-agent pathfinding framework combining reinforcement learning, topology-aware communication using cut vertices and dead-end features, search-guided training, and a priority-based action refinement step. Explicitly targets coordination failures at bottlenecks and persistent conflicts.

entry.title: Mimir: A Neuro-Symbolic Memory System with Dynamic Grounding for Embodied Agents in Interactive Environments

author.name: Haoming Xu, Zhenlin He, Hengyi Wang, Jiafeng Xu, Hao Dong

entry.summary: A neuro-symbolic memory for embodied agents that keeps world memory (object locations, states, evidence) separate from task memory (goal agenda, progress, hand state, failures) and grounds them together before each action. Provides an explicit interface for deciding which remembered facts support the currently active goal under partial observability.

entry.title: A Unified Model for Cross-Domain Clone Detection via Model Merging

author.name: Palash R. Roy, Banani Roy, Kevin A. Schneider, Chanchal K. Roy

entry.summary: Studies whether post-hoc model merging can unify specialized code-clone detectors that otherwise lose more than 70 F1 points outside their training domain. The authors compare task-vector parameter merging, greedy layer stitching, and cross-tokenizer alignment as alternatives to retraining a single detector on pooled data.

entry.title: CheMLFlow: An Open-Source Platform for Cheminformatics and Materials Informatics Applications

author.name: Brendan Smith, Susana Lopez-Moreno, Eric Dolores-Cuenca, Sangil Kim, Jose L. Mendoza-Cortes, Nijamudheen Abdulrahiman

entry.summary: CheMLFlow is an open-source workflow platform for cheminformatics and materials informatics that packages data curation, representation, model training, screening and reporting into modular reproducible pipelines, including agentic workflows. It targets the orchestration overhead that slows scientific ML research.

entry.title: RepairFormer: Automated Repair of Structured Inputs Using Transformers

author.name: Ovi Paul, Tom J King, Ali Shokri

entry.summary: RepairFormer frames repair of corrupted structured files such as JSON, DOT, OBJ and S-expressions as supervised sequence generation with a transformer, aiming to preserve original content instead of deleting it as search-based repair tools often do. The motivation is keeping testing, analysis and deployment pipelines from breaking on slightly malformed inputs.

entry.title: When More Becomes Less: Position-Dependent Repetition Effects in Language Models

author.name: Han-yu Wang

entry.summary: Shows that the effect of repeating a target token in cloze-style probes depends strongly on where the readout slot sits: repetition adjacent to the block behaves like priming and saturates, while a displaced readout produces an inverted-U where extra copies eventually reduce target probability. This means repetition-based probing results are confounded by probe position.

entry.title: A Multi-Cohort Validation of Censoring-Aware Conformal Lower Predictive Bounds for Pathology Survival Models

author.name: Mingi Hong

entry.summary: Validates a censoring-aware conformal wrapper that turns whole-slide pathology survival risk scores into calibrated lower predictive bounds on individual event times, across five TCGA cohorts internally and three CPTAC cohorts externally. It reports where coverage holds and where it degrades across configurations.

entry.title: The Cost of Binarizing Survival Outcomes in Clinical Prognostic Modeling

author.name: Shashank Yadav, David M. Routman, Andrew Y. K. Foong

entry.summary: Quantifies the harm of binarizing time-to-event outcomes in clinical prognostic modeling by replacing a binary scoring function with the Cox partial log-likelihood inside Bayesian network feature selection, using two published studies as case studies. It shows that binarization discards censored patients and changes which features look prognostic.

entry.title: Unifying quantum measurement constructions via a relative-entropy minimum change principle

author.name: Nana Liu, Mark M. Wilde

entry.summary: Develops a relative-entropy minimum change principle for quantum statistical inference, characterizing in closed form the measurement that is optimal when reversing a classical-to-quantum preparation channel. It unifies several known quantum measurement constructions under one variational principle.

entry.title: From Financial Sentiment Classification to Return Predictability: A QLoRA Benchmark of Large Language Models

author.name: Fusheng Luo

entry.summary: Benchmarks classical, encoder, and QLoRA-adapted 7-8B LLM financial sentiment classifiers on a unified three-class dataset, then separately tests whether classification accuracy translates into economically useful return predictability. It reports strong accuracy gains from QLoRA adaptation while questioning the link between linguistic performance and trading value.

entry.title: Kathleen Writes: Autoregressive Generation and Data Scaling Without Attention

author.name: George Fountzoulas

entry.summary: Continues an attention-free architecture series using a wavetable encoder and multi-scale reverberant state for byte-level autoregressive language modeling, reporting better bits-per-byte than parameter-matched transformers at every data scale from 2 to 512 MB with about 0.5M parameters. It also proposes a non-parametric metric intended to resist gaming when judging generated text quality.

entry.title: A geometry-based deep equilibrium model for image restoration under multiplicative Gamma noise

author.name: Shengkun Yang, Luca Ratti, Zhichang Guo

entry.summary: Presents a deep equilibrium framework for restoring images corrupted by multiplicative Gamma noise and blur, using an explicit interpretable regularizer built from surface area and mean curvature priors rather than an implicit learned one. A tailored mirror descent algorithm is proven to converge globally to a critical point using Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz theory.

entry.title: Predicting Brain Morphometry with MT-GNN: Mesh Evolution in Continuous Time with Graph-Based Metric Tensor Embeddings

author.name: Hao Ding, Daniel Semchin, Paul M. Thompson, Boris Gutman

entry.summary: MT-GNN predicts future brain subcortical shape by forecasting intrinsic geometry, having a graph network output per-vertex metric tensors for arbitrary visit histories and prediction horizons conditioned on a Fourier lead-time encoding. A differentiable as-rigid-as-possible solver decodes the predicted metric back into a surface for end-to-end training.

entry.title: TabletCraft: Bridging a 4,000-Year Cultural Gap with Bidirectional Akkadian NMT and Cuneiform Rendering

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: TabletCraft is an open-source system enabling bidirectional interaction with cuneiform, adding Akkadian generation and clay-tablet rendering to existing one-way Akkadian-to-English translation. It targets non-specialist users who could previously only consume, not compose, ancient Mesopotamian text.

entry.title: Efficient Multilingual Neural Machine Translation via Corpus-Driven Vocabulary Pruning: An English-Arabic Case Study

author.name: Ahmed Amine Aliane, Nasredine Semmar, Hassina Aliane

entry.summary: Proposes corpus-driven vocabulary pruning plus targeted fine-tuning to shrink the oversized embedding layers of large multilingual translation models, tested on English-Arabic with three standard MT backbones. Targets memory and compute reduction that pruning and quantization leave untouched.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Knowledge Graph Construction for Multi-Lecture Educational Reasoning

author.name: Sahil Al Farib, Momota Ahsana Meem, Sheikh Redwanul Islam, Md. Tanvir Raihan

entry.summary: An evidence-grounded pipeline that transcribes lecture videos, runs OCR on slides, and uses a vision-language model to extract only concepts and relations supported by transcript, OCR, or visual evidence into a provenance-rich knowledge graph. Evaluated on three neural-network lectures yielding a few hundred canonical concepts and relations.

entry.title: TriCLE: Tri-Modal Vision-Language Reasoning for Edge-Deployed Fine-Grained Clustering

author.name: Kishor Datta Gupta, Md. Mahfuzur Rahman, Fahad Rahman, Ahmed Rafi Hasan, Faysal Mehrab Chowdhury, Mohd Ariful Haque, Roy George

entry.summary: TriCLE synthesizes a thermal-style view and a pseudo-LiDAR depth projection from a single RGB aircraft image, then fuses all three with task instructions in a compact vision-language backbone for taxonomic aircraft grouping on edge hardware. It targets settings where real thermal and LiDAR data are unavailable.

entry.title: UBLLIE: Unified Backlight and Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Yasmin Yasin, Muhammad Usman, Ibrahim Radwan, Saeed Anwar

entry.summary: UBLLIE is an unsupervised framework handling both backlit and globally underexposed images in one model, using CLIP-guided positive and negative prompt learning for semantic supervision with a symmetric residual U-Net and atrous spatial pyramid pooling. It requires no paired ground-truth data.

entry.title: HiSC: Hierarchical Spatial Clustering Token Compression for Efficient 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Jiuhe Qu, Yingping Liang, Ying Fu

entry.summary: A training-free token compression method for 3D vision-language models that groups visual tokens into spatially grounded clusters using geometric and semantic cues, then compresses at the cluster level instead of selecting individual tokens. Aims to cut the heavy compute of multi-view 3D scene reasoning without losing spatial coverage.

entry.title: Simile Understanding in Text-to-Image Models: An Evaluation Framework

author.name: Luecheng Wang, Shintaro Ozaki, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Katsuhiko Hayashi, Jingun Kwon, Manabu Okumura, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: Builds a controlled dataset and automatic grounding metrics to test whether text-to-image models correctly interpret similes, finding that even frontier systems often render the comparison target as a literal object. Provides a scalable framework for measuring figurative language understanding in image generation.

entry.title: STEP-OPD: Rethinking Output Targets and Internal Dynamics in On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models

author.name: Qingyan Wei, Guangzhao Li, Xiaobing Tu, Yinggui Wang, Xiantao Zhang, Jinkui Ren, Xiaohong Liu, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Improves on-policy distillation for image generation by going beyond matching the teacher's output velocity, adding constraints on how the student's internal blockwise representations evolve so it is not capped by the teacher. Aimed at consolidating multiple specialized generators into one student.

entry.title: Reconstructing Persistent Worlds from Narratives for Narrative-Grounded Interactive Experiences

author.name: Yi-Chun Chen

entry.summary: Argues that narrative-grounded interactive experiences should be built by explicitly reconstructing and maintaining a persistent world implied by a narrative, rather than treating the world as an implicit byproduct of task-specific generation such as scene or gameplay synthesis. The paper positions world reconstruction as the central computational objective.

entry.title: Robust and Personalized Federated Learning for Aircraft-Engine Prognostics under Benign and Adversarial Client Heterogeneity

author.name: Chinmoy Mitra, Md. Mehedi Hasan Nipu, Mohammad Sakib Mahmood, Md. Rakibul Islam, M. F. Mridha

entry.summary: Studies federated learning for aircraft engine remaining-useful-life prediction under both benign heterogeneity, where operators see different conditions, and adversarial heterogeneity from poisoned updates. It compares four personalization remedies and evaluates five attacks against four aggregation rules on a standard turbofan degradation benchmark.

entry.title: An Inline Control Architecture for Language Models in Intelligent Transportation Systems

author.name: Narendra Kumar Dewangan, Mounira Msahli

entry.summary: Guarded-V2X proposes an inline guardrail architecture for language models embedded in vehicle-to-everything services at roadside units and edge nodes, combining rule-based ingress filtering, a lightweight safety classifier, policy-constrained structured generation, and trusted-only retrieval under real-time constraints. It targets prompt-level attack surfaces not covered by traditional authentication and message-integrity mechanisms.

entry.title: EA-Graph: Artifact-Anchored Verification Memory for Coding Agents under Upstream Drift

author.name: Hwai-Jung Hsu, Cheng-Jan Chi, Hanna Everett

entry.summary: EA-Graph stores a coding agent's verification claims anchored to the specific code artifacts and content that established them, at sub-path granularity, so that upstream changes invalidate stale claims instead of silently preserving them. When supporting content disappears the claim is marked unprovable rather than guessed.

entry.title: Efficient Online Lexicographic Generalized Low-Rank Matrix Bandits

author.name: Bo Xue, Ji Cheng, Haodong Jing, Hongzong Li, Shuang Qiu

entry.summary: A theoretical bandit paper on generalized low-rank matrix arms with multiple objectives ranked lexicographically, where the algorithm first recovers objective-specific low-rank subspaces and then learns in the reduced space. Regret guarantees are provided for the prioritized multi-objective setting.

entry.title: HyPASE: Hyperbolic Geometry for Parameter-Efficient Speech Emotion Fine-Tuning Framework for Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Tian Jin, Ruikang Zhang, Zefeng Zhao, Ding Luo, Jin Zeng

entry.summary: HyPASE adapts large audio-language models to speech emotion recognition using parameter-efficient adapters defined in hyperbolic space, treating the Poincare ball radius as a proxy for how abstract a representation is. The motivation is that emotion cues span prosodic to semantic granularity that flat Euclidean adapters model poorly.

entry.title: GeoReward: Mitigating Contextual Variable Overestimation in Vision-Language Models for Cross-Market Preference Prediction

author.name: Shuo Liu, Huixiang Cai, Weiru Zhang, Xiaoyi Zeng

entry.summary: Identifies a failure mode where vision-language models over-weight dominant visual and textual cues and ignore sparse but decisive context such as target geographic market, causing them to output the same preference regardless of region. GeoReward is a reward-based mitigation evaluated on cross-market advertising image preference prediction.

entry.title: DisMix: Order-Aware Mixup for Medical Imaging via Disentangling Ordinal and Non-Ordinal Features

author.name: Dileepa Pitawela, Gustavo Carneiro, Hsiang-Ting Chen

entry.summary: DisMix adapts mixup to ordinal classification such as disease severity grading by using a dual-codebook VQ-VAE to separate severity-related from appearance-related features, interpolating only the ordinal codes to create meaningful intermediate grades. Standard mixup instead blends both and corrupts the ordinal structure.

entry.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Priyanka Nihalchandani, Naman Srivastava, Varun Ojha, Pandarasamy Arjunan

entry.summary: Adapts pretrained time-series foundation models to private, highly non-IID building energy meter data using a federated scheme with a heterogeneous temporal mixture-of-experts adapter, where a sequence-level router selects experts specialized for periodicity, long-range structure or local variation. It balances cross-building transfer against per-building personalization.

entry.title: When Proxy Prediction Becomes Equation Reconstruction: Diagnostics and Residual Learning for Factor-Derived Proxy Supervision

author.name: Chayan Lahiri, Ahmed Shafee, Cody Fehringer

entry.summary: The paper warns that when proxy targets are computed from domain factors that are also model inputs, high accuracy can reflect reconstruction of the proxy formula rather than genuine robustness to degraded inputs. Using soil-loss prediction under controlled degradation of an erodibility factor, it offers diagnostics plus a formula-preserving residual learning method.

entry.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Dense Event Classification of Offshore Wind Infrastructure in Sentinel-1 Time Series

author.name: Thorsten Hoeser, Felix Bachofer, Claudia Kuenzer

entry.summary: A structured comparison of ten deep learning training variants for dense event classification of offshore wind infrastructure life-cycle stages from Sentinel-1 radar time series. The goal is to replace rule-based monitoring with learned models that can extract single event labels globally from large satellite archives.

entry.title: Consensus Measures for Unstructured Biomedical Text Annotations

author.name: Pascal Wullschleger, Christian Kreis, Martin A. Walter, Jennifer Foster, Marc Pouly

entry.summary: Studies how to measure inter-annotator agreement when biomedical annotators supply free-text rather than fixed labels, comparing embedding-based and LLM-based semantic equivalence measures. Finds embeddings scale but blur close concepts, while LLM judges are more accurate yet costly for chance-corrected estimation.

entry.title: Decoupling Generation and Selection for Budget-Constrained Faithful Summarization

author.name: Zeyu Wang, Guanghua Wang, Meng Xu

entry.summary: Separates summary generation from sentence selection, having a generator produce candidates that a combinatorial selector assembles under an explicit sentence budget while trading off relevance, factuality and redundancy. Supports several selection objectives without retraining and improves faithfulness metrics on multi-document benchmarks.

entry.title: SCOPE: Field-of-View-Aware Path Planning in Unknown 3D Environments via Safety-Volume Certification

author.name: Junbin Yuan, Muqing Cao, Yunwoo Lee, Brady Moon, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: Formulates safe navigation with a limited-field-of-view sensor as online certification that the entire robot-inflated motion volume has been observed free, building a graph whose vertices are provably certified positions. Decouples optimistic goal-directed guidance from certified execution by turning the first uncertified point into an explicit observation task.

entry.title: RORA: Realistic Object Reconstruction with Articulation

author.name: Hyesung Lee, Youngseon Lee, Kyutae Lee, Dongjun Lee, Yongseok Lee

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline that reconstructs simulation-ready articulated assets, including joint structure, from a single static video of an object, without requiring recordings of the object in motion. Targets the sim-to-real gap by making real-to-sim asset creation practical for multi-joint objects.

entry.title: FBID: Adaptive Personalized Federated Learning for Robust Out-of-Distribution Attack Detection in IoT Networks

author.name: An Khanh Bui, Cong Thanh Nguyen, Hoang-Anh Pham, Hoang Thai Dinh, Diep N. Nguyen

entry.summary: FBID adds server-side control to personalized federated learning for IoT intrusion detection, using a contextual multi-armed bandit to regulate how much each client personalizes and thereby limit over-personalization that hurts out-of-distribution attack detection. The aim is better generalization to unseen attacks under highly non-IID client data.

entry.title: Beyond Linear Dynamics: Neural Bilinear Dynamical Models for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Mengzhou Gao, Huangqian Yu, Pengfei Jiao

entry.summary: Proposes a bilinear latent dynamical model for time-series forecasting that lifts nonlinear dynamics with Koopman theory but replaces the usual linear latent evolution with a bilinear one, aiming to reduce error accumulation over long horizons. It targets the mismatch between linear Koopman approximations and genuinely nonlinear systems.

entry.title: Design Choices That Matter: A Functional ANOVA Analysis for Remote Sensing Multi-Label Classification

author.name: Maryam Gholami Shiri, Eva Tuba, Sa\v{s}o D\v{z}eroski, Tome Eftimov, Ana Nikolikj

entry.summary: Applies functional analysis of variance across 48 and 20 deep models on seven remote-sensing multi-label datasets to quantify how much architecture, fine-tuning strategy, learning strategy and initialization each contribute to performance variance. It replaces brittle leaderboard rankings with dataset-level sensitivity profiles.

entry.title: IMFACT: Counterfactual Explanations for Time Series via Intrinsic Mode Function Substitution

author.name: Udo Schlegel, Julian Rakuschek, Thomas Seidl, Andreas Holzinger, Tobias Schreck, Javier Del Ser

entry.summary: IMFACT generates counterfactual explanations for time-series classifiers by decomposing signals into intrinsic mode functions via empirical mode decomposition and progressively substituting selected modes with those of a nearest unlike neighbor until the prediction flips. This keeps counterfactuals physically plausible for oscillatory data like vibration.

entry.title: ArtAnno: Annotating Implicit Semantics in Artworks through LLM Agent-Driven Bidirectional Human-AI Augmentation

author.name: Xiaoyan Gu, Yifang Wang, Wenqing Zheng, Haozhong Liu, Yixia Zheng, Peiyi Jiang, Wenjie Ning, Wei Zhang, Wei Chen

entry.summary: ArtAnno is a closed-loop annotation system in which LLM agents and human art experts mutually improve, with the knowledge base and agent skills evolving through interaction rather than one-way AI suggestion plus manual correction. It was informed by a formative study with 20 annotators and targets culturally grounded implicit semantics in artworks.

entry.title: Geometry-Informed Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pre-trained Molecular GNNs for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction

author.name: Marco Vieto Vega, Long D. Nguyen, Binh P. Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper proposes geometry-informed parameter-efficient fine-tuning of pretrained molecular graph neural networks for blood-brain barrier permeability prediction, where datasets are small and class-imbalanced. The aim is to avoid overfitting from full fine-tuning while retaining sensitivity to 3D molecular structure.

entry.title: Attention, Anomalies! Handling Attention Layers in Unsupervised Federated Outlier Detection

author.name: Mihailo Ili\'c, Milo\v{s} Savi\'c, Vladimir Kurbalija, Mirjana Ivanovi\'c, Giancarlo Fortino, Du\v{s}an Jakoveti\'c

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how attention layers inside memory-augmented autoencoders should be aggregated in federated learning, since standard averaging schemes are not designed for attention and memory modules. It proposes specialized aggregation for unsupervised federated outlier detection.

entry.title: ANNOTARES: A Dataset for Extracting Logical Structures from German Statutory Texts

author.name: Ronja Schwarz, Jannik Str\"otgen

entry.summary: Introduces a span-annotated dataset for segmenting German statutory text into legal conditions and legal consequences, spanning three legal codes to test cross-statute generalization. Benchmarks rule-based, CRF, BiLSTM and transformer approaches on the new task.

entry.title: SurgNarrator: A Generative Retrieval Framework for Surgical Video Understanding

author.name: Yuqing Feng, Jiawei Ma, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Kun Yuan, Nicolas Padoy, Daniel S. Elson, Anh Nguyen, Stamatia Giannarou, Baoru Huang

entry.summary: Applies generative retrieval to surgical video understanding, aiming to keep the low latency needed intraoperatively while still handling complex scenes that contrastive models miss. Handles surgery-specific difficulties such as visually near-identical but semantically distinct events and specialized terminology.

entry.title: Splat-Based Metal Artifact Reduction in Cone-Beam CT via Compact Attenuation Modeling

author.name: Kiseok Choi, Jaemin Cho, Inchul Kim, Min H. Kim

entry.summary: Introduces a Gaussian-splat reconstruction framework with a physically grounded, compact model of energy-dependent attenuation to reduce metal artifacts in cone-beam CT. Aims to fix the smoothness bias and prohibitive cost of prior differentiable polychromatic rendering approaches.

entry.title: StaticSegFormer: An Efficient High-Performance Semantic Segmentation Based on Static Structured Pruning

author.name: Timo Bartels, Danish Nazir, Jan Piewek, Thorsten Bagdonat, Tim Fingscheidt

entry.summary: Shows that recent dynamic structured pruning methods for segmentation transformers deliver poor real GPU throughput despite good FLOP and accuracy numbers, and proposes a static structured pruning scheme for attention layers instead. Reports both lower FLOPs and materially higher frame rates on standard segmentation benchmarks.

entry.title: Promptable Animal Pose Tracking Across Species

author.name: Le Li, Daniela Ivanova, Nicolas Pugeault

entry.summary: Demonstrates that frozen vision foundation models can track user-specified animal keypoints across species from prompts, avoiding the poor generalization of fixed-skeleton supervised detectors and the accuracy cost of generic visual tracking. Motivated by scarce expert annotation in wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: HexMIL: Hierarchical Attention MIL for Ante-Hoc Explainable Detection of AI-Manipulated CT Volumes

author.name: Orazio Pontorno, Luca Guarnera, Zahid Akhtar, Sebastiano Battiato

entry.summary: A hierarchical multiple-instance-learning detector for AI-manipulated CT volumes that needs only volume-level binary labels yet produces full-resolution 3D attention maps as built-in explanations. Targets both weak generalization to unseen generators and the interpretability gap of existing medical deepfake detectors.

entry.title: SmartMage: Dynamic Modality Orchestration for 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Yue Zhang, Yingzhao Jian, Yunqiu Xu, Xiaoxiao Sun, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: A multimodal LLM for 3D scene understanding that decides per query which modalities (visual, geometric, others) to use rather than always consuming a fixed combination. The claim is that irrelevant modalities inject semantic noise and waste compute.

entry.title: TourSynbio-Search: A Large Language Model Driven Agent Framework for Unified Search Method for Protein Engineering

author.name: Yungeng Liu, Zan Chen, Yu Guang Wang, Yiqing Shen

entry.summary: TourSynbio-Search is an agent framework built on a protein-focused multimodal LLM with separate literature-search and protein-database-search modules for unified retrieval across rapidly expanding protein resources. It is a cross-listed submission originally from 2024.

entry.title: NuclearDiffusion: Text-to-Image Foundation Models for Learning Nuclear Energy Concepts

author.name: Mohammed I. Radaideh, Jeremy Moon, Andre Gala-Garza, Emma Son, Yug Shah, Majdi I. Radaideh

entry.summary: Fine-tunes three open-source diffusion models on a curated set of 1,000 captioned nuclear energy images covering reactors, fuel cycles, and radiation, to study whether text-to-image models can represent specialized engineering concepts correctly. General-purpose models frequently produce physically incorrect depictions in this domain.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Graph Transformer for Traffic Intelligence in Edge Computing

author.name: Laha Ale, Letian Lin, Na Cao, Zheng Ma, Peng Yu

entry.summary: Applies a spatiotemporal graph transformer that combines graph structure over neighboring service regions with attention over long temporal horizons to forecast cellular edge traffic for proactive resource management. It targets non-stationary long-horizon dynamics that recurrent models handle poorly.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy Hypergraph Neural Networks under Label Noise

author.name: Mengyao Zhou, Zhiheng Zhou, Xiao Han, Guiying Yan

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks label-noise robustness methods adapted from graphs to hypergraphs for node classification, then proposes a new hypergraph-specific robust learning framework. It finds that existing noisy-label strategies transfer poorly to higher-order relational structures.

entry.title: Generative Optimization for Incentivized Advertising with Global Level Constraints

author.name: Gege Chen, Ning Luo, Hao Jiang, Da Li, Wenzheng Shu, Teng Sha, Yanxiang Zeng, Wenxin Tai, Fan Zhou, Xialong Liu

entry.summary: GOAL casts continuous incentive allocation in advertising as conditional sequence generation, producing incentive magnitudes conditioned on user history and a global constraint pressure signal, with a hierarchical causal state encoder to handle fatigue and delayed feedback. It targets settings where constrained RL and uplift modeling struggle.

entry.title: The First EgoCross Challenge at EgoVis 2026: Cross-Domain Egocentric Video Question Answering

author.name: Yuqian Fu, Tianwen Qian, Yanjun Li, Yu Li, Kunyu Peng, Xu Zheng, Yongqin Xian, Alessio Tonioni, Yanwei Fu, Xiaoling Wang, Danda Paudel, Federico Tombari, Luc Van Gool, Leyi Wu, Yifan Zhao, Jinjie Zhang, Yinchuan Li, Yingcong Chen, Zixu Li, Zhiwei Chen, Zhiheng Fu, Wenbo Wang, Yupeng Hu, Weili Guan, Liqiang Nie, Takuya Murakawa, Toru Tamaki, Yi Wen, Zhenglin Du, Zhengyang Li, Lingling Li, Licheng Jiao, Wenping Ma

entry.summary: Technical report for a cross-domain egocentric video question answering challenge testing whether multimodal LLMs generalize from everyday first-person footage to surgery, industrial assembly, extreme sports and animal-perspective video. Two tracks constrain participants to an official baseline or allow open models.

entry.title: Learning to Resolve Neutron Resonances with Fully Convolutional Neural Networks

author.name: Nataly R. Panczyk, Athanasios Stamatopoulos, Josef Svoboda, Majdi I. Radaideh

entry.summary: A fully convolutional network is trained to classify points in noisy neutron transmission spectra as resonances, augmenting traditional R-Matrix fitting codes that currently need heavy manual effort and prior evaluations. The goal is faster, less biased post-experiment nuclear data processing.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Feature Selection Methods for EHR Diagnosis Codes in Opioid Use Disorder Prediction

author.name: Zihan Ding, Yinan Liu, Tengfei Ma, Rachel Wong, George Leibowitz, Benjamin Littenberg, Xia Zheng, Richard N. Rosenthal, Fusheng Wang

entry.summary: A controlled comparison of five feature selection paradigms for opioid use disorder prediction from EHR diagnosis codes, including gradient-sensitivity, LightGBM-SHAP, Elastic Net and LLM-guided semantic selection. All are evaluated in a unified preprocessing pipeline by downstream predictive performance and interpretability.

entry.title: FM4WiFi: Flow Matching for Multi-AP Coordination in Dense Deployments of Beyond Wi-Fi 8 Networks

author.name: Maksymilian Wojnar, Krzysztof Rusek, Katarzyna Kosek-Szott, Szymon Szott

entry.summary: Applies flow matching to network-wide multi-AP coordination for coordinated spatial reuse in dense Wi-Fi deployments beyond the pairwise coordination allowed by current Wi-Fi 8 specifications. The generative model produces joint transmission and power configurations fast enough to escape the scaling limits of existing optimizers.

entry.title: Neighborhood-Aware Dual Biomedical Entity Linking

author.name: Yicheng Tao, Jie Liu

entry.summary: PILOT is a three-stage biomedical entity linking pipeline combining ontology-aware retrieval, dual reranking, and score fusion to map ambiguous clinical mentions to large knowledge bases. It injects neighborhood structure from both query and knowledge base sides to handle corpus-specific annotation conventions.

entry.title: Link prediction on multi-relational graphs from an influence propagation perspective

author.name: Zidu Yin, Yuankai Qi, Dong Gong, Ehsan Abbasnejad, Kun Yue, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: Models link prediction in multi-relational graphs as influence propagation, extending an SIR epidemic model so that whether and what type of influence spreads between nodes indicates the existence and type of an edge. This fuses relevant local and global structural signals for relation prediction.

entry.title: Disentangling Language Modeling and Boundaries

author.name: Mykola Haltiuk

entry.summary: Argues that byte-level language models share an identical output space regardless of original tokenization, making knowledge transfer between them exact, and hypothesizes that next-byte prediction and patch boundary placement can be varied independently. The paper mainly frames the hypothesis and specifies the experiments that would test it rather than reporting results.

entry.title: Revisiting Pose Sensitivity in Splat-based Computed Tomography under Sparse-view Reconstruction

author.name: Kiseok Choi, Hyeongjun Cho, Inchul Kim, Min H. Kim

entry.summary: Analyzes why Gaussian-splatting-based CT reconstruction produces strong streak artifacts on real scanners, showing the cause is inaccurate acquisition pose rather than view sparsity itself. Revisits pose handling to make splat-based tomography deployable on real, non-uniform-view systems.

entry.title: Lesion Detection in CT with Frozen Self-Distilled Features: SALT, a Spatially Adaptive Label-Guided Temperature

author.name: Mahmut S. Gokmen, Evan W. Damron, Mitchell A. Klusty, Caroline N. Leach, Emily B. Collier, V. K. Cody Bumgardner

entry.summary: Argues that self-supervised pretraining objectives treat every image patch equally, so tiny lesions contribute no more signal than surrounding tissue, and instead conditions self-distillation targets on weak box-derived labels available only during pretraining. Sharpens teacher temperature and up-weights masked-patch loss inside lesion regions.

entry.title: Design and Flight of an Ion-propelled Micro Hovercraft Leveraging Ground Proximity Effects

author.name: C. Luke Nelson, Grant Nations, Mrinmoy Modak, Daniel S. Drew

entry.summary: Explores centimeter-scale hovercraft that exploit the boost in thrust density and efficiency that ion thrusters gain near a ground plane, characterizing skirt geometries empirically before building a palm-sized flying prototype. Aims at a route toward power-autonomous silent solid-state micro air vehicles.

entry.title: Optimal Constrained sc-LTL Planning in MDPs via Switching Policies

author.name: Zetong Xuan, Yu Wang

entry.summary: Solves planning in Markov decision processes where both the objective and safety constraints are given in co-safe linear temporal logic, reducing the non-Markovian constrained problem to constrained reachability on an extended model. Shows a class of switching policies built from stationary policies suffices for optimality, yielding a tractable linear program.

entry.title: iStructTab: Structured Feature Sequencing for Multimodal Learning of Image and Tabular Data

author.name: Al Zadid Sultan Bin Habib, Md Younus Ahamed, Prashnna Gyawali, Gianfranco Doretto, Donald A. Adjeroh

entry.summary: Proposes a graph-based algorithm to order tabular feature descriptors before feeding them, along with images, into an order-aware transformer with memory tokens trained to respect that ordering. The aim is to reduce redundancy and improve generalization in image-plus-tabular multimodal learning.

entry.title: CSGen: A Multi-Domain Curvilinear Structure Generation Model via Hierarchical Multimodal Diffusion

author.name: Zhe Shan, Ziming Yang, Lei Zhou, Wenwen Zhang, Cong Lin, Xia Xie

entry.summary: CSGen is a hierarchical multimodal diffusion model for generating images containing precisely controlled curvilinear structures such as vessels or cracks, trained on a new 24 thousand sample dataset spanning five domains and seven annotation types. A phased control-signal injection decouples topology from visual appearance.

entry.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

author.name: Enrico Mensa, Lorenzo Zane, Calogero Jerik Scozzaro, Matteo Delsanto, Tommaso Milani, Daniele Paolo Radicioni

entry.summary: ProverbIT is a 100-item Italian proverb benchmark testing 13 frontier LLMs and reasoning models on completion and two multiple-choice variants, including one where no correct option is present. Models complete proverbs well but behave inconsistently in the selection settings.

entry.title: Robust and Efficient Motion Reasoning for Privacy-Aware Classroom Incident Recognition

author.name: Paritosh Parmar, Landy Lan, Hong Yang, Chen Yi, Chiat Pin Tay

entry.summary: A pilot study on privacy-aware, low-compute recognition of classroom incidents from CCTV-style views, introducing a hybrid benchmark that mixes generated videos with real classroom pose data. The proposed method builds hierarchical kinematic features because incidents differ more in motion dynamics than in static pose.

entry.title: An Explainable LLM Agent Layer for Open-World Anomaly Detection in Oil Wells

author.name: Lucas Gouveia Omena Lopes, Thales Miranda de Almeida Vieira, Eduardo Toledo de Lima Junior, William Wagner Matos Lira

entry.summary: An LLM agent layer is placed downstream of an open-world anomaly detection pipeline for oil wells so that structured detector outputs are turned into explanations, operator recommendations and human-readable names for newly discovered novelty clusters. The agent uses a large Qwen mixture-of-experts model served through NVIDIA inference infrastructure on the public 3W dataset.

entry.title: MINT: Tensor Decomposition on Stacked Recurrence Matrices for Time Series Data Mining

author.name: Kaamil Kaka, Audrey Der, Evangelos E. Papalexakis, Zachary Zimmerman, Vikram Jayaram

entry.summary: MINT stacks self-similarity or recurrence matrices from many univariate time series into a tensor and mines it with tensor decomposition to find co-clustered temporal patterns. It is demonstrated on transit, electricity demand, wind turbine and vehicle telemetry data.

entry.title: SciRet: A Compute-Aware Empirical Study of Retrieval and Reranking for Scientific RAG

author.name: Kaysarul Anas Apurba, Md. Hasibul Hasan, Rofiqul Alam Shehab, Asab Azad

entry.summary: A compute-aware empirical study of a fixed scientific retrieval-augmented generation pipeline over a COVID literature corpus at three scales, comparing sparse, dense and hybrid retrieval with optional cross-encoder reranking. Finds hybrid retrieval most robust and that an out-of-domain reranker actually degrades precision on scientific text.

entry.title: The LLM Proposes, the Executive Disposes: A Self-Verifying Agent Instrument that Dissociates Commitment Drift from Binding Drift in Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Mohsen Arjmandi

entry.summary: Presents an agent architecture where a deterministic executive layer owns all state and the language model may only file typed proposals that are admitted after pre-registered predictions are checked against observations by code. The design makes verification structural rather than after-the-fact, and includes self-invalidation checks that caught defects in several of its own runs.

entry.title: Joint UAV Flight and Opportunistic Routing under Reinforcement Learning for Delay-Tolerant Networks

author.name: Xiao Wang, Shun-Ren Yang

entry.summary: Jointly optimizes UAV flight headings and decentralized opportunistic message routing in delay-tolerant networks using reinforcement learning with centralized training, aiming to create more contact opportunities under sparse connectivity and finite buffers. It targets delivery rate and congestion under limited message lifetime.

entry.title: MIDAS: Multi-LLM Iterative Data-Adaptive Summarization

author.name: Karen Lee, Dhanashree Balaram, Seojun Shon, Umair Rasheed

entry.summary: MIDAS uses multiple LLMs in an iterative loop to adapt summarization prompts per data segment rather than optimizing one static prompt, targeting enterprise settings like support tickets and incident reports with strict formatting and domain conventions. The goal is to reduce manual prompt maintenance as requirements evolve.

entry.title: MERaLiON-GR: Speech Gender Recognition Model for English and SEA Languages

author.name: Qiongqiong Wang, Ai Ti Aw, Nancy F. Chen, Ying Lay Chiu, Yang Ding, Yingxu He, Ridong Jiang, Zhuohan Liu, Yanfeng Lu, Yi Ma, Muhammad Huzaifah, Nabilah Binte Md Johan, Nattadaporn Lertcheva, Pham Minh Duc, Sailor Hardik Bhupendra, Siti Umairah Binte Mohammad Salleh, Shuo Sun, Tarun Kumar Vangani, Jeremy H. M. Wong, Jinyang Wu, Longyin Zhang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.04433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present MERaLiON-GR, a speech gender recognition system that performs binary classification (female / male) on English and Southeast Asian (SEA) l...

entry.title: Understanding Fault Tolerance of Adversarially Robust Pruned Models

author.name: Manali Dangarikar, Cory Merkel

entry.summary: An empirical study of how pruning, adversarial training and hardware weight faults such as stuck-at-zero errors interact in a small CNN on MNIST, testing whether adversarially robust models are also more fault tolerant. It targets reliability of compressed networks on neuromorphic accelerators.

entry.title: Adaptive Finite-Budget Training for CVaR Risk-Aware Q-Learning

author.name: Yifan Wu, Junjie Lei, Wenjie Huang

entry.summary: An adaptive training controller is proposed for CVaR risk-aware Q-learning that keeps the original estimator and Bellman fixed point but redesigns the training schedule with per-cell inner step sizing, decay synchronization and coverage-then-greedy sampling. It is evaluated on daily Bitcoin trading.

entry.title: MGSB: Manifold Gated Signature Branch Pressure-Domain Baseline Architecture for Two-Phase Pipeline Flows Under Distributional Shift

author.name: Issah Suleiman, Sormeh Serpoosh, Nadine Elkholy, Hicham Ferroudji, Mohammad Azizur Rahman, Matthew Hamilton

entry.summary: MGSB is a regime-aware leak detection architecture for two-phase pipeline flows that combines regime-conditioned feature fusion, a rough-path signature encoder and mean-teacher consistency training to survive distribution shift such as bubble-to-slug transitions. It is evaluated with leave-one-group-out splits to expose out-of-distribution failure that in-distribution testing hides.

entry.title: Canonical Joint Energy-Based Model on CIFAR-10: failure modes and practical indistinguishability of Predictor-Corrector and SGLD samplers

author.name: Dmytro Knopov

entry.summary: A replication study of Joint Energy-Based Models on CIFAR-10 that tests whether a Predictor-Corrector sampler beats the canonical SGLD sampler during training, cold-start generation, and OOD refinement. The finding is that the theoretically preferred sampler is practically indistinguishable without an annealed noise schedule, and it documents failure modes of canonical JEM training.

entry.title: BnBERT-iPET: Sparse Few-Shot Language Modeling for Bengali via Lottery Ticket Pruning

author.name: Sajib Hossain, Md Kamrus Samad, Anan Ghosh, Labib Imam Chowdhury, Nabeel Mohammed

entry.summary: Combines lottery-ticket pruning with iterative pattern-exploiting few-shot training for Bengali language modeling, seeking near-BERT quality at much lower memory and compute. The motivation is enabling NLP for lower-resourced languages on constrained hardware.

entry.title: Multi-Objective Ranking for Live-Streaming: Balancing Fresh and Delayed Signals with Segment-Aware Targeting

author.name: Xiaoyi Gu, Julia Tavares, Eder Santana, Carlos Mendoza-Cardenas, Nikita Mishra, Saad Ali

entry.summary: Describes a production ranking approach for entertainment live-streaming that combines delayed feedback windows, a multi-model fusion of fresh and delayed signals, and segment-aware targeting to handle sparse concurrent behaviors such as watching, chatting, following, and spending. It addresses biases that vary across user segments.

entry.title: BBOWP-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Black-Box Optimization Word Problems

author.name: Yutaro Yamada, Kei Hiroshima, Nozomu Yoshinari, Kento Uchida, Shinichi Shirakawa

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formulating an optimization problem strongly affects the quality of the final solution, yet good formulations usually require substantial expertise. Re...

entry.title: Learning a Vector-Symbolic Model for Socio-Cultural Tasks

author.name: Meera Ray, Swapnika Dulam, Christopher L. Dancy

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How can we better represent the impact of sociocultural structures on decision making in computational cognitive models? Modeling this impact requires ...

entry.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

author.name: Soumadeep Saha, Krish Sharma, Akshay Chaturvedi, Nicholas Asher

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the performance of large language models (LLMs) across a variety of reasoni...

entry.title: FLARE: Few-shot Learning-based Adaptive Reflective Engine

author.name: Dhanasekar Sundararaman, Bharat Gandhi, Aashna Garg, Minjie Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in complex, compound AI systems where performance hinges on the quality of prompts. Recent state...

entry.title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective

author.name: Dorieh Alomari, Irfan Ahmad, Maged S. Al-shaibani

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arabic script uses 28 letters, many of which share a common base shape (rasm) and are distinguished only by dot placement. Because early Arabic manuscr...

entry.title: ICO: Enhancing Semantic-Shift Jailbreaks via Iterative Context Optimization

author.name: Hujian Zhu, Yihao Huang, Felix Juefei-Xu, Xinfeng Li, Peng Zeng, Simeng Qin, Qing Guo, Geguang Pu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Foundation models have achieved remarkable success across diverse tasks, but they remain vulnerable. To investigate such vulnerabilities, semantic-shif...

entry.title: SFT Conflicts, RL Coexists: A Theoretical and Empirical Analysis of Multi-Task Learning for LLMs

author.name: Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Shangqing Tu, Hongbang Yuan, Yushi Bai, Kang Liu, Juanzi Li, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) exhibit fundamentally different behaviors in enhancing multi-task reasoning for large lang...

entry.title: Hypercubes, Hyperplanes, and Constraint-Induced Complexity Collapse in Atomic Concept Learning

author.name: Irene Tsapara

entry.summary: A theoretical paper analyzing higher-arity atomic concept learning through the geometry of hypercubes and hyperplanes over ground instances, showing that most hyperplanes collapse into finitely many equivalence classes while the full diagonal does not. The result links geometric structure to reduction-theoretic complexity of concept classes.

entry.title: COSMO: Consensus-Driven Shift Modulation for Source-Free Domain Adaptation

author.name: Bo Li, Junjie Peng, Xiaohua Xie, Jianhuang Lai

entry.summary: Addresses source-free domain adaptation by treating guidance from a pretrained vision-language model versus the source model as a per-sample reliability allocation problem, avoiding the erasure of valid source knowledge when the two disagree. Introduces a consensus-driven shift modulation mechanism for this arbitration.

entry.title: Visual Anchoring in Diffusion: Multimodal Zero-Shot Skeleton Action Recognition

author.name: Zehao Bao, Shujun Guo, Bruce X. B. Yu

entry.summary: Tackles zero-shot skeleton action recognition by scoring classes through how well a text-conditioned denoiser reconstructs noise added to skeleton features, sidestepping the need to tune fusion weights between skeleton and RGB branches. The classify-by-generation approach uses RGB context to disambiguate actions with similar joint dynamics.

entry.title: Differential 6-DOF Pose Estimation with Provable First-Order Immunity to Camera Calibration Errors

author.name: Yueqiang Zhang, Liang Deng, Yi Zhang, Baoqiong Wang, Wenjun Chen, Shuixin Pan, Yulan Guo, Qifeng Yu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.04673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) motion estimation is essential for robotic manipulation, autonomous systems, and structural displacement monitor...

entry.title: YOLOv14:Unified Cross-Domain Real-Time Object Detectionwith Adaptive Multi-View Representation

author.name: Jinling Jia, Jian Lu, Jone Yawl, Chenbin Zhang

entry.summary: Claims a new real-time detector generation combining deformable area attention, game-to-real domain adaptation, multi-view conditioning, and panoramic handling to work across fisheye, aerial, rendered, and 360-degree inputs. Positions itself as a unified cross-domain detector.

entry.title: Multi-View Face and Gesture Animation with Dynamic Gaussians

author.name: Alireza Javanmardi, Vippin Kumar Jeetmal, Christen Millerdurai, Alain Pagani, Didier Stricker

entry.summary: A multi-view pipeline using dynamic Gaussian representations to build upper-body avatars that keep both fine facial expression detail and accurate hand articulation, which prior head-only or full-body methods trade off. Targets natural communicative motion for telepresence-style applications.

entry.title: On the Effectiveness of Adaptation Strategies for VLM-Based Federated Learning in Remote Sensing

author.name: Simon L\"osche, Bar{\i}\c{s} B\"uy\"ukta\c{s}, Mathis Adler, Angelos Zavras, Ioannis Papoutsis, Beg\"um Demir

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.04791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training of deep learning models across decentralized image archives without requiring data centralizatio...

entry.title: RegisterBridgeMM: A Register-Centric Framework for RGB-Infrared Object Detection

author.name: Zian Wang, Hangchuan Liang, Yuehua Chen, Changchun Li, Chaoyi Guo, Mingzhe Liu, Fangming Gu

entry.summary: Studies how to adapt large vision-language models within federated learning for remote sensing, where clients hold heterogeneous non-IID image archives and cannot share data. Compares parameter-efficient adaptation strategies to mitigate the cost and heterogeneity problems of federated VLM training.

entry.title: Towards Valid B-Rep Generation: Training-Free Wireframe Anomaly Detection and Repair

author.name: Jingyu Wu, Youcheng Cai, Tengyu Luo, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: A training-free intervention that detects and repairs geometric and topological anomalies in intermediate wireframes of CAD generation pipelines, using a vision-language screening pass combined with geometric detectors. Improves the validity of final boundary-representation models without retraining large generators.

entry.title: Bag-of-Visual-Words for Spatial Mapping of Lung Adenocarcinoma Growth Patterns

author.name: Darya Ardan, Valentin Oreiller, Henning M\"uller
