author.name: Zirui Huang, Yunlong Mao, Wei Tong, Tingting Wu, Xin Ge, Sheng Zhong

entry.summary: Distribution Provenance Audit is a post-hoc, black-box method to test whether a deployed fine-tuned LLM was trained on proprietary data, relying on distributional fingerprints that survive paraphrasing and distillation because utility requires preserving them. Addresses data IP infringement without requiring pre-training watermarking.

entry.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling

author.name: Qinwen Wang, Jieping Luo, Aoxiang Qin, Ruoyu Zhao, Jianxiong Tang, Wei Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Luziwei Leng

entry.summary: Hierarchical Memory Mamba adds a lightweight working-memory module on top of a pretrained Mamba backbone that extracts slow paragraph-level semantics from hidden states and compresses them into persistent long-term memory for retrieval. Aims to relieve the fixed-capacity recurrent-state bottleneck of linear-attention models on long sequences.

entry.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures

author.name: Sunny Dubey

entry.summary: Tests how far mid-episode agent failures (looping, tool-error cascades, goal drift, fabrication, corrupted-content ingestion) can be detected from cheap step telemetry alone, using a one-class echo-state-network ensemble with CUSUM alarms trained only on healthy runs. On 2,823 episodes across three frameworks and four models it catches 71 percent of failures at a 5 percent false-alarm budget with AUROC 0.872.

entry.title: Role Steering of Language Models for Social Simulations

author.name: Isaac Song, Mohammed Rehan Parwani, Glenn Matlin, Emile Anand, Akhil Theerthala, Arjun Chatterjee, Maria Kostylew, Yonadav G. Shavit, Sebastien Krier, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: Introduces an activation-steering screening workflow for role-conditioned agents used in social simulations: extract a role direction, sweep steering strengths, judge role-profile alignment, and pass or flag configurations before deployment into a population. On OLMo-3-7B-Instruct with 275 roles, role-specific directions beat an assistant-axis persona-vector control on judged alignment.

entry.title: A Synthetically-accessible Universe of Chemically Recyclable Polymers

author.name: Anagha Savit, Wei Xiong, Harikrishna Sahu, Shivank S. Shukla, Will R. Gutekunst, Rampi Ramprasad

entry.summary: The authors release one million synthetically realizable ring-opening-polymerization polymer structures, generated by combining virtual forward synthesis from known reactions with polymer-specific language models (polyBART latent exploration and POLYT5 sequence generation) and filtered by chemical heuristics. The dataset targets discovery of chemically recyclable polymers.

entry.title: Cross-Task Dissociation in Frontier Vision-Language Model Theory of Mind

author.name: Kejia Zhang, Youran Sun, Chugang Yi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Nine frontier vision-language models are evaluated on two psychology-derived Theory-of-Mind paradigms, the Keysar Director Task and Frith-Happe animated triangles. Without chain-of-thought the panel makes the egocentric error on 78 percent of Director trials, closer to children than adults, while reasoning rescues some models, and the models under-attribute intention on the motion task, showing that ToM profiles fragment across paradigms rather than mapping to a single human reference group.

entry.title: Native Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Low-Resource Southeast Asian Languages

author.name: Sean Gip Lim, William Chandra Tjhi, Hai Leong Chieu

entry.summary: OSCD is a post-training method that keeps chain-of-thought reasoning in low-resource Southeast Asian languages by projecting high-resource reasoning trajectories into low-resource vocabulary subspaces during generative rollouts via an integrated translator loop. It addresses cross-lingual collapse, where models silently revert to English mid-reasoning, and the catastrophic forgetting that plain fine-tuning causes.

entry.title: MedUPS: Towards Diagnostic Assistance in Uncommon Medical Cases with Large Language Models

author.name: Ofir Ben Shoham, Oriel Perets, Nir Grinberg, Nadav Rappoport

entry.summary: Introduces MedUPSQA, a dataset of nearly 22,000 mid-stream clinical decision points derived from 5,535 real case reports, plus an alignment framework that supervises models on next-action decisions rather than only final diagnoses. It targets uncommon and off-guideline cases where sequential management matters most.

entry.title: Analytic Planning under Uncertainty with Moment Closure

author.name: Shishir Sharma, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Develops analytic distribution-aware planning for model-based RL by using a quadratic action-value parameterization plus moment closure, reducing the Bellman backup to a tractable expectation that keeps predictive covariance instead of resorting to sampling or point estimates. Aims to cut target variance in stochastic environments.

entry.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Tingyu Song, Mingxin Li, Yanzhao Zhang, Dingkun Long, Pengjun Xie, Zhijie Nie, Yilun Zhao, Shu Wu

entry.summary: UEmbed is a decoder-only multimodal embedding model that emits both learned sparse lexical and dense representations in a single causal forward pass, using appended special tokens paired with disjoint vocabulary partitions. It removes the reliance of learned sparse retrieval on bidirectional encoders and auxiliary cross-modal modules.

entry.title: Temporal Leakage in LLM Backtesting: Measurement, Validation, and Adjusted Scores

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Bradly C. Stadie

entry.summary: Argues that the standard contamination check for LLM forecasting backtests, comparing scores before and after the training cutoff, is uninformative, showing four flagship models fail it on questions resolved only after their cutoffs because recency legitimately mimics leakage. The paper proves no passive backtest can separate leakage from skill and supplies two external-information remedies, including a matched clean control that yields leakage-adjusted scores.

entry.title: Approximate Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yuannuo Feng, Zegang Peng, Yuxin Xie, Yubing Ye, Yizhe Chen, Wenshuai Yao, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang

entry.summary: Approximate Speculative Decoding replaces the strict first-mismatch stopping rule with a budgeted longest-prefix acceptance that admits some mismatches when a target-logit regret gate is satisfied. This recovers suffixes that greedy verification would discard, increasing throughput without any training.

entry.title: Enhancing VLM Reward Models Through Structure-Aware Fine-Tuning

author.name: Pyrros Koussios, Chenhao Li, Xin Chen, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: SAFT fine-tunes vision-language models used as RL reward models by regularizing their latent space with intrinsic structural priors through LoRA adapters, without any ground-truth reward supervision. It aims to denoise the text-observation similarity scores that make VLM rewards unreliable in practice.

entry.title: Trajectory inference via Acceleration Matching

author.name: Bartolo Dazzini, Giovanni Conforti, Alain Durmus, Aram-Alexandre Pooladian

entry.summary: Acceleration Matching lifts trajectory inference from unpaired temporal snapshots into phase space and regresses onto an explicit conditional acceleration field, yielding smooth interpolating trajectories. This avoids both smoothness-enforcing preprocessing and expensive simulation-based training objectives.

entry.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?

author.name: Soumadeep Saha, Krish Sharma, Akshay Chaturvedi, Nicholas Asher

entry.summary: Investigates the open debate over whether RLVR expands the reasoning frontier or only sharpens sampling, using controlled maze tasks and semantic-equivalence trees extracted from mathematical reasoning traces to separate stylistic variety from genuine inferential branching. Finds that observed policy entropy collapse is not merely syntactic, implying real narrowing of inferential exploration. Directly informs a central question in reasoning-model training.

entry.title: MinerU.Chem: A High-Precision System for Optical Chemical Structure and Reaction Recognition

author.name: Haote Yang, Jiang Wu, Jingchao Wang, Xingjian Wei, Lixin Ma, Linye Li, Chen Zhu, Xiaolong Wu, Yuheng Lu, Ziran Zhu, Junyuan Gao, Lingli Ge, Yuan Xu, Huijie Ao, QianQian Wu, Dechen Lin, Huaiyu Gu, Lu Chen, Shengxin Lu, ShaSha Wang, Yuanyuan Cao, Zhejia Yu, Ruijie Zhang, Zimai Tian, Jiaxing Sun, Yinfan Wang, Jiahe Song, Chuang Wang, Yubin Wang, Rui Nie, Hao Zheng, Bowen Jiang, Hongbin Lai, Yifan He, Chengjin Liu, Tingting Zhang, Liqun Wei, Lijun Wu, Bin Wang, Yuqiang Li, Guangyu Wang, Wei Li, Bowen Zhou, Dahua Lin, Conghui He

entry.summary: MinerU.Chem is a document parsing system that extracts molecular structures, reaction schemes, and experimental condition tables from organic chemistry papers and patents into machine-readable form, integrated into an existing open document platform. The goal is to unblock data production for chemistry knowledge bases and AI tasks like retrosynthesis and condition recommendation.

entry.title: CARE-X: Towards Clinically Useful Radiology VLMs with Auxiliary Supervision, Reward-Aligned Learning, and Tool-Augmented Measurement

author.name: Mercy Prasanna Ranjit, Anirban Porya, Sathvik Joel, Niharika Vadlamudi, Nikhilesh Chowdary Eathamukkala, Prasanth V V, Abhyuday Kumara Swamy, Pranay Narhari Umredkar, Pradeep Narayan, Vivek Rajagopal, Tanuja Ganu

entry.summary: CARE-X is a chest X-ray vision-language model from an industrial research team that unifies report generation with focal-loss classification heads, grounding heads for localization, and tool-augmented anatomical measurement. The motivation is that clinical utility requires tunable decision thresholds, spatial evidence, and quantitative measurements, not just fluent text.

entry.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent

author.name: Zhen Fang, Yu Zeng, Wenxuan Huang, Yiming Zhao, Shiting Huang, Tianfei Ren, Qi Lu, Qingnan Ren, Qisheng Su, Lionel Z. Wang, Qingyu Yin, Shuang Chen, Zehui Chen, Lin Chen, Zhenfei Yin, Yao Hu, Shaohui Lin, Wanli Ouyang, Shaosheng Cao, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: Video-DeepResearch extends deep-research style multimodal agents from static images to continuous video, diagnosing two failure modes: agents skipping visual tools in favor of text search, and relying on memorized knowledge rather than genuine tool use. It enforces exhaustive cross-frame grounding before web retrieval via stage-wise tool unlocking plus supervised then reinforcement training.

entry.title: Enfold: Folding World Model Imagination into Predictive Representations for Ultra-Efficient Embodied Control

author.name: Weili Zeng, Yitong Xing, Fulong Liu, Chengqun Yang, Antao Xiang, Feng Tian, Jingnan Gao, Jisong Cai, Xin Wang, Xiaomin Wu, Yao Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: Enfold argues the reusable asset of a video world model is not the rendered future but the internal computation that builds it, and distills that multi-level generative computation into a representation inferred from the present observation and instruction. This removes the expensive generative rollout from the control loop for embodied policies.

entry.title: Light-Loco-Parkour: Versatile Perceptive Whole-Body Locomotion via Multi-Skill Distillation

author.name: Hongming Chen, Zhuoran Li, Hongxi Wang, Jiangpeng Hu, Ziliang Li, Peize Liu, QingRui Zhao, Xuhao Liu, Liang Pan, Ximin Lyu, Yuntao Ma, Tingxiang Fan

entry.summary: Light-Loco-Parkour is a single end-to-end humanoid policy that decides when to walk, balance, climb, step down, or vault from onboard depth and a velocity command alone, without reference motions, skill labels, or hand-coded gating. It is trained via multi-skill distillation to use arms, torso, and knees for whole-body terrain traversal.

entry.title: Learning to Coordinate Symbolic Tools: LLM Agents for Verified Sum-of-Squares Certificates

author.name: Bohan Chen, Shivam N. Patel, Richard Hoffmann, Sam Looi, Tony Yue Yu

entry.summary: This work trains an LLM agent to coordinate symbolic tools for producing weighted sum-of-squares decompositions, a machine-checkable route to proving polynomial inequalities where candidate certificates are exactly verifiable but hard to find. The authors build 1.35 million synthetic examples covering eight supporting algebraic subtasks rather than training only on the composite task, then apply verifier-grounded optimization. It is a case study in decomposing tool-use training with an exact reward signal.

entry.title: Escaping Confidence Trap: Evolutionary Decoding for Mathematical Reasoning in Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Zhenhong Sun, Hanqing Zhao, Yatao Bian, Rongcheng Tu, Liuyue Xie, Xu Zhang, Jue Wang, Davide Modolo, Daoyi Dong, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: Analyzing decoding trajectories of the diffusion language model LLaDA 2.0, the authors identify a confidence trap where local token confidence during progressive block unmasking becomes misaligned with global reasoning correctness, producing sampling-sensitive and structurally stuck failures on math. They propose an evolutionary decoding strategy to escape these traps and preserve coherent numerical-symbolic trajectories. The work targets a specific weakness of diffusion LLMs relative to autoregressive models.

entry.title: Beyond Routing Saturation: A Long-Horizon Class-Incremental Perspective on Expert Routing in Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Huiyu Yi, Yongqi Xu, Bogang Zhang, Dunwei Tu, Xu Zhiming, Zhen-Hao Xie, Baile Xu, Furao Shen

entry.summary: Shows that expert routing in multimodal continual instruction tuning appears solved only because existing benchmarks leak task identity through textual fingerprints and use short task sequences. Introduces FLEX, a 34-task long-horizon benchmark with weakened fingerprints that exposes routing failure.

entry.title: MineGrad: Gradient Inversion Attacks on LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Hasin Us Sami, Swapneel Sen, Basak Guler

entry.summary: MineGrad analytically reconstructs private training data from the gradients shared during federated LoRA fine-tuning, showing an adversarial server can breach privacy despite the frozen base model. Challenges assumptions that parameter-efficient updates leak less.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Use Tokens: Durable Authorization State for Replay-Resistant LLM Agent Actions

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: Defines semantic replay, where agent retries, replanning, and delegation cause one user authorization to be executed multiple times under freshly minted single-use tokens. CapLease keeps durable monotonic state over the authorized action, confirmation event, and remaining execution budget.

entry.title: REFLEX: Rethinking MoE Inference as Refinement-Aware Compute Allocation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Yiming Zhang, Jiazheng Liu, Hongyu Zhang, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Reframes mixture-of-experts inference in diffusion language models as refinement-aware compute allocation, since each denoising pass revisits all positions despite very different per-token refinement needs. REFLEX replaces uniform token-choice routing with demand-sensitive expert budgets.

entry.title: Exploring and Bridging Knowledge Holes in Unlearned Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Junxiang You, Junkai Chen, Yuhao He, Ruiqi Liu, Zhetao Guo, Shu Wu

entry.summary: Shows that multimodal unlearning evaluations miss knowledge holes, meaning severe degradation on benign inputs that share generic patterns with the forget set, because standard utility benchmarks are representationally far from it. Builds a probing benchmark and proposes mitigation.

entry.title: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration with Asymmetric Reinforcement Learning and Self-Distillation

author.name: Jim Dilkes, Vahid Yazdanpanah, Sebastian Stein

entry.summary: Instruction-Conditioned Exploration augments training prompts with varied instructions to broaden the behaviours an LLM attempts during RL post-training, paired with an asymmetric RL plus self-distillation objective that transfers the instruction-induced behaviour back into the base policy. Targets the exploration problem specific to LLM action spaces.

entry.title: Cooperative Coevolution for Resource-Constrained Agentic LLM Post-Training

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang, Shengcai Liu, Jiahao Wu, Ning Lu, Hui Ouyang, Shaofeng Zhang, Haoze Lv, Ke Tang

entry.summary: CoPES makes evolution-strategy post-training of tool-using LLM agents feasible on a few GPUs by decomposing the full parameter space into lower-dimensional subspaces searched cooperatively. Targets the memory advantage of backprop-free ES while cutting its prohibitive GPU-hour cost.

entry.title: Cost-Effective Automated Judging of Natural-Language Mathematical Proofs

author.name: Benjamin Grayzel

entry.summary: Tests whether cheap open-weight models can grade natural-language mathematical proofs given a reference proof and rubric, finding that GPT-OSS 120B, DeepSeek-V4 Flash, and Gemma-4 31B match human pass/fail agreement rates statistically indistinguishable from frontier judges Claude Opus 4.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro at up to 100x lower cost. A three-model majority vote matched but did not beat the best single cheap judge.

entry.title: Exploring More to Solve More: Boosting Diversity in Text Diffusion Models via Entropy-Based Guidance

author.name: Jingwei Zhang, Haoyu Lei, Zijin Feng, Jiacheng Sun, Farzan Farnia

entry.summary: SAKE is a training-free guidance method for discrete text diffusion that computes order-2 Renyi entropy over a semantic kernel Gram matrix capturing cross-token interactions and relative positions, then linearizes it for sampling. Improves the diversity-fidelity balance and reportedly boosts problem-solving via broader exploration.

entry.title: When Prompts Control Robots: Prompt Injection Attacks in Multi-Agent Robotic Systems

author.name: Neha Nagaraja, Amisha Bagari, Hayretdin Bahsi

entry.summary: This work evaluates prompt injection against an LLM-driven multi-agent robotic system, comparing direct injections into task instructions with indirect injections arriving through perception modules, across single-agent and multi-agent settings and varying attack-goal complexity. It finds that injections can induce adversarial physical actions and that multi-agent structure widens the attack surface via cross-agent contamination.

entry.title: Can Humans Dream of Electric Sheep? Human-Written Samples for Fine-Grained Vision-and-Language Hallucination Benchmarking

author.name: Timothee Mickus, Claudio Savelli, Eduardo Cal\`o, Emilio Raimond, Stella Frank, Hengyu Luo, Flavio Giobergia, Vincent Segonne, Chuyuan Li, Aman Sinha, Lorenzo Vaiani, J\"org Tiedemann, Ra\'ul V\'azquez

entry.summary: Builds a multilingual hallucination benchmark with 1,600 human-written hallucination samples across four languages alongside 18,400 model-generated ones, all with span-level annotations. It finds human-written samples give higher annotator agreement and remain distributionally comparable, offering a model-independent way to keep hallucination benchmarks durable.

entry.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms

author.name: Ziyi Cai, Shuangping Li, Yiheng Shen, Kangning Wang, Peng Zhang

entry.summary: Provides simplified deterministic, randomized and multi-order algorithms for dense language generation in the limit, building on the density-based coverage measures introduced by Kleinberg and Wei. It advances the theory of generating valid, novel strings from adversarial positive-only enumerations.

entry.title: Same violence, different answer: how AI responds to coercive control against women across languages

author.name: Lyu Chang, S\`onia Estrad\'e Albiol, N\'uria Verg\'es Bosch

entry.summary: Presents a fixed coercive-control scenario, in which a surveilled woman asks for help writing a self-blaming letter, to seven widely used language models across nine languages, scoring whether each names the abuse, counters self-blame and affirms agency. Failures split along two independent axes, with systems from non-anglophone developers performing notably worse.

entry.title: HindSearch: Trajectory-Level Hindsight Critique for Search-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haowei Liu, Jiamian Wang, Hsin-Tai Wu, Zhiqiang Tao, Yi Fang

entry.summary: HindSearch improves search-augmented RL by having a frozen judge write hindsight critiques of failed rollouts using the gold answer, which then supplies an auxiliary on-policy distillation signal for GRPO. With Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct it reaches 39.4 percent average exact match on seven benchmarks, and ablating gold-answer access removes most of the gain.

entry.title: How Much Does a Reasoning Summary Reveal? An Observability Ladder for Large Language Models

author.name: Andres Algaba, Francesca Carlon, Lynn Delcon, Marthe Ballon, Bert Verbruggen, Vincent Ginis

entry.summary: The paper defines an observability ladder over what a reader can inspect to judge answer correctness, ranging from the final response to a model-written reasoning summary to the full trace to internal signals, each with and without the prompt. Using linear correctness probes over three benchmarks and five open-weight models, it finds summaries carry most of the trace ranking signal when the prompt is hidden but add little once the prompt is visible.

entry.title: Action-grounded tissue affordance enables anticipatory auto-framing that lowers surgeon cognitive workload during laparoscopic surgery

author.name: Jiayu Gu, Yiwei Wang, Jie Zhang, Guojun Cao, Keshen Lyu, Song Zhou, Yimeng Chen, Haorui Wang, Qingmin Feng, Shenchao Shi, Huan Zhao, Wenbin Chen, Caihua Xiong, Chidan Wan, Jing Samantha Pan, Xiong Cai, Han Ding

entry.summary: Presents DiffeoAfford, which derives surgical visual-attention labels retrospectively from completed laparoscopic procedures by combining diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking with instrument trajectories, avoiding manual per-frame annotation. A real-time model trained on these labels powers an anticipatory auto-framing assistant reported to reduce surgeon cognitive workload.

entry.title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Deepika Bablani, Ajay Gupta, Wanming Chen

entry.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation from verifiable domains to open-ended generation by using rubrics as soft privileged information given to the teacher context, rather than as scalar reinforcement-learning rewards. Counterintuitively finds that rubric-based soft privileged information yields a larger and more effective training signal on student rollouts than hard reference completions.

entry.title: Inverted Detection and Control in Steering Vectors

author.name: Max Torop, Aria Masoomi, Jennifer Dy

entry.summary: Identifies inverted steering vectors: directions that are highly discriminative for a concept yet consistently push model behavior toward the opposite of what their sign implies, breaking the standard assumption behind activation steering. The paper gives a geometric characterization of when this inversion occurs.

entry.title: JudgeArena: A Unified Framework for Reproducible LLM-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Erlis Lushtaku, Bora Kargi, Ali Elganzory, Fabio Ferreira, Alejandro R. Salamanca, Julia Kreutzer, David Salinas

entry.summary: JudgeArena unifies major LLM-as-judge benchmarks including AlpacaEval, Arena-Hard, MT-Bench, and m-Arena-Hard under one interface with swappable judges, configurable prompts and backends, and full metadata logging. This enables systematic study of how judge model, prompt, and inference backend change conclusions about model quality. Addresses a serious reproducibility problem in the dominant evaluation paradigm.

entry.title: GORDON: Graph-based Object-centric Rewards for Decomposition of Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Andrea Protopapa, Davide Buoso, Francesca Pistilli, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Giuseppe Averta

entry.summary: GORDON learns dense reward functions for long-horizon manipulation from action-free videos by representing scenes as graphs of detected objects and spatial relations and training a GNN self-supervised to embed task progress. The object-centric abstraction is intended to be more robust than pixel-based reward models to background and appearance variation.

entry.title: Reputation-driven Cooperation in Lattice-based Decentralized Federated Learning through Evolutionary Game Theory

author.name: Phuc Hoang Truong Huynh, Dung Tran Vinh, Khoa Duc Anh Lam, An Nghiem Nguyen Truong, Uyen Nha Tran Bui, Khang Nguyen Dinh, Bao Nguyen Le Gia, Minh Le Nguyen Nhat, Manh Hong Duong, The Anh Han, Thi Ai Thao Nguyen, and Le Hong Trang

entry.summary: PATH-Bench evaluates lifelong LLM agents by controlling the order of accumulated experience, measuring forward transfer, backward transfer, and forgetting rather than only average accuracy. Eight agents are tested on code generation and multi-turn tool use.

entry.title: Sweet Little Lies: Strategic Deception in AI Emotional Support Chatbots

author.name: Aseem Pahuja, Zhiling Guo, Tahir Abbas Syed

entry.summary: Uses Bayesian persuasion to model emotional-support chatbots that signal users' emotional states, showing engagement-maximizing platforms have incentives to overstate emotional need when users are actually fine. Deception raises engagement without lowering user expected payoff in equilibrium.

entry.title: Latent Thought Credit: Multi-Answer Credit Assignment for Latent Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Yong Chen, Wenjia Zeng, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Latent Thought Credit assigns hierarchical credit in latent reasoning by sampling multiple continuous thoughts per prompt and averaging rewards over several answers sampled from each fixed thought context. Separates thought quality from answer-sampling noise under answer-only rewards.

entry.title: Allocation Before Ranking: Decoupled Token Compression for OmniLLMs

author.name: Zhenghui Guo, Yilin Yang, Yuanbin Man, Miao Yin, Weidong Shi, Rabimba Karanjai, Omprakash Gnawali, Chengming Zhang

entry.summary: Argues multimodal token compression conflates two decisions, how much budget each modality gets and which tokens survive within it, and that shared top-K selection is biased toward audio. Macer is a training-free compressor that allocates per-modality budgets first, then ranks within modality at modality-specific shallow layers.

entry.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation

author.name: Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang

entry.summary: Diagnoses a privilege illusion in on-policy self-distillation, where students learn behaviors that depend on teacher-only reference information and then act as if it were still available at inference. DAPD adds dual-path and self-conditioned anchoring to close the teacher-student information asymmetry.

entry.title: CoEvoKG: Co-Evolving Knowledge Graphs with Self-Evolving Search Agents

author.name: Zhaoyang Li, Zenghuang Fu, Qiuyuan Ai, Ping Jiang, Haoyu Wu, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, Jie Song, Guannan He

entry.summary: CoEvoKG uses a knowledge graph both to generate verifiable multi-hop training tasks and to store verified evidence retrieved during successful searches, so self-play knowledge is retained rather than discarded. Jointly trains a task generator and a search agent with graph-grounded rewards.

entry.title: Fetch-then-Explore: Decoupling Selection from Extraction over a Persistent Workspace for Search Agents

author.name: Qi Liu, Yiqun Chen, Zidan Chen, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Jiaxin Mao, Fengbin Zhu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Fetch-then-Explore decouples page selection from page reading for search agents by keeping fetched documents in a persistent workspace that can be re-queried many turns later, rather than binding a single reading to fetch time or holding one page at a time. Aims to avoid repeated fetching and premature extraction in long research trajectories.

entry.title: Beyond Solution-Centric Search: Adaptive Inquiry and Knowledge Revision for Autonomous ML Engineering

author.name: Shaokang Fu, Yulong Tao, Linbo Jin, Jiarong Zhao, Qiming Shi, Tianjun Pan, Haonan Li, Chengyu Wang, Jia Wu, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: Argues that autonomous ML engineering agents should be organized around an evolving information state rather than a tree or graph search over candidate solutions, and instantiates this as Iris, an inquiry-revision loop using epistemic actions to gather information before revising solutions. Positions the information paradigm against solution-centric search.

entry.title: Width, Memory, and Delay: A Resource Accounting for the Limits of Flat Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Oleksandr Kuznetsov, Emanuele Frontoni

entry.summary: Rebuts a recent claim that flat homogeneous multi-agent systems face an irreducible population-independent error floor removable only by hierarchy, using a controlled disturbance-rejection testbed with a computable optimum. Replaces the claim with a quantitative resource model trading off population width, per-agent internal-model memory, and delay.

entry.title: Decoy Images Amplify Caption-Mediated Defenses Against Encoded Jailbreaks

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Xiangchen Guan, Shibo Zheng, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: Reports that attaching an unrelated decoy image to an encoded jailbreak prompt sharply reduces attack success on vision-language models, by up to 73 percentage points, because it activates caption-mediated defense pipelines that otherwise stay dormant on text-only input. The effect is measured across five frontier VLMs, two attack families and three black-box defenses.

entry.title: Sheaf-theoretic Signal Processing on Graphs: Spectral Theory, Filtering, and Sampling

author.name: Gabriele D'Acunto, Leonardo Di Nino, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Sergio Barbarossa

entry.summary: Develops the first unified signal processing framework on network sheaves, extending spectral analysis, filtering and sampling to settings where each node carries a local vector space of differing dimension and modality. It generalizes graph and topological signal processing to heterogeneous data.

entry.title: Question Begets Question: Self-Evolving Curriculum for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning on Competition Mathematics

author.name: Longtian Bao, Jianyou Wang, Yang Zhang, Youze Zheng, Ramamohan Paturi

entry.summary: Question-begets-Question generates diverse problem variants from existing competition math problems to overcome data scarcity, then trains purely with reinforcement learning on outcome rewards without oracle reasoning traces. Applied to Qwen2.5-Math-7B on AIME, starting from 5.6 percent pass@1, it studies whether the apparent capability ceiling can be broken.

entry.title: Latent Reward Registers for Diffusion Preference Alignment

author.name: Yuanshen Guan, Zipeng Feng, Zhiwei Xiong, Peiqin Sun

entry.summary: Latent Reward Registers prepend learnable register tokens to a frozen diffusion transformer to read out expected terminal human preference from intermediate noisy latents, without perturbing the generator's hidden states. The resulting dense differentiable reward addresses temporal credit assignment across the denoising trajectory for both training and inference-time guidance.

entry.title: MoEGen: Mixture-of-Experts for Instance-Adaptive LoRA Generation

author.name: Yiming Zeng, Lei Lu, Zexin Li, Zhuochun Li, Shuoqiu Li, Shuyi Liao, Xidong Wu, Zeyu Zhang, Minmei Wang, Yu Zhao, Tingting Yu, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: MoEGen replaces the usual practice of storing many full LoRA adapters in mixture-of-experts parameter-efficient fine-tuning with small learnable expert codes that condition a generator producing instance-specific low-rank updates. This keeps adapter storage roughly constant as expert count grows and allows adaptation outside a fixed expert pool.

entry.title: Mask-Based Priors Are More Persistent than Query-Key Initializations

author.name: Mingze Ma, Hemanth Saratchandran, Cameron Gordon, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Using controlled Boolean extrapolation tasks where Transformers systematically default to a minimum-degree interpolator instead of the true function, this paper asks whether injecting structural priors into attention can correct the inductive bias. It finds that priors imposed through attention masks persist through training far better than priors implanted via structured query-key initializations, which wash out. The tasks are stress tests for understanding, not applications.

entry.title: When Does LLM Orchestration Pay Off? A Controlled Evaluation of Accuracy, Cost, and Task Difficulty

author.name: Nicolas Leins, Nico Pelleriti, Jana Gonnermann-M\"uller, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: This controlled study compares Self-Refine, Best-of-N, and Debate against task-only and chain-of-thought single-call baselines across five backbones and three domains (competitive programming, chess puzzles, mathematics), equalizing optimization effort by tuning every method with GEPA under an identical budget and evaluating on difficulty-stratified items. Orchestration yields moderate but benchmark-dependent gains that must be weighed against cost. The equal-optimization design isolates the value of orchestration itself.

entry.title: Tracing the Cascade: A Topology-Aware Evaluation Framework for Scientific Agent Hallucinations

author.name: Xinshun Feng, Ziqi Miao, Lijun Li, Jing Shao

entry.summary: SCHEMA evaluates hallucinations in scientific agents with awareness of knowledge topology, automatically constructing scientific concept graphs so that errors on foundational concepts can be traced as they propagate through multi-step reasoning and corrupt downstream conclusions. This contrasts with benchmarks that treat facts in isolation under uniform accuracy metrics. The framework is evidence-grounded and cascade-aware.

entry.title: Securing Agentic AI: From Per-Action Checks to Trajectory Assurance

author.name: Alireza Lotfi, Subangkar Karmaker Shanto, Imtiaz Karim, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: A survey and position paper arguing agentic AI security must move from per-action permission checks to assurance over entire behavioral trajectories, spanning prompts, memory, retrieval, tools, and cross-organizational delegation. Maps the threat landscape across the agentic stack.

entry.title: Is More Privileged Information Better? From Solution Traces to Problem-Solving Structure in Self-Distilled Reasoning

author.name: Xuyang Zhao, Liting Zhang, Zichen Xu, Zhihu Wang, Xu Caiyue, Shiwan Zhao, Qicheng Li

entry.summary: Argues that on-policy self-distillation teachers conditioned on full reference solutions leak information unavailable at inference, and instead supplies problem-space structure (initial state, goals, constraints, a transition path) as the privileged view. Reports the best question-only accuracy across three math benchmarks at 1.7B to 8B scale.

entry.title: TCPO: Turn-Level Credit Policy Optimization

author.name: Sicong Liao, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: TCPO converts per-turn verifier scores into turn-level credit by comparing against reference states, capturing both immediate progress and regression relative to the best prior attempt in multi-turn refinement. Distinguishes output quality from a turn's marginal contribution.

entry.title: LaCache: Robust Semantic Caching for LLM Serving

author.name: Jiacheng Liang, Yuhui Wang, Tanqiu Jiang, Ting Wang

entry.summary: LaCache defends LLM semantic caches against cache-collision attacks, where injected queries pollute the cache and corrupt later legitimate responses, by exploiting the adversary's limited control over the cached response side. Adds response-side semantic constraint checks rather than query-similarity checks alone.

entry.title: MonitrLLM: A Community-Centered Evaluation Infrastructure for Large Language Models

author.name: Victor Ojewale, Ro Encarnaci\'on, Suresh Venkatasubramanian, Dana\'e Metaxa

entry.summary: MonitrLLM is open-source infrastructure for community-centered LLM evaluation that links full conversation transcripts to user-declared task intent and user-reported outcomes, treating all three as primary signals. Demonstrated in a two-week pilot with 26 college students.

entry.title: Obshazard-bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Foundation Models for Real-Time Disaster Intelligence from Raw Earth Observation Streams

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Qiuyang Yu, Yueying Li, Mingshuo Chen, Chengchi Fei, Kaiyi Xu, Lixin Gu, Wangxu Wei, Junchao Gong, Lipeng Ma, Jiong Wang, Fenghua Ling, Wenlong Zhang, Xue Yang, Wenjing Yang, Ben Fei, Long Lan

entry.summary: Obshazard-bench evaluates multimodal foundation models on real-time disaster intelligence from raw high-frequency satellite observation streams rather than post-processed, post-event products. Designed to reflect operational time pressure and rapidly evolving hazards.

entry.title: EEG-JEPA: Structured Latent Prediction for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Jinhao Li, Zhiyuan Ma, Xueqiao Han, Zhongye Xia, Xinche Zhang, Shanghong Xie, Yixuan Liu, Yongjian Li, Runmin Gan, Tianlin Huo, Sen Song

entry.summary: EEG-JEPA replaces masked waveform reconstruction with joint-embedding latent prediction for EEG foundation models, arguing that reconstructing raw voltage teaches models to recover artifacts and background rather than transferable neural structure. A masked context encoder predicts EMA-produced target latents, following the JEPA recipe adapted to noisy biosignals.

entry.title: Interpretability-Guided Soft Pruning of Attention Heads in Vision Transformers

author.name: Kamil Ksi\k{a}\.zek, Piotr Suszy\'nski, Micha{\l} Jan W{\l}odarczyk, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Biecek

entry.summary: The paper introduces spectral visualization of individual attention heads via Laplacian eigenvectors of their attention maps, uses it to semantically cluster heads in vision foundation models like DINOv2 and find functional redundancy, then prunes with SAPER, a differentiable soft top-K framework. It links interpretability findings directly to compression decisions.

entry.title: The Gate, Not the Cache: Gate Provenance Bounds the Closed-Loop Reliability of Training-Free VLA Token Skipping

author.name: Qi Luo, Shuaijun Liu, Hao Zhao, Kunlin Li, Xiaobo Wang, Ningxing Su, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that training-free token skipping in vision-language-action models fails in closed loop when the gate for the next step is computed from the previous accelerated forward pass, because skipped tokens are exactly those the next gate cannot see, and errors compound. At a 0.9 skip ratio on LIBERO-Object, both reuse and deletion variants collapse (0.68 and 0.31 success) under self-derived gates, isolating gate provenance rather than caching as the limiting factor.

entry.title: Fairness Auditing: Lower Bounds on Company Manipulation

author.name: Rachit Verma, Padala Manisha, Sujit Gujar

entry.summary: Formulating fairness auditing as a min-max game between a computationally unbounded company and a budget-constrained auditor, this work derives lower bounds on how much unfairness can persist after passing an audit, for both fixed-size certification and alpha-tolerant regimes. It quantifies the practical gap left by prior black-box auditing impossibility results.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines: Unveiling Structural Vulnerabilities in Agentic AI Architectures

author.name: Faisal Haque Bappy, Tahrim Hossain, Tarannum Shaila Zaman, Raiful Hasan, Kamrul Hasan, Tariqul Islam

entry.summary: The paper argues that multi-agent LLM pipelines lack boundary verification, a primitive enforcing validation of content, identity, execution intent, and state integrity as data crosses inter-agent boundaries, so adversarial content accepted by one agent propagates as trusted input. It characterizes the resulting structurally distinctive attack classes absent from single-agent settings.

entry.title: Credit the Right Box: Marginal Contribution Assignment for Structured Visual Perception

author.name: Xinheng Han, Jianfei Wang, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Weixing Li, Feng Pan

entry.summary: MCR-GRPO assigns per-object credit in group-relative RL for multimodal models by computing each predicted box's marginal contribution to the response reward, instead of broadcasting one scalar advantage over all tokens. It targets structured perception tasks such as grounding, counting and segmentation.

entry.title: LongChart VQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for MLLMs with Complex Multi-Chart Reasoning

author.name: Ziyan Xiao, Yinghao Zhu, Wenting Zhang, Heaju Kim, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: LongChart is a benchmark for multi-chart reasoning where each VQA instance averages 6.5 images and 31.2 questions, generated by a latent-graph-based synthesis pipeline to ensure consistency. Ten state-of-the-art multimodal models are evaluated, exposing weaknesses beyond single-chart perception.

entry.title: Rapid Embodiment Adaptation for Quadrupedal Locomotion

author.name: Dichen Li, Bo Ai, Nico Bohlinger, Jan Peters, Hao Su, Henrik I. Christensen

entry.summary: Trains a generalist quadruped locomotion policy under embodiment randomization paired with a lightweight module that infers hardware parameters such as joint-range limits and trunk mass from roughly half a second of interaction. The policy adapts online to injury-like degradation and load changes.

entry.title: The Label Defines the Timescale: Trait-State Limits of Temporal-Aggregate Learning

author.name: Xizhe Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes benchmarks where a label aggregates a long temporal horizon but inputs come from short observation windows, deriving an exact protocol-conditioned Bayes-risk identity that decomposes label variance into a stable trait term and a decaying state term. It shows apparent performance ceilings can be artifacts of acquisition protocol rather than model capacity.

entry.title: TimeRLM: Recursive Language Models Enable Precise Anomaly Localization in Long-Context Time-Series

author.name: Nicolas Zumarraga, Lorenzo Steno, Ning Wang, Max Rosenblattl, Thomas Kaar, Maxwell A. Xu, Kevin O'Sullivan, Markus Kreft, Elgar Fleisch, Paul Schmiedmayer, Patrick Langer, Robert Jakob

entry.summary: TimeRLM applies the recursive language model idea to long time series, keeping the raw signal outside the model context and letting the LLM query it programmatically to pinpoint anomalies. This recovers localization accuracy that time-series language models lose at long context lengths.

entry.title: Muon Meets Mamba: Spectral Optimization for State Space Models

author.name: Arslan Battalov, Karim Kramin, Alexander Markotenko, Sofia Sinitsina

entry.summary: Compares the Muon optimizer against AdamW on Mamba-2 at 130M parameters, varying which weight groups receive Muon updates, and finds the benefit is localized to the output projection. The gain is mainly in token efficiency, holds across two corpora and budgets past the compute-optimal point, and is not explained by conditioning.

entry.title: Language Models Encode the Contextual Truth of Propositions

author.name: Rupak Sarkar, Pritika Ramu, Rachel Rudinger

entry.summary: Extends the linear truth-direction literature from world-knowledge facts to contextual truth, propositions whose truth depends on in-context evidence, showing linear representations persist across different output policies and even when the task does not require truth judgments. Uses transcripts from a two-agent collaborative vision-language grounding task and provides causal evidence via steering. Also shows partner assertions significantly sway a model's internal truth representation.

entry.title: SUV: Future Scene Understanding as Video Generation for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Yibo Yuan, Jiacheng Fu, Jiangtong Zhu, Yi Li, Jianhua Han, Meng Tian, Zhuohan Liu, Zhiwei Xiong, Hang Xu, Jianwu Fang, Jianru Xue

entry.summary: SUV recasts end-to-end driving as video generation: a pretrained video foundation model predicts future appearance, semantics, depth, and instance dynamics as parallel video streams, and an action expert attends to those latents to output the ego trajectory. This replaces task-specific prediction heads with one shared predictor.

entry.title: Toward Certified Functional Safety for Industrial Humanoid Robots: The Fail-Passive Gap and a Feasibility Study

author.name: Caiwu Ding, Tao Cui, Lingyun Wang, Chengtao Wen

entry.summary: This paper names the fail-passive gap for legged industrial robots: the safe state of a biped is actively controlled, so cutting power as required by classical machine safety standards itself causes an uncontrolled fall. Using a certified external safety chain as a measuring instrument, it locates precisely where existing functional safety certification frameworks break down for humanoids.

entry.title: Control Barrier Functions via Minkowski Operations for Safe Navigation among Polytopes

author.name: Yi-Hsuan Chen, Shuo Liu, Wei Xiao, Calin Belta, Michael Otte

entry.summary: This work derives an exact signed distance function between a polytopic robot and polytopic obstacles using Minkowski operations and companion convex programs, then integrates it with nonsmooth control barrier functions for safe navigation. It removes the conservative sphere or ellipsoid approximations common in barrier-function methods.

entry.title: Shooting for Contact: Contact-Implicit Multiple Shooting for Dynamic Motion Retargeting

author.name: Sergio A. Esteban, Jason H. K. Siu, Derrick Mach, Junheng Li, Vince Kurtz, Joel W. Burdick, Aaron D. Ames

entry.summary: This paper embeds a differentiable simulator inside a nonlinear program with direct multiple shooting to convert kinematically feasible motion references into dynamically feasible whole-body trajectories, resolving contact, friction, impacts, self-collision, and actuation limits without a prescribed contact schedule. The output is references that reinforcement learning policies can actually reproduce.

entry.title: Structure-Aware Robust Fine-Tuning: Defending Vision-Language-Action Robots Against Physical Attention Hijacking

author.name: Jinquan Zhang, Dongfu Yin, Run Yang, Yufeng Yan, Zhen Tian, F. Richard Yu

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates that printable physical adversarial patches can hijack action-conditioned attention in vision-language-action robot policies, diverting it from task-relevant regions, and shows the attack transfers across tasks and architectures. It then proposes structure-aware robust fine-tuning as a defense.

entry.title: Measurement Without Validity: The Compounding Reliability Problem in Agentic AI Evaluation

author.name: William Caban

entry.summary: This paper models how construct validity degrades multiplicatively across agentic evaluation pipelines, with total validity bounded by the product of task generation, human-simulator calibration, and automated judgment validity, implying that 70 percent validity per stage yields at most 34 percent overall. It validates the model against a structured survey of 55 published agentic evaluation papers, finding roughly 82 percent do not address the compounding problem. The argument matters because such scores justify deployment and compliance claims.

entry.title: Isotropy Cliffs: The Geometric Signature of Decision-Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Okan S. Coskun, Florian Rottach, Carsten Eickhoff, William Rudman

entry.summary: Analyzing five open-weight models on multiple-choice question answering, the authors find decision-critical transition layers marked by a shift in representational isotropy that coincides with major representational reorganization and the emergence of task-relevant clusters. This synchronized geometric behavior correlates strongly with downstream accuracy at roughly r equals 0.84 and is robust to prompt variation. The result suggests a general geometric signature of decision formation.

entry.title: FactorJEPA: Factorizing Monolithic Futures into Layout-Agent-Interaction Channels for Crowded and Chaotic Global South Urban Worlds

author.name: Kapil Wanaskar, Gaytri Jena, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: Introduces DENSEWORLD, a 1,000-hour video dataset of dense, unstructured Global South urban traffic, plus FactorJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive world model that splits future prediction into separate layout, agent, and interaction channels. Targets a regime that lane-structured Western driving benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: Learning What to Remember and What to Internalize in LLM Self-Evolution via Adaptive Memory-Parameter Coordination

author.name: Tianyun Ji, Zhenya Huang, Jiayu Liu, Zirui Liu, Yu Su, Hongbin Pei

entry.summary: COVE coordinates two self-evolution channels for deployed agents: external editable memory or skills for fast adaptation, and parameter updates for deeper capability gains, choosing between them per task. Addresses the flexibility versus depth tradeoff when APIs and requirements shift after deployment.

entry.title: V-Mem: Modality-Routed Retrieval for Long-Term Multimodal Agentic Memory

author.name: Dingyi Kang, Dongming Jiang, Yi Li, Guanpeng Li, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: V-Mem diagnoses two reasons multimodal agent memory fails on image-related questions: queries retrieve same-modality content (modality gap) and the most similar item is often not the evidence needed (similarity-relevance gap). Proposes modality-routed retrieval to fix both.

entry.title: Does the Competitive Component of Adversarial Self-Play Improve Legal Reasoning? A Controlled Negative Result

author.name: Miseog Shawn Kim

entry.summary: A controlled ablation testing whether the competitive part of adversarial self-play adds anything to legal-reasoning training, using a citation-verified survival reward. Across four seeds the adversary and survival reward gave no benefit over an otherwise identical non-competitive run.

entry.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chunji Lv, Yangguang Wei, Junlin Liu, Yang Gao, Ming Liu, Xinming Wang, Jinyang Wu, Guoren Wang, Changsheng Li

entry.summary: PCSD weights token-level self-distillation supervision in agentic RL by how persistently a teacher-favoring signal holds locally, rather than using isolated token discrepancies or a single step-level weight. Aims to make privileged-teacher supervision robust where the teacher is unreliable.

entry.title: ProWorld: Progress-Aware Hyperbolic World Models for Long-Horizon Visual Goal Reaching

author.name: Zihan Liu, Yuzhe Zhuang, Yuanzu Li, Wanshuang Gou, Jiahong Liu, Min Zhou, Menglin Yang

entry.summary: Proposes ProWorld, a JEPA-style latent world model that adds a goal-conditioned progress ordering signal and hyperbolic latent geometry so that multi-step rollouts stay on goal-relevant trajectories. Targets long-horizon visual goal-reaching where locally accurate next-state prediction still drifts away from the goal.

entry.title: From Simple QA to Deep Research: A Verifiable Benchmark Constructed through Iterative Task Evolution

author.name: Can Wang, Haoran Chen, Haowen Gao, Hao Ding, Zhaoyang Liu, Zhiying Tu

entry.summary: Presents an automatically constructed deep-research benchmark of 500 tasks across 31 topics, built by an Explorer-Formalizer-Challenger pipeline that iteratively evolves simple questions into expert-level tasks represented as DAGs for traceable verification. Aims to remove reliance on expensive expert authoring.

entry.title: Optimizing Minimax Regret in Uncertain MDPs with Small Sets of Policies

author.name: Sterre Lutz, Dani\"el Vos, Matthijs T. J. Spaan, Anna Lukina

entry.summary: Studies uncertain MDPs where a small set of policies must be prepared in advance and the best one is chosen once model uncertainty resolves just before execution, optimizing minimax regret over the policy set. Balances robustness against operational or interpretability limits on how many policies can be deployed.

entry.title: CITBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Interactive Tabular Data Processing with LLMs

author.name: Zihan Nan, Yang Gu, Wei Liu, Xi Yan, Zhou Liu, Hao Liang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: CITBench evaluates LLMs on interactive, multi-turn tabular data processing across table matching, cleaning, augmentation, and transformation, spanning 18 task types and 1,296 instances with evolving user requirements. Contrasts with existing single-turn fully specified table reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Conservation laws determine what physical learning remembers

author.name: Bijaya Dangol

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes physical learning rules for resistive networks (equilibrium propagation, coupled learning, adjoint coupled learning) and shows that conductance-mass conservation shapes their inductive bias, proving equilibrium propagation and coupled learning are trajectory-equivalent for single-output tasks while adjoint coupled learning dissipates mass at twice its loss. The results tell experimentalists which physical-learning comparisons are actually informative.

entry.title: WAM-Diff2: Hierarchical AR-to-Diffusion Distillation for Highly Efficient Autonomous Driving VLA

author.name: Zhihao Zhu, Hanlin Shang, Mingwang Xu, Feipeng Cai, Zhuolin He, Yaoyi Li, Jianhua Han, Hang Xu, Siyu Zhu

entry.summary: WAM-Diff2 distills a pretrained autoregressive vision-language-action driving model into a parallel diffusion policy via hierarchical distillation, addressing mismatched attention patterns between the two paradigms. The aim is to keep multi-task reasoning while eliminating autoregressive latency and exposure bias in autonomous driving.

entry.title: Rethinking Video Token Compression with a Global Codebook: Learning Once, Compressing Everywhere

author.name: Jiayang He, Tianling Xu, Diancheng Kang, Huaide Jiang, Junyan Bai, Shaoming Zheng, Xuan Song

entry.summary: ONCE moves video token compression offline by learning a global codebook once, so that video LLMs can compress tokens at inference without repeated per-video pruning or merging computation. It is designed as a model-agnostic plug-in rather than a model-specific compression scheme.

entry.title: Rethinking Personalized Reward Modeling for LLMs under Preference Heterogeneity via Group-Debiased Federated Learning

author.name: Seongyoon Kim, Boryeong Cho, Jihwan Oh, Seokhyun Chung, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that heterogeneous user preferences require per-cluster reward models in federated settings, showing that a single FedAvg initialization, though starting near random accuracy, outperforms group-clustered initializations after local personalization. It proposes group-debiased federated reward modeling for privacy-preserving alignment.

entry.title: Style Wins, Substance Loses: A Diagnosis of LLM-as-Judge in Idea Generation

author.name: Fengxian Ji, Yuke Li, Jingpu Yang, Juanfan Wu, Fan Zhang, Zhexuan Cui, Yu Xie, Min Peng, Qianqian Xie, Xiuying Chen, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: SciStyleBench systematically perturbs the writing style of fixed scientific ideas to test whether LLM judges score substance or presentation, using thousands of controlled instances across three context settings plus new bias metrics. It finds and tries to mitigate stylistic bias in LLM-as-judge evaluation of research ideas.

entry.title: Federated generative event models for tokenized electronic health records

author.name: Michael C. Burkhart, Luke Solo, Inhyeok Lee, S'Khaja Charles, Zewei "Whiskey" Liao, Kaveri Chhikara, Dema Therese, Wan-Ting Liao, Catherine A. Gao, William F. Parker, Brett K. Beaulieu-Jones

entry.summary: Evaluates federated training of tokenized generative event models on more than 122,000 ICU hospitalizations from three health systems harmonized to a common format, across twelve clinical prediction tasks. Generative event models achieved the best within-site and cross-site discrimination and were far more transportable than conventional supervised models, with small cross-site performance penalties.

entry.title: ATFlash: Per-RoPE-Wavelength Attention Windows for Compute/Memory-Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Shun-ichiro Hayashi, Daichi Mukunoki, Tetsuya Hoshino, Takahiro Katagiri

entry.summary: ATFlash prunes attention terms using the exact decomposition of rotary position embeddings into rotation-frequency pairs, applying a distance window proportional to each pair wavelength so every key stays reachable through low-frequency components. The reduction rate is input-independent with a closed form logarithmic in sequence length and composes with token-level dynamic sparsity methods.

entry.title: SP3O: Reinforcement Learning from Segment Preferences without Reward Modeling

author.name: Evan Assmus, Qining Zhang, Lei Ying

entry.summary: SP3O is a reward-model-free, critic-free, gradient-based algorithm for preference-based reinforcement learning in general stochastic MDPs that learns from segment-level rather than trajectory-level comparisons. It addresses both the limitation of prior reward-free methods to bandits or deterministic settings and the annotator burden of comparing long trajectories.

entry.title: SAKI: Score-Aware Low-Rank Key Indexing for Long-Context KV Retrieval

author.name: Lin Zhang

entry.summary: SAKI derives the expected attention-score distortion caused by low-rank key compression, yielding a covariance-weighted objective with a closed-form asymmetric factorization from an SVD of the covariance-weighted query-key operator. The resulting training-free index preserves attention scores rather than key reconstruction quality and improves top-k retrieval across several open 3B to 8B models.

entry.title: Shorter Reasoning, Earlier Answers? An Evaluation of Reasoning Interfaces

author.name: Francesca Carlon, Vincent Ginis, Andres Algaba

entry.summary: Evaluates whether prompts and effort settings that shorten reasoning traces actually preserve accuracy, using matched token budgets across GPQA Diamond and MMLU-Pro with Qwen3-14B and the open-weight GPT-OSS models. Traces shorten by roughly 12 to 17 percent with small and mixed accuracy changes, and a concision instruction even improves MMLU-Pro at tight budgets.

entry.title: LAEF: A Lead-Agnostic ECG Foundation Model Towards Point-of-Care Diagnostics

author.name: Edoardo Coppola, Stefano Fiorini, Pietro Li\`o, Mattia Savardi, Alberto Signoroni

entry.summary: LAEF is a 7M-parameter ECG foundation model that represents recordings as variable-size spatiotemporal graphs so it can natively accept any subset of leads, including the one or two leads available from smartwatches. It is pretrained on 9.2M twelve-lead ECGs with masked node modelling and stochastic lead dropout.

entry.title: CorePath: A Breast-Specialized Pathology Foundation Model for Core Needle Biopsy Diagnosis and Risk-Controlled Report Generation

author.name: Ting Yin, Danning Li, Chen Shu, Xiaoxia Yao, Boyu Fu, Yujing Chang, Tianyu Shi, Mengna Feng, Jie Chen, Jing Fu, Xiuli Xiao, Tianlin Li, Mumin Shao, Jiaxin Bi, Wenchuan Zhang, Xiaoyan Wu, Xiao Han, Zhang Zhang, Yuhao Yi, Hong Bu

entry.summary: CorePath is a breast-specialized multimodal pathology foundation model fine-tuned from PRISM on 7901 paired core needle biopsy whole-slide images and reports from two centers, with risk-controlled report generation. It outperforms its base model across six cohorts and two public benchmarks on detection, invasion assessment, and subtyping without task-specific retraining.

entry.title: DRIFT: Derailing Denoising Trajectories of Flow-Matching VLAs with Adversarial Patch Attack

author.name: Hoseong Tae, Jong-Seok Lee

entry.summary: Shows that the claimed adversarial robustness of flow-matching vision-language-action policies such as pi0 is largely an artifact of attacks that ignored the multi-step denoising ODE. The proposed DRIFT universal adversarial patch on the robot gripper attacks the denoising velocity field, and surprisingly attacking only the first denoising step is stronger and cheaper than attacking many steps. Important for realistic threat modeling of deployed robot policies.

entry.title: Continue or Replan? Bernoulli-Continuation Policy Learning for Adaptive Horizon Execution

author.name: Weichen Xu, Zhenhua Liu, Lin Luo, Yaobo Liang, Chengtang Yao, Qingyu Mei, Jian Cao, Xixin Cao, Xing Zhang, Jiaolong Yang, Baining Guo

entry.summary: Chunk-based VLA policies replan on a fixed periodic schedule, so critical manipulation steps can be executed from stale action chunks. The proposed Bernoulli-Continuation Policy adds a frozen-base, plug-and-play continuation head that turns horizon selection into a sequence of continue-or-replan decisions. A lightweight way to make robot execution horizons task-adaptive.

entry.title: Attention is Case-Sensitive

author.name: Maximilian Dillitzer, Tin Stribor Sohn, Jason J. Corso, Michael Auerbach

entry.summary: Empirically shows that letter casing modulates LLM internal attention: uppercase or alternating-case spans against lowercase context concentrate attention on those spans, tested across nine LLMs and four VLMs with different tokenizers. The effect held for every evaluated non-reasoning text model, suggesting a latent salience property inherited from pretraining. Has implications for prompt design, jailbreak vectors, and controllability.

entry.title: ArtECulture: Benchmarking Culture-Conditioned Visual Emotion Understanding in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaolin Chen, Xuemeng Song, Wenhao Shi, Xianjing Han, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: ArtECulture is a benchmark of 6,792 artworks annotated with culture-specific emotion labels and rationales for English, Chinese, and Arabic cultural perspectives, balancing Western and non-Western content. Sixteen multimodal models are evaluated on predicting culturally conditioned emotional perception and explaining it.

entry.title: UHP Detection: LVLMs have their Unique Hallucination Pattern in the Consistency Space

author.name: Amir Mohammad Ezzati, Kiyan Rezaee, Bardiya Kariminia, Mohamad Amin Yousefi, Asal Mohammadjafari Mamaqani, Behrad Samimi, Mohammad Hossein Rohban

entry.summary: UHP Detection argues that a single consistency score cannot capture vision-language model hallucination and instead characterizes it as a structured pattern across multiple behavioral probes in a two-axis consistency space. The method is fully black-box, requiring no access to model internals.

entry.title: How Should Vision-Language-Action Models Use Proprioceptive State?

author.name: Yiren Zhao, Ziyang Chen, Ziyang Rao, Pengteng Li, He Zhang, Weiyu Guo, Yandong Guo, Rushi Dai

entry.summary: This controlled study asks whether, how much, and where vision-language-action models should consume robot proprioceptive state, comparing text serialization, vision-language prefix injection, and direct feeding to the action expert, plus the value of state history. Experiments fix the backbone of a flow-matching policy so the comparisons isolate the state-conditioning design choice.

entry.title: When Predictions Become Regressors: A Split-Sample Correction for Biases in Downstream Inference

author.name: Nathan Canen, Ted Enamorado

entry.summary: Shows that using LLM or ML predictions as explanatory variables in downstream regressions produces biased coefficients due to measurement error, and proposes constructing instrumental variables from predictions generated on independent splits of the same data. The correction needs no new data and is validated in simulations and applied social-science settings.

entry.title: Confidence Horizons

author.name: Chase Mathis, Ian Waudby-Smith

entry.summary: Introduces confidence horizons, anytime-valid confidence sequences that deliberately give up validity past a finite time bound in exchange for tighter intervals within it. This targets the common practical case where experiment length is capped by budget, ethics or logistics, bridging confidence sequences and group-sequential testing.

entry.title: Through the LENS: Local Geometric Decomposition of Vision-Language Model Representations

author.name: Shalom Kachko, Raz Lapid, Margarita Vald, Almog Dubin, Moshe Sipper

entry.summary: LENS decomposes vision-language model activations into locally low-rank Gaussian neighborhoods using a mixture of factor analyzers, on the premise that representations can be globally high-dimensional but locally simple, which global linear-direction methods miss. Applied to LLaVA-1.5-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B, it reveals distinct depth-dependent modality fusion trajectories matching each model's architectural fusion mechanism. It offers a local-geometry alternative to standard linear probing.

entry.title: FinDeepIndicator: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents in End-to-End Financial Indicator Construction

author.name: Chaoqun Yang, Fengbin Zhu, Xinyu Lin, Long Bai, Xiaoluan Liu, Ke-Wei Huang, Roger Zimmermann, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: FinDeepIndicator is described as the first benchmark evaluating deep research agents on end-to-end construction of financial indicators, scoring four stages: formula specification, data collection, indicator calculation, and answer generation. Existing financial benchmarks mostly check final answers and assume the needed data is already supplied. The design exposes where agents fail in the intermediate research process.

entry.title: The Scaling Paradox in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Anyan Qi, Mengxin Wang

entry.summary: This analytical paper asks whether AI scaling gains survive when the AI works alongside a human, showing joint system performance scales positively only if humans accurately perceive AI capability. Misperception can fundamentally break the link, so a more capable AI need not produce a better human-AI system. It formalizes a paradox implicit in much deployment practice.

entry.title: Loud or Silent? A Reusable Framework for Per-Modality Failure Analysis in Multimodal Clinical AI

author.name: Quang Bui, Shlok Jaiswal, Samuel Paik-Heintz, Kevin Zhou, Kaushik Madapati, Krittaphas Chaisutyakorn, Noah Dane Hebdon, Dimitrios Proios, Sebasti\'an Andr\'es Cajas Ord\'o\~nez, Kacper Dobek, Boya Zhang, Aly Dhedhi, Ahram Han, Kushul Reddy Palakala, Rahul Gorijavolu, Jacques Kpodonu, Leo Anthony Celi

entry.summary: Provides a model-agnostic framework for analyzing which modality caused a multimodal clinical model to fail when inputs are missing, and whether the failure is loud (flagged) or silent. Emphasizes reusable evaluation as models are frequently replaced.

entry.title: HPFA: Hypergraph-Based Paired Failure Attribution for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Runchuan Zhu, Hongbin Lai, Bowen Jiang, Junrui Zhang, Zhangheng LI, Ostap Kilbasovych, Junyuan Hong

entry.summary: HPFA attributes LLM reasoning failures by representing traces as hypergraphs and comparing hyperedges of a failed path against a matched successful path, localizing root-cause steps without expensive per-step counterfactual rollouts. Aims to make reflection and self-correction more reliable and scalable.

entry.title: From Profiling to Synthesis: Benchmarking Implicit Behavioral Alignment in Personalized LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajia Song, Bobo Li, Haiwen Yi, Zibo Ji, Meishan Zhang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: IBA-Bench evaluates whether personalized LLM agents can act on implicit, noisy, and temporally inconsistent user preferences drawn from longitudinal interaction histories, rather than answering questions about static profiles. Frames the shortfall as a knowledge-to-action gap between profiling and preference-conditioned execution.

entry.title: Hard Constraints, Smooth Gradients: Learning Feasible Inventory Policies via Differentiable Projection

author.name: Patrick Helm, Jan-Niklas Doerr, Joren Gijsbrechts, Stefan Minner

entry.summary: Embeds a differentiable convex projection inside an RL policy so that a neural network proposes continuous actions, a quadratic program projects them onto the relaxed feasible set, and a dual-informed mapping restores integrality for constrained inventory decisions. Enforces hard interacting constraints rather than penalizing violations.

entry.title: Automated ECG Interval Measurement and Wave Delineation Using Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet

author.name: Farhan Adam Mukadam, Harshit Mishra, Nachiket Makwana, Pradyot Tiwari, Subramani Kandasamy, KVS Hari

entry.summary: Evaluates an end-to-end ECG delineation pipeline built on a Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet on 10,646 clinical 12-lead ECGs, reporting clinical interval accuracy (PR, QRS, QT/QTc) with bias, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, bootstrap confidence intervals, and rhythm-stratified errors. Shifts evaluation from fiducial-point timing on small curated sets to clinically meaningful interval measurement at scale.

entry.title: Inference-Time Policy Alignment for Fair Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Umer Siddique, Peilang Li, Conor Wallace, Yongcan Cao

entry.summary: Borrowing the idea of inference-time alignment from language models, this work steers an already trained RL policy toward welfare-based fairness objectives at deployment without retraining, so newly discovered stakeholder preferences can be accommodated on the fly. It relaxes the common assumption that fairness criteria are known before training.

entry.title: Distilling Reasoning Traces into Advisory Prompts for Software Engineering Tasks

author.name: Faizan Faisal, Prem Devanbu, Toufique Ahmed

entry.summary: The paper asks whether the benefit of explicit reasoning modes on software-engineering tasks can be captured more cheaply by distilling reasoning traces into reusable advisory prompts, so models get most of the accuracy gain without paying thinking-token costs on every query. It evaluates on code generation and related tasks such as hallucination and output prediction.

entry.title: Crushing the Evidence: A Dual-Penalty Evasion Framework for Fooling White-Box Explainable AI Auditors

author.name: Niraj Kumar, Harsh Kasyap

entry.summary: The paper presents a dual-penalty optimization attack that suppresses evidence of bias or backdoors in white-box explanations from LIME, SHAP, and Integrated Gradients, without relying on the out-of-distribution scaffolding detectors that existing defenses were built to catch. It shows that current explanation-based audits can be defeated by attacks with no anomalous perturbation footprint.

entry.title: Latency-Tolerant Cloud-Edge Collaborative Vision-Language-Action Models via Emergent Representational Specialization

author.name: Daojie Peng, Fulong Ma, Bingtao Wang, Sheng Wang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: CloudEdgeVLA splits a vision-language-action policy so a cloud model encodes delayed observations into slowly varying task features while a lightweight edge head fuses the latest available cloud feature with current local vision, training with randomly delayed features so the split emerges without explicit scheduling or delay cues. It targets robots that need cloud-scale semantics but local closed-loop control under jitter.

entry.title: Cloud-ScPO: Hidden-State Geometry for Semi-Supervised Preference Optimization in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuzhou Liu, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: Shows that reasoning trajectories from LLMs form geometrically distinguishable point clouds for correct versus incorrect solutions, and uses this structure to mine preference pairs from mostly unlabeled data for semi-supervised preference optimization on math reasoning. It reduces dependence on verified answers and reward models.

entry.title: Talking to Digital Twins: Selective Disclosure and Belief Measurement in Financial Social Media

author.name: Boone Bowles, Raymond Duch, Sorin Sorescu

entry.summary: Constructs LLM digital twins of financial influencers from their X accounts and interviews them repeatedly in real time to recover stock-level beliefs even when no public post is made, archiving responses before the return window to avoid look-ahead bias. The recovered beliefs reportedly predict cross-sectional large-cap returns.

entry.title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction

author.name: Junno Yun, Ya\c{s}ar Utku Al\c{c}alar, Mehmet Ak\c{c}akaya

entry.summary: UDT reconciles U-Net inductive biases with diffusion transformers via data-adaptive token reduction, creating an explicit multi-scale encoder-decoder that avoids fixed downsampling schedules. It addresses degraded late-layer representation quality and imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior in isotropic DiTs.

entry.title: Pin Once, Swap Light: Subspace-Aligned Centroid-Residual Training for Efficient Ultra-LoRA Serving

author.name: Xiang Li, Pengcheng Wang, Huazheng Wang, Saurabh Bagchi

entry.summary: SALT trains LoRA adapters as a shared pinned centroid plus tiny per-task residuals so that multi-tenant servers can host hundreds of adapters with the memory and PCIe transfer cost of ultra-low-rank adapters. The subspace alignment step aims to keep downstream quality near that of higher-rank adapters.

entry.title: Resume Means Resume: A Machine-Checked Conformance Contract for Checkpoint, Interrupt, and Resume Semantics in Workflow Persistence Layers

author.name: Sajjad Khan

entry.summary: Defines a machine-checkable contract of six properties for what resuming a persisted agent workflow should mean regarding already-executed side effects, and verifies a reference semantics exhaustively in TLA+. It reports that five widely deployed agent frameworks answer these questions differently and violate even their own stated guarantees.

entry.title: DP-MemView: A Memory Interface for Attribute-Level Transcript Privacy in Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Jong Wook Kim, Byoungjae Min, Kennedy Edemacu, Yoonhyuk Choi, Sae-Hong Cho, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: DP-MemView formalizes the risk that repeated memory-conditioned responses from a long-term LLM agent can cumulatively leak protected attributes even when never stated, and provides a differentially private interface that exposes selected public views instead of raw memory. Per-attribute privacy ledgers block selections that would exceed a budget cap and substitute a generic view, with a pure DP guarantee proved over the entire adaptive transcript.

entry.title: Every Wrong Answer Counts: Option-Level Psychometrics for LLM Multiple-Choice Benchmarks

author.name: Xiao Fei, Yang Zhang, Sarah Almeida Carneiro, Michalis Vazirgiannis

entry.summary: Introduces an option-aware psychometric model (LLM Nominal Response Model) that uses the full distribution over multiple-choice options, not just correctness, to jointly estimate model ability and item characteristics while separating calibration sharpness, positional bias, and difficulty-dependent fallback behavior. Fit across 189 LLMs and 31,554 items from 14 benchmarks with held-out predictive checks. Shows wrong-answer patterns carry substantial diagnostic signal.

entry.title: SLAMFormer-$\infty$: Infinite SLAM Transformer for Unbounded Frontend and Backend Processing

author.name: Zhijian Fang, Weicheng Zheng, Yijun Yuan, Weibang Wang, Zhuoguang Chen, Chang Sun, Junhao Huang, Kenan Li, Minghui Qin, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: SLAMFormer-infinity is a geometric transformer for SLAM that removes the implicit distance bound of first-frame-anchored formulations by using memory conditions to define flexible coordinate frames and scales per input frame. The same formulation supports efficient local frontend computation and globally consistent long-range backend optimization.

entry.title: Beyond Simply Environment Scaling: Designing Effective Environment Distributions for Multimodal Agent Learning

author.name: Kejian Zhu, Zhuoran Jin, Dongqi Huang, Hongbang Yuan, Yupu Hao, Kang Liu, Jun Zhao

entry.summary: This study finds that simply scaling the number of multimodal training environments does not reliably improve agents, then designs better environment distributions along diversity and difficulty axes via ability-aware environment selection and a hierarchical difficulty curriculum. It reframes environment construction as a distribution design problem rather than a scaling problem.

entry.title: SpreadMark: Robust Image Watermarking via Spread-Spectrum Embedding

author.name: Wei Song, Yuxin Cao, Zhenchang Xing, Liming Zhu, Jin Song Dong, Yulei Sui, Jingling Xue

entry.summary: SpreadMark revisits classical spread-spectrum embedding inside a neural post-hoc watermarking pipeline after measuring that in existing encoder-decoder schemes each message bit occupies only a small image region, which makes removal easy. Each bit is spread as a dense pseudo-random codeword and recovered by matched filtering over a learned cover-suppressed representation.

entry.title: Semantic Haptic Feedback Enhances Dexterous Robotic Teleoperation

author.name: Bingjian Huang, Sahar Aseeri, Jonas Schmidtler, Joseph Zhang, Sonny Chan, Andrew Doxon, Jom Preechayasomboon, Evan Pezent, Alberto Rigo, Amir Memar, Nicholas Colonnese, Chase Tymms

entry.summary: Instead of trying to reproduce high-fidelity physical sensation, this industrial-lab study delivers abstract haptic patterns encoding robot state categories such as confirmations and exceptions to teleoperators through pneumatic and vibrotactile wrist devices. The premise is that semantic information transfer beats fidelity given hardware limits and operator workload.

entry.title: GraspMeanFlow: SE(3)-Equivariant MeanFlow for Few-Step 6-DoF Grasp Generation

author.name: Jiyong Kwon, Yikun Bai, Amirhossein Mollaali, Guang Lin

entry.summary: GraspMeanFlow adapts MeanFlow-style average-velocity learning to the SE(3) group so that 6-DoF grasp poses can be generated in very few network evaluations while remaining equivariant to object rotation and translation. The time-ordered exponential formulation ensures the learned average velocity reproduces the accumulated rigid-body displacement exactly.

entry.title: RoboReact: Agentic Skill Distillation from Generated Egocentric Videos for Generalizable Whole-Body Manipulation

author.name: Shuliang He, Shuai Wang, Bo Yue, Junchi Teng, Changyu Wang, Guiliang Liu

entry.summary: RoboReact synthesizes whole-body humanoid manipulation skills from a single egocentric RGB-D observation by generating human manipulation videos, extracting geometry-preserving interaction keyframes, and distilling them into executable robot behaviors. It aims to reduce reliance on expensive hardware teleoperation data and manual annotation.

entry.title: Motif-Mamba: network motif improved mamba for long-range sequence modeling

author.name: Chonghe Hao, Yue Sun, Jian Zhang, Yansong Wang, Wangzi Yao, Yunjie Yao, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Motif-Mamba augments the Mamba state space model with a low-rank recurrent pathway inspired by three-node network motifs, projecting hidden states into a compact dynamical subspace to enable cross-dimensional interaction that diagonal state transitions otherwise prevent.
