The goal is better long-range sequence modeling at linear cost. It is an architectural modification aimed at a known structural limitation of selective SSMs.

entry.title: Why Does the Future Branch? Identifiable Closure Tests for Stochastic Physical World Models

author.name: Yibin Dong

entry.summary: This paper proves that ordinary transition data cannot identify whether a stochastic world model's uncertainty comes from observation aliasing of distinct physical states or from genuine randomness remaining after the declared state is fixed, even with an optimal probabilistic predictor. It introduces ClosurePairs, an interventional protocol crossing compatible microstates with repeated exogenous disturbances, and a two-way variance decomposition that separates aliasing, process noise, and their interaction. This gives world model evaluation a causal rather than purely predictive criterion.

entry.title: Control Under Compression: Reliability Frontiers for Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Yinghan Hou, Zongyou Yang

entry.summary: Presents CompressAgent, an environment-verified benchmark measuring whether compressing an agent's persistent system instructions (tools, policies, recovery protocols) preserves operational reliability. Finds a nonlinear, method-dependent reliability frontier across nine control contexts and over 15,000 runs.

entry.title: Cognitive Demand Steering for Adaptive Meta-Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: John Scoville, Shengzhuang Chen, Yejin Bang, Stefan Winzeck, Jonathan Richard Schwarz

entry.summary: Cognitive Demand Steering is a training-free meta-reasoning loop in which an evaluator estimates the remaining reasoning demand at each step rather than scoring past progress, steering strategy choice forward-looking. Avoids controller training and coarse search actions.

entry.title: Where Reasoning Diverges: Localized Multi-Agent Debate for Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Weijun Gao, Xiang Ding, Haoyang Liu, Tiancheng Xing

entry.summary: Localized Multi-Agent Debate identifies the earliest conflicting reasoning step between agents and restricts debate to that local segment, committing agreed steps so later conflicts do not reopen them. Reports the best judge accuracy across ten backbones on four multi-hop QA benchmarks.

entry.title: CoEvo-Mem: Co-Evolving Retrieval Policy and Memory Bank for LLM Agents

author.name: Bowen Ye, Yongchao Xu, Zhijian Li, Xiang Yin, Junkai Ma, Wenzhao Li

entry.summary: CoEvo-Mem closes the loop between an agent's retrieval policy and its memory bank, since retrieval determines which memories get usage signals and memory updates reshape retrieval. Uses a frozen LLM for route-specific query rewrites with a lightweight residual router.

entry.title: ReasonCast: Towards Explainable Time Series Forecasting with Reasoning

author.name: Seunghan Lee, Jun Seo, Jaehoon Lee, Junhyeok Kang, Sangjun Han, Sungdong Yoo, Minjae Kim, Tae Yoon Lim, Dongwan Kang, Hwanil Choi, Soonyoung Lee, Wonbin Ahn

entry.summary: ReasonCast argues for task-fused time series models that emit a numeric forecast and a natural-language self-explanation in one coherent response, rather than separate understanding and generation paths. Introduces a setting and dataset for studying this joint capability.

entry.title: PAC Approximation and DIRECT Optimization for Parametric Markov Models

author.name: Zhiming Chi, Ying Liu, Andrea Turrini, Lijun Zhang, David N. Jansen

entry.summary: Provides PAC-style polynomial approximations of the property-satisfaction function for parametric MDPs via scenario sampling and linear programming, then uses DIRECT global optimization over the approximation for parameter synthesis. Reduces the cost of exact rational-function computation in probabilistic model checking.

entry.title: Shared Prefixes, Better Credit: Adaptive Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yiqing Liu, Zihao Wang, Hantao Yao, Wu Liu, Yongdong Zhang

entry.summary: TreeCredit assigns credit in multi-agent reasoning by expanding candidate operators from shared intermediate states into collaboration trees, estimating each operator's utility through state-matched downstream comparisons rather than attributing trajectory-level returns. Enables cheaper adaptive routing among collaboration operators.

entry.title: DLLM-TTS: Block Discrete Diffusion Language Model for Text-to-Speech Synthesis

author.name: Wasim Madha, Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana, Akshat Mandloi, Sudarshan Kamath

entry.summary: DLLM-TTS casts text-to-speech as conditional block discrete diffusion over X-Codec2 neural audio codec tokens, applying masked diffusion within blocks while decoding blocks sequentially to capture both local acoustic coherence and global text-speech alignment. Achieves parallel in-block generation with a favorable real-time factor.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Simulation-Based Inference for Operations Research with Large Language Models

author.name: Liang Guo, Lin Shaochong, Shen Zuo-Jun Max, Zhang Kun

entry.summary: A training-free inference framework for operations-research modeling that scores intermediate formulation steps with short lookahead simulations, quantifying uncertainty about whether a partial model can extend into a globally consistent optimization program. Aims to stop locally plausible steps from cascading into solver-breaking errors.

entry.title: Hierarchical BM25: Lexical Search at Billion-Document Scale

author.name: Umesh Deshpande, Swaminathan Sundararaman

entry.summary: Hierarchical BM25 trades exact lexical ranking for bounded memory and latency at billion-document scale, using a small resident coarse index to pick which of roughly a thousand topical, size-balanced document groups a query must visit before exhaustive search within them. It targets the regime where a flat 400 GB index either does not fit in DRAM or takes seconds per query from disk.

entry.title: One-Sided Quantile Coupling for Flow Matching

author.name: Jin-Young Kim, So-Yoon Cho, Hyun-Gyoon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces a one-sided coupling for flow matching that constructs a paired source sample directly from each data point via rank-to-Gaussian-quantile mapping along random orthogonal directions, avoiding quadratic-cost minibatch optimal transport. It aims to get structured-coupling benefits at near-zero overhead.

entry.title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Puzhuo Zheng, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Audits perturbation-based candidate selection for vision-language test-time scaling and finds that the apparent benefit comes from the decoding format rather than from the image perturbations themselves. It challenges the assumption that grounding-dependent selection signals explain observed gains.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Proximal Causal Inference under Hidden Confounding and Interference

author.name: Omar Faruque, Pavan Raj Ravi, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: Extends proximal causal inference to spatiotemporal data by introducing treatment- and outcome-inducing proxies that capture both local and neighborhood-level hidden confounding, deriving an outcome confounding bridge under interference. It targets climate, epidemiology and regional policy settings where exchangeability fails.

entry.title: LEAP: Lean Environment-Feedback via Adaptive Pruning for Code RL in GPU Kernel Generation

author.name: Tankun Li, Zhi Chen, Yaohua Tang

entry.summary: LEAP addresses reinforcement learning for CUDA kernel generation, where binary compile-or-pass rewards are sparse and multi-turn environment feedback is slow and dilutes credit. It prunes environment feedback adaptively to keep critic-free group-relative policy optimization tractable for low-level systems code.

entry.title: No One Wins in Nuclear War: A Social Simulation of Military Decision-making

author.name: Glenn Matlin, Isaac Song, Anthony Wen-Ming Zang, Mark Riedl

entry.summary: WOPR is a social simulation environment for studying high-stakes organizational decision-making, built on a deterministic replay-validated rules engine and first instantiated with a published nuclear war card game including private-channel negotiation. It contrasts with persona-fidelity social simulations by making mechanics verifiable and replayable.

entry.title: Robust Counterfactual Policy Optimisation via Nondeterministic Causal Models

author.name: Jessica Lally, Milad Kazemi, Nicola Paoletti, David Watson, Sander Beckers

entry.summary: Formalizes counterfactual policy optimization under probabilistic nondeterministic causal models, separating latent confounding from irreducible environment stochasticity that deterministic structural models conflate, and gives a practical sensitivity-analysis optimization for robust counterfactual policies. Validated on a sepsis treatment simulator with a hidden confounder.

entry.title: AcceptMoE: Commitment-Weighted Self-Sizing Verifier Expert Sets for Efficient MoE Speculative Decoding

author.name: Shuang Liang (Mark), Hao (Mark), Chen, Zhiwen Mo, Qianzhou Wang, Guoyu Li, Lingxiao Ma, Wayne Luk

entry.summary: AcceptMoE reduces the hidden cost of speculative decoding for mixture-of-experts targets, where verifying a token tree activates the union of experts chosen by all draft nodes even though only a few are accepted. Its verifier-side selector combines router scores with offline commitment probabilities and self-sizes the eligible expert set to cut expert-weight traffic.

entry.title: Simulation-free and finite-time diffusion model

author.name: Kentaro Kaba, Masayuki Ohzeki, Yuki Sughiyama

entry.summary: Presents a framework for designing diffusion reference processes that are both simulation-free to train and finite-time to sample, by prescribing tractable time-dependent conditional distributions and constructing the process that realizes them as marginals. It shows score matching emerges from reversing the reference process rather than being fundamental, with conditional flow matching arising as a small-noise limit.

entry.title: Provably Learning Multi-Head Attention with Queries

author.name: Sunyeop Kim, Insung Kim, Jian Guo

entry.summary: Studies black-box recovery of multi-head softmax attention parameters using only scalar outputs from queried token sequences, extending prior single-head query-complexity results. It defines a canonical head representation by merging heads with identical key-query matrices and removing degenerate merged heads.

entry.title: TraceCompiler: Skill-Guided Mining and Compilation of LLM Agent Traces into Mostly Deterministic Workflows

author.name: Salma El Yadouni (EPFL), Guanyi Li (Binome Technologies)

entry.summary: TraceCompiler mines clusters of noisy tool-using agent traces and compiles them into mostly deterministic executable workflows, admitting a dependency edge only when a consumer argument value is uniquely attributable to an earlier producer. Every hard edge carries auditable evidence and ambiguous relations impose no ordering, while bindings are classified as constants, user inputs, copied outputs, transforms, or residual LLM decisions.

entry.title: Efficient Knowledge Distillation for LLMs: Offline Top-K Logits and a Fused Chunked KL Loss

author.name: Bakbergen Ryskulov, Iker Garc\'ia-Ferrero, David Montero, David Jansen, Ali Hashemi, Jezabel R. Garcia, Antonio Tiene, Rom\'an Or\'us

entry.summary: A practitioner-focused study of making LLM knowledge distillation cheaper: caching a teacher's top-K logits offline matches online distillation at near-identical loss while freeing teacher memory, running about 29 percent faster per iteration and up to 41 percent higher throughput, plus a fused chunked KL loss. Directly targets the cost of recovering quality in compressed small models. Immediately actionable for teams shipping small models.

entry.title: OPTD: On-Policy Transition Distillation with Consistency-Guided Adaptive Compression for Few-Step Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Hualei Zhang, Shuhan Guo, Jie Zhang, Xiaoyi Pang, Jian Liu, Haoxi Li, Bohai Gu, Haoxuan Che, Jingcai Guo, Song Guo

entry.summary: OPTD performs on-policy distillation for few-step diffusion language models, addressing the mismatch where students trained on off-policy trajectories drift from the states they actually visit once parallel token commitments alter later context. It adds consistency-guided adaptive compression to decide how far each distilled transition should advance. Targets a core efficiency bottleneck of diffusion LM decoding.

entry.title: PACE: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Time-Efficient Embodied Planning

author.name: Yuchen Huang, Xijiang Ying, Zhenhua Ma, Xiaxiang Yuan, Zhijie Gao, Jiayi Huang, Ruichi Mao, Jiazheng Zhang, Hongsheng Ti, Maotao Tian, Rong Shi, Lu Zhao, Shizhuang Zhang, Zhuo Cui, He Wang, Ling Liu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: PACE attacks the minutes-long latency of reasoning language models in embodied planning by interleaving thinking with action execution and dynamically allocating reasoning token budgets, so execution time windows are no longer idle. The framework pipelines cognition against physical action instead of requiring reasoning to finish first.

entry.title: CUDA MPC: A GPU-Native Solver for Model Predictive Control

author.name: Babak Akbari, Melissa Greeff

entry.summary: CUDA MPC co-designs a model predictive control solver with GPU execution, pairing parallel-in-horizon ADMM splitting with a fused kernel that keeps the entire iterative solve and intermediate variables on the device. This avoids the repeated kernel launches and host transfers that limit typical GPU-accelerated controllers.

entry.title: LiLa-WAM: Lightweight Latent Reasoning World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Fan Yang, Yuting Su, Xiaobo Wang, Yuncheng You, Fugui Fan, Yuting Wu, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, JiaHong Ning, Peiguang Jing

entry.summary: LiLa-WAM is a world-action model for manipulation that predicts future scene evolution in a compact latent space rather than pixel space, avoiding multi-stage training pipelines. The stated headline is end-to-end trainability on a single 24GB GPU, making anticipatory control accessible under modest compute budgets.

entry.title: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

author.name: Dong Yan, Jian Liang, Dapeng Hu, Ran He, Nicholas Jing Yuan, Qi Zhang, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: AgentStream evaluates self-evolving agents under realistic streaming conditions by reorganizing existing agentic benchmarks into configurable task streams with isolated, sequential, and interleaved scenarios that vary domain composition over time. It exposes how evolution components behave when tasks arrive continuously rather than in independent evaluation batches. The framework addresses a mismatch between how self-evolving agents are tested and how they would be deployed.

entry.title: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chengbo Liu, Lifang Zhou, Ruijie Yan, Pei Tan, Ao Sun, Haojun Huang, Guichun Hua, Sining Wei, Yining Chen, Yingying He, Yutao Xie

entry.summary: RMSWeb is a three-part training recipe for compact web agents built on Qwen3-VL-Instruct at 8B and 32B, combining reflection-conditioned retries to raise trajectory collection yield, failure-mode mining to escape the dominance of routine states after supervised fine-tuning, and a salvage mechanism giving learning signal to groups that group-relative RL would otherwise discard. It addresses both data scarcity and degenerate advantage estimates in web-action RL. The focus is cost-effective deployable agents.

entry.title: Auditing Discovery Claims: A Two-Sided Criterion for Agentic Science, with the Negative Side Decidable

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jianlin Chen, Ziyao Lin, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: This paper builds a two-sided audit for capability claims by self-improving AI-for-science systems, where the negative side is decidable: a pseudoknot-free RNA folding oracle provably cannot represent crossing base pairs, bounding the prior verifier's reachable range offline before any run. The authors show an invented solver-free operator scores 43 of 60 crossing RNA targets under the very predictor it optimizes, illustrating how a fallible oracle inflates apparent discovery. Novelty is defined relative to the agent's prior self rather than the base model.

entry.title: Toward Fine-Grained Forgetting:Attribute Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Junkai Lin, Junkai Chen, Siqi Hou, Yuhao He, Ruiqi Liu, Chenhan Jin, Shengze Xu, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: This work defines attribute-level unlearning for multimodal LLMs, where the model must forget one specified attribute of a person while retaining other non-sensitive facts about the same identity, in contrast to prior benchmarks that delete whole profiles. The authors build a benchmark covering long-text, numeric, and short-text targets at multiple forget ratios and diverse question types. Their evaluation shows existing methods struggle at this finer granularity.

entry.title: G-ReAct: Graph-Guided Deep Search via Structure-State Co-Evolution

author.name: Shaoxiong Yang, Mengyuan Zhang, Shaojun Lin, Chao Li, Wei Liu, Kun Shao, Jian Luan

entry.summary: G-ReAct restructures deep search agents as state evolution over a fixed-topology query graph so intermediate constraints and progress persist across long multi-hop searches. Targets context forgetting and search drift in linear ReAct-style loops.

entry.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning

author.name: Junru Song, Wenhao Zhang, Yang Yang, Xuekai Qiu, Feifei Wang, Weien Zhou, Tingsong Jiang, Ying Wen, Yang Li, Wen Yao

entry.summary: CoNav-UAV coordinates two drones at complementary altitudes for target-oriented vision-and-language navigation using Stackelberg leader-follower learning, so global exploration and close-range approach are handled by different agents. Removes reliance on privileged information used by prior dual-UAV attempts.

entry.title: Before Reasoning Can Fail: Pre-Evidence Procedural Failures in Agentic RAG

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: Analyzes a pre-reasoning failure mode in agentic RAG where the agent retrieves snippets but finalizes an answer without reading them, using 12,000 paired trajectories on three multi-hop QA datasets to separate pre-evidence discipline failures from post-gold-read errors. Tests Read-Gate, a minimal runtime invariant forcing a read after search.

entry.title: Empirical investigation of 3D CT Foundation Models and Unsupervised Adaptation for Head and Neck Cancer Recurrence Prediction

author.name: Bilel Guetarni, Feryal Windal, David Pasquier, Halim Benhabiles

entry.summary: Benchmarks several 3D CT foundation models for head and neck cancer recurrence-free survival prediction across two public datasets totaling 3,644 patients, comparing adaptation strategies including unsupervised approaches. Assesses whether learned representations generalize across clinical settings or require task adaptation.

entry.title: Response Magnitude as a Dominant Signal for Held-Out CRISPRi Perturbation Effect Prediction

author.name: Mehrdad Shoeibi, Niloofar Yousefi

entry.summary: This study shows that on the Virtual Cell Challenge benchmark for held-out CRISPRi perturbation effects, the prediction target is largely determined by four simple deterministic scalar statistics of the input, so a deep MLP with full input access collapses toward that low-dimensional signal. It explains why simple baselines match deep perturbation predictors and characterizes how the shortcut transfers across cell types.

entry.title: CrossProjection: Geometric Grounding Beyond Viewpoint Change in Architectural Drawings

author.name: Kaho Li, Pengyu Zeng, Yuqin Dai, Jun Yin, Tianjing Feng, Shuai Lu

entry.summary: CrossProjection diagnoses whether vision-language models keep component identity and geometry consistent across architectural plans, sections, and elevations, which are cuts and facade projections rather than camera-motion-related views. Across 23 real drawing sets, GPT-5.5 reaches 82.4 percent on categorical conditions versus 62.2 percent for Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct and 57.2 percent for GLM-4.5V, with free-form geometric localization much weaker.

entry.title: SSTG-Nav: Metric-Grounded Spatial-Semantic Topological Graphs for Reusable Object Navigation

author.name: Daojie Peng, Bingtao Wang, Jun Ma

entry.summary: SSTG-Nav builds a reusable metric-semantic topological memory so a service robot that has surveyed a home or office once can turn later object-goal requests into reachable stopping places rather than re-exploring from scratch. On 1,000 HM3D-v2 episodes across 36 scenes the goal-independent topology reaches a 99.4 percent geometric success ceiling and retains distinct recovery standoffs so a single map error does not end the task.

entry.title: DexMani: Human-Derived Manipulability Guidance for Dexterous Rotation

author.name: Xiaoyang Chen, Shengcheng Luo, Haoran Guo, Jiaming Jiang, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao, Chenxi Xiao

entry.summary: DexMani transfers human demonstrations into a contact-conditioned manipulability prior that captures how each support, release, and re-contact decision reshapes the object-rotation directions still available to the hand. This gives dexterous rotation policies foresight about future manipulability instead of discovering contact schedules purely by trial and error.

entry.title: From Chasing Ghosts to Missed Attacks: Perspectives and Perceptions of SOC Practitioners on LLM Integration, Risks, and Readiness

author.name: Jonas Thurner, Nadine Jost, Stefan Albert Horstmann, Fabian Ising, Lea Groeber, Alena Naiakshina, Sebastian Schinzel

entry.summary: Based on 25 semi-structured interviews with security operations center practitioners who had used LLMs, plus interactive scenarios, the authors identify 15 use cases in six functional categories and document where analysts value automation versus where they distrust it. It grounds claims about LLM utility in security operations in actual practitioner experience.

entry.title: Hybrid Lagrangian-Eulerian Model for Lagrangian Fluid Simulation

author.name: Ruoyan Li, Wei Wang, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: A hybrid neural fluid simulator that augments particle-based Lagrangian dynamics with an Eulerian grid representation plus adaptive downsampling, to fix wasted capacity in uniform regions and long-horizon temporal drift from purely local message passing. It borrows the structure of classical hybrid numerical solvers.

entry.title: Stop When Memory Suffices: Evidence-Conditioned Progressive Execution for LLM Agents

author.name: Yidan Lin, Kaixiang Wang, Jiong Lou, Jie Li

entry.summary: Router-Mem is a long-horizon agent memory system that routes queries through progressively deeper evidence-gathering stages, stopping early when compressed memory already suffices. It aims to combine the low latency of structured memory with the coverage of deep-research retrieval.

entry.title: Deep Agentic Search for Repository-Level Code Question Answering: An Empirical Study

author.name: Amirkia Rafiei Oskooei, Bora Ilci, Alperen Kayim, Mehmet Egemen Uzun, Berat Can, Kaan Emre Kara, Ozan Orhan, Mehmet S. Aktas

entry.summary: An empirical comparison of semantic vector search versus delegated grep-based subagent search for repository-level code question answering, testing whether the context-isolation practice used by production coding agents actually pays off. It examines the tradeoff between context pollution and retrieval quality.

entry.title: Robust General Utility for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa, Zizhan Zheng

entry.summary: Extends general-utility reinforcement learning, where the objective is a functional of the occupancy measure, to the case where the deployment utility may differ from the training utility. The proposed minimax framework trains against an uncertainty set of utilities and unifies several existing robust RL formulations.

entry.title: Bi-semantic Chemical Embedder for Joint Representation Learning of SMILES and Natural Language

author.name: David Ming Segura, Jeremy Goumaz, Joshua W. Sin, Bojana Rankovi\'c, Philippe Schwaller

entry.summary: CheMatE is a ModernBERT-based embedding model trained to place molecular SMILES strings and chemistry-domain natural language in a shared representation space, using continued masked language modeling followed by Matryoshka contrastive learning. The design targets the catastrophic forgetting of language ability that afflicts chemistry-adapted models.

entry.title: ARCHead: Activation-Metric Residual Correction for Large Language Model Output Heads

author.name: \c{S}uayp Talha Kocabay, Talha R\"uzgar Akku\c{s}, Kamer Ali Yuksel

entry.summary: ARCHead compresses the language-modeling head, which backends usually leave in half precision, using a quantized low-rank core, group-wise INT4 residuals, and an activation-metric low-rank correction. On Qwen3-8B-Base it uses 25.6 percent of the half-precision head storage at 1.007 relative perplexity, versus 1.14 to 1.16 for storage-matched naive INT4.

entry.title: DAIF: A Data-Driven Intermediate Fusion Framework for Multimodal Supervised Learning via Approximate Message Passing

author.name: Sagnik Nandy, Samriddha Lahiry, Pragya Sur, Subhabrata Sen

entry.summary: DAIF learns the appropriate fusion granularity across modalities from data instead of fixing early or late fusion, using random matrix theory and non-parametric dependence measures under a Bayesian multimodal factor model. Approximate message passing supplies the analysis machinery.

entry.title: CVPO: Enhancing LLM Reinforcement Learning Reasoning via Value-Variance Adaptation and Dynamic Curriculum Learning

author.name: Ziqi Jia, Yalu Ouyang, Bo Pang, Panpan Li, Hangfei Xu, Shengzhao Wen, Shiyong Li, Yanpeng Wang

entry.summary: CVPO improves RL for LLM reasoning by using token-level value-variance as a proxy for exploration intensity to adjust advantages, together with a dynamic curriculum that counters problem difficulty drift during training. The authors give theoretical analysis bounding policy update magnitude by this variance.

entry.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility

author.name: Jo-Ku Cheng, Nikolaos Aletras, Marco Valentino

entry.summary: Proposes pre-pretraining language models on formal logical derivations, arguing these require variable binding and abstract composition that better prefigure natural language than prior symbolic tasks such as Dyck languages or procedural algorithms. Studies skill emergence and representational compressibility over larger token budgets than earlier work. Speaks to curriculum design and inductive bias in pretraining.

entry.title: SPADE: An Input-Adaptive Sparse Attention Engine for Fast Video Diffusion Models Inference

author.name: Shanghao Liu (Eric), Renze Chen (Eric), Size Zheng (Eric), Yuanqiang Liu (Eric), Yun (Eric), Liang, Hailong Yang

entry.summary: SPADE is a training-free sparse attention engine for video diffusion transformers that generates input-adaptive block-sparse masks at runtime and executes them with low-overhead index search and fused kernels. It is evaluated across several open video generation models for text-to-video and image-to-video.

entry.title: When Do Fewer Visual Tokens Accelerate Multimodal Inference? A Break-Even Study Across Decision Locations and Hardware

author.name: Hao Dou, Ruiwen Tian

entry.summary: An empirical study of when reducing visual tokens actually lowers end-to-end latency in multimodal models, accounting for decision overhead and shared computation across two GPU classes. The finding is that several popular pruning-style policies do not beat the full-token baseline once real timing is measured, while a lightweight post-vision predictor does yield reliable gains.

entry.title: OmniPack: Unified Token Compression for Efficient Omni-modal Large Language Models

author.name: Wanshun Su, Yang Shi, Feihu Liu, Ziwen Yu, Yan Min, Zhuoran Zhang, Qixun Wang, Haotian Wang, Shixuan Liu, Yuanxing Zhang, Peng Wu, Chengfu Huo, Liang Ding

entry.summary: OmniPack is a training-free token compression framework for omni-modal LLMs that applies structural compression to audio and video tokens before the language model and query-conditioned semantic refinement inside it. The two-stage split is meant to avoid losing globally distributed evidence at aggressive token budgets.

entry.title: FakeI2V-Bench: Benchmarking the Applicability of Image-level Deepfake Detectors for Deepfake Video Detection

author.name: Pei Li, Sihan Chen, Delong Ran, Tianshuo Cong

entry.summary: FakeI2V-Bench is a benchmark of roughly 97,500 videos from recent generation models built to test whether image-level deepfake detectors transfer to video and how video-level detectors hold up in harder settings. It fills a gap where video deepfake evaluation lags behind rapidly improving generators.

entry.title: Caved or Convinced: Temporal Sampling Gates Claim Deference in Video Large Language Models

author.name: Yuxin Cao, Wei Song, Jingling Xue, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: This study separates two conflated causes of sycophancy in video language models when judging event order: whether the sampled frames even contain the evidence (availability) and whether the model trusts that evidence over the user's claim (weighting). Frame reordering and sampling-offset interventions isolate the two, showing that mitigations which merely teach distrust of users can worsen rejection of true claims.

entry.title: MuEvo: LLM-Driven Evolution of Multi-Heuristic Ensemble

author.name: Haoze Lv, Ning Lu, Shengcai Liu, Shaofeng Zhang, Ke Tang

entry.summary: MuEvo extends LLM-driven automated heuristic design from evolving a single heuristic to evolving an ensemble of interacting components, using short-budget probing with a reversible lifecycle so promising components are not prematurely discarded. Feedback is applied at the ensemble level to capture inter-component dependencies.

entry.title: Passively Safe Convex Guidance for Cislunar Rendezvous and Proximity Operations

author.name: Ian M. Down, Connor Plaks, Matthew Bolliger, Michael Caudill

entry.summary: This paper formulates purely convex programs for passively safe impulsive rendezvous, approach, arrival, and abort maneuvers in cislunar near-rectilinear halo orbits under navigation uncertainty and execution error. The methods form the baseline onboard guidance for a planned NASA autonomous rendezvous demonstration mission, verified through high-fidelity closed-loop Monte Carlo simulation.

entry.title: Tired Actor: Fatigue-Informed Character Control

author.name: Shengyuan Zhang, Xinpeng Liu, Muchun Niu, Yulong Chen, Lizhuang Ma, Yue Gao, Cewu Lu, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: Tired Actor injects fatigue as a proxy for finite metabolic energy into physics-based character control, arguing that controllers assuming unlimited energy produce subtly unnatural motion. It studies how fatigue shapes motion style, strategy, and imitation quality across general animation tasks.

entry.title: CURE: Local Uncertainty Repair for Block-Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: CURE improves block-parallel speculative decoding by observing that draft errors concentrate at a few high-uncertainty tokens that destabilize the rest of the block, then applying a budget-aware dynamic repair tree that adds verification branches only at those focal points. This raises acceptance rates without incurring the cost of full tree verification. The result is better wall-clock speedup for autoregressive inference.

entry.title: PROGRESS: Coverage-guided RL to Train Search-augmented LLM Agent

author.name: Sudipta Paul, Vijay Srinivasan, Vivek Kulkarni, Aounon Kumar, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Wenbo Li, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: PROGRESS trains search-augmented agents with a teacher-guided coverage reward that explicitly shapes query decomposition, addressing the weak supervision that outcome-only rewards give to search behavior. Frozen teacher models decompose complex queries into essential subqueries used to guide the policy's search within an R1-style RL framework. The aim is better multi-step retrieval rather than just better final answers.

entry.title: Inter-Residue Geometry Attention for Antibody-Specific Epitope Prediction

author.name: Chuanliu Fan, Nan Yu, Junjie Wu, Guohong Fu

entry.summary: Introduces local-frame 3D rotary position encoding so that folded residue geometry, rather than sequence order, drives attention positions for antibody-specific epitope prediction. Removes the need for separate graph or point-cloud structure encoders.

entry.title: When Memory Updates but Behavior Does Not: Repairing Implicit Stale Dependencies in Personalized Agent Responses

author.name: Haofei Sun, Lin He

entry.summary: Tackles the case where an agent's memory is updated but its behavior still plans around stale values, noting draft-anchored checks miss unsaid dependencies. StateAuditor instead audits from stored state to draft, verifying provenance and chronology of proposed old-to-new transitions before repair.

entry.title: FRAMES: Guarded and Dual-Objective Skill Evolution for Agents in Policy-Governed Enterprise Workflows

author.name: Xuhui Wang, Ruoqi Shu, Chen Dan, Tianhua Xu, Mengxi Luo, Yanming Mai, Bo Wan

entry.summary: FRAMES evolves agent skills for policy-bound enterprise document auditing using consensus-based mutation, Pareto selection over accuracy and inference cost, and an anti-regression guarantee, all under sparse unlabeled operational feedback. Reported deployed in an internal production system.

entry.title: EchoChange: A Diffusion Language Model with Dual Pass Remasking for Factual Remote Sensing Disaster Change Captioning

author.name: Dongwei Sun, Bowen Yao, Yujie Zhang, Pei Liu, Jing Yao, Xiangyong Cao

entry.summary: EchoChange applies a multimodal discrete diffusion language model with dual-pass remasking to bi-temporal remote sensing change captioning, so early misinterpretations can be revised rather than propagating. Targets cascading factual errors in autoregressive change descriptions.

entry.title: Wnuan: Staged Post-Training for Question Answering over Proprietary Enterprise Knowledge

author.name: Xiaofeng Shi, Xiaosong Qiu, Wenxin Ma, Qian Kou, Yiming Pan, Longbin Yu, Ying Liu, Haiping Wang, Hua Zhou

entry.summary: Wnuan is a three-stage enterprise QA pipeline that builds supervision from internal documents, fine-tunes with general-data replay to limit forgetting, then applies RL focused on residual errors. Reports acceptable-answer rate rising from about 53 percent to 92 percent on a 707-question internal benchmark.

entry.title: SkillTrace: Traversing a Query-Skill Graph for Composable LLM Agents

author.name: Yue Yao, Shengyuan Wang, Xin Chen, Minke Zhang, Jia He, Bingjun Luo, Tom Gedeon

entry.summary: SkillTrace frames skill selection for composable LLM agents as traversal of a three-level graph capturing compositional relations among sub-queries, query-to-candidate similarity, and dependencies among selected skills. Reports state-of-the-art composition results on SkillsBench and ALFWorld.

entry.title: RubricReviewer: From Direct Critique to Objective and Comprehensive Rubric-Driven Peer Review

author.name: Shuyu Guo, Wenxiang Hu, Yuyue Zhao, Yougang Lyu, Xiaohui Yan

entry.summary: RubricReviewer makes rubric generation an explicit intermediate step in automated peer review, separating criterion derivation from judgment to avoid both the undirected critiques of training-free agents and the inherited noise of imitation-trained reviewers. Aims for more objective and comprehensive reviews under submission pressure.

entry.title: MemoryForge: Synthesize Lifelong Memory for Human-Like LLM Agents

author.name: Bohan Tang, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: MemoryForge replaces static persona prompts with synthesized autobiographical memory bases, so frozen LLMs retrieve situation-relevant life memories to drive behavior in role-play and user simulation. Formalizes customized lifelong memory synthesis as the enabling task.

entry.title: SLMs as Multi-Agent Routers: A Progressive SFT and Reinforcement Learning Approach

author.name: Gayathri V Kondapalli, Alexander Ng, Hirsh Pithadia, Rahul Monish, Harvey Yorke, Amir Kayhani

entry.summary: Trains a small language model with progressive supervised fine-tuning then reinforcement learning to jointly select among specialized retrieval agents and generate structured tool-call parameters, rewarded by retrieval relevance plus query-agent topic alignment. Argues intent-based routing is insufficient because it ignores signal from retrieved content.

entry.title: Trustworthiness Costs of Domain Adaptation in Small Language Models:A Cross-Architecture Empirical Study

author.name: Ramesh B. Paramkusham

entry.summary: Measures how domain adaptation of small language models affects factual calibration and adversarial robustness across three architectures (TinyLlama 1B, Gemma-2 2B, Llama 3.2 1B), three high-stakes domains, and benign versus adversarial training data. Frames the results as a trustworthiness cost accompanying well-documented performance gains.

entry.title: Element-Aware Group Learning for E-Commerce Image Generation

author.name: Jingtong Chen, Jiahui Wang, Xue Zhao, ShaoGuo Liu, Minghao Li

entry.summary: This work improves VLM-written image-editing prompts for e-commerce creatives by giving GRPO fine-grained credit at the level of design elements such as composition, background, and selling-point presentation, rather than only at the full-prompt level. It avoids the step-level supervision or learned critics that other fine-grained credit-assignment methods require.

entry.title: Stress-Relief Annealing: Polynomial-Time Simulation-Free Layout Optimization for Automated Warehouses

author.name: Xiangjie Luo, Yulun Zhang, Miyuki Koshimura, Makoto Yokoo, Jiaoyang Li

entry.summary: Stress-Relief Annealing optimizes automated warehouse layouts in polynomial time using a simulation-free objective, replacing evolutionary black-box search that requires enormous numbers of simulations. It targets throughput for fleets of hundreds to thousands of coordinating robots.

entry.title: PICTURE: Enhancing Theory-of-Mind in Large Language Models by Revealing, Not Hiding, Characters' Lack of Knowledge

author.name: Eojin Jeon, SangKeun Lee

entry.summary: PICTURE improves theory-of-mind reasoning in LLMs by generating free-form perspective-taking explanations that explicitly reveal what a character does not know, instead of the standard approach of deleting unknown events before question answering. It addresses the format rigidity that makes event hiding degrade performance.

entry.title: Recompute or Reuse? Diagnosing and Mitigating Textual Shortcuts in VLM Self-Reflection

author.name: Wenxiao Fan, Jingling Fu, Fang Li, Luohang Liu, Yu He, Lichen Ma, Zhiyang Yu, Weishan Bi, Junshi Huang, Yan Li, Gu Simiu, Kan Li

entry.summary: Across sixteen vision-language models, matched counterfactual analysis shows that evidence-bearing statements in a prior chain of thought act as a textual shortcut that competes with recomputing from the current image, explaining failures to revise reasoning when visual input changes. Removing that evidence content shifts answers more than removing length-matched filler or the previous final answer.

entry.title: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning

author.name: Yiran Gao, Tao Li, Kim Hammar

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic incident-response system that couples LLM security knowledge with digital-twin simulation and multiscale planning, so response plans can be validated against an operational system replica rather than an abstract model. Targets the gap between decision-theoretic security automation and deployable playbook replacement.

entry.title: Wiring Beats Blending: What Transfers Between Transformer Sizes -- and What Doesn't

author.name: Ravi Satya Durga Prasad Yenugula

entry.summary: Characterizes end-to-end whether a pretrained 1.4B Pythia model can be converted into a 410M sibling, finding that representations align well across sizes while parameters do not, and that dense weight projection is functionally destructive because basis mixing breaks rotary, per-head, GELU, and LayerNorm structure. Concludes that conversion value resides in initialization, decomposed into least-squares wiring versus blending under matched continued-pretraining budgets.

entry.title: Trajectory-Guided Forget-Recover Network for Continual LLM Unlearning

author.name: Zezheng Wu, Xinghe Cheng, Qinggang Zhang, Haoran Luo, Jiapu Wang, Qing Yang, Jingwei Zhang

entry.summary: TFR-Net targets continual LLM unlearning, where sequential removal requests can push forgotten knowledge into alternative pathways and repeated interventions erode retained capability. It tracks channel-level risk across requests, suppresses only persistently target-related channels, and recovers capacity to preserve utility.

entry.title: Stuck on "A": Diagnosing and Repairing Interface Injury in Attention-to-KDA Linearization of a 0.6B Language Model

author.name: Ronglong Bao

entry.summary: Converts 21 of 28 attention layers in Qwen3-0.6B-Base to Kimi Delta Attention linear layers on a consumer GPU and diagnoses what breaks: perplexity and KL match the teacher closely, yet multiple-choice accuracy falls to chance. A four-permutation diagnostic reveals the student latches onto answer labels, predicting the letter A 81 percent of the time, an interface failure invisible to standard distillation losses.

entry.title: Adversarial Fast-Moving Real-World Domains as Test Beds for Benchmarking AI Scientist Capabilities

author.name: William Bolton, Philip Torr

entry.summary: Argues that fast-moving adversarial real-world domains, where expert practitioners independently produce observable outputs, are better test beds for AI-scientist ideation than synthetic or retrospective benchmarks that risk prior exposure. The framework is instantiated in Formula 1 car-design ideation and a second structurally different domain. Addresses contamination and confounding in AI-for-science evaluation.

entry.title: Evaluating OpenAI's Privacy Filter: Cross-Lingual, Cross-Domain PII Detection Across 42 Benchmarks

author.name: Rohith Uppala

entry.summary: An independent evaluation of OpenAI's Privacy Filter, a 1.5B bidirectional PII detector released earlier in 2026, across 42 synthetic benchmarks in 22 languages and 5 domains. It leads on structured synthetic PII but degrades sharply when PII is embedded in narrative prose and collapses on non-Latin scripts, where XLM-RoBERTa wins on all 13 Indic and non-Latin languages, and GPT-4o leads on medical, legal, and financial PII. Useful third-party accountability data for a deployed safety component.

entry.title: Speculative Correction: Draft-then-Refine Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Brian K Chen, Chong Wu, Kenji Kawaguchi

entry.summary: Explores a plug-and-play inference pattern for diffusion language models: generate a complete draft, then use bidirectional diffusion to refine the whole response globally, including a speculative-correction variant where a small model drafts and a larger one revises. Evaluated on LLaDA2.1 Flash and Mini. Exploits the editing capability that distinguishes diffusion LMs from autoregressive decoding.

entry.title: FACTWASH: Catching AI Rewrites That Wash Hearsay into Fact

author.name: Alex Kwon

entry.summary: FACTWASH targets factwashing, where AI rewriting preserves a claim while stripping attribution, hedging, and temporal scope that made it checkable. The authors release a deterministic write-time gate with named flags, and analyze when cheap surface-cue detectors suffice versus when a model-based judge is required.

entry.title: DiverseDiT++: Quantifying, Analyzing, and Promoting Representation Diversity in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Binglei Li, Mengping Yang, Zhiyu Tan, Xiaomeng Yang, Zhizhong Huang, Junping Zhang, Hao Li

entry.summary: DiverseDiT++ introduces a weighted diversity score to quantify how block-wise internal representations differ across diffusion transformer layers, then uses the analysis to promote representation diversity. It aims to explain and extend representation-alignment approaches such as external-encoder alignment.

entry.title: EmbodiedVAE: Disentangled Video VAE for Efficient and Controllable Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Jiayi Luo, Hanxin Zhu, Chen Gao, Jiankun Wang, Cong Wang, Tianyu He, Jianxin Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: EmbodiedVAE argues that video autoencoders tuned for natural scenes yield latents that are neither compact nor controllable for manipulation world models, and proposes a dual-encoder video VAE that disentangles representations for robotic scenes. The intended payoff is cheaper latent diffusion world model training and more precise control.

entry.title: EvoHIL: Self-Evolving Reward and Flow-Matched Policy Optimization for Robust Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shuoqin Zhang, Tongtong Cheng, Xiru Gao, Jinzhuo Peng, Bin Zheng, Jiahao Tu, Ke Wang, Jia Pan, Zhe Hu, Kai Liu

entry.summary: EvoHIL is a human-in-the-loop RL framework for contact-rich manipulation that simultaneously adapts the reward model, the action generator and the visual domain during real-world learning. Components include a self-evolving success classifier trained from human-confirmed positives and weak negatives, plus flow-based generation of temporally coherent action chunks.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Reasoning with Incremental Knowledge for Sample Efficient Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Subrat Prasad Panda, Blaise Genest, Arvind Easwaran

entry.summary: Proposes neurosymbolic hierarchical RL in which symbolic high-level planning uses knowledge that is incrementally updated during exploration, rather than fixed knowledge baked into the architecture. The goal is better sample efficiency in sparse-reward, long-horizon tasks where symbolic knowledge is initially incomplete.

entry.title: H+ Embedding: Harmonizing Global and Token-Level Retrieval with Context-Dependent Phrases

author.name: Shusen Zhang, Junyi Hu, Ye Feng, Ziteng Wang, Zhaoyuan Pan, Guosheng Dong, Xiaojun Yuan, Jiangshou Hong, Xiangzhi Wang

entry.summary: H+ Embedding proposes a retrieval representation at an intermediate granularity between single global vectors and full token-level late interaction, learning variable-length context-dependent phrase partitions with leftover tokens kept as singletons and importance-guided unit selection. It targets terminology-heavy domains such as medicine where multi-word entities, abbreviations, and numerical constraints must be preserved. The approach aims for late-interaction quality at lower index and scoring cost.

entry.title: F-WANDA: Fisher-Reweighted Post-Training Pruning for Sustainable Deployment of Large Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Mishra (University of British Columbia)

entry.summary: F-WANDA modifies the WANDA one-shot pruning criterion by reallocating the per-row keep budget across output neurons in proportion to empirical Fisher information of pre-activations, collected in a single extra backward pass with no weight updates. At 50 percent unstructured sparsity on Llama-2-7B it reports WikiText-2 perplexity of 6.85 and MMLU gains of 1.6 points over WANDA and 1.1 over SparseGPT at roughly a third of the compute. It positions itself as an energy-frugal compression drop-in.

entry.title: TaPR: Test-Aware Policy Refinement for Feedback-Conditioned Code Generation

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: TaPR converts execution feedback in multi-turn code agents into a dense per-turn test-pass-ratio reward, correcting the mismatch where standard RL optimizes single-shot outcome rewards and thereby conflates initial generation with subsequent repair. Evaluated on six models over 219 LiveCodeBench problems, it improves pooled three-turn success and specifically targets whether the policy learns genuine self-repair. The protocol also standardizes multi-turn interaction for evaluation.

entry.title: Search-GRT: Guided Retrieval Training of Search Agents to Optimize for Complex Question Answering

author.name: Aounon Kumar, Sudipta Paul, Vivek Kulkarni, Vijay Srinivasan, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: Guided Retrieval Training improves multi-hop question answering search agents by restricting the retrieval space during training so the policy receives denser learning signal, countering the sparse rewards and cascading errors that arise when early retrieval fails. It comes from the same industrial group as the companion PROGRESS paper. The focus is on making RL for search agents trainable rather than merely outcome-scored.

entry.title: 402Pilot: An x402 Decision Layer for Autonomous Agent Micropayments

author.name: Yin Li, Yanbo He, Boo-Ho Yang, Rav Lawana, Ziyue Li, Wei Zeng, Jing Tang, Fugee Tsung

entry.summary: 402Pilot adds a buyer-side decision layer for autonomous agents making per-request micropayments, using a payment-aware contextual Thompson-sampling policy to pick providers under wallet constraints and only observing feedback for purchases made. Formalizes agent commerce as a contextual bandit with paid feedback.

entry.title: PolymerGPT: Multi-property Optimization with a Decoder-Based GPT Model for Generative Polymer Design

author.name: Charlie Pyle, Adarsh Gadari, C. Adrian Figg, Zhenquan Jia, Yaohang Li, Chunjiang Zhu

entry.summary: PolymerGPT is a decoder-only generative model conditioned on up to 37 polymer properties simultaneously, enabling multi-property inverse design rather than single-objective optimization. Addresses the under-served generative side of ML-assisted polymer discovery.

entry.title: GISAgentBench: A Practitioner-Sourced Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Agents on GIS Tasks

author.name: Abhinav Pothuri, Zhe Jiang, Zelin Xu, Di Yang

entry.summary: GISAgentBench is a practitioner-sourced benchmark of realistic multi-step geospatial analysis workflows with actual ground-truth outputs, rather than textbook tasks scored by code similarity or trajectory matching. Enables end-to-end evaluation of GIS agents.

entry.title: MemSIF: From Structured Interactions to Dual-Track Fact Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: YuFei Luo, Xiucheng Xu, Zhen Yang

entry.summary: MemSIF organizes agent memory into topical segments plus a dual-track fact store to counter two misalignments: temporal proximity not matching topical relatedness, and write-time salience not predicting future query usefulness. Targets long-horizon interaction retrieval.

entry.title: CockpitHAT: Dependency-Graph-Driven Hierarchical Attribution for Embodied Multi-Agent Cockpits

author.name: Wei Wang, Shuanghe Liu, Zhu Zhuo, Jiaqi Zhong, Xiaozhao Zhao, Xiaojie Zuo, Jie Su

entry.summary: CockpitHAT attributes failures in embodied multi-agent automotive cockpit systems using dependency distances from interaction DAGs plus multi-channel evidence, weighting high-risk safety failures during consensus analysis. Targets correctness collapse where task-level accuracy hides dangerous process-level errors.

entry.title: Evolving in the Agent Jungle via History-Informed Opponent Awareness

author.name: Zhaofeng Zhang, Linhan Xia, Rui Liu, Yihao Wang, Binrui Shen, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces OASE, which decides whether an LLM agent skill revision is genuinely beneficial in multi-agent settings where opponents also change strategies, using paired comparisons against an opponent-aware reference rather than a stale static baseline. Addresses nonstationarity in skill-library self-improvement.

entry.title: MemArbiter: Decision-Time Memory Arbitration for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajun Dong, Yutao Hu, Fengrui Fan, Shihan Dou, Yueming Wu, Deqing Zou

entry.summary: MemArbiter names the Memory-Action Gap, where retrievable memory still fails to influence the current decision, and addresses it by decomposing histories into atomic items sorted into five functional memory banks with demand-, relevance-, and time-gated presentation. Targets coherence in long-horizon agent tasks.

entry.title: ELECTRIC: Evidential Learning-Enhanced CT Reconstruction via Iterative Correction

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: ELECTRIC is a physics-guided Bayesian CT reconstruction loop where an evidential network proposes an image plus an epistemic-uncertainty surrogate that becomes an adaptive precision field inside a Poisson-weighted MAP update. Treats prior confidence as a learned state variable, with two simulation studies on low-dose CT slices.

entry.title: Verifiable Checks for Business Rule Consistency

author.name: Joseph Tafese, Milad Hooshyar, Sam Bayless, Nick Feng, Arie Gurfinkel

entry.summary: SIRNA checks whether natural-language business-rule documentation matches evolving code implementations by having an LLM translate documentation into candidate SMT formulas, validating those translations, then verifying the implementation against them with an SMT solver. It is demonstrated on tax cost-calculation rules.

entry.title: Auditable Release Control for Pedagogical Leakage in LLM Tutors

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: This paper formalizes pedagogical leakage, where an LLM tutor discloses an answer or decisive reasoning before disclosure is authorized, and imposes a complete-mediation release boundary with five disclosure contracts, trusted gates, inspectable checks, and replayable traces separating selection, generation, verification, and enforcement failures. Component attribution on 599 fixed Gemini 3.5 proposals exposes an explicit safety-utility frontier.

entry.title: Hierarchical Solomonoff Induction: An Unbounded Machine Learning Model

author.name: Nathan Young

entry.summary: Extends Solomonoff induction with a hyperprior over Solomonoff priors via de Finetti's exchangeability theorem, producing Hierarchical Solomonoff Induction, and proves it is equivalent to standard Solomonoff induction while bounding its excess error. The goal is a theoretical model of training-then-extrapolation as done by LLMs.

entry.title: VLAGuard: A Framework for Evaluating and Mitigating Physical Attention Hijacking in Vision-Language-Action Robots within Wireless Sensor Networks

author.name: Dongfu Yin, Jinquan Zhang

entry.summary: VLAGuard introduces a printable-patch attack that hijacks the action-conditioned cross-attention of vision-language-action robots, plus an attention-protective fine-tuning defense with no inference overhead. It evaluates both in simulated and physical settings framed as edge nodes in wireless sensor networks.

entry.title: What Could the Agent See at 19:05? Generating Temporal Enterprise Scenarios from Real Research and Replaying Them to Evaluate Agents

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Himani Arora

entry.summary: Proposes generating temporal enterprise scenarios and replaying them so agents can be graded against what data existed and who could see it at each moment, rather than a single end-of-episode snapshot. It addresses time-travel and permission leakage in offline enterprise agent evaluation.

entry.title: Auditing Semantic Gains in Sequential Recommendation: A Lightweight Recovery Test

author.name: Kong Wang, Zhongke He, Xiang Chen, Hongwei Zeng, Kai Deng, Long Wang, Kehua Yang

entry.summary: LIME-Rec is a lightweight audit that fuses a sequential recommender, an item co-occurrence expert and frozen text embeddings to test whether reported gains from semantic and generative-retrieval recommenders actually require language-model reasoning. It attributes improvements to specific components rather than end-to-end architectures.

entry.title: Coding Agents as Test-Suite Auditors: Finding What Official Suites Miss While Approaching What They Catch

author.name: Shuyang Xie, Shuxiao Xie, Feng Zhu, Yanli Ji, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: The paper uses an off-the-shelf coding agent as a test-suite auditor that generates adversarial tests to expose submissions wrongly accepted by online-judge suites, plus a certification chain using agreement among independent accepted solutions to confirm real bugs without trusting the judge. It offers a practical remedy to label noise in code benchmarks and training data.

entry.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution

author.name: Shijie Ren, Xiting Wang, Meng Li, Yujie Guo, Yunhang Yao, Ziheng Peng, Xunlong Wang, Yuetan Chen, Haoyang Zhou, Yunlong Liang, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: SPEE proposes experience distillation as the missing bridge between test-time methods that extract reusable experience without changing weights and training-time optimization that changes weights without accumulating explicit experience. It progressively converts interaction experience into persistent parameter-level capability for self-improving LLMs.

entry.title: Lossless Tensor Compression as Program Synthesis

author.name: Jieke Shi (James), Junda He (James), Wenjia Jiang (James), Weifeng Sun (James), Shidong Pan (James), Zhensu Sun (James), Chengran Yang (James), Peixin Zhang (James), Yifan Jia (James), Zhou Yang (James), Thong Hoang (James), Xiwei Xu (Sherry), Zhenchang Xing, David Lo

entry.summary: Brevis formulates lossless tensor compression as program synthesis, defining a typed domain-specific language of reversible operators that capture recurring tensor structure and synthesizing a bit-exact reconstruction program per tensor, guided by a learned checkpoint-specific prior. It targets the growing archival and transfer cost of model checkpoints.

entry.title: Benign interpolation and Occam's razor

author.name: Tom F. Sterkenburg, Daniel A. Herrmann, Jan-Willem Romeijn

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-science analysis arguing that recent explanations of benign interpolation, which appeal to a simplicity bias among interpolating models, leave an explanatory gap compared with classical learning theory. It clarifies for a philosophical audience what Occam-style arguments can and cannot justify methodologically.

entry.title: A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation

author.name: Abdallah Khemais

entry.summary: Provides exact theoretical conditions under which weight-space ablation and activation patching agree about a component being causally responsible for a behavior, using an idealized additive residual-stream model. Results characterize when deleting carriers collapses matched input pairs onto identical outputs and quantify the error when conditions hold only approximately.

entry.title: Omega-S: A Functional Resilience Index for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Alberto Acedo

entry.summary: Omega-S is a regularization penalty computed only from the current weight matrix that reduces catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning, requiring no old data, Fisher information, or stored reference weights. On Llama-3-8B with LoRA it retains substantially more coding ability after prose fine-tuning than no regularization, tuned weight decay, or tuned EWC across ten seeds.

entry.title: Assessment of Conditional Diffusion Model for Synthetic Histopathology Image Generation

author.name: Seyed Kahaki, Shijie Li, Weijie Chen, Nicholas Petrick

entry.summary: Argues that FID and Inception Score are poorly suited to evaluating synthetic histopathology images because they depend on ImageNet-pretrained features, and proposes domain-specific metrics plus downstream task validation instead. The work comes from FDA-affiliated researchers assessing conditional diffusion generation for pathology.

entry.title: MemArena: An Ego-Centric Benchmark for On-Device Agentic Personal Memory Assistants at Scale

author.name: Jiadong Zhang, Xiaosong Ma

entry.summary: MemArena is a benchmark for on-device personal memory assistants built from a simulated world of 50 agents over 15 days, producing dense ego-centric multi-session interaction histories with co-generated ground truth across recall, reasoning, and trustworthiness dimensions. It evaluates five open-weight readers against several memory backends including BM25 RAG and oracle retrieval.

entry.title: DenialRAG: Single-Document RAG Poisoning via Embedded Parametric Denial

author.name: Abay Zhurekbay, Tao Liu, Fan Li

entry.summary: DenialRAG poisons a retrieval corpus with a single document that explicitly names the correct answer, refutes it, and supplies an attacker-controlled justification for the wrong answer, in contrast to prior attacks that avoid mentioning the truth. Placing both answers in the same retrieved passage embeds the conflict directly in the context.

entry.title: TQLite: Multi-LLM Jury Guided Distillation for Real-time MQM Translation Quality Evaluation

author.name: Bhavin Jawade, Cameron R. Wolfe

entry.summary: Benchmarks small, large, and reasoning models on MQM-based translation quality evaluation, then introduces TQLite, a distillation framework using a multi-LLM jury to teach small models the required evaluation reasoning. The goal is real-time quality scoring at deployment scale without paying reasoning-model inference costs.

entry.title: Stochastic Saddle Avoidance Beyond Unit Excitation and Smoothness: A Pathwise Lyapunov-Perron Framework

author.name: Junwen Qiu, Bohao Ma, Andre Milzarek, Junyu Zhang

entry.summary: Proves almost-sure avoidance of strict saddle points for stochastic recursions without the unit excitation assumption that noise be uniformly informative in every direction. This matters for interpolation regimes where noise vanishes near stationarity and finite-sum problems where gradient noise lies in a low-dimensional subspace.

entry.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?

author.name: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu, Yi Hu, Jiaqi Li, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: ContinualSkillBench evaluates whether LLM agents with external skill libraries genuinely accumulate and reuse capability, across five domains of 100 interconnected subtasks ordered by difficulty. Sequential execution helps unevenly across models and domains, and in-context learning performs comparably to explicit skill libraries. Questions the value proposition of current skill-library agent frameworks.

entry.title: OncoTriad-QA: A Patient-Level Radiology-Pathology-Genomics Benchmark for Pan-Cancer Reasoning

author.name: Ahnaf Munir, Dannong Wang, Michael W. McDonald, Mubarak Shah, Pegah Khosravi, Yu Tian

entry.summary: OncoTriad-QA is a patient-level pan-cancer benchmark with 86.1k questions over 9,281 TCGA cases, aligning CT/MRI imaging, whole-slide pathology, mutations, copy-number, methylation, RNA-seq, and clinical metadata. It tests whether medical LLMs and VLMs can integrate several evidence streams rather than answering isolated single-modality questions. Fills a real gap in clinically realistic multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: Emulate or Estimate? The Divergent Strengths of Base and Post-Trained Language Models for Opinion Simulation

author.name: Seth Grief-Albert, Jessica Bo, Difan Jiao, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: Resolves conflicting findings on LLM opinion simulation by distinguishing emulation (generating individual responses that aggregate to a distribution) from estimation (directly predicting the population distribution), evaluating six matched base and post-trained models on the Pew American Trends Panel. Base models are stronger emulators while post-trained models are better estimators. Clarifies methodology for computational social science uses of LLMs.

entry.title: GUI-Lens: Coarse-to-Fine Cropping for GUI Grounding with General-Purpose VLMs

author.name: Zichuan Fu, Shirong Wang, Wenlin Zhang, Guojing Li, Yimin Deng, Jingtong Gao, Junjia Qi, Hanyu Yan, Yefeng Zheng, Xiaopeng Li, Wanyu Wang, Xian Wu, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: GUI-Lens lets a general-purpose vision-language model ground GUI instructions through a coarse-to-fine cropping loop with OCR text and detected UI elements, instead of committing to a single direct click prediction. This prevents an inaccurate first estimate from propagating on dense high-resolution interfaces.

entry.title: StreamDAM: Presence-Aware Memory for Real-Time Streaming Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Xiang Chen

entry.summary: StreamDAM shows that accuracy-leading video object segmentation trackers collapse under an honest 30 frames per second streaming protocol where late frames are penalized, tracing the failure to slow memory pipelines and lack of object-presence awareness. It rebuilds the memory machinery to run at frame rate governed by a learned presence signal.

entry.title: When and Where to Look: Adaptive Visual Evidence Scheduling for Efficient Long Video Understanding

author.name: Ke Li, Jiayu Chen, Maoliang Li, Zihao Zheng, Hailong Zou, Hengyi Zhang, Xuanzhe Liu, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: EcoFrame is a training-free scheduler that decides how many video frames a vision-language model needs and where to look for more, using output entropy to stop early and feedback signals to expand the candidate pool. It aims for agent-like adaptivity without the cost of multi-round agentic search.

entry.title: CoT-Core: Accelerating LLM Evaluation via CoT-Aware Coreset Selection

author.name: Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang, Peijie Dong, Xiang Liu, Huacan Wang, Bo Li, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: CoT-Core is a training-free method for selecting a small representative subset of benchmark questions so LLM evaluation can be run cheaply during iterative development. Instead of lexical similarity, it clusters questions by embedding zero-shot chain-of-thought reasoning trajectories, capturing shared underlying logic and avoiding the cold-start problem of item-response-theory approaches. This targets the growing cost of continuous evaluation in model development pipelines.

entry.title: Request-Level Energy Attribution for Batched LLM Serving

author.name: Qi Luo, Kunlin Li, Ziwen Wang, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen

entry.summary: JouleShare tackles the problem that GPU power telemetry is aggregate while sustainability reporting and chargeback need per-request energy figures in batched serving. An offline replay harness under vLLM establishes measured ground truth for request-level energy, allowing the authors to quantify how far common accounting heuristics deviate from a Shapley-fair allocation. It provides the first measured baseline for evaluating attribution rules.

entry.title: Personalizing Large Language Model Agents with Small Policy Models

author.name: Dian Jin, Zhi Zhang, Huichao Li, Yihe Pan, Rundong Huang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: FABLE personalizes a frozen, possibly black-box LLM agent by learning a lightweight per-user execution policy from scalar bandit feedback, factorizing decisions about memory use, information acquisition, and response style. It avoids fine-tuning a proprietary backbone by placing a contextual bandit layer outside the host agent. This targets execution-level adaptation rather than merely surfacing user facts in the prompt.

entry.title: More Debate, Same Evidence: Structural Limits of Homogeneous Multi-Agent Groundedness

author.name: Yuelyu Ji

entry.summary: This study tests the common assumption that multi-agent judge panels improve groundedness verification, evaluating a homogeneous three-agent panel against a single-agent reference on six fact-verification and hallucination benchmarks. Accuracy differences range from plus 8.5 to minus 4.4 percentage points, with reliable gains on only two datasets, one reliable loss, and three inconclusive. The result argues that debate among similar models adds process without adding evidence.

entry.title: DGA$_2$D: Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Zimu Chen, Sirui Mao, Wentao Yang, Yuxiang Bai, Liyuanjun Lai

entry.summary: DGA2D structures the open-ended program space for LLM-driven automated heuristic design as a directed graph where nodes are functional components, aiming to move beyond rigid solver templates toward system-level algorithm design for NP-hard problems. The graph structure is intended to address unreliable generated operators, huge search spaces, and poor credit assignment. It follows the FunSearch and evolutionary program-search lineage.

entry.title: Assuming You Knew: Fixing an Epistemic Semantics for Flow Policies Using Agentic AI

author.name: David A. Naumann

entry.summary: This paper corrects and machine-checks in the Rocq proof assistant an epistemic semantics for information flow policies with selective downgrading, repairing a formalization from a 2018 security conference paper that was acknowledged as flawed. Notably, the corrected proof development was produced with the aid of an agentic AI coding assistant. It doubles as a case study in AI-assisted formal verification of security semantics.

entry.title: Modeling Social Dynamics with an LLM-Enabled Agent Based Network-Dynamic (LAND) Model

author.name: Lynnette Hui Xian Ng, Kathleen M. Carley

entry.summary: The LAND model couples LLM-driven agents with network dynamics to simulate large-scale social behavior, instantiated in a scenario where 314,244 heterogeneous cyber-social and human agents exchange 529,327 messages over 30 days around a fictional contest. The authors analyze emergent dynamics across ego-network topology, semantic network evolution, coordination, and influence. It is a methodological demonstration of LLM-enabled social simulation at scale.

entry.title: Agentic Stage-One Stellarator Optimization: Autonomous Multi-Objective Search for Finite-Beta Equilibria

author.name: Tingjia Zhang, Hongke Lu, Zhuoran Meng, Runlai Xu

entry.summary: An agentic system autonomously orchestrates stage-one stellarator design, coordinating multi-objective optimization over 3D plasma boundaries and finite-beta MHD equilibria including resolution and objective-priority choices. Aims to raise design throughput beyond expert-driven iteration.

entry.title: Computing with Agentic Oracles

author.name: Jie Wang

entry.summary: Extends stochastic-oracle Turing machine theory to agentic oracles that pursue goals and touch environments, distinguishing orchestration token costs visible to the caller from hidden agentic token costs. Provides a complexity-style accounting framework for AI-augmented computation.

entry.title: Constructing Executable Analytical Knowledge Representations for Meta-Analysis Synthesis Using an Agentic Harness

author.name: Lingbo Li, Anuradha Mathrani, Teo Susnjak

entry.summary: Proposes an Executable Analytical Knowledge Representation that makes meta-analysis decisions such as effect-size formulation, outcome alignment, and admissibility explicit and independently verifiable rather than hidden in generated code or model outputs. Implemented via an agentic harness.

entry.title: HALT: Verification-Aware Stopping for Retrieval-Augmented Search Agents

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: HALT is a lightweight stopping policy for retrieval-augmented search agents that halts when accumulated evidence covers the expected hop claims, instead of relying on generator confidence. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks it cuts redundant retrieval while mostly preserving exact-match accuracy.

entry.title: Self-Certification of Representation Adequacy: Sequential Certification at Minimum Task Loss

author.name: Zijie Huang

entry.summary: Develops a four-layer theory of whether an agent can certify from its own transcript that its compressed state representation is adequate for optimal action, showing an irreducible per-round loss when the representation aliases histories requiring different actions. Prices external verification via a total-variation threshold and casts certification as optimal stopping in task-loss currency.

entry.title: AgentMemBench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Management Strategies in Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Ahmed Cherif

entry.summary: AgentMemBench compares five long-term memory strategies for conversational agents (context windowing, external key-value store, graph episodic memory, summarization, web-augmented memory) under identical conditions on LoCoMo, MultiDoc2Dial, and MSC. Reports retrieval, answer quality, faithfulness, footprint, and cost metrics together.

entry.title: SPARC-Rad: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset and Evaluation Pipeline for Spatial and Anatomical Reasoning in Radiology Vision-Language Models

author.name: Satvik Tripathi, Mustafa Ege Seker, Kristian Quevada, Ebubechukwu D Enwerem, Pratham Khandelwal, Emine Meltem, Bera Koca, Shahriar Faghani, Jacinta Arnold, Dania Daye, Tessa S. Cook

entry.summary: SPARC-Rad is a manually curated benchmark of 300 radiologist-authored image-question pairs from healthy-control CT, MRI, and radiography studies, targeting spatial and anatomical reasoning rather than disease classification or report generation. It fills a gap in medical vision-language evaluation where existing benchmarks reward pattern recall over geometric and anatomical grounding.

entry.title: Counting the Cost of War Under Satellite Embargo: Zero-Shot Estimation of Impacted Infrastructure

author.name: Saleh Sakib Ahmed, M. Sohel Rahman

entry.summary: This work estimates conflict-damaged buildings without post-strike satellite imagery by having LLMs extract weapon payload data from incident reports, projecting blast radii via Hopkinson-Cranz scaling onto archival maps, then counting exposed structures with adaptive field-of-view segmentation and pseudo-height estimation. It offers a workaround when imagery blackouts block humanitarian damage assessment.

entry.title: ORCA: ORgan-Centroid Aggregation for Training-Free 3D CT Visual Token Compression

author.name: Renjie Liang, Zijian Xu, Jinqian Pan, Chengkun Sun, Zhengkang Fan, Shawn Li, You Qin, Mei Liu, Jie Xu

entry.summary: ORCA is a training-free visual token compressor for 3D CT input to vision-language models that merges adjacent tokens using organ segmentation guidance and adds sinusoidal encodings of each region's centroid to retain spatial layout. It replaces grid-average pooling, which can blend lesion, organ, and air into a single token.

entry.title: Tensor Probabilistic Model Checking of Finite-Horizon Markov Chains (Extended Version)

author.name: Jianlin Li, Nick Guo, Peter Ye, Yizhou Zhang

entry.summary: The paper recasts step-bounded reachability verification of Markov chains as dense tensor computation, proves the mapping sound, and implements it so off-the-shelf compiler toolchains can run the verification on GPUs and other accelerators. It targets the dense-transition regime where sparse symbolic and explicit representations scale poorly.

entry.title: Pretrain on Small Synthetic Data, Scale Large for Free: Symmetry-Aware Foundation Model for Logic Rule Induction

author.name: Yin Jun Phua

entry.summary: This work builds a symmetry-respecting foundation model for logical rule induction, adding a canonical export that decodes a discrete DNF rule from literal scores and is exactly equivariant to atom renaming, example order, polarity flips, and label swaps. Enforcing these symmetries lets a model pretrained on small synthetic schemas generalize to larger unseen schemas without retraining.

entry.title: CeQe: Grounding Lexical Retrieval in Semantic Evidence

author.name: Adam Kahirov, Umesh Deshpande, Swaminathan Sundararaman

entry.summary: CE-QE expands BM25 queries with terms that a cross-encoder, applied to top semantic search results, treats as decisive according to its per-token relevance attributions. Unlike classical pseudo-relevance feedback that recycles BM25's own possibly wrong top hits, expansion is seeded from semantic retrieval, letting lexical search cross the vocabulary gap.

entry.title: RadYOLO: Computationally Efficient 3D Object Detection and Segmentation in CT and MRI

author.name: Kai Geissler, Laurens M\"uller-Groh, Hans Meine

entry.summary: RadYOLO adapts YOLO11 to 3D medical volumes for joint detection and segmentation, and is compared against nnU-Net and nnDetection on five CT and MRI datasets. It beats nnDetection on four of five datasets and is stronger on lesion detection than nnU-Net while running fast on resource-constrained hardware.

entry.title: Coverage-Driven Adaptive Keyframe Selection for Video Understanding

author.name: Junyang Zhang, Puhan Luo, Chen Tang, Yuxi Shi, Xiang-Yang Li

entry.summary: CSES is a training-free keyframe selector for long-video understanding that adaptively decides how many frames to score and how many to keep, by estimating how peaked the frame-query relevance profile is rather than scoring hundreds or thousands of frames uniformly. It cuts vision-language model inference cost while preserving query-relevant coverage.

entry.title: Less Is More: Tuning Configurable Systems with Imperfect Fidelity

author.name: Yulong Ye, Miqing Li, Tao Chen

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a less-can-be-more effect in configuration tuning: spending part of the budget measuring in a cheaper, imperfect-fidelity environment that merely resembles the target environment substantially improves final tuning quality per unit cost. The authors codify a conceptual fidelity framework for configurable systems to explain and exploit this.

entry.title: Who Belongs in the Eval Set? A Capability-Taxonomy-Driven Pipeline for Curating Regression Eval Sets in Agent-Extensibility Platforms

author.name: Tezan Sahu, Aritra Das, Pankaj Mittal, Sudipta Das

entry.summary: Describes an industrial pipeline for curating platform-side regression evaluation sets for agent extensibility surfaces in Microsoft 365 Copilot, projecting incoming customer eval queries into a capability taxonomy under a hard query-count budget. It formalizes a curation problem that existing customer-side eval frameworks ignore.

entry.title: KING: Embodiment-Aware Kinematic Graph Neural Network for Unified Motion Representation of Legged and Wheeled Robots

author.name: Taku Okawara, Aoki Takanose, Kenji Koide, Shuji Oishi, Masashi Yokozuka

entry.summary: KING is a graph neural network kinematic model that encodes robot embodiment structure (joints, wheels, feet) as a graph so a single learned motion model transfers across legged and wheeled platforms. It improves odometry in feature-poor environments where visual sensing and IMU integration fail.

entry.title: DynActiveGS: Active Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Hongbo Duan, Pengting Luo, Chengzhi Zhao, Yuanhao Chiang, Fangming Liu, Xueqian Wang

entry.summary: DynActiveGS performs active 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction in dynamic scenes by explicitly separating structural uncertainty from motion-induced uncertainty, then using those fields for viewpoint selection and path planning. It suppresses motion-corrupted observations during autonomous exploration.

entry.title: When Replanning Becomes the Bottleneck: Budgeted Replanning for Embodied Agents
