Provides quantitative comparison of tactical options in an underexplored game.

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI

author.name: Taye Akinrele, Sindhuja Penchala, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: Survey organizing the cognitive shortcomings of generative and agentic AI into five dimensions: persistent state modeling, goal-directed autonomy, self-monitoring and control, environment interaction, and learning and adaptation. Intended as a taxonomy-driven map of what still blocks reliable long-horizon operation.

entry.title: AiFlow: Token-Native Reactive Orchestration with Bounded Backpressure for Streaming LLM Applications

author.name: Qunhui Zhang

entry.summary: AiFlow proposes a token-native reactive orchestration model that normalizes provider streaming deltas into typed events flowing through a directed graph, with per-node guardians enforcing queue bounds, worker concurrency, ordering, overflow policy, cancellation propagation, and retry discipline. It replaces ad hoc callback code for backpressure in streaming LLM applications.

entry.title: Loanword or Switch? The Annotation Boundary, Not the Model, Drives Kazakh-Russian Code-Switching Identification

author.name: Bogdan Savelyev

entry.summary: This paper shows that off-the-shelf language identification and letter heuristics over-report Kazakh-Russian code-switching because integrated Russian loanwords in shared Cyrillic script look like switches. The authors release a document-level gold LID set whose guidelines keep borrowings as Kazakh, plus a mixed-only sentiment pool, and show across six approaches that the bottleneck is the annotation boundary rather than model class.

entry.title: FedCARE: A Multi-Objective Personalised Federated Learning Framework for Smart Healthcare

author.name: Rojalini Tripathy, Padmalochan Bera, Shreya Ghosh, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: FedCARE personalizes federated learning for hospitals that pursue different and sometimes conflicting clinical objectives while holding partially non-overlapping feature sets. It combines multi-objective optimization with personalization rather than assuming a single shared global objective.

entry.title: Amortized Interventional Forecasting for Multivariate CIR Processes

author.name: Andreas Sauter, Sumit Sourabh, Drona Kandhai, Erman Acar

entry.summary: Proposes an amortized model that predicts multi-horizon responses to external shocks in multivariate mean-reverting financial processes without per-scenario retraining, plus a causal generative process for benchmarking. The point is that standard correlated CIR models cannot answer interventional questions.

entry.title: CRS-Triage: Confidence- and Reliability-Aware Selective Triage under Incomplete Clinical Evidence

author.name: Guan Qiang, Yushen Chen, Tianlong Liu, David Rotenberg, Ethan H. Kim, Fang Fang

entry.summary: CRS-Triage predicts emergency department acuity from incomplete and unreliable EHR data while emitting a confidence score, deferring cases below a threshold to clinicians. It explicitly accounts for evidence reliability as well as predictive confidence.

entry.title: A Direct Route to Markov Chain Convergence via Asymptotic Equivalence with the Target

author.name: Patrick Forr\'e

entry.summary: Gives a self-contained proof of the Markov chain convergence theorem via a criterion the author calls asymptotic equivalence with the target, based on singular masses in Lebesgue decompositions vanishing in both directions. The criterion is shown necessary and sufficient on countably generated spaces and verified in several general cases. Foundational probability theory with implications for MCMC analysis.

entry.title: How Many Labels Are Enough? ALDA: Active Learning Deployment Advisor for Medical Image Classification

author.name: Julia Machnio, Mads Nielsen, Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi

entry.summary: ALDA helps practitioners choose an active-learning strategy before committing an annotation budget, by fitting parametric learning curves during a short pilot phase and predicting whether and when each strategy reaches a clinical performance target. Framed around the real risk that a poorly chosen AL strategy raises rather than lowers labeling cost. Deployment-oriented contribution for medical imaging projects.

entry.title: ANCHOR-RE: An Agentic Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Grounded Biomedical Relation Extraction

author.name: Shufan Ming, Yikun Han, Gibong Hong, Rui Zhang, Halil Kilicoglu

entry.summary: ANCHOR-RE combines ontology-guided reasoning, external knowledge grounding, and data-driven verification rules with LLM inference for biomedical relation extraction, aiming to keep symbolic precision while gaining LLM contextual recall. Evaluated on SemRepGS, DDI, and ChemProt with both proprietary and open-weight models, plus generalization tests beyond the benchmarks. Relevant to automated biomedical knowledge base construction.

entry.title: NanoMorph-3D: An End-to-End Physics-Driven Unrolling Framework for Nanomaterial Reconstruction

author.name: Beiyuan Zhang, Hesong Li, Ziqi Wu, Ruiwen Shao, Ying Fu

entry.summary: NanoMorph-3D is an end-to-end unrolled physics-driven network for 3D nanomaterial reconstruction from electron tomography, tackling the missing-wedge problem and heavy noise. It trains on a large synthetic dataset that models nonlinear electron attenuation and organizes shapes by a nanomorphological taxonomy.

entry.title: When Oracle Conditioning Misleads Deployment: Conditioning-Availability Bias in Echocardiographic Segmentation

author.name: Dang P. M. Cao, Hieu D. Pham, Hieu Pham

entry.summary: This paper shows that phase-conditioned cardiac ultrasound segmentation models trained and evaluated with clean oracle auxiliary signals can fail badly when only estimated signals are available at deployment, a protocol-level form of shortcut learning. It proposes paired gap measurements plus deployment-aware checkpoint selection and phase perturbation testing.

entry.title: Towards Reliable and Reproducible Fetal Brain Biometry: A Deep Learning Approach Using MRI

author.name: Francesca Maccarone, Marina Di Stefano, Giorgio Longari, Giulia Frigerio, Gloria Rizzato, Rocco Prudentino, Nivedita Agarwal, Tommaso Ciceri, Denis Peruzzo, Simone Melzi

entry.summary: A fully automated four-stage deep learning pipeline extracts fetal brain biometric measurements from super-resolution reconstructed 3D MRI, jointly predicting distances and the anatomical landmarks that define them. Interpretable landmark output is intended to make automated measurements auditable against manual clinical practice.

entry.title: A Wearable Stiffness-Rendering Haptic Device with a Honeycomb Jamming Mechanism for Bilateral Teleoperation

author.name: Thomas M. Kwok, Bohan Zhang, Wai Tuck Chow

entry.summary: The HJ-Haptic is a 20 gram wearable device using a honeycomb jamming mechanism under vacuum to render object stiffness between roughly 1.15 and 2.64 newtons per millimeter for bilateral teleoperation. Flexural testing and teleoperated grasping trials show operators can modulate grip force based on the feedback.

entry.title: A False Average: Chain-of-Thought Monitors Collapse Where They Are the Only Defense

author.name: Shikhar Shiromani, Leo Richter

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, The authors show that chain-of-thought monitoring collapses exactly where it is the only defense: rewriting an agent's reasoning to read as good-faith engineering while leaving every command and output byte-identical drops a held-out monitor's catch rate on that subset from about 95 percent to under 11 percent in a single gradient-free attempt. Because aggregate monitor accuracy is dominated by hacks visible in the actions, it hides this near-total failure, and the attack transfers across monitor families and agent settings.

entry.title: CN101 - A Digital Thermodynamic Computer for Generative AI

author.name: Lars Holdijk, Denis Melanson, Zier Mensch, Brandon Birchall, Vincent Cheung, Nicholas Lehrter, Maxwell Aifer, Samuel Duffield, Jan Ole Ernst, Rajath Salegame, Antonio J. Martinez, Gavin Crooks, Miranda Cheng, Zach Belateche, Marc Bright, Patrick J. Coles, Faris Sbahi

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, CN101 is a digital thermodynamic computer for generative AI in which stochastic physical dynamics are the computational primitive, computing answers as time-averaged statistics of an equilibrating trajectory. Crucially it moves this equilibration-style computation off Langevin dynamics and analog substrates into a digital implementation, removing much of the engineering difficulty that has confined the paradigm to analog hardware.

entry.title: An AI Approach to Verified Production Cryptographic Libraries

author.name: Chuyue Sun, Su Fong, Zhiyi Kuang, Yizheng Jiao, Nina Narodytska, Haoze Wu, David L. Dill, Clark Barrett

entry.summary: Covered in yesterday's Research roundup, CryptoProver synthesizes internal specifications and Verus-checked proofs for production Rust cryptography from high-level API contracts, producing an independent proof of curve25519-dalek and a first verification of RustCrypto's chacha20 against RFC 8439. It moves LLM-assisted formal verification from isolated proof obligations to real deployed libraries.

entry.title: Slides2MindMap: Reconstructing Cognitively Efficient Knowledge Hierarchies from Lecture Slides

author.name: Yuzhi Wang, Rongjun Ye, Shengyuan Chen, Huachi Zhou, Jiaqi Bai, Chuang Zhou, Zhicong Hong, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: The authors define the Slides2MindMap task of reconstructing cognitively efficient knowledge hierarchies from entire course slide decks and release S2M-Bench, comprising 12,774 slide pages with expert-annotated mind maps across 24 university courses. Evaluation is grounded in cognitive science criteria balancing global and local knowledge focus. The application area is intelligent education tooling.

entry.title: From AI Technical Debt to Agentic Technical Debt: A Systematic Mapping of Root Causes and Manifestations in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Muhammad Tukur, Hayatullahi B. Adeyemo, Tao Chen, Nour Ali, Anis Zarrad, Marco Agus, Rick Kazman, Rami Bahsoon

entry.summary: This systematic mapping study introduces Agentic Technical Debt as a category distinct from prior AI technical debt models, arguing that autonomous reasoning, multi-agent collaboration, tool orchestration, and persistent memory create debt that emerges, propagates, and amplifies dynamically rather than sitting in static components. It catalogs root causes and manifestations across agentic systems. The intended audience is software architecture and maintenance practitioners.

entry.title: Homebot: A Personal AI Agent for Conversational Home Assistance and Automation

author.name: Shengyuan Ye, Yixin Zhang, Han Liang, Liekang Zeng, Jiangsu Du, Mu Yuan

entry.summary: Homebot is a locally deployable household assistant that unifies voice and messaging channels over a shared runtime combining LLM responses with registered tools and skills, using wake-word activation, streaming ASR and TTS, and an explicit dialogue-state protocol. Emphasizes clear channel, tool, and skill contracts for customization.

entry.title: A Fortran General-Purpose Transpiler: Proof of Concept

author.name: Shivamshan Sivanesan, Kazem Ardaneh

entry.summary: FGPT is a proof-of-concept compiler pipeline that transpiles Fortran into GPU-adapted Fortran, automatically differentiable Fortran via Tapenade, or NumPy and JAX code. It targets the scientific-computing expertise gap where legacy Fortran codebases must reach modern differentiable and accelerator ecosystems.

entry.title: Symbolic Attack Chain Generation from Atomic Red Team Techniques: An Empirical Study of Predicate Representation Granularity

author.name: Ramya Varunsegar

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether the nine-category predicate scheme used by state-of-the-art automated attack-chain planners is actually necessary, comparing predicate granularities in a pipeline where an LLM translates Atomic Red Team techniques into PDDL and a classical planner reasons deterministically. It measures the effect of representation choices on plan validity, cost, and fidelity.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Characterization of Particles and Fibers by Optical Microscopy

author.name: Simiao Sun, Kenneth Ng, Lynn Lee, Astrid Harth, Asami Odate, Aggelos Katsaggelos, Manuel Ballester Matito, Nicholas Eastaugh, Marc Walton

entry.summary: The authors distill a multimodal teacher that combines microscopy image embeddings with text embeddings for illumination modality, magnification, and specimen identity into a student model, producing block-structured embeddings whose components remain physically interpretable. The goal is reliable automated characterization of particles and fibers under varying optical conditions.

entry.title: DSETA: A Dual-Stage Continual Learning Framework for Travel Time Prediction in Dynamic Traffic Environments

author.name: Yanming Lyu, Yue Cheng, Lingkun Li, Ruipeng Gao, Xinyue Liu, Hui Gao, Qiang Ni

entry.summary: DSETA is a continual-learning framework for ride-hailing arrival-time prediction that splits incremental updates into inter-day and intra-day stages so long-term traffic trends are disentangled from short-term congestion shocks. It targets accuracy degradation under distribution shift in production ETA systems.

entry.title: UOT-IR: Structured Routing of High-Polyphony Symbolic Music into Fixed-Budget Representations

author.name: Ziyue Kang, Nan Nan, Chenhao Lin, Xiaohong Guan

entry.summary: UOT-IR treats compression of densely orchestrated symbolic music into fixed track or slot budgets as a structured routing problem solved with constrained unbalanced optimal transport, without training. The aim is to preserve structural roles, orchestration compatibility, and playability where heuristic simplification fails.

entry.title: FL-OA: A Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning Framework with Outsourced Auditing for Intelligent Devices

author.name: Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Fenghua Xu, Teng Hu, Jian Meng, Jiguo Yu

entry.summary: FL-OA is a Byzantine-robust federated learning framework that outsources update auditing to collaborating parties, aiming to work without assuming a majority of honest clients or a clean server-side root dataset. It also addresses benign-update divergence and high-dimensional comparison difficulties.

entry.title: Enhancing Visual Perception in Foggy Conditions via Multiclass Fog Density Modeling

author.name: Mohamad Mofeed Chaar, Galia Weidl

entry.summary: Studies autonomous driving perception under five synthetic fog density levels derived from Waymo data with learned depth estimation, and finds that training separate density-specific models beats a single unified model, especially in severe fog. It quantifies the benefit of conditioning perception on weather severity.

entry.title: QWRF-Net: A Quantum-Wavelet Framework with Rectified Flow for Short-Term Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Zhuo Wang, Chaorong Li, Wenjie Luo, Chuanhu Deng

entry.summary: QWRF-Net combines quantum-inspired components, wavelet multi-scale decomposition and rectified flow generation for short-term radar precipitation nowcasting, aiming to preserve intense convective cores at longer lead times. It targets hydrometeorological early warning for flash flooding.

entry.title: SPECTRA: Band-Routed Embedding and Stage-Wise LoRA for Cross-Sensor Fine-Tuning of Geospatial Foundation Models

author.name: Xingyan Li, Jordan A. Caraballo-Vega, Jie Gong, Mark L. Carroll, Jianwu Wang

entry.summary: SPECTRA adapts Earth-observation foundation models to downstream sensors whose spectral bands differ from pretraining, using band-routed embeddings plus stage-wise LoRA to cut adaptation cost. It tackles spectral mismatch and fine-tuning efficiency jointly rather than separately.

entry.title: EntailLLM: Verifying LLM-Generated Vulnerability Discovery Paths with Domain Knowledge via Logic Programming

author.name: Kaustuv Mukherji, Jaikrishna Manojkumar Patil, Colton Payne, Paulo Shakarian, Dana Warmsley, Nigel Stepp, Evelyn Kim

entry.summary: EntailLLM checks whether LLM-proposed vulnerability discovery paths through a binary's call graph are logically entailed by an independent domain knowledge graph, using temporal annotated logic for verification. It evaluates across several CWE classes in safety-critical software such as medical devices.

entry.title: DeGS: A Scalable 3DGS Architecture via Decoupled Workload Parsing and Reorganization

author.name: Minnan Pei, Gang Li, Zeyu Zhu, Siting Wang, Junwen Si, Zhuoran Song, Yu Feng, Fangxin Liu, Xiaoyao Liang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: DeGS is a hardware architecture for 3D Gaussian splatting inference that decouples the tightly coupled checking-and-blending dataflow, reorganizing workloads to remove spatial redundancy from irregular Gaussian coverage and temporal redundancy from asynchronous pixel termination. This restores scalability as the number of processing elements grows.

entry.title: UniqueSplat: View-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Haixu Song, Xiaoke Yang, Shengjun Zhang, Jiwen Lu, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: UniqueSplat makes feed-forward Gaussian splatting view-conditioned, predicting Gaussians tailored to each query viewpoint instead of one fixed set shared across all views as in pixelSplat and MVSplat. The view prior is baked into network parameters so Gaussians adapt dynamically at query time.

entry.title: HarMoE: Multi-Source Chest Radiograph Pretraining with Dataset-Disentangled Experts

author.name: Haozhe Luo, Ziyu Zhou, Shelley Zixin Shu, Mauricio Reyes

entry.summary: HarMoE pretrains chest radiograph models from many heterogeneous multi-label classification datasets rather than relying mainly on a single image-report corpus, using dataset-disentangled mixture-of-experts routing to keep clinical semantics from being entangled with dataset identity. This aims to improve transfer across sources with different label ontologies and acquisition pipelines.

entry.title: Topological Simplification in Predictive Coding Networks

author.name: Adam Shaw, Jiayu Li, Michael Sperling, Michael Kim, Alvin Jin

entry.summary: Uses layer-wise persistent homology to study how predictive coding networks reshape representation topology, finding that smaller networks collapse connected components earlier across layers and reporting correlations between topological simplification and model size or performance. Provides quantitative structural insight into a neuro-inspired bidirectional architecture.

entry.title: Forecasting Revenue with its Customer-Base Drivers: When and Why Coordination Helps

author.name: Kyeongbin Kim, Daniel McCarthy, Dokyun Lee

entry.summary: Introduces a customer-based multi-task transformer that forecasts revenue by jointly modeling acquisition, repeat purchase, order size, and their coordination across 966 firms of weekly transaction data. Reports large error reductions over established customer-base benchmarks and a small, statistically insignificant edge over direct total-sales forecasting.

entry.title: The Ignition Is Real, and It Lives at the Readout: Latent composition, difficulty-clocked ignition, and the interface-constituted commit in a recurrent-depth reasoner

author.name: Simon Lam-Muir

entry.summary: Attempts to determine whether the reported compositional ignition in latent-reasoning models is genuine computation, an instrument artifact, or inherited from verbal training data, by regrowing an independent 30M-parameter recurrent-depth reasoner from the same recipe and seed and tracking both vocabulary readout and hidden state. It reports that the ignition event appears at the readout, arrives later for deeper problems, and reproduces across two same-seed realizations with divergent training trajectories.

entry.title: TabletCraft: Bridging a 4,000-Year Cultural Gap with Bidirectional Akkadian NMT and Cuneiform Rendering

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: TabletCraft is an open-source system for bidirectional Akkadian translation plus rendering of composed text as cuneiform tablets, extending beyond prior scholar-oriented one-way translation. It lets non-specialists write in the world's oldest writing system rather than only read translations.

entry.title: Surrogate Substitution Preserves PHI Detectability: A Multi-Detector Equivalence Study

author.name: Qiming Bao, Sherry J. H. Feng, Kim Chester Eugenio, Meng Fon

entry.summary: Studies whether replacing protected health information with realistic same-type surrogates (instead of placeholder tags) degrades the ability of downstream PII detectors to find those spans. Using paired equivalence testing (TOST) on 57k spans across multiple detectors, the work provides a methodological protocol that scores utility only on masked spans. Matters for privacy-preserving clinical NLP pipelines.

entry.title: Conformal risk control for model-form uncertainty in parametric non-intrusive reduced-order models

author.name: Edgar Jaber (CB, ENS Paris Saclay), R\'emy Vallot (CB, Michelin), Thibault Dairay (CB, Michelin), Mathilde Mougeot (CB, ENSIIE, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for quantifying model-form uncertainty in non-intrusive reduced-order models of parametric PDEs by randomly perturbing reduced bases on the Stiefel manifold and wrapping the result in distribution-free conformal risk control. Aims to give reliability guarantees in extrapolation and small-data regimes. Relevant to industrial surrogate modeling and simulation.

entry.title: SRAP: SVD-Refined Adversarial Perturbations for Imperceptible Face-Swap Defense

author.name: Sungwon Cho, Kwanghyun Ko, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: Analyzes why PGD-based protective perturbations against face-swapping look visually bad, attributing it to spatially diffuse perturbations and salient high-frequency energy concentrated in later singular components. SRAP refines perturbations using identity-sensitivity estimates and SVD truncation to preserve protection while improving imperceptibility. Contributes to proactive deepfake defenses.

entry.title: Divide-and-Conquer: Towards Generalizable Amortized Bayesian Inference for the Drift Diffusion Model

author.name: Yufei Wu, Shanqing Gao, Andreas Voss, Francis Tuerlinckx

entry.summary: Proposes decomposing drift diffusion model datasets into pairwise shards so a single amortized Bayesian inference network can generalize across study designs, rather than requiring retraining per design. Inference is done on shards and recombined, exploiting the model's independence assumption. Practically useful for cognitive science workflows.

entry.title: Socially Grounded Agentic AI: Coordinating Plural Perspectives through Social Theory

author.name: Matt Ratto, Abhishek Moturu, Daniel Silver

entry.summary: Argues that pluralistic alignment lacks an account of how values are socially organized, contested, and coordinated, and imports concepts from sociology to structure how agentic systems represent and reconcile multiple legitimate perspectives. Offers conceptual and design resources rather than experiments. Contributes to the theory side of alignment beyond single-value optimization.

entry.title: Modeling Scientific Experiment Scenes: Dataset and Model

author.name: Minghao Zou, Qingtian Zeng, Shangkun Liu, Cong Liu, Paul L. Rosin, Guanghui Yue, Jun Liu, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: PhysScene is presented as the first scene graph generation dataset for physics laboratory experiment scenes, with dense annotations of instruments and fine-grained physical relations. The authors highlight long-tailed predicate distributions and a visual-textual semantic gap as core challenges.

entry.title: CrossScope: A Role-Asymmetric World Model for Joint Dual-Scope Surgical Video Prediction

author.name: Wanhao Liu, Jinsong Lin, Rulin Zhou, Chi Kit Ng, Wenbin Pan, Zhiqing Tang, Dongyue Li, Liwei Luo, Yanshen Wu, Panshuo Li, Zhiyong Xiong, Huxin Gao, Tamas Haidegger, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: CrossScope is a surgical world model that predicts future frames from two independently moving endoscopes in mother-child ERCP, transferring cross-view evidence asymmetrically according to each view's role rather than assuming symmetric fusion. It formalizes role-asymmetric dual-scope future prediction.

entry.title: Residual Flow Matching with Dynamic Cross-Interaction for 3D Multi-Person Motion Prediction

author.name: Wei Wei, Yinyuan Zhao, Ruixuan Yu

entry.summary: This method predicts 3D multi-person motion with flow matching over residuals from a deterministic coarse kinematic prior, rather than generating skeletal sequences from pure noise, and adds a dynamic cross-interaction mechanism between agents. The prior stabilizes structure during early noise-dominated steps.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Implicit Super-Resolution Network for Pathological Images

author.name: Jiaming Liang, QiHui Han, Haolin Chen, Chengxin Ye, Jiawen Liu, Jiazhou Chen, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai

entry.summary: Morph-ISR treats super-resolution of whole-slide pathology images as continuous coordinate-based reconstruction with morphology-aware priors, aiming to preserve cellular texture and boundaries rather than oversmoothing. The goal is to let cheaper low-resolution scanners support diagnostic-quality digital pathology.

entry.title: PLS-Calib: A Partial Least Squares Framework for Event Camera and Odometry Calibration under Ground Motion Constraints

author.name: Guangyu Li, Xiao Li, Yujie Wu, Changshuo Wang, Prayag Tiwari, Jiang Cai, Fangwen Yu, Mingkun Xu

entry.summary: PLS-Calib performs extrinsic rotation calibration between an event camera and wheel odometry for ground robots that cannot excite all six degrees of freedom, using partial least squares regression to model latent motion relationships. It is proposed as a numerically stabler alternative to canonical correlation analysis approaches that suffer ill-conditioned covariance matrices.

entry.title: Contact-Driven Localization in a Freeform Robotic Self-Assembled Structure

author.name: Mohammadali Rashidioun, Michael Sosa, Petras Swissler

entry.summary: This paper localizes modular self-assembling robots using only binary contact information about which neighbors are docked, via a virtual-force scheme where robots are attracted to connected neighbors and repelled from unconnected ones. The aim is to eliminate dependence on external tracking or expensive sensors in swarm self-reconfiguration.

entry.title: Ekova: A Personality-Support Agent for Self-Discovery Dialogue

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: Ekova proposes Personality Support as a paradigm distinct from emotional support, aiming to help users articulate and understand themselves rather than relieve distress. It contributes a Chinese dataset of 8,590 self-discovery dialogue samples across five interaction personas and a multi-persona system trained with a style-tailored fine-tuning framework. The authors are explicit that this is not clinical intervention.

entry.title: Neuro-Evolved Heuristics for Variable Gapped Common Subsequence Identification

author.name: Marko Djukanovi\'c, Christian Blum, Aleksandar Kartelj, Saso Dzeroski, Ziga Zebec

entry.summary: This work automates the design of beam-search heuristics for the multi-sequence variable gapped longest common subsequence problem, representing heuristics as a fixed-architecture neural network whose weights are optimized by a genetic algorithm in a neuro-evolutionary loop. It replaces hand-crafted guidance functions that generalize poorly. Applications include sequence alignment and time-series analysis.

entry.title: Logographic Character Visual Pretraining via Semantic-based Contrastive Learning

author.name: Daqian Shi, Wei Cao, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lida Shi, Xiaolei Diao, Cedric M John

entry.summary: The paper proposes contrastive visual pretraining for logographic characters (e.g., Chinese) that injects visual-semantic component information so recognition works despite heavily imbalanced, long-tailed character frequency distributions. It targets historical and low-frequency character resources where large balanced datasets do not exist.

entry.title: OrEdge: Efficient Multi-Modal Anomaly Detection in Distributed Software Systems via Orthogonal-Domain Learning

author.name: Amr M. Zaki, Farhoud Jafari Kaleibar, Honggeun Ji, Komal Sarda, Marin Litoiu

entry.summary: OrEdge performs real-time multi-modal anomaly detection over logs, metrics, and traces in distributed software systems using orthogonal-domain temporal reconstruction instead of attention or graph architectures, aiming for much smaller models and lower compute. It targets edge-deployable observability.

entry.title: Structured Proxy Features for Multimodal NSCLC Survival Prediction from Pretreatment CT

author.name: Huu Phong Nguyen, Delower Hossain, Ehsan Saghapour, Zhandos Sembay, Jake Y. Chen

entry.summary: This study tests whether adding six simulation-derived proxy features that encode interactions among tumor characteristics improves multimodal survival prediction for non-small-cell lung cancer from pretreatment CT, radiomics, and clinical variables. The premise is that standard radiomic and deep features treat imaging descriptors as independent quantities.

entry.title: PartMat: Material-Aware 3D Part Decomposition with a Single Global Latent

author.name: Guangming Fu, Jin Song, Yiyun Fei, Guoqiu Li, Ruigao Yang, Jianan Jiang

entry.summary: PartMat decomposes a single 3D object into material-consistent parts such as fabric, wood, or metal using one global latent, rather than functional-semantic parts generated independently per part. This avoids compute scaling linearly with part count and better matches editing needs in applications like interior design.

entry.title: PatTree: a novel approach for automated creation of multimodal, graph-based patient representations for medical classification tasks

author.name: Julia Gehrmann, Lars Quakulinski, Hamza Naseem, Oya Beyan

entry.summary: PatTree automatically constructs graph-based, multimodal patient representations from messy real-world clinical data, avoiding the resource-intensive harmonization normally needed before integration. The goal is scalable and reproducible multimodal clinical classification despite missing values, mixed modalities, and inconsistent semantics.

entry.title: Automatic Patient-Specific Microwave Ablation Planning Accelerated by a Physics-Guided Deep Learning Model

author.name: Seonaeng Cho, Minjee Seo, Minju Seol, Juil Park, Joon Ho Kwon, Kyungho Yoon

entry.summary: Builds a digital-twin planning framework for liver microwave ablation that replaces expensive multiphysics simulation with a physics-guided neural surrogate inside a genetic algorithm optimizing antenna trajectory, power, and duration. The surrogate is trained on simulations over patient-specific tumor and vessel anatomy.

entry.title: LLM-Derived Priors for Thompson Sampling in Cold-Start Comment Recommendation

author.name: Eugene Lee, Oseong Choi, Byungsoo Kang, Taeyeong Jang

entry.summary: Uses LLMs to convert the text of user comments into informative Bayesian priors that warm-start Thompson sampling for comment recommendation, addressing cold start when arms have no interaction history. Segment-level hierarchies account for aggregate differences in response patterns. A practical bridge between semantic models and bandit exploration.

entry.title: Mapping the City Through the Lens of Language Models

author.name: Wanqi Liu, Rong Zhao, Zhizhou Sha, Qinyu Cui, Yecheng Zhang

entry.summary: Measures the implicit urban assumptions ten open-weight LLMs make when a city is underspecified, by having them rate anonymized morphological profiles of real urban centers on 40 audited indicators, with reliability screens, lineage-aware aggregation, and independent replication. Finds a shared preference for larger, faster-growing, infrastructure-dense, less sprawling profiles. Relevant to bias auditing in planning and policy uses of LLMs.

entry.title: A Unified 2D Framework for DeepLesion Detection, Segmentation and Short Report Generation

author.name: Ruida Cheng, Tejas S. Mathai, Benjamin Hou, Qingqing Zhu, Zhiyong Lu, Matthew McAuliffe, Ronald M. Summers

entry.summary: An NIH-affiliated group builds a single 2D pipeline over the DeepLesion CT dataset that detects lesion boxes, segments them, and generates short radiology findings text with LLM-based reasoning. It reports moderate detection (mAP50 about 70) and segmentation (Dice about 63) plus BLEU/ROUGE report metrics. It matters as an integrated clinical workflow prototype rather than a methodological advance.

entry.title: Open-Linguistic Concept Unified Learning for Cross-Site Interpretable Dermatology Image Diagnosis

author.name: Chengyu Wu, Junpeng Tan, Wanxiang Luo, Yaqi Wang, Yandong Wen, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: This paper builds concept-based interpretable dermatology diagnosis that generalizes across sites and modalities by unifying heterogeneous clinical concept taxonomies into an open-linguistic space, so a vision-language model does not need per-dataset label engineering. It also allows clinician interventions beyond a fixed predefined concept list.

entry.title: Energy Efficiency of Locally Deployed LLMs: A Preliminary Quantitative GPU Power Benchmark on Consumer Hardware

author.name: Philipp M. Z\"ahl, Anika Hennig

entry.summary: A hardware-level energy benchmark measures GPU power draw for nine open-source models from 1B to 7B parameters running locally on a single consumer RTX 4060Ti via Ollama, reporting joules per prompt, joules per output token, and throughput. Results indicate that architecture and quantization matter beyond raw parameter count for energy cost. It provides a reproducible protocol for on-premise sustainability accounting.

entry.title: Don't Offer What Can't Be Done: Deterministic Executability Gating for LLM Skill Selection at Scale

author.name: Ortal Ashkenazi, Vitalii Kloz, Mykhailo Ulianchenko

entry.summary: Describes a deployed three-stage skill-selection pipeline for a commercial customer-care assistant that adds a deterministic gate filtering out skills that cannot actually execute given account state. Argues semantic relevance alone is insufficient for production agent routing.

entry.title: Understanding Online Failure Prediction in Linux Through Complementary Multi-View Explainability

author.name: Diogo D\'oria, Jo\~ao R. Campos

entry.summary: This experience report builds an explainable online failure prediction pipeline for Linux, combining consensus-based feature selection with temporal onset analysis, subsystem-level causal analysis, and complementary diagnostics. The motivation is that accurate alerts are useless without diagnostic insight, and that high accuracy may reflect workload-specific telemetry correlations rather than real failure processes.

entry.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism

author.name: Donna M Bye, Levin Kuhlmann

entry.summary: A critical humanities-style argument that the dominant framing of AI anthropomorphism as user error reflects institutional authority rather than established evidence, and that it delegitimizes users' relational experiences with AI systems. It calls for re-examining who gets to define appropriate human-AI interaction.

entry.title: AI-assisted Script Management for Requirements Elicitation Interviews

author.name: Anmol Singhal, Paulo Carvalho, Travis Breaux

entry.summary: Presents an AI-assisted workflow for requirements elicitation interviews that generates theory-guided scripts from business goals and provides live topic-coverage tracking and probing support. It studies how integrated rather than isolated AI support changes the interview process and resulting requirements artifacts.

entry.title: FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Zhengyang Zhang, Ziyu Lu, PengCheng Li, Hongbo Duan, Yi Liu, Pengting Luo, Peiyu Zhuang, Xinghui Li, Shaohua Ma

entry.summary: FAST-GS replaces single-polynomial motion models in 4D Gaussian splatting with a Fourier decomposition that separates low-frequency global trajectories from high-frequency local motion, aiming to reduce cumulative trajectory drift in long dynamic sequences. It preserves real-time rendering while improving quality on complex motion.

entry.title: RamanPFN: learning from Raman spectral structure with a tabular foundation model

author.name: Xingyu Pan, Huan Wang, Jinjia Guo, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong, Jixi Lu

entry.summary: RamanPFN adapts a pretrained tabular foundation model to Raman spectra by preserving spectral structure and joint visibility of related bands, instead of the feature-subsampled views that standard in-context tabular inference uses on very wide inputs. It targets small labelled spectral datasets where task-specific deep networks and latent-variable chemometrics both struggle.

entry.title: Open-Set Visual Text Forensics via Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow

author.name: Jiangling Zhang, Shuxuan Gao, Zeyu Chen, Yichao Liu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This generative forensics method localizes manipulated text in images by estimating the local restoration cost needed to bring a query image back to authentic visual-text statistics, using a sparsity-constrained rectified flow rather than a discriminative forgery classifier. Self-supervised artifact injection mitigates training data scarcity for unseen open-set attacks.

entry.title: Syntax Meets Semantics: Understanding Scientific Formulae

author.name: Yuni Susanti, Moritz Schubotz

entry.summary: Empirically studies the correspondence between the syntactic form of scientific formulae and their semantic descriptions, finding that native representation spaces show very weak observable alignment despite latent correlation. The work matters for mathematical information retrieval and scholarly search systems.

entry.title: DyFrDet: Towards Accurate Small Object Detection via Dynamic Frequency Suppression with Label Disambiguation

author.name: Zihan Yang, Yang Guo, Hongxing Zhang, Dan Lu, Siyuan Yao

entry.summary: DyFrDet targets small-object detection by dynamically suppressing frequency-domain background noise via an adaptive feature pyramid and by disambiguating noisy assignment labels. Reports improved localization for objects with few discriminative pixels.

entry.title: UNVaMP: Neural Knowledge Tracing with Variational Regularization of Latent Knowledge Dynamics

author.name: Carson J. Cook, Ahmed J. Zerouali, Anthony Schmidt, Reginald Ziedzor, Paul Lin, Luke G. Eglington

entry.summary: UNVaMP is a knowledge-tracing architecture that combines observed student interactions with memory to produce latent knowledge trajectories, with explicit control over trajectory smoothness via variational regularization. It can run as a pure neural predictor or as a hybrid with an interpretable measurement layer.

entry.title: Conditionally Identifiable Latent-Environment Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Recommendation

author.name: Qianqian Wang, Wenwu Gong, Yunshan Li, Zhenqing Wu, Ruili Wang, Lili Yang

entry.summary: Formulates out-of-distribution recommendation as conditionally identifiable risk-aware learning, modeling a latent environment with a user-conditioned exponential family and a feature-indexed polynomial for how the environment shifts preferences. Provides identifiability conditions under sufficient variation and correct specification. Adds statistical rigor to latent-environment recommenders.

entry.title: FaithIR: Rethinking Infrared Image Super-Resolution from Perceptual Sharpness to Task Relevant Fidelity

author.name: Axi Niu, Zhenguo Wu, Kang Zhang, Qingsen Yan, Jinqiu Sun, Yanning Zhang

entry.summary: FaithIR argues infrared super-resolution should optimize downstream task fidelity rather than perceptual sharpness, since existing methods hallucinate textures that distort real thermal structure. It combines a patch-level conditioning branch with pixel-domain dense restoration to preserve thermal semantics.

entry.title: GVCCTurbo: Rate-Compute Quality Scheduling for Codebook Driven Generative Compression

author.name: Ziyue Zeng, Dingjie Peng, Xun Su, Hiroshi Watanabe

entry.summary: GVCCTurbo schedules generative-prior refreshes separately from codebook correction slots in ultra-low-bitrate codebook-driven compression, so a target bitrate maps to a sampler trajectory length and refresh period. This prevents shortening the sampler from also deleting the correction capacity that carries target-specific information.

entry.title: Learning Biomechanically Plausible Human Motion from Sparse Radar Point Clouds

author.name: Jonas Leo Mueller, Markus Gambietz, Alexander Weiss, Daniel Krauss, Bjoern M. Eskofier

entry.summary: This paper embeds a full-body skeletal model into an end-to-end differentiable radar-based human pose estimation pipeline, predicting subject-specific segment proportions from radar features and supervising joint angles through differentiable forward kinematics. The result is anatomically plausible poses instead of unconstrained keypoints.

entry.title: DeRP: An Algorithm for Self-Assembly of Power-Delivery Networks using Recursive Branching in Information-Limited Environments

author.name: Mohammadali Rashidioun, Sangwoo Park, Petras Swissler

entry.summary: DeRP is a decentralized algorithm in which robots act as conduits and recursively self-assemble a branching power-delivery network from a single source to multiple sinks, choosing local pivot points that approximate Steiner tree branch points. It relies only on local communication and bearing sensing toward sinks.

entry.title: MA-HEAD-Net: Adaptive Rule-Guided Multi-Agent DRL for AoI Minimization in UAV-Assisted Emergency Networks

author.name: Yixin Zhang, Zhuohui Yao, Wenchi Cheng, Walid Saad

entry.summary: Combines rule-guided heuristics with multi-agent deep RL to minimize age of information in UAV emergency communication networks, modeling bursty arrivals and finite-blocklength effects. Aims at time-critical post-disaster rescue scheduling.

entry.title: Cross-Fitted Residual Utility for Primary-Preserving Cognitive Decision Correction in Automatic Modulation Classification

author.name: Linzhuo Han, Zongyong Cui, Houbiao Li

entry.summary: Studies when a cognitive radio receiver should override a trusted default modulation classifier, learning candidate-specific residual utility via cross-fitting and freezing decision thresholds on a disjoint split before held-out evaluation. Evaluated on three automatic modulation classification datasets.

entry.title: Abduction Without a Body? Representational Grounding and the Abduction Loop for Scientific Hypothesis Generation

author.name: Michael Farmer

entry.summary: Philosophical argument that continuous sensorimotor embodiment is not required for all scientific abduction, focusing on identity abduction where two independently developed structures are recognized as the same object via representational grounding. Suggests diagrams and representation transformations expose latent invariants that yield new inferential affordances.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems

author.name: Juan Li, Wei Cai, Yan Bai

entry.summary: Presents a neuro-symbolic governance framework in which AI agents in decentralized digital-twin ecosystems carry multi-layer semantic profiles that let symbolic policy engines verify identity, capability and compliance. It is aimed at cross-institutional multi-agent deployments lacking trust infrastructure.

entry.title: ARM: Detector-Agnostic Changepoint Attribution with Finite-Sample Error Control

author.name: Chenchen Peng, Mixia Wu, Qijing Yan, Da Chen, Zhiqi Shen

entry.summary: ARM is a detector-agnostic wrapper that, after a changepoint is detected in multivariate data, certifies which coordinates actually changed with finite-sample error control and labels each as a location or scale change. It fills a gap between uncontrolled variable rankings and coarse block-level certificates.

entry.title: PICopilot: An LLM-based Agentic Framework for Assisting Photonic Integrated Circuit Design via Script Generation

author.name: Xiaohan Jiang, Zeyu Li, Wei Zhang, Jiang Xu

entry.summary: PICopilot is an LLM agent framework that generates and refines scripts for photonic integrated circuit design, aiming to close the productivity gap created by the shift from GUI tools to script-based design APIs. It is presented as the first LLM-based assistant for this design flow.

entry.title: LAB-Tab: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Network Adaptation for Few-Shot Tabular Generation

author.name: Zijian Shen, Taijie Chen, Bin Zhou, Ziyang Jiang, Jintao Ke

entry.summary: LAB-Tab fits a Bayesian network on abundant source-domain tabular data and then uses an LLM to propose plausible structural adaptations for a target domain where only a few records exist. It aims to avoid both overfitting sparse target statistics and blindly reusing stale source dependencies.

entry.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Efficient Options Pricing Models

author.name: Harris Cobb, Wenbo Hao, Yingjie Liu

entry.summary: Applies neural networks with local converging inputs to correct coarse-mesh numerical solutions for multi-asset option pricing, requiring little high-fidelity training data. Demonstrations cover cash-or-nothing options under Black-Scholes in up to three dimensions and barrier options under Heston volatility.

entry.title: FedCritic-MIMO: Communication-Efficient Serverless Federated Critic Learning for Massive-MIMO Resource Control in Open and Disaggregated 6G RANs

author.name: Amin Farajzadeh, Melike Erol-Kantarci

entry.summary: FedCritic-MIMO is a serverless federated multi-agent RL scheme for 6G radio access networks where cell controllers keep local actors and share only compatible critic parameters. It targets joint scheduling, power allocation, and beamforming under tight inter-controller signaling budgets.

entry.title: A Physics-Flavored Transformer Network for Parametrizing Contraction Dynamics of Engineered Skeletal Muscle Tissues

author.name: Mattias Luber, Timo Betz

entry.summary: Embeds a stretched-exponential mechanistic model inside a CNN-Transformer to automatically extract physically meaningful contraction kinetics parameters from engineered skeletal muscle tissue recordings. This replaces reliance on simplistic peak-force metrics for pharmacological screening.

entry.title: FedRings: A Scalable and Topology-Aware Federated Learning Framework for LEO Satellite Constellations

author.name: Ziwu Liu, In\^es Pinto Gouveia, Rehana Yasmin, Paulo Esteves-Verissimo, Ali Shoker

entry.summary: FedRings organizes low-Earth-orbit satellites into ring topologies for decentralized federated learning, with spatio-temporal routing aligned to visibility windows and adaptive sparse incremental aggregation to cut communication. Addresses the short contact times and dynamic topology that break centralized or synchronous FL. Relevant to space-based sensing and edge learning.

entry.title: Robust Low-Tubal-Rank Tensor Completion under Cross-Concentrated Sampling

author.name: Hanqin Cai, Longxiu Huang, Jing Qin, Chengyue Wu

entry.summary: Studies robust recovery of low-tubal-rank third-order tensors from cross-concentrated sampling, where only entries within selected horizontal and lateral slices are observed and some are grossly corrupted. The proposed Robust Iterative t-CUR uses blockwise Welsch correction and projected gradient descent on partitioned blocks. Extends structured tensor completion to the outlier setting.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: A Multidimensional Evaluation of Statistical Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Monnie McGee, Mateo Langston Smith, Julian Cabrera

entry.summary: Evaluates statistical reasoning in 15 current-generation LLMs on 90 questions from four statistics exams, combining accuracy with response behavior, structural topic modeling, and lexical similarity to examine how explanations are constructed. Accuracy ranged from 55 to 78 percent while topic structure was largely shared across models. Argues accuracy alone hides important differences in explanatory quality.

entry.title: Clinically-Grounded Hierarchical Classification for Consistent Chest X-ray Interpretation

author.name: Jong Hak Moon, Minjun Kim, Minjun Kim

entry.summary: CHASE performs chest X-ray interpretation as a single-stage hierarchical classification over anatomical regions, sub-regions, and pathological findings, enforcing consistency between coarse and fine predictions. This mirrors radiologist coarse-to-fine reasoning instead of treating findings as flat independent labels.

entry.title: CROSS: Cascaded Distillation and Dual-Constraint Grounding for Remote Sensing Referring Segmentation

author.name: Tingzhang Luo, Ruizhong Liu, Yichao Liu, Cheng Fan, Yu Liu, Jianyuan Guo

entry.summary: CROSS tightens the coupling between a vision-language model and a promptable segmenter for referring segmentation in satellite imagery, adding cascaded distillation and dual constraints to counter localization drift and object-centric bias. It aims to make the pipeline sensitive to spatial relations, not just dominant object semantics.

entry.title: FreqAdapt: Frequency-Adaptive Processing for RAW Object Detection

author.name: Hanxi Li, Huiling Li

entry.summary: FreqAdapt is a lightweight module that adapts RAW sensor data for object detection by mapping image signal processing operations into the Fourier domain and separating components by physical properties. It exploits the richer information and better noise characteristics of RAW over compressed sRGB, particularly in low light.

entry.title: S$^3$-Diff: Structural Semantic Synergy Diffusion Model for High Fidelity Super Resolution of Pathological Images

author.name: Jiaming Liang, QiHui Han, Guangye Ou, Jiawen Liu, Haolin Chen, Xi Zhong, Jiazhou Chen, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai

entry.summary: S3-Diff is a diffusion framework for super-resolving pathology images that anchors generation to tissue structure using a frozen segmentation model and gradient distillation, aiming to avoid over-smoothing and semantic drift that harm diagnosis. Low-resolution slides are common in practice due to device, storage, and transmission limits.

entry.title: A Low-Cost Hybrid Reservoir Computing Model for Isolated Sign Language Video Recognition

author.name: Nitin Kumar Singh, Arie Rachmad Syulistyo, Yuichiro Tanaka, Hakaru Tamukoh

entry.summary: This paper combines MediaPipe keypoint extraction with a hybrid deep and bidirectional reservoir computing pipeline and ridge regression readout for isolated sign language recognition on low-cost edge hardware. The motivation is avoiding the compute cost of deep sequence models.

entry.title: Unsupervised Adversarial Domain Adaptation for Uterine layer Segmentation: From Labeled Cine to Unlabeled Dynamic EPI MRI

author.name: Smiti Tripathy, Milauni Desai, Jordina Aviles Verdera, Jana Hutter

entry.summary: This work introduces a dynamic multi-echo EPI MRI protocol to jointly characterize uterine peristalsis and tissue relaxation changes at low field, and uses unsupervised adversarial domain adaptation to transfer uterine layer segmentation from labeled cine MRI to unlabeled EPI data. The adaptation avoids the burden of manual annotation on the noisier modality.

entry.title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration

author.name: Minghui Liwang, Wenhan Jia, Xinlei Yi, Wenbo Zhu, Yuhan Su, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: FORTUNE plans 3D paths and assigns tasks for multiple UAVs under uncertain ground point-of-interest demands, modeling persistent, predictable, and emergent demand types in one framework. It adds altitude-dependent societal costs such as noise exposure and public safety risk to balance sensing quality against community impact.

entry.title: Optimization and Constraint Modeling using LLMs with a Retrieval Augmented Generation Process

author.name: Prateek Roy, Akash Singirikonda

entry.summary: The authors build a synthetic corpus of 500 optimization problems derived from Text2Zinc seeds and persona-conditioned generation, then test whether retrieval augmentation over this corpus improves LLM-generated optimization and constraint models. The focus is on combinatorial formulations where models often produce structurally inconsistent output. It is an empirical study of RAG as a fix for formal modeling errors.

entry.title: Co-evolution of social reward and punishment under institutional interventions

author.name: Van An Nguyen, Vuong Khang Huynh, Hoai Thuong Nguyen, Duc Tin Duong, An Nguyen Gia, Tat Kien Nguyen, Huu Loi Bui, My Nguyen Tra, Ho Nam Duong, Ba Thanh Phan, Thanh Vo, Dinh Anh Trung Hoang, Adeela Bashir, Zhao Song, Manh Hong Duong, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Studies replicator dynamics and lattice agent-based simulations where peer punishment and reward coexist with a central institution that can target any strategy subset. Evaluates which intervention mixes maximize cooperation and enforcement efficiency.

entry.title: Skillsets on the Chain: A Blockchain-based Zero-Trust Framework for Agentic AI Networking

author.name: Yayu Gao, Yong Xiao, Hao Hu, Xubo Li, Zhiwei Liu, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: TrustAgentNet proposes a two-tier blockchain design for agentic AI networks: a global chain governing skillset metadata lifecycle with off-chain auditing, plus transient task-specific chains for trustless multi-agent collaboration. It targets the mismatch between what third-party agent skills claim and what they actually do.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence and Modeling & Simulation: An Overview

author.name: Niclas Feldkamp, Philippe J. Giabbanelli, Istvan David

entry.summary: This overview maps the two-way relationship between AI and modeling and simulation: AI augmenting or replacing simulation components at each stage from specification through validation and output analysis, and simulation serving as data generator, training environment, and evaluation platform for AI. It is a structured community-oriented survey.

entry.title: Asking Questions the Right Way: A Multi-Agent Conversational System for Prompt Formulation in Complex Task Resolution

author.name: B. Sankar, Pawni Yadav, Srinidhi Ranjini Girish, Amogh A. S

entry.summary: PAWNI is an eight-agent conversational interface that turns unstructured user queries into structured prompts through guided question-and-answer dialogue backed by a self-evolving knowledge base, organized around 18 prompt elements in three tiers. It optimizes the question rather than the model response.

entry.title: Statistical Mechanics of Learning on Product Wasserstein Manifolds

author.name: Srinivasa Rao P Vangmayi P Reddy

entry.summary: Reframes weight-distribution constraints in learning theory as defining intrinsic geometry rather than reducing capacity, formulating deep networks and variational quantum circuits as gradient flows on products of classical and quantum Wasserstein manifolds. It applies statistical mechanics tools within this geometric setting.

entry.title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration

author.name: Zepu Wang, Jingze Liang, Weijie Xiao, Kexin Chen

entry.summary: This work jointly handles extreme low-light RAW enhancement and motion blur, contributing the SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation on real low-light RAW pairs plus a unified RAW tokenizer and a MeanFlow-based restoration model. It argues prior low-light methods ignore motion degradations that occur in practice.

entry.title: BRiG-AFA: Bellman Risk-to-Go Learning for Non-Myopic Active Feature Acquisition

author.name: Jiaorong Feng, Qian Li, Ying Li

entry.summary: BRiG-AFA learns a candidate-conditioned risk-to-go function separately for each remaining acquisition budget, fitted backward with Bellman targets from one-step terminal classification risk, to decide which feature to measure next. It offers a supervised, non-myopic alternative to greedy heuristics, deep reinforcement learning, and generative conditional density estimation.

entry.title: From fragmented data to actionable design: Physics-calibrated learning for plastic upcycling

author.name: Jingyang Bai, Zijia Wang, Xiangyi Long, Marcos Millan, Binjian Nie, Mingyue Ding

entry.summary: This work learns from heavily incomplete plastic-upcycling experiment literature by treating structured missingness as an informative signal, using a physics-calibrated, missingness-gated mixture-of-experts that avoids target imputation and reconstructs physically consistent product distributions. Complete-case learning would have discarded about 89 percent of the curated experiments.

entry.title: Schedule-Informed Temporal Fusion Forecasting of Hourly Airport Security-Checkpoint Throughput

author.name: Yinxiao Zhang, Sen Wang, Yi Gao

entry.summary: Builds an airport checkpoint throughput forecaster that converts flight schedules into passenger-arrival intensity signals using truncated Poisson kernels and feeds them to a temporal fusion transformer alongside historical throughput. Applied to two years of screening and schedule data for a major hub to support staffing decisions.

entry.title: A Hyperfinite Framework for Score-Based Generative Modeling

author.name: Sunder Ram Krishnan

entry.summary: Reformulates score-based diffusion using nonstandard analysis, starting from an internal diffusion on a hyperfinite grid and deriving the generator, the correspondence with Fokker-Planck, and a constructive reverse-time drift identity. It shows the internal score-matching objective recovers the score function.

entry.title: AI World Cup 2026: Benchmarking Large Language Models for End-to-End Football Tournament Prediction

author.name: Jonaid Shianifar, Iias Faiud

entry.summary: Reports a completed forecasting benchmark in which ten LLM assistants each produced a single pre-tournament prediction of the entire 2026 World Cup under identical snapshots, prompts, schemas, and scoring, then scored against all 104 actual matches. GPT-5.5 Thinking, an existing model, ranked first. The value lies in standardized, prospective, non-contaminated forecasting evaluation.

entry.title: Accelerating Dynamic Graph Clustering on GPU Architectures with cuGraph

author.name: Nelson Aloysio Reis de Almeida Passos, Emanuele Carlini, Salvatore Trani

entry.summary: Ports spectral clustering and modularity-based community detection to GPUs via the NVIDIA RAPIDS cuGraph ecosystem, extending them to snapshot-based dynamic graphs with multi-GPU Leiden optimization and a Bethe-Hessian eigendecomposition backend. Reports up to roughly three orders of magnitude speedup over CPU references under equal-work budgets. Infrastructure contribution for temporal graph analytics.

entry.title: Character Iconicity vs. Arbitrariness: An Arabic NLP Perspective

author.name: Dorieh Alomari, Irfan Ahmad, Maged S. Al-shaibani

entry.summary: Uses the historical fact that early undotted Arabic manuscripts remained readable to test whether dotless Arabic NLP performance depends on preserving original rasm groupings or merely on any consistent mapping to a reduced symbol set. Compares dotted, dotless, and arbitrary constrained remappings. A clean linguistic experiment on iconicity versus arbitrariness in orthographic representation.

entry.title: Localize, Don't Beautify: Client-Side Control of Image-Editing APIs for Cosmetic Surgery Previews

author.name: Sukhrobbek Ilyosbekov

entry.summary: A pilot benchmark tests how much a client can constrain commercial image-editing APIs to a requested facial region for cosmetic surgery previews, comparing prompt-only control, landmark-mask compositing, and inpainting. The finding is that closed editing APIs frequently alter unrequested attributes such as skin texture or lighting.

entry.title: Test Time Adaptation Methods for Point Cloud Registration in Laparoscopic Surgery

author.name: Nina Bodelot, Soufiane Belharbi, Eric Granger

entry.summary: The work adapts test-time adaptation techniques, originally built for classification, to 3D point cloud registration between intraoperative reconstructions and preoperative organ meshes in laparoscopy. It addresses the asymmetric synthetic-to-real domain shift where only the intraoperative cloud is noisy and occluded.

entry.title: LDU-Bench: Multimodal LLM Evaluation for Lithography Defect Understanding under Layout-Varying Circuit Backgrounds

author.name: Huanglong Ji, Botong Zhao, Shujing Lv, Yue Lv

entry.summary: LDU-Bench evaluates multimodal LLMs on lithography defect review across four tasks: triage, morphology recognition, coarse localization, and image-conditioned cause analysis, using real semiconductor review images. It tests whether models can reason about defect causes rather than only flag anomalies.

entry.title: SGFormer: Structure-Guided Transformer for Robust Local Feature Matching

author.name: Runyu Zhu

entry.summary: SGFormer identifies attention divergence in detector-free local feature matching, where unconstrained global attention places confident matches outside the true overlapping region under large viewpoint change. It adds structural guidance to focus attention on salient structures for photogrammetry and 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: Active Stiffness Control of a Supportive Continuum Robot

author.name: Rana Danesh, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi, Farhad Aghili

entry.summary: Presents an active task-space stiffness control framework for tendon-driven supportive continuum robots, where a second arm mechanically couples to the primary arm to raise load capacity. The method projects closed-chain variable-strain dynamics onto constrained coordinates so stiffness can be regulated online for varying payloads.

entry.title: Trust and Its Betrayal under Three Representational Strategies

author.name: Mihnea C. Moldoveanu, Joel A. C. Baum

entry.summary: This theoretical paper models trust as a subjunctive epistemic state, formalizing competence as the belief that the trustee would know a truth and integrity as the belief that they would disclose it. Three representations are compared: lexicographic assumption, ordinal closeness in Lewis-Stalnaker spheres, and strong belief in conditional probability systems, with attention to whether betrayal is representable in each. The relevance to AI is indirect but bears on human trust in automated agents.

entry.title: An Information Theoretic Treatment of Yager's Probability Distribution Negation

author.name: Roberto Bruno, Ugo Vaccaro

entry.summary: The paper gives an information-theoretic and majorization-based analysis of Yager's negation of a probability distribution, unifying and strengthening previously scattered properties and its generalizations. The conclusion is that Yager's definition is the principled choice under a range of criteria.

entry.title: Neural network realization of binary refinement iterates via a two-chart atlas selector

author.name: Tsogtgerel Gantumur

entry.summary: Gives a new constructive proof that finite iterates of scalar binary refinement operators admit exact ReLU network realizations with fixed width and depth growing linearly in the number of refinement steps. The difficulty addressed is that refinement is driven by discontinuous binary digit choices while ReLU networks are continuous, handled via a two-chart atlas selector.

entry.title: Distilled Roads: Generalisable Road Network Extraction Across Sensors, Resolutions, and Region

author.name: Sanayya, Rakshith Sathish, Ashwathi Nambiar

entry.summary: Reframes global road-network extraction from satellite imagery as a continual adaptation problem rather than an architecture problem, combining distillation with adaptation to handle new sensors, resolutions, and regions without full retraining or catastrophic forgetting. Targets the poor generalization of models trained on narrow region-resolution combinations. Useful for large-scale remote sensing mapping.

entry.title: Learning a Vector-Symbolic Model for Socio-Cultural Tasks

author.name: Meera Ray, Swapnika Dulam, Christopher L. Dancy

entry.summary: Proposes a declarative memory system for the ACT-R cognitive architecture using vector-symbolic representations, so that sociocultural associations and self-representations can be modeled at multiple levels of semantic abstraction. Argues co-occurrence-based LLM or corpus embeddings alone miss the role of self-representation in culturally shaped decision making. Contributes to cognitive architecture and computational social modeling.

entry.title: AIDE: Automated Instruction via Distilled Expertise for Reference-Free Motor Skill Coaching

author.name: Yoshiki Ito

entry.summary: AIDE distills a teacher that sees paired learner and expert poses into a student that generates natural-language coaching feedback from the learner's pose sequence alone at inference. This removes the need for expert reference demonstrations at deployment time.

entry.title: SeCo-SBIR: Semantically Consistent Prompt Learning for Zero-Shot Sketch-Based Image Retrieval

author.name: Long Hoang Dang, Tuan Nguyen Huu, Nguyen Minh Hieu, Tu Minh Phuong

entry.summary: SeCo-SBIR adapts CLIP for zero-shot sketch-based image retrieval by routing learnable prompts through the text encoder and injecting the resulting representations into every visual layer, aiming to bridge the sketch-photo gap without overfitting to seen categories. It explicitly balances task adaptation against retained zero-shot generalization.

entry.title: Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles for EEG--fNIRS Imagined-Handwriting Decoding

author.name: Xiao Fan, Hongbin Guo, Yubo Han, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: FRED decodes imagined handwriting from synchronized EEG and fNIRS by training compact multi-scale temporal networks on three complementary EEG frequency views and ensembling across bands. Cross-band ensemble members make less correlated errors than same-band replicas, improving subject-independent four-class accuracy.

entry.title: Recurrent Contrastive Learning for Imbalanced Medical Image Classification

author.name: Zhiyuan Zhu, Xinling Meng, Junxuan Yu, Jiongquan Chen, Qiongying Ni, Tuhang Shao, Yuhao Huang, Luping Zhou, Ruiyang Huang, Yuxue Wang, Rongliang Zhang, Xue Wang, Tianhong Tang, Likun Wang, Junbo Chen, Yong Jiang, Yongping Lu, Xin Yang

entry.summary: Recurrent Contrastive Learning tackles class imbalance in medical image classification by reusing historical feature states across training phases to enlarge the latent support region of rare classes, rather than only resampling or reweighting losses. It builds on a strong self-supervised vision backbone with lightweight adaptation.

entry.title: Detecting Pose Estimation Failures via Keypoint Self-Consistency

author.name: Robin Chan

entry.summary: This paper proposes hand-crafted geometric features capturing self-consistency among predicted 2D keypoints to flag likely failures of keypoint-based 6D pose estimation, since rigid rotations should preserve object shape. Detecting unreliable pose estimates matters for downstream robotic use.

entry.title: Compass: Degradation-Simulated Reciprocal Learning with Lightweight Needle RWKV for Multimodal Crack Segmentation under Missing Modalities

author.name: Hui Liu, Chen Jia, Fan Shi, Xu Cheng, Mianzhao Wang, Shengyong Chen

entry.summary: Compass segments cracks in industrial multimodal imagery robustly when modalities are missing, using a degradation-simulation stream that mimics worse conditions and distills reciprocally with the full-modality stream, plus a lightweight recurrent block and evidential topology-preserving fusion. The emphasis is on low compute for deployment.

entry.title: Impacts of Single-objective Landscapes on Multi-objective Optimization

author.name: Shoichiro Tanaka, Keiki Takadama, Hiroyuki Sato

entry.summary: This study examines how the local optima networks of the constituent single-objective problems relate to the Pareto optima network of the combined multi-objective combinatorial problem, decomposing the joint network into components characterized by overlap relations. Results indicate most Pareto optimal solutions are reachable from single-objective optima.

entry.title: PATH-Bench: Path-Dependent Evaluation of Lifelong Agents

author.name: Xidong Yang, Xingyi Zhang, Wenhao Li, Wenyan Liu, Junjie Sheng, Yun Hua, Wei Yin, Tao Fang, Chuyun Shen, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.01149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lifelong LLM agents increasingly adapt through external learning states that store past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills, yet ex...

entry.title: Emergence Invariance: From Symbolized Thought to Interface Refinement

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: A philosophical formalization arguing language is a consequence-governed symbolic projection of broader cognition, so language-first LLMs inherit structural incompletenesses that emergent capabilities cannot fully compensate. Introduces symbolization premises and asks whether emergence closes every missing distinction.

entry.title: SymNet: A Multi-Task Network for Joint Radio Map Reconstruction and Transmitter Localization

author.name: Lyuzhou Ye, Thanh Dat Le, Yan Huang

entry.summary: SymNet is a multi-task neural network that jointly reconstructs directional radio coverage maps and localizes the transmitter from sparse measurements, arguing that in directional propagation the strongest-signal point no longer coincides with the transmitter. The work matters for wireless network planning and spectrum management where angular effects, reflections, and building occlusion break omnidirectional assumptions.

entry.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head

author.name: Pablo Moraes, Monica Rodriguez, Christopher Peters, Hiago Sodre, Tobias Doernbach, Bruna Guterres, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: This applied case study estimates human attention for an expressive robotic head by combining a fast geometric face and head-pose layer with a slower vision-language semantic layer that labels whether a person attends to the robot, uses a phone, or looks elsewhere, fused by a finite state machine controlling interaction behavior. It is a systems integration report for adaptive human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Rethinking and formalising the state across languages: a unified computational learning theory account

author.name: Mohamed El Idrissi

entry.summary: The paper argues that the linguistic notion of state, traditionally treated as an Afroasiatic construct-state peculiarity, is a general context-dependent morphosyntactic mechanism selecting grammatical templates, and formalizes it as a set-valued function over templates within a template-based modular cognitive framework with an accompanying learning algorithm. Riffian serves as the primary empirical basis.

entry.title: Rethinking Generative AI Literacy: An Integrative, Developmental, and Dialectical Framework for K-12 Teacher Education

entry.summary: This position and review paper proposes RAIL-Ed, a framework for generative AI literacy in K-12 teacher education, developed from a systematic review of dozens of prior frameworks and studies. It treats ethics, equity, and agency as constitutive rather than add-on competencies.

entry.title: Can Urban Blight Be Accessed with Vision-language Models: A Case Study in Detroit

author.name: Xiaohao Yang, Aohua Tian, Derek Van Berkel, Xu Qiang, Mark Lindquist

entry.summary: This case study uses open-weight vision-language models with structured prompts over multiple street-level views to estimate residential blight in Detroit, scoring roof, wall, and opening conditions and comparing against survey-based references. It explores whether VLMs can replace labor-intensive periodic blight surveys.

entry.title: Multi-Source Dynamic Graph Learning for Compound-Flood Forecasting in Managed Coastal Systems

author.name: Liangjun You, Min Wu, Orlando Woods, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: An anchored multi-source dynamic graph learning framework forecasts compound coastal flooding by fusing signals from many monitoring stations while preventing cross-site fusion from destabilizing local temporal predictions. It emphasizes reproducing prolonged high-water plateaus that average error metrics hide.

entry.title: TALSC: Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration for Infrastructure-Assisted Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mengmeng Zhu, Yuxuan Sun, Wei Chen, Bo Ai

entry.summary: TALSC decides when an autonomous vehicle should offload perception to a large vision-language model at an edge server versus rely on its small on-board model, modeling age-of-information decay so that stale but accurate remote answers are not overvalued. It formalizes the accuracy-versus-timeliness trade-off in infrastructure-assisted driving.

entry.title: TBSG-Net: Temporal Bipartite Scene Graph Network for Fine-Grained Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Ji Huang, Yongsheng Dai, Tianyu Ren, Barry Devereux, Hui Wang

entry.summary: TBSG-Net replaces static frame-level scene graphs in video moment retrieval with a temporal bipartite scene graph that models how object relations evolve and explicitly encodes relation durations. This targets the loss of temporal dependencies and imprecise localization in scene-graph-based retrieval.

entry.title: GLAIM: Learning Global and Local Adaptive Inter-Variable Dependency for Multivariate Time Series Imputation

author.name: Mingyang Wang, Rongwen Li, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: GLAIM imputes missing values in multivariate time series by combining a stable global inter-variable dependency structure with adaptive per-sample local dependencies, so that local adaptivity does not propagate errors when observations are sparse. It explicitly trades off the failure modes of purely global and purely local dependency modeling.

entry.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework

author.name: Junjie Yin (Fran), Buxin She (Fran), Xinyu Feng (Fran), Fangxing (Fran), Li

entry.summary: Proposes an executable, hands-on curriculum framework for teaching AI in power and energy systems, motivated by a survey where the large majority of practitioners report setup barriers and want domain-specific courses. Advocates engineering-grounded AI workflows that respect power-system rules rather than treating models as generic black boxes.

entry.title: Designing Social Robots for Inclusive Child Wellbeing Assessment: Insights from Communities Supporting Developmental Language Disorder and Forced Migration

author.name: Fethiye Irmak Dogan, Yue Lou, Alva Markelius, Emma Geijer-Simpson, Gustaf Gredeb\"ack, Tamsin Jane Ford, Ginevra Castellano, Hatice Gunes, Georgina Warner, Jenny L. Gibson

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.03820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Assessing children's wellbeing and mental health can be particularly challenging for children experiencing communication barriers, such as children wit...

entry.title: The Bayesian Reflex: A Predictive Coding Engine for Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Sourabh Bhattacharya

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Bayesian Reflex, a framework instantiating predictive coding through hierarchical generative belief maintenance, sequential Bayesian updating by prediction-error minimization, and uncertainty-driven action via active inference. It argues that recent advances in ellipsoidal decomposition sampling, recursive Gaussian processes, and derivative-aware Bayesian optimization supply the previously missing scalable ingredients. It is a synthesis and architectural proposal rather than an empirical result.

entry.title: Supporting Cybersecurity Risk Management for Medical Devices via the SECUMAN Ontology and Shapes

author.name: Martin Diller, Anne Esslinger, Piotr Gorczyca, Evi Hartig, Lia Kacholdt, Hannes Strass

entry.summary: SECUMAN is an OWL ontology plus SHACL shapes for representing cybersecurity risk-management documentation for connected medical devices, covering risk context, assessment, control measures, and residual-risk evaluation, aligned with VDE Spec 90025. It makes consistency checking, certification review, and reuse tractable where documentation is currently semi-structured prose.

entry.title: A Unified Resolution-Conditioned Framework for Orthogonal Line-Scanning Image Fusion

author.name: Yiming Gong, Kai Wang

entry.summary: A single resolution-conditioned network fuses orthogonal line-scan microscopy images to recover near-isotropic resolution, using feature-wise linear modulation on the resolving-power ratio so one model spans many optical configurations. An adaptive linear-attention variant replaces fixed-kernel rank enhancement.

entry.title: CRIL-U-Net: Compact Ratio-Interaction Learning for Focal Cortical Dysplasia Segmentation from T1w and FLAIR MRI

author.name: Soumen Ghosh, Amit Soni Arya, Tilottama Goswami, Subhojit Mandal, John Phamnguyen, Rajat Vashistha

entry.summary: CRIL-U-Net is a 3D U-Net with a module that mixes T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI voxel-wise and through bidirectional ratio interactions rather than simple channel concatenation, targeting small and subtle focal cortical dysplasia lesions. It is compared to standard and self-attention 3D U-Nets with cross-validation.

entry.title: BayesSeg: A Bayesian Optimization Framework for State Segmentation of Electricity Consumption Time Series

author.name: Zhenya Zhang, Wendi Zhu, Ping Wang, Hongmei Cheng, Shuguang Zhang

entry.summary: BayesSeg unifies time-series segmentation, multidimensional evaluation, and automatic hyperparameter optimization for non-intrusive load monitoring, using a dual steady-state criterion based on tail values and means of preceding subsequences plus complement-set parsing to separate steady and transition segments. Bayesian optimization replaces heuristic parameter tuning. The target application is appliance recognition from household electricity data.

entry.title: Multi-Dimensional Assessment for AI Cognition (MAAC): A Theoretical Framework for Process-Oriented Cognitive Evaluation of Text-Based AI Systems

author.name: Abdalla Doleh, Ratna Babu Chinnam

entry.summary: MAAC proposes shifting AI evaluation from outcome benchmarks to process-oriented cognitive assessment, defining nine dimensions including cognitive load, tool execution, memory integration, and content quality for text-based systems. The stated goal is diagnostic insight into how systems reason rather than only what they output. The paper is a theoretical framework without reported empirical validation.

entry.title: DeBERTa-Sentinel: Toward Transparent and Trustworthy Detection of AI-Generated Text

author.name: Muhammad Yousaf Rehman, Muhammad Islam

entry.summary: DeBERTa-Sentinel detects AI-generated text using DeBERTa-v3 disentangled attention and exposes token-level explanations for transparency, targeting generalization to unseen generators and paraphrase attacks. It positions interpretability as a requirement for trustworthy detection.
