This yields finer-grained operator utility estimates than query-level or trajectory-level supervision for adaptive routing.

entry.title: Obshazard-bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Foundation Models for Real-Time Disaster Intelligence from Raw Earth Observation Streams

author.name: Fengxiang Wang, Qiuyang Yu, Yueying Li, Mingshuo Chen, Chengchi Fei, Kaiyi Xu, Lixin Gu, Wangxu Wei, Junchao Gong, Lipeng Ma, Jiong Wang, Fenghua Ling, Wenlong Zhang, Xue Yang, Wenjing Yang, Ben Fei, Long Lan

entry.summary: Obshazard-bench evaluates multimodal foundation models on real-time disaster intelligence using raw high-frequency satellite observation streams rather than curated post-event products or gridded reanalysis. Designed to reflect operational constraints where hazards evolve quickly and decisions are time-limited.

entry.title: Which Modality Decides? Counterfactual Modality Attribution for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Vahidin Hasic, Chao Wang, Luis C. Garcia-Peraza-Herrera, David Watson, Senka Krivic

entry.summary: Counterfactual Modality Attribution quantifies how much a multimodal LLM's prediction is driven by image versus text by comparing image-only, text-only and joint conditions, rather than highlighting influential regions or tokens. The aim is to expose cases where a model gets the right answer from the wrong modality, revealing shortcut learning.

entry.title: Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yibo Wan, Jinyu Cai, Seekiong-Ng

entry.summary: ReCAP replaces the fixed text prompts or learned static tokens used by CLIP-based medical anomaly detectors with input-conditioned visual prototypes, re-centering separated normal and abnormal prototypes per test image via bounded gated modulation. The aim is language-free anomaly detection and lesion localization that transfers across unseen organs and imaging modalities.

entry.title: An Embedded RISC-V Evaluation of Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks in Hard-Constrained Recurrent Physics-Informed Models

author.name: Enzo Nicolas Spotorno, Josafat Leal Filho

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks against multilayer perceptrons as the residual branch of hard-constrained recurrent physics-informed models on embedded RISC-V hardware, asking whether KAN parameter efficiency survives deployment given the very different execution profile of learnable B-spline activations. Identical trained weights are used to isolate inference cost.

entry.title: SG-Layout: Structured Scene Graph-Guided Layout Generation with LLMs

author.name: Junsheng Wang, Chao Chen, Mengying Xie, Mingyan Li, Fuqiang Gu

entry.summary: SG-Layout injects scene-graph embeddings into an LLM via a relational graph encoder and projector, then instruction-tunes with LoRA so the model generates spatially coherent layouts from natural language. Targets LLM weakness at explicit geometric relations and structural dependencies.

entry.title: DeVIT: Low-Power Vision Transformer Acceleration Using Delta Computation

author.name: Reyhaneh Hosseinzadeh, Parham Zilouchian Moghaddam, Mehdi Modarressi

entry.summary: DeVIT is a hardware accelerator design that exploits value locality in quantized vision transformers by computing on deltas between similar values to cut power and memory bandwidth. Targets deployment of transformers on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: DeepVoyager-VL: Incentivizing Vision-in-the-Loop Search for Long-Horizon Multimodal Agents

author.name: Huanyao Zhang, Jiepeng Zhou, Runhao Zhao, Yanzhe Shan, Jiaoyang Chen, Bowen Zhou, Bo Li, Fang Wang, Jialong Wu, Zhengwei Tao, Lang Mei, Xiaohan Yu, Liyan Liu, Chong Chen, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: DeepVoyager-VL trains multimodal agents to keep vision in the loop during long-horizon deep search, so visual evidence drives subsequent retrieval steps rather than only appearing at input or answer time. It targets knowledge-intensive open-world questions that static parametric knowledge cannot answer.

entry.title: Recompute or Reuse? Diagnosing and Mitigating Textual Shortcuts in VLM Self-Reflection

author.name: Wenxiao Fan, Jingling Fu, Fang Li, Luohang Liu, Yu He, Lichen Ma, Zhiyang Yu, Weishan Bi, Junshi Huang, Yan Li, Gu Simiu, Kan Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that vision-language models often reuse evidence-bearing text from a prior chain of thought instead of re-examining changed images, and that removing that evidence content shifts answers more than removing other context. Across sixteen VLMs this textual shortcut, not merely weak visual attention, explains failures of self-reflection.

entry.title: IACM-RL: Intent-Aware Context Management and Reinforcement Learning for Complex Tool Invocation under Dynamic Intent Fluctuations

author.name: Dingwei Zhu, Jiahan Li, Chengjun Pan, Yunxian Yang, Yunbin Zhao, Yunke Zhang, Zhonghang Lu, Zhuohui Sheng, Chenhao Huang, Jiahang Lin, Yajie Yang, Junlin Shang, Shichun Liu, Yuhui Wang, Honglin Guo, Junjie Ye, Xin Guo, Jiazheng Zhang, Ming Zhang, Shihan Dou, Zhiheng Xi, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: IACM-RL makes long-horizon LLM tool use robust to changing user intent by synthesizing training trajectories across thirteen fluctuation scenarios and maintaining an explicit belief state, so obsolete constraints do not dilute attention and trigger intent drift or infinite API loops. It pairs the data pipeline with a diagnostic metric suite and reinforcement learning.

entry.title: GROVE: Growing and Reasoning over Temporally Stratified Memory from Streaming Video Experience

author.name: Sitong Gong, Caixin Kang, Tianyu Yan, Guo Chen, Bo Zheng, Kaipeng Zhang, Yunzhi Zhuge, Xiang Ruan, Huchuan Lu, Yifei Huang

entry.summary: GROVE is a training-free memory framework for wearable assistants that grows causally from a continuous video stream, consolidating fine-grained perceptual evidence into time-stamped moments, episodes, and recurring cross-day patterns, each with a matched retrieval skill. One memory supports both answering questions about visual history and proactively recognizing when past experience is relevant now.

entry.title: Leak It: A Probabilistic Approach to Training-Data Extraction from Black-Box Language Models

author.name: Victor Maricato

entry.summary: Reframes black-box training-data leakage as estimating functionals of the sampling distribution and stress-tests it against model-free blind baselines. Reports that on a popular membership-inference dataset a bag-of-words classifier alone reaches near-perfect AUC while sampling-based signals add nothing, and on an IID split no signal beats blind baselines.

entry.title: On the Identifiability of Masked Prediction: Mode Blindness and Mask Schedules

author.name: Yichao Cai, Javen Qinfeng Shi

entry.summary: Asks when masked prediction objectives actually identify the underlying joint distribution, and shows that for data with two well-separated modes the answer is determined by the mask schedule alone. Schedules dominated by large visible contexts are provably blind to global mode weights, motivating an epsilon-identifiability measure.

entry.title: Meganeura: Portable GPU Training and Inference through Vulkan and Metal

author.name: Dzmitry Malyshau

entry.summary: Meganeura is a compact native compiler and runtime that performs both training and inference on consumer GPUs via Vulkan and Metal, including autodiff, optimizers, checkpointing and memory planning. It is benchmarked against PyTorch on NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and Intel hardware with strict versus fast numerical gating.

entry.title: Finite-Time Analysis of Discounted Exponential-Utility Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ankur Naskar, Vivek T A, Aditya Kumar, Gugan Thoppe, Prashanth L. A

entry.summary: Provides finite-time convergence rates of order one over root-n for two recently proposed model-free algorithms that optimize a discounted exponential-utility (risk-sensitive) objective under asynchronous Markovian sampling, using parameter-free stepsizes. This upgrades prior asymptotic-only guarantees.

entry.title: CoRe-GNN: Multilevel Message passing on Coarsened graphs

author.name: Antonin Joly, Nicolas Keriven, Aline Roumy

entry.summary: Reframes several scalable GNN training methods as structured modifications of the propagation matrix, showing graph coarsening and Cluster-GCN as complementary failure modes of the same node-grouping decomposition. CoRe-GNN combines coarsened multilevel message passing with intra-cluster propagation to reduce memory while retaining long-range information.

entry.title: Constrained Co-Design for Photonic Bayesian Neural Networks

author.name: Hendrik Borras, Xiao Wang, Bernhard Klein, Robin Janssen, Frank Br\"uckerhoff-Pl\"uckelmann, Wolfram Pernice, Holger Fr\"oning

entry.summary: Co-designs Bayesian neural networks with photonic probabilistic hardware whose analog samplers are imperfect, explicitly modeling quantization, programming error, dynamic range and representable mean and variance constraints. The goal is calibrated uncertainty and out-of-distribution robustness at low latency and energy on optical accelerators.

entry.title: Fast Trainable Multilinear Bases for Image Compression

author.name: Shiwen An, Zhongyi Ni, Huanhai Zhou, Jin-Guo Liu

entry.summary: Generalizes fixed transforms like DCT and DFT to trainable isometric multilinear bases parameterized as isometric tensor networks, adding only polylogarithmically many parameters while keeping near-linear runtime and exact invertibility. A search framework finds the basis that best compresses a given image dataset.

entry.title: Non-KKT Accumulation in Entropic Mirror Descent

author.name: Kuangyu Ding, Kim-Chuan Toh

entry.summary: Answers negatively a basic question in constrained optimization by constructing smooth objectives for which bounded entropic mirror descent sequences accumulate at non-KKT points. The mechanism is that the Legendre gradient blows up at the boundary, so the inverse entropy metric vanishes on active coordinates and destroys dual feasibility in the limit.

entry.title: Practical Online KV Cache Compaction for LLM Agents: An Empirical Study

author.name: Yujian Liu, Jiabao Ji, Li An, Rohit Jain, Gungor Polatkan, Siyu Zhu, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: Empirically studies KV cache compaction under the realistic online constraint faced by agents, where content must be compressed before future queries are known. Compares token eviction versus attention matching with cheap proxy queries on browsing and search benchmarks.

entry.title: PALMs: Using Multi Construct-Grounded Rationales for Modeling Population Preferences in LLMs

author.name: Priyanka Dey, Brihi Joshi, Preyashi Poddar, Jieyu Zhao, Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: Aligns separate model variants to five national populations by synthesizing rationales grounded in psychological and cultural constructs and using them as latent supervision during preference tuning. Evaluates on personality, values, cultural norms, and morality, outperforming baseline persona prompting.

entry.title: Global Optimization and Inference-Time Region Grafting for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Donghyeok Koh, Gyuwan Kim, Jinyeong Bak, Seung-Hoon Na, Tao Yang, Haneol Jang, Cheoneum Park

entry.summary: GRAFT keeps a globally optimized agentic workflow but replaces only failing regions at inference time, using label-free execution-quality signals to accept local substitutions. This avoids the prohibitive cost of re-optimizing an entire workflow per input while still allowing runtime adaptation.

entry.title: Image-Space Rule Discovery

author.name: Misora Sugiyama, Toya Oyama, Hirokatsu Kataoka

entry.summary: WISRD tests whether image-editing models can read instructions embedded in images, infer the underlying visual rule, and produce correctly edited outputs, covering marking, filling, copying, counting, and suppression of unnecessary edits. It frames the evaluation like a human worksheet or nonverbal IQ test across eleven core tasks and multiple information conditions.

entry.title: Dynamic Resolution Routing for Efficient Egocentric Grounding

author.name: Huixin Sun, Wangbo Zhao, Fanyue Wei, Qiuxia Lin, Pengzhan Sun, Angela Yao

entry.summary: SmartRes cuts the cost of high-resolution egocentric grounding by routing computation in pixel space: a low-resolution global pass plus a lightweight router that selectively upsamples object-centric patches. Argues token-pruning approaches are unreliable for selecting spatial evidence.

entry.title: DiffPrune: differentiable information throttling for token pruning in vision-language models

author.name: Landi He, Mingde Yao, Shawn Young, Lijian Xu

entry.summary: DiffPrune trains visual token pruning scores by continuously throttling each token's information during training rather than using Gumbel-Softmax discrete relaxations, so scores directly reflect the cost of information loss. Yields interpretable importance scores tied to task degradation.

entry.title: GIFT: Geometry-Invariant Fine-Tuning for Non-Lambertian Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Xianghui Fan, Zhaoyu Chen, Bingqian Wu, Dayu Li, Xin Zeng, Huanran Cui, Guangzhen Xu, Xiangru Huang, Hang Yang

entry.summary: GIFT fine-tunes monocular depth foundation models so they stop hallucinating reflected or transmitted content on mirrors and glass, exploiting the insight that surface geometry is invariant while appearance changes with the environment. It is parameter-efficient and needs no ground-truth depth measurements.

entry.title: Assistant Placement Aria: A Benchmark for Egocentric Placement Assistance

author.name: Amir Belder, Gon\c{c}alo Dias Pais, Refael Vivanti, Omri Carmi, Daniel DeTone, Oren Shrout, Ido Gattegno, Ayellet Tal

entry.summary: Assistant Placement Aria introduces a benchmark for virtual placement, the task of identifying all plausible locations to put an object given scene geometry, semantics, and human-centric constraints, rather than a single predefined target. It uses egocentric data and involves researchers associated with egocentric perception hardware.

entry.title: Motif-Mamba: network motif improved mamba for long-range sequence modeling

author.name: Chonghe Hao, Yue Sun, Jian Zhang, Yansong Wang, Wangzi Yao, Yunjie Yao, Tielin Zhang

entry.summary: Motif-Mamba augments state space models with a low-rank recurrent pathway inspired by three-node network motifs, adding cross-dimensional state interactions that plain diagonal Mamba transitions lack. The aim is better long-range sequence modeling at linear cost.

entry.title: RMSWeb: Reflection, Failure-Mode Mining, and Salvage-DS for Web Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Chengbo Liu, Lifang Zhou, Ruijie Yan, Pei Tan, Ao Sun, Haojun Huang, Guichun Hua, Sining Wei, Yining Chen, Yingying He, Yutao Xie

entry.summary: RMSWeb is a training recipe for compact web agents combining reflection-conditioned retries to collect better trajectories, mining of failure modes to focus data, and a salvage mechanism giving learning signal to groups rejected by group-relative RL. It is applied to 8B and 32B vision-language backbones.

entry.title: Mask-Based Priors Are More Persistent than Query-Key Initializations

author.name: Mingze Ma, Hemanth Saratchandran, Cameron Gordon, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Studies why Transformers extrapolate wrongly on Boolean tasks, defaulting to a minimum-degree interpolator, and asks whether structural priors injected into attention can fix it. It finds that priors imposed through attention masks persist through training far better than priors imposed via query-key initialization.

entry.title: CURE: Local Uncertainty Repair for Block-Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: CURE improves block-parallel speculative decoding by observing that draft errors concentrate at a few high-uncertainty tokens, then spending a limited repair budget on a dynamic tree that fixes those focal points. This raises acceptance rates without heavy tree-verification overhead.

entry.title: Through the LENS: Local Geometric Decomposition of Vision-Language Model Representations

author.name: Shalom Kachko, Raz Lapid, Margarita Vald, Almog Dubin, Moshe Sipper

entry.summary: LENS decomposes vision-language model activations into locally low-rank Gaussian neighborhoods using a mixture of factor analyzers, capturing structure that global linear probing methods miss. Applied to two open VLMs it reveals distinct depth-dependent modality fusion trajectories matching each model's architecture.

entry.title: Measurement Without Validity: The Compounding Reliability Problem in Agentic AI Evaluation

author.name: William Caban

entry.summary: Argues that agentic AI benchmark scores are less trustworthy than deployment and compliance decisions assume, citing validity flaws found in seven of ten audited benchmarks, large variance between LLM user simulators, and compounding unreliability across evaluation layers. It warns about regulatory reliance on such scores.

entry.title: The Scaling Paradox in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Anyan Qi, Mengxin Wang

entry.summary: Develops an analytical model of when scaling-law improvements in AI capability actually translate into better joint human-AI performance, showing positive scaling requires humans to perceive AI capability accurately. Human misperception can break or even reverse the benefit of a stronger model.

entry.title: Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals: Separating Matching and Content Retrieval Across Depth

author.name: Kehan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Role-Decoupled Attention Residuals, which let a Transformer layer read queries and keys from one depth-mixture of earlier representations while values read from an independently learned depth route. The motivating claim is that deciding where attention matches and what content it retrieves are functionally distinct and should not be tied to the same layer.

entry.title: Perspectives on Tsallis Statistics for Artificial Intelligence

author.name: Kleyton da Costa, Bernardo Modenesi

entry.summary: A structured survey and perspective on how Tsallis statistics, controlled by a single entropic parameter, already underpins sparse attention such as sparsemax and entmax, maximum-entropy RL with tunable exploration, heavy-tailed probabilistic models, and generalized losses. It proposes viewing these as instances of one framework and sketches open directions.

entry.title: CraftAlign: Feature-Grounded Evaluation and Revision Guidance for AI Stories

author.name: Yang Yang, Boyun Xu, Shaofeng Liang, Yun Han, Zining Zhong, Songning Lai, Kaishen Yuan, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: CraftAlign evaluates AI-generated stories against craft-level features such as cliche density, over-explanation, linear causality, and stereotyped endings, and turns those diagnostics into story-wide revision guidance rather than local edits. It targets the recognizable flatness of machine fiction beyond binary human-versus-AI detection.

entry.title: KoVRE: Training an Efficient Embedding Model for Korean Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Yongbin Choi, Gyuho Shim, Youngjoon Jang

entry.summary: KoVRE is a single-vector Korean visual document retrieval embedding model trained on roughly 709k Korean and English query-page pairs with positive-aware hard-negative mining, plus controlled ablations on data composition and negative selection. It targets the English-centric and storage-heavy nature of existing document-image retrievers.

entry.title: CockpitHAT: Dependency-Graph-Driven Hierarchical Attribution for Embodied Multi-Agent Cockpits

author.name: Wei Wang, Shuanghe Liu, Zhu Zhuo, Jiaqi Zhong, Xiaozhao Zhao, Xiaojie Zuo, Jie Su

entry.summary: CockpitHAT attributes failures in embodied multi-agent automotive cockpit systems where high task accuracy masks dangerous process-level errors, replacing positional text windows with dependency-distance thresholds from interaction graphs and adding multi-channel embodied evidence. It weights high-risk failures more heavily during confidence-weighted consensus among analyst models.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Complex Eigenfrequency Identification and Mode Structure Reconstruction of the Ground-State ITG Branch

author.name: Dengdi Sun, Bingbing Zhang, Xiao Wang, Zikang Yan, Yuqiang Tao, Qingquan Yang, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: Applies physics-informed neural networks to simultaneously identify complex eigenfrequencies and reconstruct two-dimensional complex-valued mode fields for ion-temperature-gradient drift waves in the steep-gradient edge of high-confinement tokamak plasmas. It addresses localized high-frequency oscillations and strong coupling between mode field and eigenfrequency that destabilize joint PINN optimization.

entry.title: Evolving in the Agent Jungle via History-Informed Opponent Awareness

author.name: Zhaofeng Zhang, Linhan Xia, Rui Liu, Yihao Wang, Binrui Shen, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: OASE addresses skill-library evolution when opponents are also adapting, so the reference point for judging a skill revision is constantly stale. It uses paired comparisons between candidate and incumbent skills to keep only revisions that are genuinely beneficial in a moving multi-agent environment.

entry.title: Before Reasoning Fails: Pre-Evidence Procedural Failures in Agentic RAG

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: Studies a procedural failure mode where agentic RAG systems retrieve snippets but answer without reading them, separating pre-evidence discipline failures from post-read reasoning failures across 12,000 paired trajectories. Proposes Read-Gate, a runtime invariant forcing a read after each search.

entry.title: From Profiling to Synthesis: Benchmarking Implicit Behavioral Alignment in Personalized LLM Agents

author.name: Jiajia Song, Bobo Li, Haiwen Yi, Zibo Ji, Meishan Zhang, Hao Fei, Min Zhang, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu

entry.summary: IBA-Bench evaluates whether personalized agents actually act on user preferences inferred from noisy longitudinal interaction histories, rather than just answering questions about a stated profile. It names the gap between knowing a preference and executing on it as the knowledge-to-action gap.

entry.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures

author.name: Sunny Dubey

entry.summary: Trains cheap one-class monitors on healthy agent runs to detect mid-episode failures such as looping, tool-error cascades, goal drift and fabrication from step telemetry alone, avoiding per-step LLM judging. On 2,823 episodes across three frameworks and four models an echo-state-network ensemble with CUSUM alarms catches about 71 percent of failures at a 5 percent false-alarm budget.

entry.title: GRAIN: Molecules Are Not the Right Granularity -- Active-Ingredient Modeling for Safe Medication Recommendation

author.name: Juao Fan, Jinhan Li, Shengxin Zhu

entry.summary: GRAIN reframes medication recommendation from electronic health records around active ingredients rather than drug codes or molecular substructures, using a selective state-space backbone over long irregular patient visit histories. The claim is that active-ingredient granularity better matches how drug-drug interaction knowledge is actually organized, improving accuracy while reducing polypharmacy risk.

entry.title: Unleashing the Potential of Large Language Models: A Blueprint for Real-Time, Enterprise-Ready Deployments

author.name: Muhammad Faizan Raza (Luna), Shuo (Luna), Yang, Satish Mahadevan Srinivasan, Joanna F. DeFranco

entry.summary: This blueprint paper presents an integrated LLMOps architecture for real-time regulated deployments, combining adaptive data ingestion, continual learning with sparse temporal adapter routing and freshness-aware replay, an SLO-aware adaptive retrieval policy that predicts per-query passage budgets, and automated human-in-the-loop feedback. Each component is framed as a reusable software design pattern with an associated benchmark.

entry.title: AiFlow: Token-Native Reactive Orchestration with Bounded Backpressure for Streaming LLM Applications

author.name: Qunhui Zhang

entry.summary: AiFlow proposes a token-native reactive orchestration model for streaming LLM applications, normalizing provider token deltas into typed events on a directed streaming graph where each node enforces local queue bounds, concurrency, ordering, overflow policy, cancellation propagation and retry discipline. It replaces the ad hoc callback code most frameworks leave to developers for backpressure management.

entry.title: Loanword or Switch? The Annotation Boundary, Not the Model, Drives Kazakh-Russian Code-Switching Identification

author.name: Bogdan Savelyev

entry.summary: This work releases a document-level gold language-identification set for Kazakh-Russian social text with guidelines that count integrated borrowings as Kazakh and reserve the mixed label for clause-level switching, plus a mixed-only sentiment pool for a filter-first cascade. Comparing FastText, Lingua, HeLI variants, character-trigram naive Bayes and XLM-R shows the bottleneck is the loanword-versus-switch annotation boundary rather than model choice.

entry.title: FL-OA: A Byzantine-Robust Federated Learning Framework with Outsourced Auditing for Intelligent Devices

author.name: Hongliang Zhang, Zhongyuan Yu, Fenghua Xu, Teng Hu, Jian Meng, Jiguo Yu

entry.summary: FL-OA is a Byzantine-robust federated learning framework that outsources auditing of client updates, aiming to drop assumptions like a majority of honest clients or a server-side clean root dataset. It also addresses divergence among benign updates and high-dimensional comparison difficulty.

entry.title: Imprecise Belief Fusion Improves Multi-agent Social Learning

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Jonathan Lawry, Michael Crosscombe

entry.summary: Models social learning where agents hold propositional-logic beliefs and combine them with a fusion operator parametrised by imprecision, then asks whether more imprecise fusion improves collective accuracy. Uses both difference-equation and agent-based analyses to show benefits of imprecision.

entry.title: Disagree to Accelerate: Closing the Loop on Diffusion Feature Forecasts

author.name: Yanchao Li, Jiaqing Xie, Ben Gao, Wanhao Liu, Yanbo Wang, T. Y. Tsui, Jinfei Liu, Yuqiang Li, Tianfan Fu

entry.summary: This paper accelerates diffusion sampling by treating the disagreement between two cheap feature forecasts as a free runtime reliability signal, then adaptively deciding how much to trust cached forecasts at each skipped step. It converts open-loop feature caching into a closed-loop, confidence-gated scheme.

entry.title: Analytic Planning under Uncertainty with Moment Closure

author.name: Shishir Sharma, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Presents DiffeoAfford, which derives surgical visual-attention labels retrospectively from completed laparoscopic procedures by combining diffeomorphism-constrained tissue tracking with instrument trajectories, avoiding manual per-frame annotation. The resulting real-time predictor drives an auto-framing camera assistant reported to reduce surgeon cognitive workload.

entry.title: Agentic Bayesian Optimization through Surrogate-Augmented Autoresearch

author.name: Paul Brunzema, Louis Tiao, Nhat Le, Kevin De Angeli, Yao Xuan, Djordje Gligorijevic

entry.summary: Combines Bayesian optimization with an LLM agent that can flexibly consult surrogates, documentation, and code rather than being pinned to a single fixed role such as surrogate or acquisition proxy. The goal is to inject informal domain priors while preserving BO systematic exploration guarantees.

entry.title: Distill What the Student Can See: Fisher-Projected On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Leyan Xue, Feng Xiong, Mingjun Ma, Changqing Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that on-policy distillation wrongly assumes the full teacher distribution is an appropriate target regardless of student capacity, showing empirically that students realize less of the prescribed shift as targets approach the full teacher. Proposes projecting teacher signals onto directions the student can actually represent, using Fisher information, for vision-language reasoning.

entry.title: Conformalized Large Language Models under Configuration Shift

author.name: Yuqicheng Zhu, Jialin Yu, Lin Li, Gengyuan Zhang, Zhen Yang, Steffen Staab, Puneet Dokania, Philip Torr, Jie Tang, Evgeny Kharlamov

entry.summary: Points out that conformal prediction for LLMs depends on the whole inference pipeline, so changing prompt templates, decoding parameters, or deployment settings can silently break exchangeability and coverage guarantees. Systematically measures this configuration shift along three axes.

entry.title: Uncertainty Is Not Enough: Value-of-Information Routing for Mixtures of LoRA Experts

author.name: Tom Saliencro, Rohan Desai, Priya Nair, Maya Lindqvist, Daniel Whitmore

entry.summary: VI-MoLE argues that uncertainty-triggered expert activation in mixtures of LoRA adapters conflates uncertainty with useful extra computation, and instead learns the counterfactual risk remaining after each expert prefix to allocate a global adapter budget by certified value of information. Calibration data yields simultaneous upper-risk certificates for the routing decisions.

entry.title: QR-Erase: Efficient Subspace-Based Machine Unlearning with Layer Localization

author.name: Tyler Lizzo, Larry Heck

entry.summary: Introduces a machine unlearning method that uses pivoted QR decomposition instead of expensive SVD to identify and remove task-specific subspaces from model weights, with a variant that restricts edits to the layers most concentrated in target information. The authors provide subspace recovery error bounds under a spectral gap assumption.

entry.title: Training Small LLMs as Spatial Multi-Agent Policies

author.name: Yi Mao, Andrew Perrault

entry.summary: Shows that small frozen LLMs prompted with low-level actions fail entirely at spatial cooperative games, then equips each game with a library of symbolic short-horizon options drafted by a frontier coding model and executed by a planner. Training then targets option selection within a macro-action decentralized POMDP framework, making small LLMs viable multi-agent policies.

entry.title: Private Generative Bootstrap via Blocking

author.name: Jinwon Sohn, Veronika Ro\v{c}kov\'a

entry.summary: Proposes a differentially private Bayesian bootstrap that assigns random weights to randomly formed groups of individuals rather than to individuals, so that each person's contribution is masked within a block. Combines this with amortized inference so private learning is decoupled from posterior sampling.

entry.title: Beyond Modern Asymptotics for Log-Likelihood Ratios in Logistic Regression

author.name: Hugo Chardon, Reese Pathak, Nikita Zhivotovskiy

entry.summary: Characterizes, up to constants, the finite-sample worst-case behaviour of the log-likelihood ratio statistic in logistic regression uniformly over designs, giving a nonasymptotic analogue of the classic Wilks chi-squared result. Low-dimensional cases show surprising iterated-logarithm scaling.

entry.title: Bridging the English-Arabic Medical Knowledge Gap: Targeted Low-Rank Adaptation via Causal Layer Selection

author.name: Chaimae Abouzahir, Musa Khan, Hala Ali-Hassan, Congbo Ma, Khaled Saleh, Yousra Sadqi, Jihad Mallat, Walid Al-Eisawi, Nizar Habash, Farah E. Shamout

entry.summary: Uses tuned lens probing and causal activation patching to show that Arabic medical knowledge is present in intermediate layers of LLMs but fails to reach the output, then applies low-rank adaptation only to the layer window where cross-lingual representations diverge. This targeted tuning outperforms broader fine-tuning on Arabic medical question answering.

entry.title: The Learning Objective Governs Perceptual Narrowing: A Cross-Lingual, Layer-Wise, Ten-Seed Study of Self-Supervised Speech Encoders

author.name: Sejin Yoo

entry.summary: Trains small speech transformers on child-directed and read speech to ask which self-supervised objective reproduces the developmental loss of non-native phoneme discrimination. Finds reconstruction objectives degrade non-native discrimination while predictive contrastive objectives improve it, with ten-seed statistical replication.

entry.title: RAGOCR: Optical Compression of Retrieval-Augmented Text via Visual Representation

author.name: Jiayang Yu, Jialun Zhong, Lei Zou

entry.summary: Compresses retrieved documents for RAG into compact visual representations conditioned on the query, combining the query awareness of hard compression with the high ratios of soft compression. Uses optical or image-based encoding to shrink long retrieved contexts.

entry.title: Exemplars in Disguise: Pure Exemplar Models Mimic Abstraction-First Learning

author.name: Zachary Nicholas Houghton, Vsevolod Kapatsinski

entry.summary: Challenges recent claims that language models learn abstract class-level generalizations before item-specific knowledge, showing that pure memorizing exemplar models can appear to do either depending on their sensitivity to individual observations. Argues the diagnostic methods used cannot distinguish the two hypotheses.

entry.title: ShiJianBench: From Dialogue to Decision for Long-Horizon Evaluation of Investment Advisors

author.name: Jie Gong, Maowei Jiang, Zhiwei Liu, Yang Qiao, Wenxi Wu, Mengxi Xiao, Enze Zhang, Ziyan Kuang, Yankai Chen, Caishuang Huang, Meng Zhou, Xiku Du, Xue Liu, Guojun Xiong, Min Peng, Qianqian Xie, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: Introduces an offline framework for evaluating conversational investment advisors by simulating matched investor trajectories with stateful, motive-driven agent investors under fixed historical market feedback, calibrated against behaviour from over 7,000 real users. Shifts evaluation from response quality to downstream decision consequences.

entry.title: A Triple-Robustness Analysis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Requirements Traceability

author.name: Meftun Akarsu, Burak \"Ozdemir, Do\u{g}ancan B\"uy\"uk\c{c}olak, Recep Kaan Karaman

entry.summary: Runs a triple-robustness study of graph-based versus vector retrieval for multi-hop requirements traceability, varying embedder, corpus, and judge across thousands of runs. A key finding is that graph retrieval floods the context at low retrieved-set precision while the synthesizer nonetheless cites selectively, meaning conclusions flip depending on where citation quality is measured.

entry.title: CultureVidBench: Benchmarking Cultural Understanding in Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Xianjing Han, Yuhan Su, Yang Deng, Dong Ma, Wee Peng Tay, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: CultureVidBench provides 1,000 prompts spanning twelve countries and fourteen cultural aspects to test whether text-to-video models render culturally specific objects, rituals, visible text, and audio cues. Existing video benchmarks focus on perceptual quality and text alignment rather than cultural fidelity.

entry.title: From Pixels to PCells: A Neurosymbolic Approach to Photonic Component Creation

author.name: Aadarsh Agarwal, Kenaish Al Qubaisi, Dirk Englund

entry.summary: PixCell has multimodal agents convert an image of a photonic component into a parametric program over a small geometric domain-specific language, with deterministic rendering making verification much cheaper than generation. Agents using the verifier interface reach mean overlap above 0.9 versus roughly 0.42 for multi-seed sampling with revision.

entry.title: DreamTraj: Generating 6-DoF Object Trajectories by Reading Unrendered Video Diffusion Latents

author.name: Tongsheng Ding, Zhen Luo, Yixuan Yang, Boyu Wang, Luyang Xie, Jinyu Yang, Feng Zheng

entry.summary: Releases over 5,000 egocentric object-centric manipulation trajectories paired with fine-grained language instructions, and proposes predicting six-degree-of-freedom object trajectories by reading unrendered video diffusion latents from a single RGB image plus instruction. This avoids the cost and error of generating full videos then running perception pipelines.

entry.title: Zero-Cost Virtual RNA: Approximating Immunotherapy Signatures via Cross-Modal WSI Retrieval

author.name: Sigrid Vila-Bagaria, Mar Teixid\'o, Miquel Pi\~nol, Felip Vilardell, Robert Montal, Veronica Vilaplana

entry.summary: VITA aligns histopathology slide images with RNA expression in a shared latent space so that, at test time, only a standard stained slide is needed to retrieve similar historical cases and approximate a costly 10-gene immunotherapy signature for gastric cancer. It reports moderate accuracy and rank correlation, positioning retrieval as a cheaper proxy for transcriptomic assays.

entry.title: Mitigating Visual Degradation in MLLMs via Spatial-Spectral Visual Anchor Learning

author.name: Qianlong Yang, Bowen Ye, Xianda Guo, Yanlun Peng, Wenke Huang, Hongyuan Zhang, Yulei Jia

entry.summary: Diagnoses that multimodal LLM internal visual representations drift away from their original semantics after visual instruction tuning, and shows that simply aligning with external vision foundation models does not fix the drift. Introduces anchor prompts that absorb vision-model knowledge to stabilize representations.

entry.title: Learning Where to Look and How to Judge: Resolution-agnostic Image Quality Assessment with Quality-aware Saliency

author.name: Hakan Emre Gedik, Shashank Gupta, Alan Bovik

entry.summary: ReLIQS is a CLIP-based no-reference image quality model that operates at native resolution with quality-aware saliency, trains jointly across datasets with mismatched subjective score scales, and adapts to compute budgets. Aims to fix resizing-induced loss of quality cues.

entry.title: PhotoHOI: Synthesizing 3D Hand-Object Interactions from a Single RGB Photograph

author.name: Zhenhao Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Wei Min, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: PhotoHOI synthesizes 3D hand-object interaction sequences from one RGB photo plus a free-form language instruction, using a vision-language model to parse the scene into a structured task specification before recovering compact 3D geometry and generating motion. Removes the need for predefined object meshes or trajectories.

entry.title: ASTRA: Asynchronous Spatio-Temporal Reconstruction via Trajectory Alignment

author.name: Junyu Zhu, Hao Zhu, Xinzhuo Zhang, Hongdong Li, Zhan Ma, Xun Cao

entry.summary: ASTRA reconstructs dynamic 3D scenes when multi-camera captures are temporally unsynchronized, replacing photometric offset estimation with trajectory alignment. It identifies texture-induced collapse and deformation-induced coupling as the reasons appearance-based synchronization fails.

entry.title: SPIRIT: Spatio-temporal Pairwise Relational Modeling of Instrument-Tissue Interactions for Surgical Action Triplet Recognition

author.name: Saurav Sharma, Lorenzo Arboit, Nabani Banik, Sarah Meuli, Julia Alekseenko, Jan Liechti, Franziska Heitzinger, Michela Orsi, Didier Mutter, Daniel Gero, Philipp C. Nett, Beat P. Muller, Joel L. Lavanchy, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: SPIRIT models pairwise spatio-temporal relations between instruments and tissue to recognize surgical action triplets, with explicit attention to whether learned representations transfer across hospitals. Includes multi-center evaluation that prior triplet datasets did not support.

entry.title: A General-Purpose VLM Can Teach an Astronomy Foundation Model to Better Recognize Galaxy Morphology

author.name: Dichang Zhang, Jiaqi Deng, Yixuan Shao, Yuanpeng Liu, Jiali Cui, Zhiqiang Lao, Heather Yu, Liang Peng, Simon Birrer, Dimitris Samaras

entry.summary: Shows that general-purpose vision-language model question answering contains useful visual-semantic priors that can weakly supervise galaxy morphology classifiers, improving results under tight human labeling budgets. Introduces a survey-oriented visual question answering benchmark and finds current models informative but not reliable enough to replace expert labels.

entry.title: Learning to Tessellate: Point Cloud Generation via Recursive Spectral Partitioning

author.name: Monan Sun, Bangzhen Liu, Huaidong Zhang, Shengfeng He

entry.summary: PointRSP reframes autoregressive point cloud generation as a topology-preserving tessellation, using recursive spectral partitioning to build a non-balanced binary tree of tokens instead of heuristic spatial sorting or random downsampling. The goal is to keep generated shapes structurally coherent by respecting intrinsic point cloud topology during tokenization.

entry.title: GenTrack: Physical Alignment for Robot-Native Motion Generation and Zero-Shot Humanoid Tracking

author.name: Zeyu Ling, Xinyao Yu, Renye Yan, Jikang Cheng, Zhanke Wang, Qing Shuai, Changqing Zou

entry.summary: GenTrack alternates between aligning a text-to-motion generator using execution feedback and retraining a humanoid tracker on the newly generated references, closing the loop between motion synthesis and robot executability. It is evaluated on a Unitree G1 with two tracking backbones across zero-shot tracking settings.

entry.title: Grasp Execution Without a Planner: Configuration-Space Grasp Distance Fields with Certified Safety & Guaranteed Quality

author.name: Clinton Enwerem, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: Grasp Distance Fields define a smooth softmin distance field over valid grasp configurations in arm-hand configuration space, so a stationary feedback controller can execute a grasp by descending its gradient without a planner, stored trajectory, or explicit grasp selection. Safety is enforced by filtering commands through a control barrier and Lyapunov function quadratic program covering self-collision, workspace, object, and obstacle constraints.

entry.title: Sparse Meets Dense: Correspondence Guided Robotic Manipulation with Rigid-Deformable Interactions

author.name: Ziyu Zhu, Yue Chen, Xirui Liang, Hojin Bae, Yuran Wang, Zhen Yuan, Ruihai Wu, Hao Dong

entry.summary: This work proposes a hybrid sparse-and-dense correspondence representation tailored to rigid-deformable interactions such as hanging clothes or dressing, arguing that 6D poses or structural keypoints cannot capture the rich multi-point contacts and deformable dynamics involved. Structure-, task-, and interaction-aware correspondences are combined to guide manipulation.

entry.title: Learning Smooth SE(3) Trajectories under Left-Invariant Riemannian Metrics

author.name: Yuwei Wu, Vijay Kumar

entry.summary: A learning-based approach to approximating smooth higher-order rigid-body trajectories on SE(3) under general left-invariant Riemannian metrics, avoiding expensive boundary value solvers. It aims to make geometrically consistent trajectory generation fast enough for real-time planning.

entry.title: AffordTrajDP: Dynamic Affordance-Guided Visuomotor Policy Learning for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Gaoyuan Wu, Ziyu Shan, Haoyang Du, Yuyao Jiang, Ziwei Wang

entry.summary: AffordTrajDP replaces static contact-point affordances with dynamic affordance trajectories propagated over time in an object-centric frame, guiding visuomotor policies through the whole manipulation. This aims to prevent post-contact trajectory drift in precision-critical tasks.

entry.title: TRACE: Ergodic Trajectory Optimization for Active Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Ziyue Zheng, Linli Shi, Bingkun He, Wen Jiang, Ziyun Wang

entry.summary: TRACE reframes active 3D reconstruction with Gaussian splatting as ergodic coverage, where the time-averaged sensor trajectory should match an information distribution derived online from map uncertainty and visibility. This replaces greedy next-best-view selection plus short-horizon path stitching.

entry.title: MixedComplementarityProblems.jl: A Fast, Batched, Open-Source Interior Point Solver for Mixed Complementarity Problems

author.name: David Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: An open-source Julia interior-point solver for parametric mixed complementarity problems, which encode optimality conditions of nonlinear programs and noncooperative games common in multi-agent robot planning. It matches the closed-source PATH solver on benchmarks while adding batched GPU parallelism and automatic differentiation support.

entry.title: A Statistical Framework for Data-Driven Discovery of Differential Performance in Clinical Risk Prediction Models

author.name: Aidan Neher, Julian Wolfson

entry.summary: A statistical framework that discovers, rather than pre-specifies, subgroups where a clinical risk prediction model performs differentially, including intersectional subgroups defined by multiple characteristics. This addresses the limitation that current fairness audits require analysts to name the groups in advance.

entry.title: Coordinate Optimality Reformulation for Mixed-Integer Convex Programs with Indicators

author.name: Tong Xu, Salar Fattahi, Andr\'es G\'omez, Simge K\"u\c{c}\"ukyavuz

entry.summary: CORe augments mixed-integer convex formulations with indicator variables by adding coordinate-wise optimality conditions, tightening relaxations while preserving global optimality. The reformulations substantially improve branch-and-bound performance on sparse and structured problems such as sparse regression.

entry.title: Why biological weapons are scary, and what we can do about it

author.name: djbinder

entry.summary: An accessible explainer on why engineered biological weapons pose extreme catastrophic risk, using dose-lethality comparisons to convey the potency of pathogens relative to chemical and physical threats, and outlining mitigation directions. It is aimed at building intuition for biosecurity priorities.

entry.title: AI in Mathematics, 2026: From Assistant to Top Researcher

author.name: Ondřej_Kubů

entry.summary: A working mathematician surveys how quickly AI systems moved from executing routine steps to selecting research direction in mathematics during 2026, updating an earlier talk after rapid developments. The post mixes firsthand disciplinary observation with commentary on incentives and the migration of talent to AI labs.

entry.title: Introducing our Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Interconnects launches two free public resources: an artifacts hub tracking trending open models with inference-token and capability data, and an adoption dashboard tracking downloads and derivative models by geography and organization. The stated aim is to quantify open model ecosystem adoption and the US-China gap.

entry.title: TaPR: Test-Aware Policy Refinement for Feedback-Conditioned Code Generation

author.name: Aofan Liu, Jingxiang Meng, Fangxin Liu, Yongbiao Chen

entry.summary: TaPR converts execution feedback into dense per-turn rewards based on test-pass ratio for multi-turn code agents, correcting the mismatch created by single-shot outcome rewards that conflate first-attempt generation with self-repair. It reports improved three-turn success across six models on LiveCodeBench problems.

entry.title: HALT: Verification-Aware Stopping for Retrieval-Augmented Search Agents

author.name: Daeyoung Roh, Donghee Han

entry.summary: HALT decides when a retrieval-augmented search agent should stop searching by checking whether accumulated evidence covers each required hop claim, rather than trusting generator confidence. It cuts redundant retrieval on three multi-hop QA benchmarks while roughly preserving exact-match accuracy.

entry.title: Hard Constraints, Smooth Gradients: Learning Feasible Inventory Policies via Differentiable Projection

author.name: Patrick Helm, Jan-Niklas Doerr, Joren Gijsbrechts, Stefan Minner

entry.summary: Embeds a differentiable quadratic-program projection plus a dual-informed integer mapping inside an RL policy so inventory decisions satisfy hard interacting feasibility constraints rather than being penalized after the fact. Combines MILP-style constraint handling with scalable learned policies.

entry.title: SkillTrace: Traversing a Query-Skill Graph for Composable LLM Agents

author.name: Yue Yao, Shengyuan Wang, Xin Chen, Minke Zhang, Jia He, Bingjun Luo, Tom Gedeon

entry.summary: SkillTrace formulates skill composition as traversal over a three-level graph capturing compositional relations among sub-queries, query-to-skill similarity, and dependencies among selected skills. Reports state-of-the-art composition results on a skills benchmark and ALFWorld.

entry.title: RubricReviewer: From Direct Critique to Objective and Comprehensive Rubric-Driven Peer Review

author.name: Shuyu Guo, Wenxiang Hu, Yuyue Zhao, Yougang Lyu, Xiaohui Yan

entry.summary: RubricReviewer makes rubric generation an explicit intermediate step in automated peer review, separating criteria derivation from judgement to avoid both undirected training-free critiques and noisy imitation of human scores. Aims for more objective and comprehensive machine-generated reviews.

entry.title: MemoryForge: Synthesize Lifelong Memory for Human-Like LLM Agents

author.name: Bohan Tang, Yiwen Guo

entry.summary: MemoryForge replaces static persona prompts with synthesized autobiographical lifelong memory bases that frozen LLMs retrieve from situationally to produce more consistent, human-like role behavior. Formalizes customized lifelong memory synthesis as the enabling task for memory-based conditioning.

entry.title: DLLM-TTS: Block Discrete Diffusion Language Model for Text-to-Speech Synthesis

author.name: Wasim Madha, Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana, Akshat Mandloi, Sudarshan Kamath

entry.summary: DLLM-TTS formulates text-to-speech as conditional block discrete diffusion over neural audio codec tokens, applying masked diffusion within blocks while processing blocks sequentially. Achieves parallel in-block token prediction for fast synthesis while retaining global text-speech alignment.

entry.title: Width, Memory, and Delay: A Resource Accounting for the Limits of Flat Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Oleksandr Kuznetsov, Emanuele Frontoni

entry.summary: Rebuts a recent claim that flat homogeneous multi-agent systems face an irreducible population-independent error floor removable only by hierarchy, using a disturbance-rejection testbed with a computable optimum. Replaces the claim with a resource model trading off population width, per-agent internal-model memory, and communication delay.

entry.title: Boosting Generalizable Depth Estimation in Endoscopy by Mixture of Lightweight Experts and Intrinsic Image Alignment

author.name: Liangjing Shao, Beilei Cui, Yiming Huang, Changjing Liu, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EndoMINI is a self-supervised depth and ego-motion estimation framework for endoscopy that uses a mixture of low-rank experts for parameter-efficient adaptation across diverse scenes and adds an intrinsic image alignment loss to suppress specular reflectance effects. It targets generalization across illumination and tissue appearance variation in surgical video.

entry.title: Unleashing the Power of Text: Text-Guided Flow Matching for Image Fusion under Complex Degradations

author.name: Axi Niu (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Jieheng Li (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Kang Zhang (School of Electrical Engineering, KAIST, Daejeon, Republic of Korea), Qingsen Yan (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Jinqiu Sun (School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China), Yanning Zhang (School of Computer Science, Northwestern Polytechnical University, Xi'an, China)

entry.summary: TGFusion is a text-guided latent flow-matching framework for infrared-visible image fusion under realistic degradations, replacing fixed global text injection with guidance that adapts to spatially varying degradation, local structure and thermal saliency. It unifies restoration and fusion in one generative process.

entry.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism

author.name: Donna M Bye, Levin Kuhlmann

entry.summary: A critical humanities-style argument that the dominant framing of AI anthropomorphism as user error rests on institutional authority rather than established epistemic grounds, and that this framing itself harms users who form relational interactions with AI. Calls for reassessing how legitimacy of human experience with AI is adjudicated.

entry.title: Riemannian Attention Mechanisms for Transformers: A Theoretical Framework and Architecture Design

author.name: Sen Song

entry.summary: Proposes replacing the Euclidean inner product in attention with learned per-token Riemannian metrics, proving such scores are non-Gram and cannot be factorized as a low-dimensional query-key product, and discussing implications for the known rank-collapse result in deep attention stacks. The paper is explicit that non-Gram structure is not itself a rank-preservation proof.

entry.title: Linear Multi-Timescale Retention as a Memory-Efficient Vision-Language Bridge

author.name: Ashfak Yeafi, Mehedi Hasan, Md Khairul Islam

entry.summary: Proposes a linear-complexity retention module with multi-timescale log-linear decays and adaptive write gating as a memory-efficient bridge between vision encoders and language models, replacing quadratic softmax cross-attention. Aims to keep spatial sequence routing that naive MLP connectors discard.

entry.title: MNC: Scope-Bound Semantic Declassification for Private LLM-Agent Communication

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: Minimum-Necessary Communication is a typed declassification protocol for multi-agent LLM systems that selects a task-sufficient disclosure from application-authored candidates and binds it to explicit recipient, purpose, forwarding, lifetime, logging, and memory scopes enforced by a reference monitor. It targets leakage through internal messages, tool arguments, logs, and persistent memory rather than only public outputs.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient LLM Serving via Disaggregated Attention--FFN and Flexible Frequency Scaling

author.name: Cunchen Hu, Liangliang Xu, Tian Liu, Min Lyu, Yongkun Li, Sa Wang, Shuo Quan, Yanan Yang, Wenda Tang, Yiduo Wang, Fu Yu, Jie Wu

entry.summary: AFlex reduces LLM serving energy by observing that attention and feed-forward operators have different energy-optimal GPU frequencies that shift with inference phase and workload, then controlling frequencies separately for disaggregated attention and FFN execution. It navigates the resulting large search space while meeting latency service objectives.

entry.title: Divisive Normalization Shapes Low-Rank Slow Manifolds for Continuous Working Memory

author.name: Zhaotian Gu, Jie Su, Weiwei Wang, Chang Liu, Tianyi Qian, Dahui Wang

entry.summary: The authors add divisive normalization, a canonical cortical computation, to a recurrent network and show through dynamical systems analysis that it produces low-rank slow manifolds supporting stable continuous working memory. This avoids both the fine-tuning fragility of classical continuous attractors and the tendency of GRUs and LSTMs to shatter continuous variables into discrete point attractors.

entry.title: AdaThinkV: Adaptive Thinking for Token-Efficient Video Reasoning

author.name: Jingqi Tian, Haoji Zhang, Lin Chen, Hongbo Jin, Haonan Xu, Tianrui Zhu, Xingming Shui, Shilin Ma, Wenjing Yang, Yansong Tang

entry.summary: AdaThinkV lets a video multimodal model decide per question whether to produce explicit chain-of-thought reasoning, learning this from matched reasoning and direct-answer rollouts during reinforcement learning rather than from difficulty labels, thresholds, or external routers. A ThinkGain signal trades accuracy improvement against extra response length.

entry.title: CompanionBench: A Theory-Anchored, Real-World-Grounded Benchmark for AI Emotional Companionship

author.name: Yao Liu, Guangjia Chai, Yuming Huang, Jihao Huang, Lei Wang, Junchen Wan

entry.summary: CompanionBench is an interactive bilingual benchmark for AI emotional companionship that grounds both scenarios and a trained user simulator in de-identified real conversation data, uses a hidden disclosure gate to branch trajectories on agent behavior, and operationalizes ten capabilities drawn from psychology and counseling theory. It also addresses judge biases such as same-family favoritism and scale drift.

entry.title: Lossless Tensor Compression as Program Synthesis

author.name: Jieke Shi (James), Junda He (James), Wenjia Jiang (James), Weifeng Sun (James), Shidong Pan (James), Zhensu Sun (James), Chengran Yang (James), Peixin Zhang (James), Yifan Jia (James), Zhou Yang (James), Thong Hoang (James), Xiwei Xu (Sherry), Zhenchang Xing, David Lo

entry.summary: Brevis casts lossless tensor and model checkpoint compression as program synthesis, defining a typed domain-specific language of reversible operators that capture repeated regions and floating-point field structure, then synthesizing a program that bit-exactly reconstructs the tensor. A learned checkpoint-specific production prior guides the search.

entry.title: Mitigating Backdoors via Decoy Shortcuts and Knowledge Decoupling

author.name: Zixuan Zhu, Rui Wang, Lihua Jing, Jinwen Zhong

entry.summary: Observes that backdoor behavior preferentially concentrates in a simple parallel branch when trained jointly with the main network, and exploits this by attaching a lightweight shortcut honeypot that absorbs the poison. Discarding the shortcut after training removes the backdoor without extra clean data, aided by a knowledge-decoupling objective.

entry.title: When May a Model Replace the Experiment? Audits, Licenses, and the Price of Trust in Surrogate-Driven Design

author.name: Shuangxiu (Max), Ma (Zachary), Wenhe (Zachary), Zhao

entry.summary: Analyzes mathematically, with three fully ground-truthed design tasks, when machine-learning surrogates may be trusted to grade candidates or feed their own predictions back into a search. Shows predictive accuracy alone cannot certify trust, characterizes the audit cost any safety certificate must pay, and states when substitution provably pays off.

entry.title: Staged Multi-Agent Training (SMAT) for Hip Exoskeletons: Metabolic and Biomechanical Validation of a Simulation-Trained Co-Adaptive Controller

author.name: Yifei Yuan, Jakob Wolf, Ghaith Androwis, Xianlian Zhou

entry.summary: Reports metabolic and biomechanical validation on real users of a hip exoskeleton controller trained entirely in simulation with a four-stage curriculum that co-adapts a musculoskeletal human model and the device policy. Whole-body metabolic measurement is the accepted benchmark for assistive walking, making this a meaningful sim-to-real check.

entry.title: DynamicManip: Enabling Dynamic Manipulation from a Single Static Demonstration

author.name: Haoran Liao, Pengyue Wang, Shuoyu Chen, Kehan Cheng, Xuhang Chen, Yuhao Lin, Mu Lin, Zhizhao Liang, Xiaoyi Fan, Chengyi Xing, Dan Niu, Yi-Lin Wei, Wei-Shi Zheng

entry.summary: Tackles dynamic robot manipulation with a pipeline that synthesizes diverse moving-object demonstrations from a single static demonstration, paired with a low-latency imitation policy for real-time execution. This targets the twin problems of data cost and reaction speed in dynamic tasks.

entry.title: Statistical comparisons of time-series feature sets on classification tasks

author.name: Trent Henderson, Ben D. Fulcher

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks six open-source time-series feature libraries plus three simple distributional and spectral baselines across 124 univariate classification problems using a normalization-based comparison protocol. The result clarifies which feature sets actually add value over trivial baselines.

entry.title: Reassessing the Feasibility of PPG-Based Non-Invasive Blood Glucose Level Estimation

author.name: Supraja Ramesh, Markus Neufeld, Michael K\"uttner, Tobias R\"oddiger, Michael Beigl

entry.summary: Builds a reproducible pipeline to re-evaluate five published methods for estimating blood glucose from photoplethysmography under progressively stricter splits. Models that appear competitive under random window splits collapse to near-zero or negative explained variance once participants are separated, indicating leakage-driven results in the prior literature.

entry.title: Tunneling the Loss Landscape: Bypassing Memorization with Monte Carlo Parameter Swapping

author.name: Lai Shun Chan, Xiaotian Zhang, Yue Shang, Ge Zhang, Entao Yang

entry.summary: Tests the statistical-physics account of grokking as glass relaxation by applying Monte Carlo parameter swapping to help networks tunnel out of memorization minima in the loss landscape. The work moves the computational glass framing from theory toward an actionable training intervention.

entry.title: SpatioLM: Towards General Physical Spatial Intelligence in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jing Wu, Jianhua Wu, Jiayi Guan, Jiahong Chen, Jinghui Lu, Hangjun Ye, Bingzhao Gao, Long Chen

entry.summary: Adds a plug-and-play, non-invasive spatial module to vision-language models that elicits latent spatial knowledge without requiring extra 3D inputs or third-party spatial encoders, using pseudo depth and camera parameters as supervision. The design aims to boost spatial reasoning while preserving general-purpose capability after fine-tuning.

entry.title: Interaction Is Not Necessary for Order-Optimal 1-Bit Mean Estimation

author.name: Jiachen Hu, Han Zhong

entry.summary: Shows that one-bit mean estimation under moment constraints does not need adaptive two-stage protocols: a fully non-adaptive randomized query design matches the optimal adaptive sample complexity. Simplifies distributed and communication-limited estimation protocols.

entry.title: ArabicDialectSafety: A Dialect-Aware Benchmark for Arabic Content Safety Classification

author.name: Wajdi Zaghouani, Md. Rafiul Biswas, Kholoud Khalil Aldous, Mabrouka Bessghaier

entry.summary: Releases a human-curated Arabic safety benchmark of 25,000 prompts spanning Modern Standard Arabic and five regional dialects, labelled for dialect and seven harm categories with binary and fine-grained tasks. A fine-tuned Arabic encoder substantially outperforms prompted frontier LLMs, showing dialect coverage gaps in current safety classifiers.

entry.title: CrossLex: A Source-Grounded Benchmark for Cross-Jurisdictional Legal Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaocui Yang, Xican Tan, Shoujie Chen, Shihan Xiao, Keke Tong, Xinyu Zhou

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark where identical fact patterns are paired with authoritative legal sources from China, California, and Germany so that correct answers diverge by jurisdiction. Tests whether LLMs recognize jurisdiction-specific rules across contract, consumer, criminal, family, and labour law.

entry.title: HopRefusalBench: Diagnosing Refusal Failures in Search-Augmented Agents for Multi-Hop Reasoning

author.name: Jianan Xie, Xin Sun, Zhongqi Chen, Xing Zheng, Qiang Liu, Bowen Song

entry.summary: Builds a controlled benchmark of 889 genuinely unanswerable multi-hop questions crossing three causes of unanswerability with three positions in the reasoning chain, to test whether search agents abstain appropriately. Reveals refusal failures that only appear after valid intermediate retrieval steps.

entry.title: EviSD: Evidence-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Agents

author.name: Jianan Xie, Xin Sun, Zhongqi Chen, Xing Zheng, Shu Wu, Bowen Song, Liang Wang

entry.summary: Trains search agents by letting the same model act as a privileged teacher that rescores its own actions with access to supporting evidence and gold answers, converting the teacher-student gap into a bounded correction to outcome-based advantages. Provides finer-grained credit than trajectory-level rewards.

entry.title: PGMem: Tightly Coupled Persona-Memory Graph for Lifelong Personalized Agents

author.name: Wonjun Choi, Yerim Kim, Yukyung Lee, Susik Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes PGMem, a heterogeneous graph that links dialogue event nodes to persona nodes via typed provenance and evidence edges so each persona claim stays traceable to the interactions that justify or revise it. Retrieval expands from query-relevant seeds and ranks by evidential validity, beating summary- and persona-profile baselines on three long-term dialogue benchmarks with small backbones.

entry.title: TRAM: Enhancing Multimodal Reasoning with Trajectory-Derived Auxiliary Memory

author.name: Kang Liu, Zijing Wang, Yongkang Liu, Mengjie Zhao, Xiaocui Yang, Shi Feng, Yifei Zhang, Daling Wang

entry.summary: TRAM adds an auxiliary memory distilled from the reasoning trajectory itself, not just the image, so that intermediate relations and constraints established early remain accessible as multimodal reasoning chains grow long. Attribution analysis motivates the design by showing correctness correlates with trajectory grounding rather than image attribution alone.

entry.title: PredAct-Bench: Benchmarking Tool-Augmented Dialogue under Controlled Tool Noise

author.name: Abdulrahman AlRabah, Xiaocheng Yang, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Abdussalam Alawini

entry.summary: PredActBench evaluates task-oriented dialogue agents paired with statistically imperfect prediction tools, using education as a measurable domain, and models human trust in the agent as itself uncertain. It targets the unrealistic assumption in existing benchmarks that tool outputs are always correct.

entry.title: Noise-Robust Conditional Flow Matching: Generating Clean Samples from Noisy Datasets

author.name: Adrian Urba\'nski, Gabriel della Maggiora, Artur Yakimovich

entry.summary: Adapts conditional flow matching so that a generative model trained only on noisy scientific measurements learns the underlying clean population distribution instead of reproducing corruption. Motivated by imaging domains where clean reference data is costly or unobtainable.

entry.title: Optical Flow from Photons

author.name: Wendi Liu, Weichao Zeng, Weihang Ran, Yujie Lu, Yinqiang Zheng

entry.summary: QuantaFlow estimates dense optical flow directly from binary single-photon streams, resolving the circularity that motion-aware temporal aggregation needs the flow it is trying to compute. It targets high-speed and low-light scenes where conventional cameras blur or underexpose.

entry.title: Hybrid-Domain Posterior Sampling for Inverse Problems via Latent Flow Matching

author.name: Hongjie Wu, Yiping Xie, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: Diagnoses a geometric limitation of latent generative models for inverse problems, where severe autoencoder compression yields a rank-deficient decoder Jacobian that makes high-frequency measurement residuals invisible to latent gradients. The proposed hybrid-domain posterior sampling decouples physical measurement consistency from latent-space generation to recover that lost detail.

entry.title: Ground, Cover, and Refine: Evidence-Centric Frame Selection for Long-Video Question Answering

author.name: Fan Wei, Siru Zhong, Runmin Dong, Miao Yang, Zhaoyang Luo, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: GCR is a training-free frame selection method for long-video question answering that treats fixed-budget selection as evidence curation, grounding timestamped text into temporal events, ensuring coverage, then refining choices. Aims to avoid clustering around local relevance peaks and to better align text with visual evidence.

entry.title: Grounding and Explaining Visual Evidence for AI-Generated Image Detection in Human-Centric Scenes

author.name: Kun Guo, Yuzhou Yang, Haoyue Wang, Qichao Ying, Sheng Li, Zhenxing Qian

entry.summary: Introduces a human-centric dataset of roughly 80,000 real and generated images and a method that jointly localizes forgery evidence and explains it, so explanations stay consistent with the highlighted regions. Aims at interpretable detection of AI-generated imagery of people.

entry.title: Local Margin Restoration for Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yan Huang, Guowei Wang, Xu Wang, Kangjun Liu, Xin Lin

entry.summary: Local Margin Restoration is a one-step test-time adaptation method for CLIP-style models that avoids the error reinforcement and mode collapse caused by top-1 confidence updates, by protecting margins among semantically related classes. Targets stable continual adaptation over unlabeled test streams.

entry.title: GEOID-Flood: A Large-Scale Multi-Modal Benchmark Dataset for Flood Segmentation

author.name: Gaetano Chiriaco, Luca Barco, Andrea Bragagnolo, Claudio Rossi, Edoardo Arnaudo

entry.summary: GEOID-Flood is a large multi-modal flood segmentation benchmark with over 14,000 tiles covering 219 events in 65 countries, pairing pre- and post-event radar with co-registered optical imagery. It is designed to test whether geospatial foundation models actually add value on this downstream task.

entry.title: Does Explainability Transfer? A Controlled Benchmark of Attribution Methods on Vision Transformers and CNNs

author.name: Sathiyamohan Nishankar, Nethmi Pathirana, Pubudu Sanjeewani, Asanka Perera, Selvarajah Thuseethan

entry.summary: A controlled benchmark of 13 attribution explainability methods across eight backbones spanning convolutional networks, plain and hierarchical transformers, hybrids, and linear-attention models, measured on faithfulness, localization, robustness, complexity, and cost. Tests whether conclusions drawn on convolutional networks still hold for modern transformers.

entry.title: Compliant Sphere Lattice Contact: Distributed Contact Modeling for Sphere-Based Robot Representations

author.name: Nataliya Nechyporenko, Ava Abderezaei, Alessandro Roncone

entry.summary: Compliant Sphere Lattice Contact adds physically meaningful distributed contact to sphere-based robot models by treating the surface spheres as a compliant lattice with anchor and lateral springs that deform to produce pressure distributions, rotational stiffness, and frictional moments. This recovers contact patch physics that point-contact sphere models discard while keeping differentiable, fast collision geometry.

entry.title: SelfWAM: A Self-Grounded Unified World Action Model for Fast Robot Control

author.name: Bikang Pan, Fan Liu, Haotao Lu, Jingya Wang, Ye Shi

entry.summary: SelfWAM is a unified world action model on a modality-specialized mixture-of-transformers that jointly predicts actions, action-conditioned future RGB frames, and robot self-masks, grounding prediction in the robot visible body and its action-induced motion. During training future visual queries can attend to a clean copy of the demonstrated action so video prediction becomes genuinely action-conditioned rather than generic task progression.

entry.title: RADAR Perception for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance onboard small-scale Quadrotor UAVs

author.name: Dnyandeep Mandaokar, Bernhard Rinner

entry.summary: The first onboard mmWave radar perception and control stack for fast dynamic obstacle avoidance on small quadrotors, combining an interacting-multiple-model tracker with a control-barrier-function controller. The authors derive latency and range conditions sufficient for successful avoidance.

entry.title: PROGRESS: Coverage-guided RL to Train Search-augmented LLM Agent

author.name: Sudipta Paul, Vijay Srinivasan, Vivek Kulkarni, Aounon Kumar, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Wenbo Li, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: PROGRESS trains search-augmented agents with a teacher-guided coverage reward that shapes how the policy decomposes complex queries into subqueries, rather than relying only on final-outcome rewards. Frozen teachers supply the essential subqueries as lightweight process supervision.

entry.title: Ranking Image Fusion the Way Humans Do: A Learned Pairwise Preference Metric for Infrared-Visible Fusion Assessment

author.name: Haoran Liu, Mingzhe Liu, Peng Li, Guibin Zan

entry.summary: Trains a source-conditioned model to predict human A/B/Tie preferences between fused infrared-visible images, providing a scalable surrogate for pairwise subjective assessment whose cost otherwise grows quadratically in the number of algorithms. Targets the disagreement among conventional scalar fusion metrics.

entry.title: VGER: Voxel-Guided Global Event Ranking for Event Cloud Attribution

author.name: Youxin Jiang, Baoheng Fu, Hongwei Ren, Xiangqian Wu

entry.summary: VGER is a training-free attribution method for point-based event-camera networks that ranks individual events globally using voxel-level guidance, rather than naively porting point-cloud saliency methods that ignore event spatio-temporal structure. Aims to expose which events drive a model's prediction.

entry.title: tFUSOperator: Operator Learning for Transcranial Focused Ultrasound Digital Twins

author.name: Minjee Seo, Haris Ghafoor, Minju Seol, Seonaeng Cho, Kyungho Yoon

entry.summary: tFUSOperator recasts transcranial focused ultrasound field simulation as operator learning, mapping free-field pressure, skull anatomy and treatment parameters to the intracranial acoustic field in a shared coordinate space. It targets fast, repeatable field estimation for digital-twin treatment planning where full numerical solvers are too slow.

entry.title: Scikit-fingerprints: Python library for scikit-learn compatible molecular fingerprints and chemoinformatics

author.name: Jakub Adamczyk, Adam Staniszewski

entry.summary: Presents scikit-fingerprints, an RDKit-based Python library that exposes molecular fingerprints, filters, similarity measures, applicability-domain estimation and chemistry-aware splits through scikit-learn compatible interfaces. It lets a full chemoinformatics workflow from SMILES to deployed model be built from familiar components.

entry.title: Isotonic Bradley-Terry Model for Paired Comparison Data

author.name: Ryoya Yamasaki

entry.summary: Replaces the fixed inverse link function of Bradley-Terry and Thurstone-Mosteller paired-comparison models with a monotone (isotonic) link learned from data, reducing misspecification when predicting win probabilities and ranking players. Provides estimation for the joint isotonic link and strength parameters.

entry.title: Aggregate-then-Calibrate for Human-centered Assessment with Theoretical Guarantees

author.name: Zejun Xie, Xintong Li, Guang Wang, Desheng Zhang

entry.summary: Aggregate-then-Calibrate handles assessment tasks with no verifiable ground truth by first aggregating heterogeneous human comparative judgments into a consensus ranking that accounts for annotator reliability, then isotonically calibrating any model's scores onto that order. Theoretical guarantees accompany the two-stage procedure.

entry.title: MedSAM2-Anatomy: Training-Free Inference-Time Optimization for Musculoskeletal Segmentation

author.name: John Garcia Henao, Nicholas B\"unger, Benedikt Herzog, Cindy Guerrero Toro, Benjamin Vella, Matthias Biner, Rico Br\"utsch, Carmen Castroviejo Fernandez, Felix \"Ottl, Norman Juchler, Armando Hoch, Bettina Hochreiter, Sven Hirsch, Sebastiano Caprara

entry.summary: MedSAM2-Anatomy improves frozen musculoskeletal segmentation under domain shift with no retraining and no human prompting: a frozen CNN expert produces anatomical priors that are converted into multiple prompt hypotheses for a frozen promptable 3D foundation model, and candidate masks are fused with implausible priors rejected. All adaptation happens at inference time.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Auditing Spatial Provenance in Visual Token Pruning for OCR-Critical MLLM Inference

author.name: Feixiang Liu, Qiang Qiu, Hao Zhang, Xinyue Wang

entry.summary: Audits whether tokens retained by visual pruning methods are geometrically traceable to the image region that actually supports the answer, finding accuracy can be preserved even when no retained token covers the relevant OCR region. Confidence intervals on paired image-cluster comparisons show near-identical accuracy at thirty percent retention despite very different evidence provenance.

entry.title: Latent-Centroid Steering: Single-Pass Classifier-Free Guidance for Command-Aligned Autonomous Driving

author.name: Meibo Hu, Jiamian Wang, Pichao Wang, Zhiqiang Tao

entry.summary: Identifies a command-following gap in vision-language driving models where predicted trajectories are weakly sensitive to navigation instructions, attributing it to conditional policy collapse under regression training. The proposed latent-centroid steering applies classifier-free guidance in a single forward pass to restore language conditioning.

entry.title: UniSim-SLAM: Feed-Forward SLAM with Unified Sim(3) Optimization

author.name: Inha Lee, Dongjae Jeong, Junhee Lee, Kyungdon Joo

entry.summary: UniSim-SLAM combines fast two-view keyframe tracking with periodic multi-view submap refinement, fusing predictions from geometric foundation models that live in inconsistent local scales. A unified similarity-transform factor graph jointly optimizes poses and scales to reduce drift over long sequences.

entry.title: MoCRA: Mixture of Compositional Rank-1 Atoms for 4K All-in-One Video Restoration

author.name: Yongcong Wang, Pu Wang, Hingchin Chen, Runci Bai, Yucheng Xin, Chen Wu, Chengchao Shen, Guangwei Gao, Siyuan Yao, Pengwen Dai, Zhuoran Zheng

entry.summary: MoCRA handles blind all-in-one video restoration at native 4K by mixing compositional rank-1 adaptation atoms, and introduces a paired 4K benchmark rendering haze, rain, noise, and low light over identical clean clips. Motivated by the observation that some degradations survive downsampling while others do not.

entry.title: SVGEval: A Vision-Grounded Framework for Perceptual-Quality Benchmarking and Evaluation in Text-to-SVG Generation

author.name: Yiming Wang, Ye Chen, Hanqi Chen, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: SVGEval benchmarks whether multimodal models can judge text-to-vector-graphics generation quality using rendered visual output rather than code inspection, with multi-round expert human annotations. Finds existing code-centric or raster-borrowed metrics poorly reflect human perception.

entry.title: DerainSplat: Feed-Forward Clean 3D Gaussian Splatting from Sparse Rainy Views

author.name: Fuzhen Jiang, Changyue Shi, Chuxiao Yang, Xinyuan Hu, Wenjie Ye, Minghao Chen

entry.summary: DerainSplat reconstructs clean 3D Gaussian scenes directly from a few rainy input views in a feed-forward pass, supported by a new large multi-view deraining dataset generated through a staged synthesis pipeline. Motivated by embodied AI and driving needs where feed-forward 3D methods collapse under rain.

entry.title: Sen-Cap: Sensor-Flexible and Noise-Resilient Human Motion Capture via LiDAR-Camera Integration

author.name: Aoru Xue (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China), Yujing Sun (Digital Trust Centre, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Yiming Ren (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China, Digital Trust Centre, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Kwok-Yan Lam (Digital Trust Centre, Nanyang Technological University, Singapore), Mao Ye (EABOT.AI, China), Yuexin Ma (ShanghaiTech University, Shanghai, China)
