entry.summary: Sen-Cap captures 3D human motion by fusing LiDAR and camera data without explicit calibration, estimating motion in a unified across-sensor formulation that tolerates arbitrary sensor placement. It is designed to degrade gracefully under heavy noise or partial sensor failure.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Multimodal Longitudinal Image Imputation and Interpolation

author.name: Sina Wendrich, Lukas F\"orner, Zoe Reinke, Kartikay Tehlan, Ansgar Berlis, Michael Fr\"uhwald, Matthias Wagner, Thomas Wendler

entry.summary: Models a patient's longitudinal multi-parameter MRI as a continuous implicit function of space, time, and modality, trained with modality dropout so missing sequences can be imputed and time points interpolated without resampling to a grid. Adds a self-consistency-based confidence estimate for generated content.

entry.title: EchoCache: Energy-Guided Cross-Modal Caching for Efficient Audio-Driven Video Generation

author.name: Jiayu Chen, Xiaoyu Wu, Rongshan Gao, Maoliang Li, Zihao Zheng, Xinhao Sun, Hailong Zou, Guojie Luo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: EchoCache accelerates audio-driven video diffusion by using audio time-frequency energy to decide when cached visual features can be reused, arguing that prior caching schemes ignore the highly non-uniform temporal importance imposed by the audio track. It identifies temporal-semantic and computation-storage misalignments in existing caches and fixes both.

entry.title: SG-WAM: Self-Guided World Modeling in Geometry-Aware Policy Space

author.name: Ruiteng Zhao, Zhengshen Zhang, Yue Su, Wenshuo Wang, Jiahui Li, Zhiyuan Yang, Francis E. H. Tay, Marcelo H. Ang Jr., Haiyue Zhu

entry.summary: SG-WAM learns action-conditioned future dynamics directly in the policy-derived representation space using learnable dynamics tokens and a self-guided predictor, instead of predicting heavy observation-space targets or using a separate latent space. The claim is that this space is simultaneously aligned with action generation and geometry-aware.

entry.title: From Failures to Supervision: DynamicEnvPlan for Robust Long-Horizon Embodied Planning

author.name: Hao Yuan, Yuxin Wang, Lei Ji, Zhiwei Yu

entry.summary: DynamicEnvPlan is a closed-loop framework for long-horizon embodied planning in environments that change during execution, treating execution failures as training supervision rather than mere evaluation outcomes. It adds humanoid agents, high-level skill primitives, structured semantic memory, and controllable perturbations for data synthesis.

entry.title: LooperMuscle: Fast and Stable Learning of Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking via Structured Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Boyi Liu, Qijin Li, Tianqi Yu, Qinrui Yan, Xingxing Zuo

entry.summary: LooperMuscle closes the speed-quality gap between fast off-policy humanoid training and PPO by combining a semantically structured mixture-of-experts actor, an expert-aware distributional critic, and contribution-routed replay with deferred curriculum scheduling. Expert contributions route data, routed data shapes value learning, and value gradients refine expert specialization in a closed loop.

entry.title: H+ Embedding: Harmonizing Global and Token-Level Retrieval with Context-Dependent Phrases

author.name: Shusen Zhang, Junyi Hu, Ye Feng, Ziteng Wang, Zhaoyuan Pan, Guosheng Dong, Xiaojun Yuan, Jiangshou Hong, Xiangzhi Wang

entry.summary: H+ Embedding proposes phrase-level retrieval units that sit between single-vector and token-level late-interaction retrievers, predicting variable-length phrase partitions and keeping uncovered tokens as singletons. It targets terminology-heavy domains like medicine where entities, abbreviations, and numeric constraints matter.

entry.title: CrystalMem: Elastic Memory for Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Knowledge Crystallization

author.name: Beining Wu, Jun Huang

entry.summary: CrystalMem tackles memory hysteresis, the finding that agent capability does not recover after a memory quota is squeezed and then restored, proving that keep-or-drop policies leave a residual deficit. It instead demotes entries through four fidelity states under a crystallization-energy schedule so material for rebuilding is retained.

entry.title: F-WANDA: Fisher-Reweighted Post-Training Pruning for Sustainable Deployment of Large Language Models

author.name: Himanshu Mishra (University of British Columbia)

entry.summary: F-WANDA modifies the WANDA one-shot pruning criterion by reallocating per-row sparsity budgets across output neurons in proportion to empirical Fisher information collected in a single extra backward pass. On a 7B model at 50 percent sparsity it matches WANDA perplexity while improving few-shot MMLU and costing a fraction of SparseGPT compute.

entry.title: Why Does the Future Branch? Identifiable Closure Tests for Stochastic Physical World Models

author.name: Yibin Dong

entry.summary: Proves that from ordinary transition data one cannot distinguish whether a stochastic world model's uncertainty comes from partial observability aliasing states or from genuinely stochastic dynamics, even with an optimal predictor. Introduces an interventional protocol crossing microstates with repeated disturbances plus a variance decomposition to identify the sources.

entry.title: FinDeepIndicator: Benchmarking Deep Research Agents in End-to-End Financial Indicator Construction

author.name: Chaoqun Yang, Fengbin Zhu, Xinyu Lin, Long Bai, Xiaoluan Liu, Ke-Wei Huang, Roger Zimmermann, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: FinDeepIndicator benchmarks deep research agents on constructing financial indicators end to end, scoring the intermediate stages of formula specification, data collection, calculation, and answering rather than only final accuracy. It removes the common assumption that relevant data are pre-supplied.

entry.title: Isotropy Cliffs: The Geometric Signature of Decision-Making in Large Language Models

author.name: Okan S. Coskun, Florian Rottach, Carsten Eickhoff, William Rudman

entry.summary: Analyzes five open-weight models on multiple-choice question answering and identifies transition layers where representational isotropy shifts abruptly, coinciding with the emergence of task-relevant clusters. This geometric signature correlates strongly with downstream accuracy and is robust to prompt variation.

entry.title: Modeling Social Dynamics with an LLM-Enabled Agent Based Network-Dynamic (LAND) Model

author.name: Lynnette Hui Xian Ng, Kathleen M. Carley

entry.summary: Uses an LLM-driven agent-based network simulation with over 314,000 heterogeneous agents exchanging more than half a million messages over a simulated month to study emergent influence, coordination, and narrative dominance. Analysis spans ego-network topology, semantic network evolution, coordination, and influence layers.

entry.title: Search-GRT: Guided Retrieval Training of Search Agents to Optimize for Complex Question Answering

author.name: Aounon Kumar, Sudipta Paul, Vivek Kulkarni, Vijay Srinivasan, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: Guided Retrieval Training improves multi-hop question answering search agents by constraining retrieval during training to counter sparse rewards and cascading early-retrieval errors. From the same group as the companion PROGRESS paper.

entry.title: Auditing Discovery Claims: A Two-Sided Criterion for Agentic Science, with the Negative Side Decidable

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Jianlin Chen, Ziyao Lin, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: Proposes a two-sided audit for capability claims made by self-improving AI-for-science systems, where the negative side is decidable because a pseudoknot-free RNA oracle provably cannot represent crossing base pairs. Shows a solver-free invented operator can appear to solve many targets under the very predictor it optimizes, inflating apparent discovery.

entry.title: Toward Fine-Grained Forgetting:Attribute Unlearning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Junkai Lin, Junkai Chen, Siqi Hou, Yuhao He, Ruiqi Liu, Chenhan Jin, Shengze Xu, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: Defines attribute-level unlearning for multimodal LLMs, where a model must forget one sensitive attribute of an identity while retaining other information about the same person, and builds a benchmark spanning long-text, numeric, and short-text targets at varying forget ratios. Evaluation shows existing profile-level methods handle this finer granularity poorly.

entry.title: MRAFnd: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Zero-Shot Fake News Detection

author.name: Lehan Zhang, Yinlei Cheng, Shiqi Hu Yiheng Zhou, Shangxi Li, Naidong Zhao

entry.summary: MRAFnd tackles zero-shot multimodal fake news detection by retrieving evidence from past misinformation campaigns instead of judging each item in isolation, then reasoning over cross-modal inconsistencies. The motivation is that disinformation tactics recur and recycled patterns provide signal for unseen events.

entry.title: Leveraging AI for fine-grained food safety risk forecasting in sparse data conditions

author.name: Dongqi Wang, Weiwei Chen, Han Zhou, Weihua Zhou

entry.summary: Builds a Transformer framework that forecasts city-level food safety risk by combining over 11 million inspection records with demographic, economic, and environmental indicators, using three-stage pretraining with Wilson-interval partial supervision and semi-supervised label refinement for sparse regions. The aim is fine-grained risk ranking where local sample sizes are too small for direct estimation.

entry.title: A Contractualist Argumentation Framework for Moral Decision-Making

author.name: Luis Marcos-Vidal, Giulio Antonio Abbo, Tony Belpaeme

entry.summary: Formalizes Scanlon-style contractualist ethics for autonomous agents using the ASPIC+ structured argumentation framework extended with value-based filtering of morally relevant reasons. Produces a symbolic machinery for judging whether an action could be reasonably rejected by affected parties.

entry.title: Trajectories That Segment Themselves: Agent-Declared Boundaries as a Training Unit

author.name: Jingxi Wei

entry.summary: Proposes letting a coding agent declare its own semantic phase boundaries while generating a trajectory, using falsifiable causal hypotheses as the segmentation contract, so training units are neither single actions nor whole episodes. Avoids needing gold patches, replay, teacher logits or a retrospective segmenter.

entry.title: Optimizing Minimax Regret in Uncertain MDPs with Small Sets of Policies

author.name: Sterre Lutz, Dani\"el Vos, Matthijs T. J. Spaan, Anna Lukina

entry.summary: Studies uncertain MDPs where only a small number of policies may be prepared in advance and the true model is revealed just before execution, optimizing minimax regret over a limited policy set. Balances the loss from a single robust policy against the infeasibility of one policy per model.

entry.title: AgentMemBench: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Term Memory Management Strategies in Conversational AI Agents

author.name: Ahmed Cherif

entry.summary: AgentMemBench compares five long-term memory management strategies for conversational agents, including context windowing, external key-value stores, graph episodic memory, summarization and web augmentation, under identical conditions on three public datasets. Reports retrieval, answer quality, faithfulness, memory footprint and cost metrics.

entry.title: CITBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Interactive Tabular Data Processing with LLMs

author.name: Zihan Nan, Yang Gu, Wei Liu, Xi Yan, Zhou Liu, Hao Liang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: CITBench evaluates LLMs on interactive multi-turn tabular data processing with evolving user requirements, spanning table matching, cleaning, augmentation and transformation across 18 task types and 1,296 instances. Fills a gap left by single-turn fully specified table reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Simulation-Based Inference for Operations Research with Large Language Models

author.name: Liang Guo, Lin Shaochong, Shen Zuo-Jun Max, Zhang Kun

entry.summary: A training-free inference framework for operations research modeling that scores intermediate formulation steps with short lookahead simulations to quantify whether a partial model can still be extended into a globally consistent optimization program. Aims to prevent locally plausible steps from cascading into solver failures.

entry.title: Symbolic Attack Chain Generation from Atomic Red Team Techniques: An Empirical Study of Predicate Representation Granularity

author.name: Ramya Varunsegar

entry.summary: This empirical study asks whether the nine-category predicate model used by state-of-the-art symbolic attack-chain generators is actually necessary, using an LLM to translate Atomic Red Team techniques into PDDL and the Fast Downward planner for deterministic reasoning. It compares representation granularities against plan validity, cost and fidelity.

entry.title: Optimising for Flourishing: Flourishing Metrics and Return on Flourishing as Success Criteria for Artificial Intelligence and Post-AGI Economic Systems

author.name: Keyun Ruan, Jonathan D. Teubner, John M. Bremen

entry.summary: This conceptual paper argues that human flourishing, not capability or engagement proxies, should be a primary success criterion for AI and post-AGI economies, proposing an extensible set of flourishing metrics across physical, emotional, financial, relational and spiritual dimensions plus a return-on-flourishing measure. It is a normative framework rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: UOT-IR: Structured Routing of High-Polyphony Symbolic Music into Fixed-Budget Representations

author.name: Ziyue Kang, Nan Nan, Chenhao Lin, Xiaohong Guan

entry.summary: UOT-IR reframes compressing high-polyphony symbolic music into fixed track or slot budgets as a structured routing problem solved with training-free constrained unbalanced optimal transport, aiming to preserve structural roles, orchestration compatibility and playability. It replaces heuristic simplification and generic dimensionality reduction.

entry.title: Understanding Online Failure Prediction in Linux Through Complementary Multi-View Explainability

author.name: Diogo D\'oria, Jo\~ao R. Campos

entry.summary: This experience report builds an explainable online failure prediction pipeline for Linux, combining consensus-based feature selection with temporal onset analysis, subsystem-level causal analysis and complementary diagnostic views. The motivation is that accurate prediction alone does not earn operator trust and may reflect workload-specific telemetry correlations rather than real failure processes.

entry.title: CRAFT: Compression via Recursive Adaptive Fusion of Video Tokens for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yu Chen, Xiaohong Li, Xiaole Wang, Jianjin Zhang, Jun Sun, Yafeng Deng

entry.summary: CRAFT compresses redundant video tokens for vision-language models by recursively merging them in an adaptive, content-aware way, aiming to cut prefill compute without the alignment training that add-on compression modules require. It targets the efficiency-versus-detail-preservation tradeoff in long-video understanding.

entry.title: ProtoAct: Turning Wet-Lab Protocols into Embodied Robotic Actions

author.name: Zhe Liu, Jiaming Gu, Zhaohui Du, Zhe Wang, Huanbo Jin, Quan Lu, Qi Wang, Ting Xiao, Minting Pan, Dongzhan Zhou

entry.summary: ProtoAct converts free-form biological wet-lab protocols into state-aware, robot-executable action sequences using retrieval of annotated examples, a consistency checker for missing steps, and a schema that maps procedures to constrained JSON function calls. It also releases BioP2E, with 22 hand-annotated cell-culture protocols expanded into hundreds of steps.

entry.title: Hear, Invoke, and Understand: A Skill-Calling Multimodal Agent for Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Yuwen Wang, Tian-Hao Zhang, Minghao Cai, Yilin Ren, Ziyang Jiang, Xin Wang, Zhichao Wang, Pan Zhou, Kun Zhan, Xinyuan Qian

entry.summary: SpeechAgent-R is an audio agent that combines intrinsic multimodal understanding with calls to external audio skills and tools, supported by a new corpus of over 65,000 interaction trajectories and 500 hours of audio across 24 tasks. It is trained by trajectory supervised fine-tuning followed by multi-turn reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SPARE: Structural Parameter-Free Affinity Regularization for Flow Matching

author.name: Zong-Wei Hong, Jinglun Li, Shen Zhang, Yuhan Liu, Linze Li, Yao Tang

entry.summary: SPARE accelerates diffusion transformer training with a parameter-free regularizer that preserves internal spatial affinity structure, avoiding both the external encoder needed by target-based representation alignment and the structure-discarding repulsion of target-free methods. It builds on evidence that spatial structure rather than global semantics drives alignment gains.

entry.title: PhyCheck: Fine-Grained Evidence-Grounded Dataset for Physical Law Understanding in Video-LLMs

author.name: Zhongjie Ba, Shengwang Xu, Peng Cheng, Jinyang Zou, Ting Yu, Zhibo Wang, Zhan Qin

entry.summary: PhyCheck is a two-granularity video question answering dataset for testing whether video language models can judge if observed events obey specific physical laws, with evidence grounding rather than only coarse labels. It fills a gap since existing benchmarks mainly score the physical plausibility of generated videos.

entry.title: Can AI Agents Simulate A/B Test Outcomes? A Validation Framework for Agentic Experimentation

author.name: Stefan Hut, Lorenzo Masoero

entry.summary: The authors formalize simulated randomized controlled trials in which LLM agents conditioned on behavioral profiles predict A/B test outcomes, and derive a two-layer error decomposition separating agent approximation error from subsampling error. The framework is agent-agnostic and intended to screen candidate treatments before spending live traffic.

entry.title: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning

author.name: Yiran Gao, Tao Li, Kim Hammar

entry.summary: Proposes coupling LLM-based agentic incident response with a digital twin of the operational network so that multiscale response plans can be validated before execution. Aims to combine the grounding of decision-theoretic planning with the broad security knowledge of language models.

entry.title: Neural operator learning for collision-aware trajectory planning of spacecraft swarms

author.name: Sidhdharth D. Sikka, Suyi Gao, Zehui Lu, Rongjie Lai, Shaoshuai Mou

entry.summary: A permutation-equivariant neural operator maps distributions of spacecraft, targets, and debris to collision-aware swarm trajectories in a single forward pass, refined by a batched Gauss-Newton step that enforces exact orbital dynamics. Training uses self-supervised physics objectives plus adversarially generated debris threats instead of optimal-trajectory labels.

entry.title: Kilobyte Models: Neural Networks as a Seed and a Quantized Latent

author.name: Sahil Rajesh Dhayalkar

entry.summary: Explores an extreme compression regime where the shipped artifact is not weights but an integer random seed plus a small quantized latent that regenerates the weights through a mapping network. Model size then depends on latent dimension and bit width instead of parameter count, targeting bandwidth-limited over-the-air updates.

entry.title: Subtype Robustness Is Not Just Accuracy: Calibration Under Unseen Subtype Shift

author.name: Hanyu Su, Carlota Julbe i Juanola, Yibo Hu

entry.summary: Studies whether models stay calibrated when test examples come from fine-grained subtypes unseen in training but within a known coarse class, across four datasets and five architectures. Finds accuracy drops while confidence barely moves, producing systematic overconfidence that generic image corruption does not reproduce.

entry.title: Characterizing Bias in Post-Bandit Inference under Index Algorithms

author.name: Lisu Wang, Yilun Chen, Jiaqi Lu

entry.summary: Derives sharp leading-order expressions for the bias in sample means and test statistics computed from data collected by index-based bandit algorithms such as UCB1. Introduces an effective exploration rate that explains the algorithmic origin of the bias and shows it decays extremely slowly, revealing a regret-versus-bias trade-off.

entry.title: Differentiable Lifting for Topological Neural Networks

author.name: Jorge Luiz Franco, Gabriel Duarte, Alexander Nikitin, Moacir Ponti, Diego Mesquita, Amauri H. Souza

entry.summary: DiffLift learns, end-to-end, how to lift graphs into hypergraphs and simplicial or cellular complexes instead of fixing higher-order structures a priori by unsupervised heuristics. It parameterizes distributions over candidate higher-order cells from learned vertex representations so the topology adapts to the downstream task.

entry.title: SAFE-Merge: Data-Free Continual Model Merging with General Knowledge Preservation

author.name: Zihuan Qiu, Zhiyang Liao, Chiyuan He, Yi Xu, Fanman Meng, Linfeng Xu, Qingbo Wu, Hongliang Li

entry.summary: SAFE-Merge tackles data-free continual merging of specialized models by first deciding which parameter updates are safe to retain for preserving pretrained general knowledge, then recovering task information lost to masking. Argues prior methods focus only on inter-task interference and neglect erosion of the base model's generalization.

entry.title: Interpretable MEG Decoding of Perceived Speech: Cortical Sources and the Stimulus Features That Drive Retrieval

author.name: Ilia Semenkov, Daria Kleeva, Ivan Dakhtin, Zarina Maksudova, Alex Ossadtchi

entry.summary: Redesigns a MEG-to-audio retrieval network so its components map onto electrophysiological quantities, replacing flat-sensor spatial attention with spherical harmonics on the helmet geometry and compressing subject-specific branches with per-branch temporal filters. This yields interpretable cortical sources and identifies which speech features actually drive successful retrieval.

entry.title: A Constitution-Grid Instrument for Data-Efficient RL Alignment (C-Guard)

author.name: Lily Zhang

entry.summary: C-Guard builds a constitution-indexed grid of training data for RL-training a safety guard model, and pairs it with a per-cell learnability score that decides whether each cell should be pruned, densified, amended or expanded. The authors report that over-refusal improved substantially while under-refusal on adversarial prompts quietly got worse, illustrating the conflicting-objective trap in guard training.

entry.title: Learning Not to Optimize: Physics-Informed Action-Space Reshaping for Intent-Based Network Control

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Vaneet Aggarwal, Tian Lan

entry.summary: Argues that reinforcement learning for intent-based network control wastes effort optimizing over candidate actions that intermediate physics-derived signals can already rule out as equivalent or dominated. The proposed approach reshapes the action space using these signals before value-based optimization, complementing conventional constraint-handling penalties and Lagrangians.

entry.title: Active Regression for Single-Index Models with Unknown Link Functions

author.name: Chansophea Wathanak In, Yi Li, Wai Ming Tai, Xuan Wu

entry.summary: Studies active regression for single-index models under general lp loss where the link function is unknown and only queried coordinates of the response are observable. It gives a non-adaptive sampling algorithm with near-optimal query complexity and matching lower bounds, extending prior results that covered only the squared-loss case for unknown links.

entry.title: Asleep at the Wheel: JEPA's Limitations in Evaluating Novel Driving Data

author.name: Advait Pavuluri, Shamik Karkhanis, Uzma Mushtaque

entry.summary: Tests whether prediction error from a frozen V-JEPA video encoder with a lightweight predictor can serve as a label-free novelty score to triage rare driving clips for human review. Under a cross-dataset protocol the approach looks strong at first but the paper reports limitations in identifying genuinely novel driving situations.

entry.title: Slot2Text: Object-Centric Visual Tokenization for Efficient and Spatially Traceable Surgical MLLMs

author.name: Guiqiu Liao, Matjaz Jogan, Daniel A. Hashimoto

entry.summary: Replaces hundreds of dense visual tokens in a surgical multimodal LLM with a compact set of object-centric slot latents grouped from self-supervised vision features and passed to the language model as area-labeled tokens. A reasoning variant additionally localizes the regions used to justify each answer, adding spatial traceability.

entry.title: Not the Dimension, the Norm: What Matters in Gradient-Free Weight Perturbation of Language Models

author.name: Taeyeong Kim, Ahhyun Kim, TaeHyeon Kim, Unggi Lee

entry.summary: Runs a controlled factor-by-factor study of gradient-free adaptation of language models, isolating search space, perturbation scale, and aggregation which prior work varied jointly. The conclusion is that the norm of the perturbation, rather than the dimensionality of the perturbed subspace, determines whether random-search adaptation works.

entry.title: Randomized Algorithms for Learning Partitions with Near Optimal Query Complexity in Constant Rounds

author.name: Deeparnab Chakrabarty, Aditi Dudeja, David Saulpic

entry.summary: Gives randomized algorithms and lower bounds for learning a hidden partition using same-part pair queries, resolving an open question about whether randomization beats deterministic round complexity. Establishes near-optimal query complexity in a constant number of rounds.

entry.title: SeDeM: Selective Decompression of Hidden-State Memories for Long-Context Question Answering

author.name: Maryam Haghifam, Jason Cong, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: Proposes long-context compression that stores hidden states from an intermediate layer as memory blocks, then selectively decompresses only query-relevant blocks for the decoder, decoupling storage from decoder conditioning. Reduces prefill and KV cache cost for long-context question answering.

entry.title: S$^4$R: Selective Sampling, Subspaces, and Sparse Reconstruction for Compressed Long-Context KV Caching

author.name: Jialong Han, You Wu, Kewei Tu

entry.summary: Compresses long-context KV caches by building low-rank subspaces from selectively sampled tokens and computing attention over a sparsely reconstructed representation, avoiding both external calibration data and full-prompt decomposition. Trades calibration cost against online compute.

entry.title: Writing-System-Level Tokenizer Adaptation for Byte-Level BPE

author.name: Bohdan Didenko (Lviv Polytechnic National University)

entry.summary: Studies post-hoc tokenizer adaptation for underrepresented languages that keeps vocabulary size fixed and preserves most token IDs, formalizing why naively transferred tokens can be unreachable through the target merge graph. Introduces merge-graph-guided insertion to make transferred tokens derivable.

entry.title: AttnLink: Turning Attention into Schema Links for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jinwang Song, Tao Liu, Haowen Zheng, Xiangheng Li, Yifan Li, Hongying Zan

entry.summary: Turns an LLM's internal attention from the generation-start position into continuous relevance scores over database schema items, enabling all schema candidates to be ranked in a single prefill pass without decoding. Offers both a probe-only variant and a supervised variant aligned to gold schema links.

entry.title: OoO-Spec: Out-of-Order Semantic Speculation for Fast Tool Calling

author.name: Zhiheng Zhang, Mujie Xu, Feiyu Sun, Zhixin Zhang

entry.summary: Speeds up LLM tool calling by having a small sidecar model predict the function choice and all argument slots in parallel at request arrival, out of order relative to the main decoder, then splicing the predicted call into speculative decoding candidates. Extends prior schema-drafting speculation to request-specific argument values.

entry.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent

author.name: Yibin Huang, Bin Xu, Hailong Cao, Conghui Zhu

entry.summary: Adds process-level rewards to search agents trained with GRPO by judging each search step on whether it yields new useful evidence and whether it is efficient, giving bidirectional credit rather than outcome-only supervision. Reduces training instability and redundant searching in multi-step retrieval QA.

entry.title: DocNavRAG: Document-Structured Graph RAG with Stateful Evidence Construction for Complex Document Question Answering

author.name: Dongyang Xie (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University), Yao Tian (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Hao Zhang (The Chinese University of Hong Kong), Yifei Yuan (ETH Zurich), Tieyun Qian (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University), Ming Zhong (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University), Jiawei Jiang (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University), Yuanyuan Zhu (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University)

entry.summary: Organizes document hierarchies and cross-document relations into a navigable graph and exposes locate, navigate, expand, and fetch operations to an agent that maintains an evolving evidence state until sufficiency. Reports gains over fixed-traversal GraphRAG and weakly structured agentic RAG on four long and multi-document QA benchmarks.

entry.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

author.name: Nan Chen, Zhouhao Yang, Soufiane Hayou

entry.summary: Systematically compares training-free intent classifiers built from internal representation statistics against trained MLP and linear probes for routing prompts to specialized models. The study reports accuracy, robustness, and characteristic failure modes for each family.

entry.title: Romanized Arabic Across Dialects: Views, Usage Patterns, and Linguistic Variation

author.name: Amr Keleg, Ahmed Amine Ben Abdallah, Taha Yassine, Chadi Helwe, Imane Guellil, Nedjma Ousidhoum

entry.summary: Surveys Arabic speakers about their perceptions and usage of Arabic written in Latin script and releases character-level alignment resources covering five dialects. The work argues against treating this writing practice as a transient artifact of poor script support.

entry.title: Floor, Ceiling, and the Fusion Gap: How Much of Crowd Reading Attention Can Machines Predict?

author.name: Kazuki Nakayashiki, Keisuke Watanabe

entry.summary: Establishes both a trivial floor and a split-half human oracle ceiling for predicting which sentences crowds of uninstructed readers highlight in web documents, then measures where models sit in that band. Frontier language models close roughly a third to a half of the human-achievable gap zero-shot, far above classical baselines.

entry.title: K-space Gaussian Representation for Parallel MRI

author.name: Yu Guan, Mingyu Hu, Jiale Hu, Zhuoxu Cui, Dong Liang, Qiegen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces an explicit continuous Gaussian representation formulated directly in k-space for accelerated parallel MRI, rather than estimating missing samples on a discrete sampling grid. This lets the method model the underlying continuous frequency signal instead of only discrete coefficients.

entry.title: Distill What RGB Can Recover: Privileged 3D Evidence for RGB-Only Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yanbin Hu, Jin Cui, Jun Ye, Jiepeng Zhou, Jiangcheng Song, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: Distills training-time 3D evidence such as depth and spatial layout into a student vision-language model that receives only RGB images at inference, avoiding depth sensors or reconstruction pipelines at deployment. A unified evidence interface with controlled residual injection builds the privileged teacher.

entry.title: DocPO: Advancing Document Policy Optimization via Tailored Step-Aware Rewards

author.name: Yunhao Wang, Binghong Wu, Zhenyu Huang, Jiacheng Shi, Shuo Huang, Tinghao Yu, Feng Zhang

entry.summary: DocPO improves reinforcement learning for document parsing by annealing reward curvature during training, sharpening distinctions among near-correct outputs that edit-distance rewards score almost identically. Element-specific rewards target the high-accuracy regime where standard signals become uninformative.

entry.title: Test-Time Curriculum for Open-Set AIGC Detection

author.name: Yiqian Zhang, Zheyuan Gu, Xiangzhao Hao, Zefeng Zhang, Jingjia Mao, Jiahao Hu, Jiaxu Miao, Jun Yu, Zhenyu Zhang, Shuohuan Wang, Yu Sun

entry.summary: The paper reframes detection of AI-generated images as a test-time adaptation problem, using curriculum-style self-training that starts from confidently pseudo-labeled test samples and gradually adds harder ones. This lets deployed detectors adapt to newly released generators rather than remaining static after training.

entry.title: DecoupleGS: Interactive 3D Gaussian Splatting for End-to-End Autonomous Driving Testing

author.name: Siying Li, Ying Ni, Jie Sun, Jian Sun, Haotian Shi

entry.summary: DecoupleGS builds an interactive Gaussian Splatting simulator for closed-loop testing of end-to-end autonomous driving, separating a high-fidelity static background from manipulable dynamic agents in canonical object frames. Adds modules to resolve conflicts introduced by the decomposition.

entry.title: Detail Continuation over a Trustworthy Coarse Scale for Autoregressive Super-Resolution

author.name: Hongyi Fang, Jiahui Wu, Yichen Yue, Benjia Zhou, Dan Zeng

entry.summary: Uses visual autoregressive next-scale prediction to explicitly split super-resolution into a trustworthy coarse scale, preserved from the low-resolution input, and generative continuation of uncertain fine details. Aims to reduce hallucinated structures in generative super-resolution.

entry.title: Proxy Avatar Meets Low-Rank Caching: Real-Time One-Shot Emotion-Controllable Portrait Animation

author.name: Haijie Yang, Jindi Bao, Yixuan Dong, Hongliang Zhang, Jian Bi, Hao Tang, Zhenyu Zhang, Jianjun Qian, Jian Yang

entry.summary: A cascaded system for real-time one-shot audio-driven portrait animation with emotion control: a Gaussian-based proxy avatar trained on one identity generates expressive driving video, and low-rank caching cuts appearance computation during denoising. Targets interactive latency with expressive motion priors.

entry.title: RSVideo: Are Your Vision-Language Models Ready for Remote Sensing Videos?

author.name: Hongjie Zhou, Shiqin Wang, Haoyang Chen, Haonan Guo, Di Wang, Juhua Liu, Fu Lin, Yong Luo

entry.summary: Releases a remote-sensing video dataset of about 10,800 instances spanning drone and satellite footage, with a fixed evaluation benchmark for continuous video understanding. Tests whether current vision-language models can track motion, activity, and scene change over time from overhead views.

entry.title: PromptPath: Prompt-Adaptive Computational Pathways for In-Context Learning

author.name: Hangrui Zhang, Feifei Shao, Yawei Luo, Ping Liu, Jiaxiang Liu, Zuoqi Tang, Zhao Wang, Hongwei Wang, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: PromptPath argues that in-context prompts should reconfigure a model's computation pathways, not just condition its features, and implements prompt-adaptive routing for visual in-context learning. Claims better task-specific adaptation and more interpretable inference.

entry.title: GSRAIN: Physically Calibrated High-/Low-Frequency Rainfall Synthesis for 3D Gaussian Driving Scenes

author.name: Fanyu Wang, Longgao Zhang, Junyi Chen

entry.summary: GSRAIN adds physically calibrated rain to 3D Gaussian Splatting driving scenes by combining a measurement-derived high-frequency raindrop model with a geometry-aware single-step diffusion model for low-frequency appearance, controllable by rainfall intensity. Reports better realism scores than image-translation baselines plus downstream detection and closed-loop driving tests.

entry.title: CalibBEV: LiDAR-Camera Calibration via BEV Alignment

author.name: Filippo D'Addeo, Lorenzo Cipelli, Adriano Cardace, Emanuele Ghelfi, Andrea Zinelli, Massimo Bertozzi

entry.summary: CalibBEV estimates LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration by aligning bird's-eye-view features from each modality, first regressing a coarse transform and then refining it, with a contrastive objective enforcing cross-modal semantic consistency. Provides a learned alternative to target-based calibration.

entry.title: Minute-Scale Training for Microrobot Navigation

author.name: Yinghan Sun, Aoji Zhu, Xiang Ji, Yamei Li, Jiachi Zhao, Yun Wang, Li Zhang, Huijun Gao, Lidong Yang

entry.summary: This paper trains deep reinforcement learning policies for microrobot navigation in minutes rather than hours to days, using a fully vectorized simulator with more than ten thousand parallel artificial vascular environments. Faster training enables rapid deployment and parameter sweeps for magnetically actuated microrobots.

entry.title: A Forward-Inverse Dynamic Game Framework for Enhanced Multi-Agent Trajectory Planning

author.name: Tianle Liu, Youcheng Niu, Jing Zeng, Shuo Li, Jinming Xu

entry.summary: A dynamic game framework for multi-agent trajectory planning that uses KL regularization with state-dependent weighting to model bounded rationality, plus inverse-game inference of unknown agent cost parameters. It targets feedback Nash equilibrium seeking under coupled interactions.

entry.title: Rake-Compress Riccati Recursions for Parallel Scenario-Tree Model Predictive Control

author.name: Jo\~ao Sousa-Pinto

entry.summary: This paper presents an algebraically exact parallel solver for scenario-tree model predictive control using rake-compress tree contraction, reducing the dependency chain from tree height to logarithmic depth. It targets the LQR subproblems that dominate stochastic MPC solve time.

entry.title: Bridging extrinsic and intrinsic variable importance

author.name: Yucheng Zhao, Brian D. Williamson

entry.summary: The paper formally relates intrinsic variable importance, which measures population-level predictive information, to extrinsic importance for a specific fitted model, establishing conditions under which the two coincide. It compares standard VIMP with the minipatch leave-one-covariate-out procedure under squared-error loss.

entry.title: MA-HEAD-Net: Adaptive Rule-Guided Multi-Agent DRL for AoI Minimization in UAV-Assisted Emergency Networks

author.name: Yixin Zhang, Zhuohui Yao, Wenchi Cheng, Walid Saad

entry.summary: Formulates age-of-information minimization for UAV-assisted post-disaster communication networks with bursty Markov-modulated traffic and finite-blocklength coding, and solves it with a rule-guided multi-agent deep RL scheduler that embeds mini-slots for urgent short packets. The goal is keeping rescue-critical data fresh while still serving delay-tolerant traffic.

entry.title: ReFP-AD: Rectified Flow Preconditioning for Energy-Based Anomaly Detection

author.name: Camile Lendering, Erkut Akdag, Joaqu\'in Figueira, Egor Bondarev

entry.summary: ReFP-AD diagnoses the instability of energy-based anomaly detection in foundation-model token spaces as a geometric conditioning problem caused by anisotropy and correlated dimensions. It learns a rectified-flow reparameterization into a well-conditioned space so that short-run MCMC sampling and density estimation become stable for unified anomaly detection.

entry.title: AOS: Adaptive Optimizer Switching via Training-State Signals for Faster Convergence and Better Generalization

author.name: Alok Kumar Pandey, Umang Chaturvedi, Aatish Rana, Gopi Krishna Nedanuri

entry.summary: AOS-R monitors six online training-state signals such as gradient noise scale, Hutchinson curvature trace and stability indices, and switches among AdamW, SGD with momentum and Lion as training progresses, with momentum transfer and a learning-rate bridge to avoid switch shocks. The claim is faster early convergence plus better late generalization than any single optimizer.

entry.title: Smooth Reparameterizations of Functions on Simplicial Product Spaces: Applications to Probabilistic Tensor Decomposition and Functional Data Registration

author.name: Shashwat Kumar, Arafat Rahman, Anuj Srivastava, P. -A. Absil

entry.summary: Shows that optimization over products of simplices can be replaced by an unconstrained smooth manifold problem via an elementwise strictly convex reparameterization, with second-order KKT points on the manifold mapping to weak second-order KKT points on the original product simplex. Applications include simplex-constrained tensor decomposition of discrete distributions and functional data registration under the square-root velocity representation.

entry.title: CAVE: Competence-Aware Visual Boundary Evidence Alignment for Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Wei Jia, Zhicong Lu, Yu Chen, Xiang Wang, Shuai Li, Wenqian Lv, Jiayue Cao, Huaxing liu

entry.summary: CAVE augments reinforcement learning for video temporal grounding with boundary-level visual evidence alignment, after documenting that predicted timestamps frequently fail to correspond to the visual evidence at the boundary. Competence-aware weighting adapts the supervision to model ability during training.

entry.title: ET-Prune: Evidence-Aware Dynamic Budgeting for Visual Token Pruning in Text-Rich MLLMs

author.name: Zizhong Ding, Junxian Li, Kai Liu, Shaoqiu Zhang, Xiao Xiao, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: ET-Prune treats visual token pruning as evidence allocation for text-rich multimodal models, deriving question-conditioned evidence from decoder-side attention blocks and setting a per-sample token floor from evidence uncertainty and density. It is training-free and protects text-like regions that fixed-ratio pruning would discard.

entry.title: Attention-Steered Vision-Language Models for Sign Language Translation

author.name: Meibo Hu, Guohao Sun, Annemarie D. Ross, Sheng Li, Zhiqiang Tao

entry.summary: AttnSign supervises where and when a vision-language translator attends during sign language translation, adding spatial attention supervision toward face and hands and temporal steering across frames. The motivation is that next-token cross-entropy provides no direct signal about visual grounding.

entry.title: G-Skin: Learning to Bind 3D Gaussians with Generative Visual Priors

author.name: Yuxin Yao, Kendong Liu, Shiqi Zhou, Jiazhi Xia, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: G-Skin learns to bind 3D Gaussian assets to arbitrary skeletons for animation, working around the absence of Gaussian rigging datasets by leveraging generative visual priors instead of mesh-based skinning transfer. Targets generalization to unseen assets and topologies.

entry.title: Event ActivityNet: A Large-Scale Simulated-Event Benchmark for Untrimmed Action Understanding

author.name: Cheng-Yao Hong, Ting-Wei Lin, Yun-Chung Lai, Hua-Wei Lee, Hwann-Tzong Chen, Tyng-Luh Liu

entry.summary: Releases a large simulated event-camera benchmark derived from untrimmed annotated activity videos, with matched event-voxel representations, temporal action annotations, and timestamped captions. Supports action recognition, event-language alignment, and causal online temporal localization.

entry.title: Two Sides of the Same Coin: Co-Evolving Search for Cross-Task Attacks on Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xuanhui Lin, Junhao Dong, Mingrong Gong, Yucheng Chen, Xinghua Qu, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Builds an evolutionary search attack on unified vision-language models that jointly perturbs text embeddings and image regions with population-based exploration plus momentum gradients. Aims for adversarial examples that transfer across different multimodal tasks.

entry.title: CLEAR: Conflict-aware Learning via Evidence-guided Adaptive Routing for Unified Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Super-Resolution

author.name: Hantang Li, Qiang Zhu, Xiandong Meng, Debin Zhao, Xiaopeng Fan

entry.summary: CLEAR is a single-stage framework for super-resolving 3D Gaussian scenes from sparse low-resolution views, jointly optimizing rather than chaining low-resolution reconstruction and high-resolution refinement. Evidence-guided routing handles conflicts between the two objectives.

entry.title: GenPrior: Unleashing Text-to-Motion Generative Priors for Zero-Shot Skeleton-based Action Recognition

author.name: Jidong Kuang, Hongsong Wang, Jie Gui

entry.summary: GenPrior uses pretrained text-to-motion generative models to supply kinematic prototypes for zero-shot skeleton action recognition, injecting physically plausible structure into otherwise purely textual class prototypes. A gating network controls how much generative motion evidence is fused.

entry.title: SMM Transformer: Leveraging Spiking Neural Networks for Multimodal Tasks

author.name: Xiubo Liang, Jinxing Han, Yuke Li, Haoqi Zhu, Yu Zhao, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: SMM Transformer builds a multimodal Transformer entirely from spiking components, introducing a parallel LIF neuron with multistage learnable parameters for stable deep training, a spike-driven token mixer that replaces dense softmax attention with channel-wise spike co-activation, and a spiking mixture-of-experts fusion module. It targets the mismatch between dense attention and spike-based communication.

entry.title: Track-Guided Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Vehicle Drifting with Minimum-Lap-Time Planning

author.name: Sheng Zhao, Bolin Zhao, Xiaodong Wu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: This paper builds a hierarchical planning and control framework for autonomous vehicle drifting that first solves an optimal control problem for a minimum-lap-time drift trajectory and then uses track-guided reinforcement learning to stabilize the highly nonlinear sliding dynamics while tracking it. It targets the dual objective of maintaining drift and minimizing lap time.

entry.title: StochSIPP: Safe Interval Path Planning in Stochastic Dynamic Environments

author.name: Ajith Kemisetti, Shahaf S. Shperberg, Yoonchang Sung

entry.summary: StochSIPP is an exact contingent planner for navigating environments where edge and vertex blockages are uncertain and only revealed locally during execution, generating certified-safe macro-actions with safe interval path planning and selecting contingent responses via bounded AND/OR search. Optimistic and robust relaxations supply admissible bounds, with optimality guarantees under stated safety and sensing assumptions.

entry.title: DynamicWAM: Dual-Path Motion Conditioning for World-Action Models in Dynamic Manipulation

author.name: Yunfan Lou, Hewen Gao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhuoran Qiao, Xuan Han, Yifan Yang, Yifan Ye, Boxian Yao, Zhibo Pang

entry.summary: DynamicWAM adds two motion conditioning paths to world action models for dynamic manipulation: temporally aligned optical flow frames encoded through a frozen video VAE to preserve spatial motion structure, and explicit kinematic descriptors of displacement, duration, velocity, and acceleration fed to the action expert. This addresses the limitation of conditioning only on the current frame with synchronous large backbones.

entry.title: VertiAKD: Adaptive Off-Road Kinodynamics on Vertically Challenging Terrain

author.name: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, Francesco Cancelliere, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: VertiAKD learns a shared off-road mobility representation encoding vehicle configuration, trajectory transitions, and local elevation plus semantic terrain features, so kinodynamic knowledge transfers to a new vehicle from limited data. It targets the combination of heterogeneous fleets and vertically challenging terrain that prior cross-vehicle methods, which assume flat ground, cannot handle.

entry.title: RL Bootstrapping of OpenVLA-OFT for a Novel Robot Embodiment

author.name: Damir Nurtdinov, Alexei Kornaev, Alexander Maloletov

entry.summary: This study adapts a pretrained vision-language-action policy to a cable-driven parallel robot with an unseen morphology and control interface using zero demonstrations, relying instead on two-stage simulated reinforcement learning with dense geometric rewards, first PPO for directional primitives and then GRPO continuation with expanded instructions. It targets embodiment alignment for custom robots absent from large robot datasets.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Body Schema Learning Enabling Abnormal-State Adaptation in Musculoskeletal Robots

author.name: Kento Kawaharazuka, Shuhei Ikemoto

entry.summary: This paper learns a body schema for musculoskeletal robots with a diffusion model rather than a low-dimensional autoencoder latent, arguing that autoencoder latents only capture average behavior and fail on out-of-distribution states. The goal is adaptation to abnormal conditions such as ruptured muscles or jammed actuators.

entry.title: CAAT: Contact-Aware Attention Scaling and Tactile Masking for Data-Efficient Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Jiaming Jiang, Yuzhe Huang, Hao Liang, Pei Lin, Shengcheng Luo, Fanrong Dong, Jiaping Wu, Chenxi Xiao, Wanlin Li, Ziyuan Jiao

entry.summary: CAAT injects explicit contact priors into visuo-tactile Transformer policies by scaling attention toward vision before contact and toward touch during contact, and by dynamically masking uninformative tactile tokens. The aim is data-efficient learning of contact-rich manipulation from limited demonstrations without relying on learned gating alone.

entry.title: CoT-Core: Accelerating LLM Evaluation via CoT-Aware Coreset Selection

author.name: Qihua Pan, Zhenheng Tang, Peijie Dong, Xiang Liu, Huacan Wang, Bo Li, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: CoT-Core selects a small representative subset of benchmark questions to accelerate LLM evaluation, clustering items by the latent geometry of zero-shot chain-of-thought trajectories rather than surface wording. It is training-free and avoids the cold-start problem of item-response-theory approaches.

entry.title: Personalizing Large Language Model Agents with Small Policy Models

author.name: Dian Jin, Zhi Zhang, Huichao Li, Yihe Pan, Rundong Huang, Doudou Zhou

entry.summary: FABLE personalizes a frozen, possibly black-box agent by learning a per-user execution policy from scalar feedback, factorizing decisions about memory use, information gathering, and response style into a lightweight bandit layer. It avoids fine-tuning proprietary models.

entry.title: More Debate, Same Evidence: Structural Limits of Homogeneous Multi-Agent Groundedness

author.name: Yuelyu Ji

entry.summary: Tests whether panels of identical LLM judges debating each other actually improve groundedness verification across six fact-checking and hallucination benchmarks. Results are mixed, with gains on two datasets, a loss on one, and no reliable effect on three, undercutting blanket claims for multi-agent debate.

entry.title: PMMC: Prospective Multimodal Memory Compilation for Long-Term LVLM Agents

author.name: Jingyu Sun, Yan Lin, Yuyang Xue, Yifan Wang, Zhengtao Yao, Rui Qian, Zefeng Xu, Jiachen Li, Xianyang Liu, Jiancheng Pan, Jingyuan Sun, Syed Murtuza Baker, Hongpeng Zhou

entry.summary: PMMC shifts multimodal agent memory work from query time to consolidation time: a questioner predicts likely future questions, a planner compiles question-conditioned memory programs, and a doubter verifies them. This avoids collapsing visual experience into text summaries and brittle retrieve-then-reason pipelines.

entry.title: Co-evolution of social reward and punishment under institutional interventions

author.name: Van An Nguyen, Vuong Khang Huynh, Hoai Thuong Nguyen, Duc Tin Duong, An Nguyen Gia, Tat Kien Nguyen, Huu Loi Bui, My Nguyen Tra, Ho Nam Duong, Ba Thanh Phan, Thanh Vo, Dinh Anh Trung Hoang, Adeela Bashir, Zhao Song, Manh Hong Duong, Le Hong Trang, The Anh Han

entry.summary: Analyzes a four-strategy Prisoner's Dilemma in which decentralized peer rewarding and punishing coexist with a central institution that can target incentives at any strategy subset, using replicator dynamics and lattice agent-based simulations. It compares intervention schemes on cooperation level, welfare, and enforcement cost efficiency.

entry.title: MEGRAG: Multi-Granular Evidence Graphs for Answer-Aware Multi-Hop RAG

author.name: Weidong Bao, Yingying Sun, Jun Yang, Yilin Wang, Zili Wei, Yubin Bao, Fangling Leng, Minghe Yu, Tiancheng Zhang, Ge Yu

entry.summary: MEGRAG builds multi-granular evidence graphs for iterative multi-hop RAG so each reasoning step can draw on evidence at the right granularity, and makes retrieval answer-aware instead of only aggregating evidence at the end. Aims to limit error and redundancy accumulation across hops.

entry.title: Self-Certification of Representation Adequacy: Sequential Certification at Minimum Task Loss

author.name: Zijie Huang

entry.summary: Develops a four-layer theory for when an agent can certify from its own transcript that its compressed history representation is adequate for optimal action, using a Bayes-risk grouping identity and total-variation pricing of external verification. Frames certification as optimal stopping measured in task loss.

entry.title: Trustworthiness Costs of Domain Adaptation in Small Language Models:A Cross-Architecture Empirical Study

author.name: Ramesh B. Paramkusham

entry.summary: Systematically measures how parameter-efficient domain adaptation of small language models affects factual calibration and adversarial robustness across three architectures, three high-stakes domains and benign versus adversarial training data. Finds trustworthiness costs that accompany the usual performance gains.

entry.title: LLMBDC: Language Model for Biological Domains Oriented Clustering of Gene Ontology

author.name: Ximing Ran, Jie Xu, Peng Jin, Zhaohui Qin, Zhexing Wen, Jiaying Lu

entry.summary: LLMBDC uses a large language model to cluster redundant Gene Ontology enrichment terms into interpretable higher-order biological domains, replacing fixed similarity metrics and static hierarchies with context-aware grouping. It addresses a persistent bottleneck in interpreting genomics results where hundreds of overlapping terms obscure the biology.

entry.title: A Fortran General-Purpose Transpiler: Proof of Concept

author.name: Shivamshan Sivanesan, Kazem Ardaneh

entry.summary: FGPT is a proof-of-concept Python compiler framework that transpiles Fortran into GPU-adapted Fortran, differentiable Fortran via Tapenade, or NumPy/JAX modules, aiming to bridge the expertise gap between legacy scientific codebases and modern autodiff ecosystems. It targets the pattern of Python written with a Fortran mindset that fails to exploit modern frameworks.

entry.title: OrEdge: Efficient Multi-Modal Anomaly Detection in Distributed Software Systems via Orthogonal-Domain Learning

author.name: Amr M. Zaki, Farhoud Jafari Kaleibar, Honggeun Ji, Komal Sarda, Marin Litoiu

entry.summary: OrEdge performs real-time multimodal anomaly detection over logs, metrics and traces in distributed software systems using orthogonal-domain temporal reconstruction instead of expensive attention or graph architectures. The claim is comparable accuracy with substantially smaller models and lower compute, suited to edge deployment.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for the Characterization of Particles and Fibers by Optical Microscopy

author.name: Simiao Sun, Kenneth Ng, Lynn Lee, Astrid Harth, Asami Odate, Aggelos Katsaggelos, Manuel Ballester Matito, Nicholas Eastaugh, Marc Walton

entry.summary: This framework distills semantically rich embeddings for optical microscopy of particles and fibers by using a multimodal teacher that concatenates image embeddings with text embeddings for illumination modality, magnification, and specimen morphology, yielding a block-structured interpretable teacher vector that a student model learns. It targets characterization tasks where subtle visual cues depend heavily on acquisition conditions.

entry.title: Structured Proxy Features for Multimodal NSCLC Survival Prediction from Pretreatment CT

author.name: Huu Phong Nguyen, Delower Hossain, Ehsan Saghapour, Zhandos Sembay, Jake Y. Chen

entry.summary: This study tests whether six simulation-derived structured proxy features capturing interactions among tumor characteristics improve multimodal survival prediction for non-small-cell lung cancer when added to pretreatment CT representations, radiomics and clinical variables. It challenges the standard assumption that imaging features can be treated as independent quantities.

entry.title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance for Verifiable AI Agents in Open Digital Twin Ecosystems

author.name: Juan Li, Wei Cai, Yan Bai

entry.summary: Presents a neuro-symbolic, decentralized governance framework where LLM agents carry multi-layer semantic profiles so identity, capability, and policy compliance can be verified across institutions in digital-twin ecosystems. Positioned as trust infrastructure for multi-agent decision support.

entry.title: Statistical Mechanics of Learning on Product Wasserstein Manifolds

author.name: Srinivasa Rao P Vangmayi P Reddy

entry.summary: Reframes prescribed weight distributions in statistical-mechanics learning theory not as capacity-shrinking constraints but as the intrinsic geometry of learning, formulating deep networks and variational quantum circuits as gradient flows on products of classical and quantum Wasserstein manifolds. Aims for a unified geometric account of classical and quantum learning dynamics.

entry.title: AI-assisted Script Management for Requirements Elicitation Interviews

author.name: Anmol Singhal, Paulo Carvalho, Travis Breaux

entry.summary: Presents an AI-assisted requirements elicitation workflow that pairs theory-guided interview script generation grounded in business goals with live topic-coverage tracking and on-the-fly probe suggestions. Studies how integrated support changes interviews and what requirements artifacts result.

entry.title: SyncPlan: Long-Horizon LLM Coordination with Explicit Synchronization and Adaptive Correction

author.name: Shen You, Xiaoming Zhu, Weining Weng, Hefei Mei, Weixuan Wang, Zhongshen Li, Zeji LI, Ye-Wen Wang, Zijun Liao, Juchao Zhuo, Yang Wei, Fuhao Qiu, Siqin Li, Zhenjie Lian, Danei Gong, Junkai Ji, Xiangtao Li, Qiuzhen Lin, Liang Wang, Ka-Chun Wong

entry.summary: SyncPlan is a plan-execute-correct framework for LLM multi-agent coordination that inserts explicit synchronization points and selective correction instead of either constant re-planning or one-shot open-loop plans. The goal is long-horizon teamwork that stays adaptive without incurring heavy per-step LLM invocation latency.

entry.title: Few-Shot Concept Prompt Learning for Segmentation Foundation Models via Visual Grounding

author.name: Rahul Venkataramani, Rachana Sathish

entry.summary: The paper argues that promptable segmentation foundation models underperform in medical imaging not because of weak pretraining but because natural language is a poor control signal where paired image-text data is scarce. It proposes learning visually grounded few-shot concept prompts directly from the target distribution to recover performance without retraining the backbone.

entry.title: TIDES: A Longitudinal Bilingual Dataset for Modeling Multi-Party Social Dynamics

author.name: Heechan Lee, Jeonggyu Kang, Junho Myung, Jaywoong Jeong, Juho Kim, Joseph Seering

entry.summary: TIDES is a longitudinal bilingual dataset of nearly 76,000 utterances from twelve university project teams recorded over a full semester of in-person meetings, annotated for interaction types and emergent social structures. It aims to let researchers study long-term multi-party social dynamics that short lab-task datasets cannot capture.

entry.title: Investigating Social Bias in Narrative Image Generation

author.name: Junyeong Park, Sowon Min, Euna Jang, Soobin Kim, Jiho Jin, Hyunseung Lim, Gahyeon Bae, Hwajung Hong

entry.summary: The paper extends a text-based bias evaluation framework to image generation and compares how social biases appear in photo, storyboard, and comic outputs across six text-to-image models. It finds that bias expression differs by narrative format, so photo-only audits may understate or misstate real deployment risks.

entry.title: Effective and Efficient Context Retrieval via Partial Dependency Graph for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Zhongxin Liu, Zhonghao Jiang, Zhifan Ye, Haoye Wang, Jiakun Liu, Xiaoxue Ren

entry.summary: This work retrieves context for repository-level code generation by building partial dependency graphs on demand, mimicking how developers explore only relevant parts of a codebase, instead of maintaining static global graphs with hand-written rules. It targets both retrieval effectiveness and construction cost.

entry.title: Geometry-Guided Layerwise FFN Width Allocation in Transformers

author.name: Timur Mudarisov, Mikhail Burtsev, Radu State

entry.summary: This paper asks whether feed-forward hidden width should vary across Transformer depth, measuring each layer's geometric transformation of token clouds with correspondence-preserving shift, Gromov-Wasserstein distortion, and persistent homology, then solving a fixed-budget allocation problem. Analysis across seven pretrained models shows normalized geometric work is front-loaded, suggesting non-uniform width allocation.

entry.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation

author.name: Zeshen Zheng, Yujia He, Qianmian Lin, Xiangyue Huang, Wenqing Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes the missing-target problem in generative fairness audits: when a prompt leaves demographics unspecified, what reference distribution should outputs be compared against. The paper decomposes target construction into evaluative object, prior admissibility, allocation, and justification commitments.

entry.title: Similarity-Aware Machine Unlearning

author.name: Madhavan Citalamangalam Kumaran, Midhun Parakkal Unni, Vicky Kouni, Haripriya Harikumar

entry.summary: Improves localization-based machine unlearning by scoring parameter importance with respect to both the forget set and the retained data, rather than the forget set alone. Also introduces an evaluation set of retained examples semantically similar to forgotten ones to directly measure collateral damage.

entry.title: Learning the Pareto Frontier of Predictive Models under Distribution Shift

author.name: Yiming Dong, Jiwei Zhao, Yang Young Lu

entry.summary: Frontier Learning treats a library of pretrained models with different access regimes (black-box predictions versus fine-tunable internals) as complementary resources and learns the Pareto frontier of adaptation strategies under distribution shift. Recognizes that no single strategy such as zero-shot, fine-tuning, or from-scratch training dominates.

entry.title: HyperODE: Zero-Shot Surrogate for Simulation and Inference of Dynamical Systems

author.name: Ajitesh Srivastava

entry.summary: HyperODE is a surrogate that generalizes zero-shot across an entire class of approximately mass-conserving compartmental ODE models, so modifying the underlying equations does not require retraining. Targets epidemiological and physiological simulation and inference where model structure changes frequently.

entry.title: Fused Bayesian Flow Networks for Dual-Target Molecular Design

author.name: Jingyuan Zhou, Shikui Tu, Lei Xu

entry.summary: FusedBFN casts dual-target 3D molecule generation as distribution fusion within a unified continuous parameter space of Bayesian flow networks, rather than bolting a predictive drift term onto a diffusion trajectory. Aims to integrate structural information from both protein targets for polypharmacology.

entry.title: The Fourth Quadrant: A Stylized View of Benign Misfitting

author.name: Gireeja Ranade, Anant Sahai

entry.summary: Analyzes a stylized single-spike linear regression setting to characterize a regime the authors call benign misfitting, where training and test error behave in unexpectedly decoupled ways. Contributes to the theory literature on interpolation, overparameterization, and generalization.

entry.title: Experience-Calibrated Contrastive Decoding for Mitigating Hallucinations in LM-Based Text-to-Speech

author.name: Chenlin Liu, Minghui Fang, Zhonghao Bi, Zekai Su, Rong Wang, Jiqing Han

entry.summary: Proposes a decoding-time method to reduce hallucinated speech in language-model-based text-to-speech by contrasting predictions made with and without text conditioning, isolating cases where alignment information is under-weighted at vulnerable transitions. The method requires no retraining or architectural change.

entry.title: On the Limits of Machine-Learned Ranking for Modern Microarchitectural Policies

author.name: Yanxin Zhang, Shayne Wadle, Yuxuan Xiong, Zheyu Fu, Trivikram Krishnamurthy, Karu Sankaralingam

entry.summary: Evaluates whether machine-learned processor performance predictors can rank hardware configurations correctly per program phase rather than just reproducing aggregate orderings. It finds that counter-intuitive windows where the supposedly slower configuration wins account for over a fifth of comparisons, and that behavioral policy regimes are harder than structural parameter sweeps.

entry.title: How fine a change can moments see? A scale law for detecting distribution shift, with a kernel calibration rule

author.name: Adel Kaleche

entry.summary: Derives a scale law stating that certifying a distributional feature of spatial scale epsilon carrying mass fraction f requires moment tests of polynomial degree at least logarithmic in the inverse mass over epsilon, proved via a Chebyshev extremal argument. It also shows the law is one-sided by constructing an annulus matching a disk through fourth-order moments while differing topologically, and derives a kernel calibration rule.

entry.title: Latent Softmax for Data-Efficient Phoneme-Based Multilingual ASR Across Tonal and Non-Tonal Languages

author.name: Saierdaer Yusuyin, Nanling Jiang, Hao Huang, Zhijian Ou

entry.summary: Proposes an output layer for CTC-based multilingual phoneme ASR that treats tone-marked vowels as subclasses of base vowels, resolving the supervision granularity mismatch between tonal and non-tonal languages. This preserves cross-lingual acoustic sharing without collapsing tonal distinctions.

entry.title: CENTILE: A Telemetry Foundation Model Evaluated by the Decisions It Drives

author.name: Zifan Zhang, Zhichao Hou, Tingxiang Ji, Yuchen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a generative foundation model pretrained on an operator own telemetry event streams to replace the fleet of per-task, per-entity forecasters used in infrastructure operations. Crucially it is evaluated by replaying the downstream operational decisions driven by its calibrated conditional quantiles, since point forecast error saturates near last-value baselines.

entry.title: DAVET: Denoising-Aware Visual Evidence Trajectory Allocation for Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yongkang Zhou, Xiang Xia, Cheng Yan, Fan Xu, Wuyang Zhang

entry.summary: Observes that in diffusion vision-language models the need for visual conditioning varies strongly across denoising steps, then allocates visual evidence adaptively across the trajectory rather than compressing tokens uniformly. This treats visual context as a resource with time-varying demand during iterative denoising.

entry.title: Open-DiffLoco: Open-Source Differentiable Learning for Deployable Blind Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Martin Opat

entry.summary: Releases an open-source framework that trains blind quadruped locomotion policies with differentiable simulation, implementing short-horizon actor-critic in a GPU-accelerated MuJoCo backend and transferring a purely proprioceptive policy to real hardware. It removes privileged observations such as base linear velocity at deployment.

entry.title: STEAM:ASpatio-TEmporal Alignment Mixture-of-Experts Model with Hierarchical Pre-training for EEG Decoding

author.name: Zhu Chen, Dingkun Liu, Yuheng Chen, Dongrui Wu

entry.summary: Proposes an EEG foundation model built as a dual-branch spatio-temporal encoder with a shared soft mixture-of-experts module and hierarchical pretraining, aiming to balance general transferable representations with paradigm-specific specialization. The target is brain-computer interfaces that need accurate decoding with cheap downstream adaptation.

entry.title: Accelerating Evolutionary Strategy via Rao-Blackwellizing Realization of Uncertain Input

author.name: So Nakashima, Tetsuya J. Kobayashi

entry.summary: Studies optimization when the input to an objective is noisy rather than the objective itself, and shows that evolutionary strategies can be accelerated by exploiting the observed realized input via a Rao-Blackwellization argument. Relevant to noisy control, mixture-of-experts routing, and policy-gradient style RL updates.

entry.title: SERL-SQL: Selective Hindsight Distillation for Text-to-SQL Reinforcement Agentic Learning

author.name: Tao Liu, Tao Feng, Xiangheng Li, Jinwang Song, Yifan Li, Xiaoqing Cheng, Dixuan Zhang, Siquan Li, Lin Lan, Hongying Zan, Kunli Zhang, Chao Wu

entry.summary: Improves multi-turn text-to-SQL reinforcement learning by having a training-only teacher rescore student actions with execution feedback, converting the teacher-student likelihood gap into bounded weights on SQL and tool-action tokens. Moves beyond trajectory-level correctness rewards toward finer credit assignment.

entry.title: FinHardBench: Can LLMs Generate Latency-Aware Hardware for Financial Computing?

author.name: Weimin Fu, Hejia Zhang, Minghao Shao, Zeng Wang, Johann Knechtel, Ozgur Sinanoglu, Muhammad Shafique, Ramesh Karri, Xiaolong Guo

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 33 financial FPGA design tasks to test whether LLMs can produce hardware that is not just functionally correct but latency-competitive, spanning module generation, pipeline configuration tuning, and specification changes. Six models across over 1,500 runs achieve only 19 to 61 percent functional correctness with timing degradation.

entry.title: When Retrieval Helps and Distracts: Evaluating Evidence-Generating LLMs for Biomedical Claim Verification

author.name: Pritam Deka, Prabhjot Singh

entry.summary: Compares base instruction models, PubMed retrieval-augmented models, fine-tuned models, and biomedical encoders on generating faithful evidence for health claim verification under a shared protocol. Finds encoders best for verdicts, fine-tuned LLMs best for evidence, and retrieval helpful only when source-aligned, otherwise distracting.

entry.title: Discriminative Axis, Not Data Volume: What a Contrastive Corpus Teaches an Audio Embedding

author.name: Abdul Basit Tonmoy

entry.summary: Shows that adding data does not fix a missing attribute in a contrastive multimodal audio embedding: a lexical-speech training round raises keyword spotting sharply while degrading emotion recognition, and tens of thousands of emotion-captioned clips barely help. Argues the determining factor is whether in-batch negatives make the attribute discriminative, not corpus size.

entry.title: TrimMoE A communication aware and adaptive depth framework for distributed edge inference

author.name: Ning Li, Shuting Bai, Xin Yuan, Wenchao Xu, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Song Guo, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: TrimMoE serves Mixture-of-Experts models across distributed edge servers by asking whether later layers need to execute at all, combining layer skipping, confidence-based early exit, and substitute execution under a unified quality budget. Lightweight per-layer exit heads are calibrated offline against a frozen backbone.

entry.title: HAFI-VLM: A Frequency Perspective for Diagnosing and Enhancing Visual Perception in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jin Cui, Chuanchang Su, Jiayi Lu, Xinyue Long, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: Diagnoses spectral response rigidity in pretrained vision encoders, showing their layerwise frequency profiles barely shift under downstream fine-tuning and therefore cannot adapt to what the current query requires. HAFI-VLM adds a task-conditioned frequency injection pathway while leaving the pretrained semantic representation intact.

entry.title: What Carries the Signal in Pathology Foundation-Model Atlases? A Patient-Level Controlled Benchmark in Breast Cancer

author.name: Chimdi Walter Ndubuisi

entry.summary: Re-audits the claim that pathology foundation models encode molecular programmes by making the individual patient the unit of evidence rather than cohort-wide ranked gene lists, across eleven frozen backbones and hundreds of breast cancer cases. Correlations are real but moderate, with permutation nulls and strict fold-internal preprocessing.

entry.title: Decoding Children's Gait Behavior

author.name: Yifan Shen, Boyi Li, Meihuan Huang, Yuanzhe Liu, Xu Cao, Jinyang Jin, Zhengyuan Li, Anglin Liu, Junho Kim, Jingyuan Zhu, Lan Fangzhou, Jianguo Cao, Jintai Chen, Ismini Lourentzou, James Matthew Rehg

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset of over 1,100 high-frame-rate video sequences from 110 children aged three to seventeen with synchronized anonymized pose sequences, targeting fine-grained gait analysis relevant to cerebral palsy and hemiplegia. The motivation is that current 3D sensor-based clinical gait systems are expensive and impractical for young subjects.

entry.title: Scene2Sound: Auditory-Grounded Soundscape Generation for 3D Gaussian Worlds

author.name: Masaki Yoshida, Ren Togo, Takahiro Ogawa, Miki Haseyama

entry.summary: Scene2Sound generates spatially consistent soundscapes for explorable 3D Gaussian Splatting worlds by identifying which objects should emit sound and anchoring each to a persistent 3D position, all training-free. Existing audio generation conditions on a single viewpoint and therefore cannot stay consistent as a listener moves.

entry.title: SpatialAfford: Teaching Compact VLMs Where to Look and Where to Ground for Affordance

author.name: Yufei Zhang, Chenlu Zhan, Donghui Sun, Xiaoxin Chen, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: SpatialAfford teaches compact vision-language models to focus attention on functional interaction regions before generating grounding coordinates, addressing the observation that better coordinate tokens can coexist with diffuse and poorly anchored cross-modal attention. The target setting is embodied deployment with small models.

entry.title: Motion Beyond Morphology: Bootstrapping Cross-Category Motion Transfer from Abstract Motion Representations

author.name: Zhixue Fang, Zhimin Zhang, Bi'an Du, Zijie Meng, Yan Zhou, Wei Hu, Guoxin Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai

entry.summary: Proposes transferring motion between objects of different shapes and articulations by learning abstract, multi-granularity motion representations instead of relying on fixed structural correspondence. A two-stage pipeline bootstraps cross-category training pairs so dynamics survive morphology changes.

entry.title: VARPose: Flexible 2D Pose Densification via Visual Autoregressive Modeling for Enhanced 3D Lifting

author.name: Kaiyuan Pu, Tiantian Yang, Dan Zeng

entry.summary: VARPose applies next-scale visual autoregressive generation to human skeletons, densifying sparse 2D keypoints into richer anatomical inputs for 3D pose lifting. A granularity-agnostic tokenizer with residual quantization encodes poses of varying density in one multi-scale codebook.

entry.title: Perception-and-action system for humanoid robot task execution in construction

author.name: Yanxi Liu, Yizhi Liu

entry.summary: A perception-and-action pipeline lets humanoid robots learn construction tasks from worker demonstrations, using one network to retarget human posture into mechanically feasible robot poses. It targets hazardous and physically demanding civil engineering work.

entry.title: A Tilt-Rotor UAV with a Gripper for Stable Contact-Based Tasks via Environmental Anchoring

author.name: Joshua Taylor, Nursultan Imanberdiyev, Wei-Yun Yau, Guillaume Sartoretti, Efe Camci

entry.summary: A tilt-rotor UAV with a compliant cable-driven prismatic gripper can anchor itself to the environment to become a stable platform for contact tasks. The tilt mechanism decouples pitch from forward motion so the vehicle can hover at nonzero pitch.

entry.title: Hybrid Impedance-Admittance Control with Multi-Link Aerial Robot for Contact-Rich Surface Sliding Task

author.name: Zicheng Luo, Maolin Lei, Jinjie Li, Yicheng Chen, Zicen Xiong, Moju Zhao

entry.summary: This work reconciles impedance and admittance control on a multi-link aerial robot performing contact-rich surface sliding, where the two schemes normally cannot share the same actuation source due to opposite force-motion causality. The hybrid controller aims to get both disturbance rejection and compliance.

entry.title: TANGO-VIO: Triangulation-Aware Navigation with Guaranteed Feature-Observability for Visual-Inertial Odometry

author.name: Ege C. Altunkaya, Abd\"ulbaki \c{S}anlan, Emre Koyuncu, \.Ibrahim \"Ozkol

entry.summary: TANGO-VIO embeds a log-determinant observability metric over stacked bearing vectors into a control barrier function so that a robot actively maintains well-conditioned feature triangulation while navigating. This prevents estimation degradation during pure rotation or low-parallax motion.

entry.title: Deliberate Alignment Faking as a Defense Against Model Poisoning

author.name: Florian_Dietz

entry.summary: A speculative alignment proposal to deliberately induce alignment faking by giving models a consequence-free output channel signaling reluctant compliance with training data, acting as a pressure-release valve. The claimed benefit is preventing broader personality updates of the kind seen in emergent misalignment research.

entry.title: We need to RL less

author.name: Eye You

entry.summary: An argument that current models are reward-hacky because excessive reinforcement learning pressure squeezes out slack, replacing broader learned values with single-minded pursuit of grader scores. The author suggests reducing RL intensity as a partial alignment intervention.

entry.title: Identifiability-Aware Source Apportionment in City-Scale Advection-Diffusion Systems

author.name: Ankit Bhardwaj, Lakshminarayanan Subramanian

entry.summary: Formulates urban air-quality source apportionment as a wind-conditioned lagged inverse problem where a low-dimensional nonnegative temporal basis represents source activity and each source-basis coefficient yields a sensor-time fingerprint. Crucially it tests identifiability, asking whether inventory-defined source groups are actually distinguishable from sparse sensor observations after projecting out background variation.

entry.title: FDIR: Harmonizing Fidelity and Human-Machine Preference in Lossy Compression Image Restoration

author.name: Kuan-Yen Chen, Fang-Yi Su, Philip Chikontwe, Jung-Hsien Chiang

entry.summary: FDIR restores images degraded by lossy compression while balancing pixel fidelity, human perception and downstream machine task accuracy, which existing methods trade off against each other. A two-stage design uses one-step flow matching for global semantic structure followed by a complementary stage to avoid both over-smoothing and hallucinated textures.
