entry.summary: Spike-HTR is a hybrid spiking recognizer for handwritten text that converts a static image into a coarse-to-fine input stream so short spiking horizons suffice, and reduces the number of width positions processed by the sequence mixer. It exploits the fact that most pixels are background and most sequence positions are blank.

entry.title: Localization in Spatiotemporal Fields via Environmental PDEs

author.name: Jose Fuentes, Abdullah Al Redwan Newaz, Ana Cavalcanti, Leonardo Bobadilla

entry.summary: This paper localizes vehicles by using spatiotemporal physical fields governed by PDEs such as shallow water equations and advection-diffusion as location signatures, fusing multiple predicted field channels as multimodal measurements. A Rao-Blackwellized particle filter splits the state into sampled nonlinear and analytically tracked components.

entry.title: Push-Wiper: Toward General-Purpose Robotic Cleaning across Varied Stains and Surfaces with Segmented Pushing Trajectories

author.name: Renhao Lu, Mingxin Wang, Chenyang Cao, Yang Yang, Guoping Pan, Kangkang Dong, Yi Cheng, Houde Liu

entry.summary: Push-Wiper reframes cleaning viscous stains as an aggregation problem, using a sponge to progressively gather material with segmented pushing trajectories generated by a diffusion policy, then detaching the collected residue and self-cleaning the sponge. This avoids the smearing of conventional wiping and the surface damage risk of scrubbing.

entry.title: Sampling-Based Visibility Task Planning

author.name: Stav Ashur, Avishai Sintov

entry.summary: This paper develops sampling-based task and motion planning algorithms specialized for visibility-based instruments such as cameras, flashlights, and directional antennas, whose field-of-view constraints break common heuristics and distance metrics. Two new samplers are introduced for this class of tools.

entry.title: Dynamic UAV-based search operations using probabilistic diffusion modeling of Man Overboard incident victims

author.name: Dimosthenis Angelis, Evangelos Boukas

entry.summary: A UAV search strategy for man-overboard incidents predicts the drifting search area with an extended Kalman filter driven by an oceanographic leeway drift model, then compares five coverage patterns. The work is motivated by very high fatality rates in such incidents.

entry.title: Emergence Invariance: From Symbolized Thought to Interface Refinement

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: A philosophical position paper arguing language is a formalized subset of situated cognition, so language-first probabilistic models inherit structural incompletenesses even as scale produces compensatory emergent abilities. It formalizes a symbolization premise and asks whether emergence can ever recover every missing distinction.

entry.title: DeBERTa-Sentinel: Toward Transparent and Trustworthy Detection of AI-Generated Text

author.name: Muhammad Yousaf Rehman, Muhammad Islam

entry.summary: Fine-tunes DeBERTa-v3 for AI-generated text detection with token-level explanations, positioning transparency against black-box commercial detectors and claiming better robustness to paraphrasing than prior transformer detectors. Framed as responsible detection infrastructure for the web.

entry.title: PartMat: Material-Aware 3D Part Decomposition with a Single Global Latent

author.name: Guangming Fu, Jin Song, Yiyun Fei, Guoqiu Li, Ruigao Yang, Jianan Jiang

entry.summary: PartMat decomposes a 3D object into material-consistent parts, such as fabric, wood, and metal, from a reference image and whole-object geometry, representing all parts with a single global latent instead of generating them independently. This keeps cost from scaling linearly with part count while producing edit-ready assets.

entry.title: UniqueSplat: View-conditioned 3D Gaussian Splatting for Generalizable 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Haixu Song, Xiaoke Yang, Shengjun Zhang, Jiwen Lu, Yueqi Duan

entry.summary: UniqueSplat makes feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting view-conditioned, predicting Gaussians tailored to each target viewpoint rather than a single fixed set per scene as in pixelSplat and MVSplat. The view prior is baked into network parameters so Gaussians adapt dynamically at query time.

entry.title: Open-Set Visual Text Forensics via Sparse-Constraint Rectified Flow

author.name: Jiangling Zhang, Shuxuan Gao, Zeyu Chen, Yichao Liu, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: This paper detects and localizes AI-generated manipulation of visual text by estimating the local restoration cost needed to bring a query image back to authentic visual-text statistics, using a sparse-constraint adaptation of rectified flow rather than learning forgery-specific boundaries. Self-supervised artifact injection mitigates training data scarcity.

entry.title: Amortizing the Calibration Triple: A Projection-Consistent Neural Operator for Local-Stochastic Volatility

author.name: Xiaozhen Wang, Ana\"is Despr\'es, Martin Dureau, Francois Buet-Golfouse

entry.summary: Learns a neural operator that amortizes the slow iterative calibration of local-stochastic volatility models, jointly outputting an arbitrage-constrained implied volatility surface, the corresponding local volatility, the leverage function, and the conditional moment required for projection consistency. Both DeepONet and Fourier neural operator backbones are evaluated.

entry.title: Semantic Alignment of AI Models: Concept Collapse, Checkpoint Dynamics, and Cross-Lingual Transfer

author.name: Tyler Ashoff, Jordan Rodu

entry.summary: Uses topological methods to compare high-dimensional language model embedding spaces against interpretable low-dimensional baselines such as ontologies and curated knowledge graphs. The stated goal is to characterize semantic structure and track model adaptation and cross-lingual transfer beyond saturated outcome benchmarks.

entry.title: Characterizing Treatment-Context Medication Evidence Across Clinic Notes and Structured EHR Medication History

author.name: Mingyang Jiang, Congning Ni, Weixin Liu, Zhijun Yin

entry.summary: Presents a note-grounded pipeline that uses LLM-assisted reference building, human review, and deterministic normalization to reconcile medication mentions in clinic notes with structured EHR medication history. Held-out evaluation on over 5,000 mention rows shows improved canonical agreement, quantifying how much same-visit disagreement is genuine versus an artifact of extraction and normalization.

entry.title: PhysAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable Remote Heart Rate Estimation

author.name: Yehui Yang, Bo Zhao, Junzhe Cao, Hui Ma, Yue Sun, Wenjin Wang, Zitong Yu

entry.summary: PhysAgent is an inference-time multi-agent framework that arbitrates among conflicting heart-rate candidates produced by different remote photoplethysmography estimators, rather than training a new base model or asking a multimodal LLM to output heart rate directly. Verification agents check physiological plausibility of each candidate.

entry.title: RSC-GestureNet: Reliability-Aware Selective Causal Recognition of Chinese Traffic Police Gestures

author.name: Cheng Li, Renjun Gao, Boyi Fu

entry.summary: RSC-GestureNet recognizes traffic police hand signals causally from continuous video while down-weighting unreliable pose joints and selectively emitting only calibrated predictions. Also releases a corruption benchmark with several pose and image perturbations.

entry.title: SDDMO-Bench: A Benchmark Suite for Streaming Data-Driven Dynamic Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Wenjie Xiao, Hui Bai, Junhao Chen

entry.summary: SDDMO-Bench converts classical dynamic multi-objective test problems into streaming environments with controllable distributional drift and sequential data revelation, giving ground-truth optima and drift annotations that real problems lack. It crosses five time-dependent base functions with six drift patterns to standardize comparison.

entry.title: RAG-TESTER: Automated End-to-End Testing of Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

author.name: Ange Maiztegi, Jon Ayerdi, Miren Illarramendi, Aitor Arrieta

entry.summary: RagTester automatically generates documents, test inputs, and expected outputs for retrieval-augmented systems, executes them, and grades answers with an LLM judge, targeting hard passages, unanswerable queries, and coverage gaps. It is evaluated across 24 generator-embedder combinations.

entry.title: WM-Cov: Test Adequacy for Interactive World-Model-Style Autonomous Driving Simulation

author.name: Jianxun Cui, Ping Wu, Stanisa Peric, Marko Milojkovic, Vladan Devedzic

entry.summary: WM-Cov defines test adequacy for autonomous-driving evaluation using interactive world-model simulators, where the scenario evolves in response to the planner under test rather than replaying a fixed trajectory. It provides a provider-agnostic layer for deciding when closed-loop evidence is sufficient to stop testing.

entry.title: Diagnose Before You Compress: Prediction-Independent Bottleneck Witness Refinement for LLM Serving Traces

author.name: Liming Liu, Chao Hu, Mingfei Lu, Cong Tan, Yiwei Ge, Chijin Zhou, Yongjun Xie, Runzhe Wang, Xiaohai Shi, Heyuan Shi

entry.summary: Proposes bottleneck-preserving witnessing for compressing production LLM serving traces, arguing that rare non-representative requests are precisely the ones that reveal component bottlenecks. It avoids circular evaluation that arises when predicted bottlenecks are used as ground truth.

entry.title: DASH: Decoupled Adaptive Surrogate - Acquisition Harness for Automated Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Changquan Zhao, Yuxiang Sun, Ruihao Zhu, Cheng Hua, Yulian He

entry.summary: DASH decouples surrogate model selection from acquisition function adaptation in automated Bayesian optimization, arguing surrogates should be chosen on predictive reliability while acquisitions respond to campaign context. It uses an LLM to help drive the adaptive selection.

entry.title: HetGPS: Scalable Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Physics-Anchored Adaptive Safety for EV Charging

author.name: Xiangwei Wang, Nanduni Nimalsiri, Yu Xia, Peng Wang, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: HetGPS combines a learned graph risk model that sets intervention strength with a physics model that sets the correction direction, applied to safe multi-agent electric vehicle charging coordination. Parameter sharing keeps model size independent of fleet size across five nested distribution networks.

entry.title: PosterMELD: Multi-Agent Paper-to-Poster Generation for Controllable Design Diversity with Editable Print-Ready Outputs

author.name: Haojie Hu, Chenhao Dang, Yaojia Liu, Hengrui Kang, Conghui He, Weijia Li

entry.summary: PosterMELD generates scientific posters with a template-conditioned multi-agent pipeline that plans capacity-aware slots before rendering, uses deterministic gates plus VLM review, and exports editable PowerPoint and image artifacts. Reports a print-ready rate metric over 621 papers instead of only scoring completed outputs.

entry.title: Not All EEG Moments Are Equal: Position-Adaptive Time Scheduling for EEG Generation

author.name: Boheng Liu, Ziyu Li, Chenghua Duan, Qing Li, Xia Wu

entry.summary: Argues that flow-matching EEG generators wrongly assume a single global time progression for all channels and segments, and introduces position-adaptive time scheduling driven by per-position reconstruction error plus factorized spatio-temporal attention. Targets data scarcity in brain-computer interface modeling.

entry.title: Automated ECG Interval Measurement and Wave Delineation Using Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet

author.name: Farhan Adam Mukadam, Harshit Mishra, Nachiket Makwana, Pradyot Tiwari, Subramani Kandasamy, KVS Hari

entry.summary: Evaluates an end-to-end ECG delineation pipeline based on a Fast Fourier Convolution ResNet on 10,646 clinical 12-lead recordings, reporting clinical interval accuracy with bias, Bland-Altman limits of agreement, bootstrap intervals and rhythm-stratified errors. Shifts evaluation from fiducial-point timing on small curated sets to clinically meaningful interval measurement at scale.

entry.title: Evidence-Unit Fairness and the Limits of Query-Adaptive Sparse-Dense Fusion in Financial Document Retrieval

author.name: Chenyu Wu, You Lin

entry.summary: TrustAgentNet proposes a dual-tier blockchain design for agent networks: a global chain tracking skillset metadata lifecycles with off-chain auditing, plus transient task-specific chains for trustless multi-agent collaboration. It targets the mismatch between what third-party agent skills claim and what they actually do under trust-by-declaration assumptions.

entry.title: Hybrid Attention Estimation Pipeline for Adaptive HRI Using an Expressive Robotic Head

author.name: Pablo Moraes, Monica Rodriguez, Christopher Peters, Hiago Sodre, Tobias Doernbach, Bruna Guterres, Ricardo Grando

entry.summary: An applied HRI case study builds an attention-estimation pipeline for an expressive robotic head that fuses a fast geometric face and head-pose layer with a slower vision-language model producing contextual labels (attending to robot, using phone, attending elsewhere), integrated by a finite state machine. It demonstrates practical multi-rate fusion of classical perception with semantic VLM judgments.

entry.title: When Extreme Darkness Meets Motion Blur: MeanFlow for Unified RAW Restoration

author.name: Zepu Wang, Jingze Liang, Weijie Xiao, Kexin Chen

entry.summary: This work tackles extremely low-light RAW image restoration when motion blur is also present, releasing the SIDED dataset with controlled motion degradation on real low-light RAW pairs and proposing a unified RAW tokenizer plus a MeanFlow-based restoration model. It targets a realistic degradation combination that prior low-light methods ignore.

entry.title: PICopilot: An LLM-based Agentic Framework for Assisting Photonic Integrated Circuit Design via Script Generation

author.name: Xiaohan Jiang, Zeyu Li, Wei Zhang, Jiang Xu

entry.summary: PICopilot is an LLM-based agentic assistant that generates design scripts for photonic integrated circuits, addressing the productivity gap created by the shift from GUI design tools to script-based flows requiring API expertise. It claims to be the first such framework for PIC design automation.

entry.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs

author.name: Shuaijun Liu, Qifu Wen, Shuyang Hao, Qi Luo, Chenglong Zhang, Feiyang You, Chengyu Wu, Ningxin Su

entry.summary: CoWAM adds a selective intervention layer over world-action-model-based bimanual robot policies, encoding synchronization, role compatibility, and collision constraints as typed coordination contracts with calibrated gates. The nominal action is only overridden when an alternative provably satisfies all obligations, with abstention as a fallback.

entry.title: Progressive$^2$: A Teacher-Student Progressive Co-Evolving Knowledge Distillation Method for Substantial Model Compression

author.name: Tiancong Cheng, Ying Zhang, Zhiwen Yu, Yifang Yin, Bin Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a distillation scheme where a progressively strengthened teacher and a progressively shrunken student co-evolve, aimed at cases where the server model and client capacity gap is very large. Targets substantial compression without the usual collapse in transfer quality.

entry.title: A Physics-Chemistry-Informed Neural Network (PCINN) for Real-Time Spatial-ALD Coverage Prediction and Reliable Kinetics Inversion

author.name: Ning Hu, Chang Liu, Yunlei Jiang, Yuan Dong

entry.summary: Builds a hybrid physics-and-chemistry-informed surrogate for spatial atomic layer deposition coverage prediction that reaches CFD-level accuracy from only 30 training simulations while answering queries in milliseconds. The network learns a constrained correction rather than acting as a full black box, and also supports kinetics inversion.

entry.title: Modeling Unknown Nonlocal PDE Systems via Flow Map Learning

author.name: Zhongshu Xu, Ying Li, Yanzhi Zhang, Dongbin Xiu

entry.summary: Learns the finite-time evolution operator (flow map) of unknown nonlocal PDEs directly from solution data instead of approximating the nonlocal operators themselves, with modal and nodal formulations. Demonstrates stable long-horizon prediction of fractional diffusion and wave equations from short observation windows.

entry.title: From field-scale to large-scale spectral libraries: Tabular foundation models in soil spectroscopy

author.name: Viacheslav Barkov, Jonas Schmidinger, Robin Gebbers, Martin Atzmueller

entry.summary: Benchmarks a tabular in-context foundation model against CNNs, rule-based regression, random forests, and PLS across 85 soil spectroscopy regression tasks spanning field scale to a global spectral library. Provides guidance on regression and dimensionality-reduction choices for high-dimensional collinear spectra.

entry.title: AdvPlan-Bench: Adversarial Evaluation of Structured Plan-Generation Agents

author.name: Alina Kapanova, Arun Kanhai, Natan Vidra, Spurthi Setty

entry.summary: AdvPlan-Bench evaluates structured plan-generation agents adversarially, representing plans as typed action chains and scoring them against an opposing agent's best responses using game-theoretic diagnostics such as advantage and Nash gap. Offline and synthetic-score based, it targets the gap between judging plans in isolation and under opposition.

entry.title: SparseKAN: Compressing Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks Across Basis Functions, Neurons, and Bits

author.name: Kazi Ahmed Asif Fuad, Lizhong Chen

entry.summary: SparseKAN compresses Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks along three axes at once - basis functions, neurons, and numerical precision - using hierarchical learnable gates trained with a differentiable cost objective. Learned structure is then hardened to explicit budgets and physically compacted for real savings.

entry.title: Breaking Diversity Collapse in Spiking Pseudo-Ensembles for Efficient OOD Detection in Remote Sensing

author.name: Srinivas Anumasa, Rushi Shah, Qiran Zou, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Attaches multiple lightweight classification heads to a frozen spiking network backbone to approximate a deep ensemble for out-of-distribution detection at low compute cost. An agree-disagree training objective prevents the heads from collapsing into correlated predictions while preserving in-distribution accuracy.

entry.title: BiKAN: Restoring Collapsed Basis of Binary Kolmogorov--Arnold Networks

author.name: Kazi Ahmed Asif Fuad, Lizhong Chen

entry.summary: Identifies that binarizing polynomial Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks collapses the elementwise basis because all even powers become one and odd powers become the input, destroying expressivity. BiKAN restores pairwise structure by adding selected degree-two Walsh characters generated via circular channel rolls and learned binary projections using the same XNOR and popcount primitives.

entry.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality

author.name: Shengzhi Deng, Chenqi Ye, Yanze Guo

entry.summary: Argues that the pseudorandom number streams consumed by diffusion training and sampling are deterministic orbits whose structure can be partially predicted and even exploited, affecting loss, gradients and generation quality. Uses a small MLP orbit predictor plus a diffusion probe trained on random tensors to test exploitability.

entry.title: Enriched text-guided variational multimodal knowledge distillation network (VMD) for automated diagnosis of plaque vulnerability in 3D carotid artery MRI

author.name: Bo Cao, Fan Yu, Mengmeng Feng, SenHao Zhang, Xin Meng, Yue Zhang, Zhen Qian, Jie Lu

entry.summary: Builds a variational multimodal knowledge distillation network that injects radiologist domain knowledge as enriched text supervision to diagnose carotid plaque vulnerability from 3D MRI. The approach distills multimodal clinical reasoning into a model that operates on imaging at inference.

entry.title: Domain-Generalized Adaptive Semantic Communication for Collaborative Perception

author.name: Fan Gao, Youzheng Wang, Ning Ge

entry.summary: RSTA is a semantic communication framework for vehicle-to-everything collaborative perception that handles simultaneous observation-domain shift and unseen wireless channel corruption. It combines cross-domain prototype alignment and cross-channel gradient consistency during pretraining with a reliability-gated entropy-minimization adapter at deployment.

entry.title: Rethinking Total Absorption Gamma Spectroscopy Deconvolution: Supervised Machine Learning vs Response-Matrix Methods

author.name: J. Balibrea-Correa, E. N{\'a}cher, C. Fonseca-Vargas, J. L. Tain

entry.summary: Systematically compares supervised machine learning estimators against classical response-matrix deconvolution for extracting beta-feeding distributions in total absorption gamma spectroscopy, using realistic Monte Carlo simulations of a real spectrometer. The comparison clarifies when non-parametric learned estimators help on this ill-posed inverse problem.

entry.title: Generative Models for Modeling and Synthesizing MIMO Channels in Adverse Weather Conditions

author.name: Vignesh Nandakumar, Faraz Barati, Brian L. Evans

entry.summary: Synthesizes MIMO channel state information for adverse weather conditions by training a weather-conditioned diffusion model on channels measured or simulated in mild conditions, covering three weather types at three intensities. This provides data for evaluating 5G and 6G coverage where real measurements are scarce.

entry.title: CARNet: Channel-Adaptive Receiver Network for Robust NextG Communications

author.name: Chao Jiang, Zhuo Xu, Yongli Yan

entry.summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts neural receiver where routing selects ResNet-based experts specialized for different wireless channel conditions, aiming to fix the poor generalization of static neural receivers. Targets next-generation communication physical-layer detection.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Representations for Binary Program Clustering: From Empirical Study to Retrieval-Augmented Learning

author.name: Martin Mocko, Daniela Chud\'a

entry.summary: First systematic study of self-supervised and tabular representation learning methods for clustering binary programs and malware families, adapting vision SSL objectives to tabular malware features and then adding retrieval-augmented learning. Establishes performance ceilings on public malware datasets.

entry.title: DE-NER : Zero-shot Named Entity Recognition via Dialogue Elicitation of Large Language Models

author.name: Xuankang Zhang, Jiangming Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a dialogue-elicitation framework for zero-shot named entity recognition that uses conversational turns to draw out entity knowledge from LLMs instead of relying on hand-tuned prompts and demonstrations. Reports roughly four F1 points average gain over competitive zero-shot baselines.

entry.title: Observatorio Lazaro: A self-populating database of anglicism usage in the Spanish press

author.name: Elena Alvarez-Mellado

entry.summary: Documents a continuously running system that has monitored English lexical borrowings in the Spanish digital press since 2020 using a neural sequence labeller, now covering over two million borrowings across nearly two million articles. Provides a public interface and API for diachronic lexical research.

entry.title: RH-RAG: Trustworthy Long-Form Generation for Privacy-Constrained Settings

author.name: Raj Shekhar Singh

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-agent retrieval-augmented pipeline with planner, drafting, and verification stages for generating long-form documents from internal reports using only locally deployed open-weight models. Targets organizations that cannot send proprietary data to cloud APIs.

entry.title: Analyzing Speech Condition Effects in Dysarthric ASR: A Layer-wise Probing Study

author.name: Darwin Jelestin Muthu, Navya Gupta, Wei Lin Tay, Zhengchen Zhang, Daniel Wang Zhengkui, Rong Tong

entry.summary: Probes a transformer ASR encoder layer by layer on Mandarin dysarthric speech versus transcript-matched TTS resynthesis, showing phoneme boundary information stays weak throughout while difficulty is encoded in the deepest layers. Lexical tone emerges as a persistent error source for disordered speech.

entry.title: Device-First Feedback: Toward Mobile-Native LLM-Driven Neural Architecture Search

author.name: Saif U Din, Muhammad Ahsan Hussain, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: Builds a fully automated loop in which an LLM fine-tuned to generate convolutional architectures is evaluated not only on GPU accuracy but on integer-quantized mobile export and measured on-device latency, feeding results back into the training corpus. Demonstrated on two image benchmarks with a physical tablet in the loop.

entry.title: Real-Time Visual Obstruction Detection in Surgical Augmented Reality

author.name: Shih-Chin Yang, Yanming Xiu, Hanting Ye, Qi Chen, Elias Rotondo, Maria Gorlatova

entry.summary: Presents a latency-aware pipeline that detects when virtual surgical AR overlays obstruct task-relevant real-world objects, combining vision-language object recognition with segmentation-based obstruction reasoning. A cascaded small-to-large model architecture with early exit and token pruning keeps inference within interactive budgets.

entry.title: Test-time Adaptation of Pelvic Bone Segmentation Models via Dynamic Reliability-Guided

author.name: Ling Ren, Chao Deng, Ziming Wang, Yuecong Xu, Kai Zheng

entry.summary: ReGA is a closed-loop test-time adaptation framework for pelvic bone CT segmentation that scores pseudo-label reliability via a segmentation inference consistency criterion, targeting cross-hospital domain shift in robot-assisted trauma surgery. It addresses boundary degradation, anatomical inconsistency, and severe voxel class imbalance.

entry.title: DiffuseAgent-MI: Distributionally-Grounded,Tool-Integrated Self-Evolving Agents for Faithful Visual Reasoning

author.name: An Lanji, Dawei Liu, Jin Li, Haoran Xu, Mei Chen, Yu Tian

entry.summary: DiffuseAgent-MI constrains a tool-using visual reasoning agent with an energy model over interpretable feature units so that generated evidence stays near the native data distribution, aiming to close the gap between stated reasoning and the computation that produced the answer. It frames visual mechanistic interpretability distributionally.

entry.title: PixelSR: Efficient Screen Content Super-Resolution via Pixel Classification

author.name: Zhiheng Li, Lei Chen, Jie Zhou, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: PixelSR exploits the repetitive sharp structure of screen content (text and graphics) by binning pixels into content-dependent groups and computing attention within groups during training, aiming for both better super-resolution quality and faster inference. It targets a domain where natural-image priors are a poor fit.

entry.title: Parameter-Dynamic Adaptive Fusion and Calibration Network for RGBT Tracking

author.name: Zhaoding Ding, Chenglong Li, Jiandong Jin, Kewei Ying, Wentao Wu

entry.summary: PAFCNet uses a hypernetwork to generate target-conditioned fusion and temporal calibration parameters for RGB-thermal tracking, so fusion adapts to changing target appearance and modality quality. Contrasts with fixed-parameter or discrete operation-selection fusion.

entry.title: Measuring Product Quality Using Images: The CLIP Q-Score and an Application to Real Estate

author.name: Fabian Slonimczyk, Danila Karapsin

entry.summary: The CLIP Q-score extracts an objective product quality signal from photographs using contrastive language-image pretraining, and is applied to roughly half a million real estate listing images. Higher scores align with language model quality assessments and predict both prices and time on market for sales and rentals.

entry.title: Adaptive Human-Robot Collaborative Painting Combining Preference-Based Optimization and Dynamic Motion Primitives

author.name: C. Cella, M. Ristic, M. Faroni, A. M. Zanchettin, P. Rocco

entry.summary: A human-robot collaborative painting framework combines preference-based optimization of control parameters via human feedback with modified dynamic movement primitives for reactive adaptation. The robot reorients the workpiece in real time to match the operator hand.

entry.title: Energy Efficiency of Locally Deployed LLMs: A Preliminary Quantitative GPU Power Benchmark on Consumer Hardware

author.name: Philipp M. Z\"ahl, Anika Hennig

entry.summary: A hardware-level benchmark of nine small open-weight models running locally on a single consumer GPU, measuring power draw, joules per prompt and per token, and throughput. It finds that parameter count alone poorly predicts energy cost, with architecture and quantization mattering substantially.

entry.title: Similarity Weighted Aggregation with Global Differential Privacy for Federated Brain Lesion Segmentation

author.name: Muhammad Irfan Khan, Eero Lehtonen, Joni Obradovic, Elina Kontio, Esa Alhoniemi, Suleiman A. Khan, Mojtaba Jafaritadi

entry.summary: DP-SimAgg combines similarity-weighted aggregation with server-side differential privacy for federated brain lesion segmentation, clipping client updates and injecting calibrated noise while weighting contributions to handle non-IID data across institutions. It targets the privacy-utility tradeoff in medical imaging collaborations.

entry.title: Chess on Ice: Curling Tactical Decision-Making via Backward Induction and Deep Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Patrick Oberlin, Matteo Cederle, Aren Karapetyan, Saverio Bolognani, Gian Antonio Susto, Florian D\"orfler

entry.summary: Applies deep deterministic policy gradient RL, adapted to exploit the finite-horizon structure and backward induction, to evaluate tactical options in curling under continuous stochastic action outcomes. Provides a quantitative alternative to prior statistical analyses of the sport.

entry.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI

author.name: Taye Akinrele, Sindhuja Penchala, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi

entry.summary: A taxonomy-driven survey of cognitive capability gaps limiting generative and agentic AI, organized around persistent state modeling, goal-directed autonomy, self-monitoring and control, environment interaction, and learning and adaptation. Intended to structure research toward more reliable long-horizon systems.

entry.title: Logographic Character Visual Pretraining via Semantic-based Contrastive Learning

author.name: Daqian Shi, Wei Cao, Xiaoyu Zheng, Lida Shi, Xiaolei Diao, Cedric M John

entry.summary: The paper proposes contrastive visual pretraining for logographic characters (e.g., Chinese) that injects visual-semantic knowledge about character components to cope with severely imbalanced and long-tailed character distributions. It targets recognition, denoising and historical text completion where standard supervised training needs large balanced datasets.

entry.title: Rethinking and formalising the state across languages: a unified computational learning theory account

author.name: Mohamed El Idrissi

entry.summary: This linguistics-oriented paper reformulates the notion of grammatical state, traditionally tied to Afroasiatic construct annexation, as a general context-dependent mechanism that selects grammatical templates across synthetic languages, formalized as a set-valued function with an accompanying learning algorithm and Riffian as the empirical base. It connects theoretical morphosyntax to computational learning theory.

entry.title: Multi-tenant Kubernetes Use Cases for AI, Secure Computing and Data Services, and More

author.name: Jake Watson, Sadaf R Alam, Christopher Woods, Abdelwahab Kawafi, Thomas Green, Ian Johnson, Ellis Pires, Jessica R. Jones, Utz-Uwe Haus

entry.summary: This infrastructure paper surveys multi-tenant Kubernetes use cases in supercomputing settings for AI workloads, confidential computing on sensitive data, and data services, arguing that single-tenant batch systems lack the flexibility and reproducibility cloud users expect while not replacing batch schedulers for large MPI jobs. It is an operational experience and requirements report.

entry.title: ARM: Detector-Agnostic Changepoint Attribution with Finite-Sample Error Control

author.name: Chenchen Peng, Mixia Wu, Qijing Yan, Da Chen, Zhiqi Shen

entry.summary: ARM is a detector-agnostic wrapper that, after a changepoint is found in a multivariate series, certifies which individual coordinates actually changed with finite-sample error control and labels each as a location or scale shift. It fills a gap between block-level certification and unguaranteed variable-selection rankings.

entry.title: LAB-Tab: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Network Adaptation for Few-Shot Tabular Generation

author.name: Zijian Shen, Taijie Chen, Bin Zhou, Ziyang Jiang, Jintao Ke

entry.summary: LAB-Tab generates synthetic tabular data for a target domain from only a few target records plus richer related source data, by fitting a Bayesian network on the source and using an LLM to propose plausible structural edits for the target. This avoids both overfitting sparse target statistics and blindly reusing stale source dependencies.

entry.title: FAST-GS: Frequency Aware Space-time Gaussian Splatting for Photorealistic Dynamic Novel View Synthesis

author.name: Zhengyang Zhang, Ziyu Lu, PengCheng Li, Hongbo Duan, Yi Liu, Pengting Luo, Peiyu Zhuang, Xinghui Li, Shaohua Ma

entry.summary: FAST-GS replaces single-polynomial motion models in 4D Gaussian splatting with a Fourier decomposition that captures both low-frequency global trajectories and high-frequency local detail, aiming to reduce cumulative trajectory drift in long dynamic sequences. Real-time rendering is retained.

entry.title: TALSC: Timeliness-Aware Large-Small VLM Collaboration for Infrastructure-Assisted Autonomous Driving

author.name: Mengmeng Zhu, Yuxuan Sun, Wei Chen, Bo Ai

entry.summary: TALSC schedules when an autonomous vehicle should rely on its small onboard vision-language model versus offloading to a large model at an edge server, modeling Age of Information so that accuracy gains are weighed against latency-induced staleness. It formalizes the timeliness-accuracy tradeoff in infrastructure-assisted driving.

entry.title: RamanPFN: learning from Raman spectral structure with a tabular foundation model

author.name: Xingyu Pan, Huan Wang, Jinjia Guo, Zhenlin Zhao, Siming Dong, Jixi Lu

entry.summary: RamanPFN adapts tabular in-context foundation model inference to Raman spectroscopy by preserving the joint visibility of related spectral bands that naive wide-input feature subsampling destroys. It targets small-label, high-dimensional spectral prediction without task-specific training.

entry.title: Syntax Meets Semantics: Understanding Scientific Formulae

author.name: Yuni Susanti, Moritz Schubotz

entry.summary: Empirically studies whether the syntactic form of scientific formulae and their semantic descriptions live in comparable representation spaces, finding very weak observable correspondence despite latent correlation. Relevant to mathematical information retrieval and formula-aware search.

entry.title: Towards Effective Federated Multimodal Graph Learning via Navigating Multifaceted Heterogeneity

author.name: Yinlin Zhu, Di Wu, Yi Zhang, Xunkai Li, Wang Luo, Wei-Jin Huang, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan

entry.summary: Extends federated graph learning to multimodal-attributed graphs, addressing simultaneous heterogeneity in client tasks, modality quality, and topology. Proposes mechanisms so clients with divergent objectives and modality domains can still collaborate without sharing raw data.

entry.title: When Do Surrogate Updates Improve Decisions? A Local Theory of Trajectory-Wise Transfer

author.name: Yuyang Shen

entry.summary: Develops a local theory of when reducing a surrogate trajectory loss also reduces downstream decision risk, defining per-trajectory learnability and decision utility within a restricted update space. Provides one-step transfer conditions and analysis of how transfer accumulates over repeated updates.

entry.title: Latent-Regime Bias Auditing for Volatility Forecasting

author.name: Arthur Chagas, Pedro Bento, Yan Aquino, Arthur Buzelin, Wagner Meira Jr., Cristiano Arbex Valle

entry.summary: Introduces a model-agnostic audit that clusters market-state windows into latent regimes and then evaluates volatility forecasts per regime, exposing conditional bias and tail underprediction hidden by aggregate RMSE or MAE. Applied to crypto and ETF data, models with similar overall accuracy show very different regime-specific risk failures.

entry.title: LOCUS-DT: Localization via Observation-Conditioned Uncertainty Scoring with Digital Twins

author.name: Haozhe Lei, Roberto Bomfin, Marwa Chafii, Sundeep Rangan

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that treats indoor radio localization as posterior inference, using a ray-tracing digital twin of a known building to generate synthetic multipath signatures for candidate transmitter positions and score them against measurements. The goal is to represent multimodal uncertainty rather than emitting a single point estimate in cluttered indoor environments.

entry.title: Comparing and Modeling Argumentation in German Political Communication across Arenas

author.name: Nina Vikhrova, Johannes K\"uhling, Sebastian Haunss, Sebastian Pad\'o

entry.summary: Releases a 17,000-sentence annotated corpus of argumentative passages across German plenary speeches, committee meetings, and press conferences, then models how argumentation patterns differ by arena. Supports computational study of political deliberation.

entry.title: OSSDD - a New Open Dataset for Sentinel-1 Ship Detection

author.name: Horst Hammer, Sylvia Hochstuhl, Antje Thiele, Tobias Brosch, Padraig Davidson, Tim Remiger, Michael Teutsch

entry.summary: Presents a freely available Sentinel-1 SAR ship detection dataset with about 15,000 amplitude image tiles, built from an existing classification dataset to address the scarcity of SAR detection training data. Motivated by maritime awareness applications such as illegal fishing monitoring.

entry.title: Fermat Active Laplace Learning for Semi-Supervised Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Vutichart Buranasiri, James M. Murphy

entry.summary: Two active learning algorithms for hyperspectral image classification combine density-aware Fermat distances with Poisson-reweighted Laplace label propagation, plus a landmark-based approximation for scalability. They query informative pixels using an uncertainty acquisition function in a semi-supervised graph learning setting.

entry.title: Automatic LV Localization and Short-Axis Plane Estimation from Arbitrary CMR Slice

author.name: Yi Yu, Yixuan Liu, Ziyu Zhang, Parker Martin, Zhenyu Bu, Yuchi Han, Yuan Xue

entry.summary: This paper formulates joint left ventricle localization and continuous 3D orientation estimation from a single arbitrary cardiac MRI slice, replacing discrete view classification or multi-slice geometric intersection. It introduces a polar-coupled circular embedding to represent orientation continuously and unambiguously.

entry.title: Situation Aware Frontier Prioritization for Quadruped Search and Rescue

author.name: Kevin Farias, Santiago Martin, Barbara Flores, Vinicio Melgar, Igor Nunes, Hiago Sodre, Pablo Moraes, Ricardo B. Grando

entry.summary: A frontier-selection method for quadruped search and rescue that ranks frontiers by information gain, observation deficit, rescue relevance, terrain penalty, and travel cost rather than pure map expansion. It is evaluated in Gazebo simulation with a quadruped platform.

entry.title: Physics-informed neural networks for two-dimensional wall-reactive solute dispersion in canonical shear flows

author.name: Nanda Poddar, Subham Dhar

entry.summary: A physics-informed neural network framework solves two-dimensional wall-reactive solute dispersion in canonical shear flows with absorbing-wall Robin boundary conditions. It embeds the convection-diffusion equation into the loss to resolve plume evolution without grid-based solvers.

entry.title: Evaluating Forecasting Techniques for Hardware Errors on a Large-scale HPC System

author.name: Kaiyuan Liao, Xiwei Xuan, Tanwi Mallick, Kevin Brown, Christopher D. Carothers, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: Uses seven years of production logs from the Theta supercomputer to compare classical statistical and deep time-series models for forecasting hardware error events. Accuracy depends heavily on the temporal structure of the error series, with LSTM and Transformer models doing well on regular errors and all methods struggling on sparse bursty ones.

entry.title: Beyond Illumination: A Conditional Mutual Information-Guided Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Ya-nan Guan, Shaonan Zhang, Tao Dai, Tianqu Zhuang, Yongchao Qiao, Zhensen Chen, Shu-Tao Xia, Hang Guo

entry.summary: CMIG-Net improves low-light image enhancement by modeling conditional mutual information between intensity and chrominance branches, which prior dual-branch color-space methods treat independently. Reports gains from letting the two components interact.

entry.title: USP-Mamba: Unmixing-Derived Spectral and Structural Prompting for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Shi Chen, Jie Zhang, Yicong Zhou

entry.summary: USP-Mamba super-resolves hyperspectral images by deriving spectral and structural prompts from spectral unmixing, so state-space parameters are aligned with intrinsic image characteristics rather than generic learned features. Also addresses the loss of spatial adjacency caused by fixed scanning orders.

entry.title: Slides2MindMap: Reconstructing Cognitively Efficient Knowledge Hierarchies from Lecture Slides

author.name: Yuzhi Wang, Rongjun Ye, Shengyuan Chen, Huachi Zhou, Jiaqi Bai, Chuang Zhou, Zhicong Hong, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: Defines the task of reconstructing cognitively efficient knowledge hierarchies from full course slide decks and releases a benchmark of 12,774 expert-annotated slide pages across 24 university courses. Includes a cognitive-science-grounded evaluation framework balancing global and local knowledge focus.

entry.title: From AI Technical Debt to Agentic Technical Debt: A Systematic Mapping of Root Causes and Manifestations in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Muhammad Tukur, Hayatullahi B. Adeyemo, Tao Chen, Nour Ali, Anis Zarrad, Marco Agus, Rick Kazman, Rami Bahsoon

entry.summary: Introduces agentic technical debt as a distinct category arising from autonomous reasoning, multi-agent collaboration, tool orchestration, and persistent memory, and systematically maps its root causes and manifestations. Argues existing AI technical debt models assume static component pipelines and miss emergent behaviors.

entry.title: PATH-Bench: Path-Dependent Evaluation of Lifelong Agents

author.name: Xidong Yang, Xingyi Zhang, Wenhao Li, Wenyan Liu, Junjie Sheng, Yun Hua, Wei Yin, Tao Fang, Chuyun Shen, Xiangfeng Wang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.01149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lifelong LLM agents increasingly adapt through external learning states that store past interactions as retrievable memories or reusable skills, yet ex...

entry.title: Homebot: A Personal AI Agent for Conversational Home Assistance and Automation

author.name: Shengyuan Ye, Yixin Zhang, Han Liang, Liekang Zeng, Jiangsu Du, Mu Yuan

entry.summary: Homebot is a locally deployable household assistant agent that unifies voice and messaging channels over a shared runtime with tools and skills, wake-word activation, streaming speech recognition and synthesis, and an explicit dialogue-state protocol. Emphasizes on-device deployment and customizable channel and tool contracts.

entry.title: Abduction Without a Body? Representational Grounding and the Abduction Loop for Scientific Hypothesis Generation

author.name: Michael Farmer

entry.summary: Philosophical argument that scientific abductive inference does not always require continuous sensorimotor embodiment, focusing on identity abduction reached through representational transformations that expose latent invariants. Uses scientific diagrams as the practical substrate for such non-embodied inference.

entry.title: Skillsets on the Chain: A Blockchain-based Zero-Trust Framework for Agentic AI Networking

author.name: Yayu Gao, Yong Xiao, Hao Hu, Xubo Li, Zhiwei Liu, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic AI networking (AgentNet) systems rely heavily on third-party skillset implementations and distributed multi-agent collaboration, yet they fac...

entry.title: Can Urban Blight Be Accessed with Vision-language Models: A Case Study in Detroit

author.name: Xiaohao Yang, Aohua Tian, Derek Van Berkel, Xu Qiang, Mark Lindquist

entry.summary: The study tests whether open vision-language models can estimate residential blight from multiple street-level views in Detroit, using structured prompts about roof integrity, wall damage, and boarded openings to produce binary and probabilistic disrepair judgments. Results are compared against survey-based ground truth.

entry.title: Multi-Source Dynamic Graph Learning for Compound-Flood Forecasting in Managed Coastal Systems

author.name: Liangjun You, Min Wu, Orlando Woods, Dongsheng Luo

entry.summary: This work forecasts compound coastal flooding by fusing signals from many heterogeneous monitoring stations through an anchored dynamic graph framework, explicitly targeting prolonged high-water plateaus that average error metrics hide. The anchoring is designed to prevent cross-site fusion from destabilizing local temporal forecasts.

entry.title: TransNRank: Towards Accurate Neoantigen Ranking with Transformer

author.name: Zhiyin An, Yuenan Hou, Shumeng Duan, Yiming Zhou, Yuanting Zheng, Leming Shi

entry.summary: TransNRank applies a transformer with self-attention and a positive-aware training objective to rank candidate neoantigens for personalized cancer immunotherapy, addressing extreme class imbalance and noisy labels. It aims to improve positive recall over linear and gradient-boosted baselines.

entry.title: TS-MAMP: A Remanufactured Agricultural Robot Powered by Second-Life EV Components and NMS-Free On-Device Weed Detection

author.name: Weijie Shi, Zicheng Xu, Zhenbang Cheng, Haoran Xuan, Mingbo Duan, Gan Ge

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agriculture 4.0 robotic systems improve field efficiency yet remain too capital-intensive for the fragmented smallholdings that dominate global agric...

entry.title: GLAIM: Learning Global and Local Adaptive Inter-Variable Dependency for Multivariate Time Series Imputation

author.name: Mingyang Wang, Rongwen Li, Xiao Wang, Changjian Chen

entry.summary: GLAIM imputes missing values in multivariate time series by combining a stable global inter-variable dependency structure with adaptive local dependencies, so that local adaptation does not propagate errors when observations are sparse. It targets the tradeoff between stability and adaptivity in dependency modeling.

entry.title: From fragmented data to actionable design: Physics-calibrated learning for plastic upcycling

author.name: Jingyang Bai, Zijia Wang, Xiangyi Long, Marcos Millan, Binjian Nie, Mingyue Ding

entry.summary: This work learns structure-property relationships for thermochemical plastic upcycling from fragmented literature data where complete-case filtering would discard about 89 percent of experiments, using a physics-calibrated, missingness-gated mixture-of-experts that treats structured missingness as an informative signal instead of imputing targets. It reconstructs physically consistent product distributions across heterogeneous laboratories.

entry.title: Grounding Agentic VLMs with Dedicated Segmentation for Fine-Grained Vehicle Damage Assessment

author.name: Vishwajeet Shivaji Hogale, Anjali Pai, Nitya Ravi

entry.summary: Shows that a strong vision-language model classifies vehicle damage accurately but grounds it poorly in space, hallucinating damage in reflections and missing thin scratches. The authors pair the VLM with a dedicated segmentation module to restore reliable pixel-level localization in an insurance-style assessment pipeline.

entry.title: Action-grounded tissue affordance enables anticipatory auto-framing that lowers surgeon cognitive workload during laparoscopic surgery

author.name: Jiayu Gu, Yiwei Wang, Jie Zhang, Guojun Cao, Keshen Lyu, Song Zhou, Yimeng Chen, Haorui Wang, Qingmin Feng, Shenchao Shi, Huan Zhao, Wenbin Chen, Caihua Xiong, Chidan Wan, Jing Samantha Pan, Xiong Cai, Han Ding

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational attention models could help surgeons manage the visual demands of laparoscopy, but they require dense spatial labels that are difficult...

entry.title: DyFrDet: Towards Accurate Small Object Detection via Dynamic Frequency Suppression with Label Disambiguation

author.name: Zihan Yang, Yang Guo, Hongxing Zhang, Dan Lu, Siyuan Yao

entry.summary: DyFrDet targets small-object detection by dynamically suppressing frequency-domain background noise and disambiguating noisy assignment labels. It adds a frequency-aware feature pyramid to improve localization of objects with few pixels.

entry.title: RHEA: Reliability-Harmonized Reconstruction and Assignment for Robust Multimodal-Attributed Graph Clustering

author.name: Yinlin Zhu, Di Wu, Ziyu Han, Zekai Chenm, Wang Luo, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan

entry.summary: RHEA clusters multimodal-attributed graphs while accounting for node-specific modality reliability, using graph neighborhoods under attribute homophily to supply evidence for corrupted or missing modalities. Targets robustness failures of methods that assume uniformly clean attributes.

entry.title: xMICD: Explainable Representation of Multiple ICD Codes

author.name: Pat Vatiwutipong, Kumkup Keeratisiwakul, Albert Phuoc Kien Van Truong, Nutcha Yodrabum, Wasin Pansiritanachot, Marvin N. Wright, Thanapon Noraset

entry.summary: xMICD builds low-dimensional patient representations from sets of diagnosis codes that keep clinically meaningful groupings while retaining predictive power. Aims to break the usual trade-off between interpretable code grouping and opaque high-performing embeddings.

entry.title: Factorized AdaBoost.MH Achieves the Same Convergence Rate as AdaBoost.MH

author.name: Xin Zou, Jingyuan Xu

entry.summary: Proves that a factorized variant of multi-class AdaBoost, which shares one binary base classifier across classes with a per-class vote vector, attains the same convergence rate as the standard algorithm. Resolves an open question about whether a sufficiently heavy vote vector can always be chosen.

entry.title: AlphaG-OPD: Reliability-Gated Sibling Counterfactuals for On-Policy Distillation in Symbolic Alpha Factor Discovery

author.name: Yaoyu Su

entry.summary: Turns terminal evaluations of symbolic financial factors into local action-level supervision by exposing grammar-valid sibling actions at partial syntax-tree states of a generative flow network policy, gated by reliability checks. Addresses the lack of credit assignment for intermediate structural decisions in symbolic discovery.

entry.title: Start Classifying: Categorical Critics for LLM Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhijian Zhou, Long Li, Xuan Zhang, Zongkai Liu, Yulei Qin, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Xiaoyu Tan, Chao Qu, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for large language models typically trains its critic by mean-squared-error (MSE) regression on scalar value targets...

entry.title: Hybrid-Field Sparse Channel Representation and Recovery for XL-RIS-Assisted mmWave MIMO Systems

author.name: Wenkai Liu, Nan Ma, Jianqiao Chen, Hongtao Zhang, Ping Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a double-timescale channel estimation framework for extremely large reconfigurable intelligent surfaces at mmWave that decouples sparse dictionary representation from recovery, exploiting quasi-static geometry to avoid a huge cascaded dictionary. This reduces computation and storage for hybrid near-field and far-field channels.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum CNN for Cross-Sensor Spaceborne Volcanic Thermal Activity Recognition Worldwide

author.name: Claudia Corradino, Federica Torrisi, Alessandro Grilli, Tommaso Catuogno, Mattia Verducci, Elisabetta Paladino, Luigi Giannelli, Alessandro Sebastianelli

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid quantum-classical AlexNet for recognizing volcanic thermal activity across heterogeneous satellite sensors, motivated by on-board processing constraints on memory, compute and labeled data. The classical convolutional feature extractor is coupled to a quantum layer for global cross-sensor generalization.

entry.title: Partially-Observable Transmission Control for UAV-Enabled Federated Learning in IoT Networks

author.name: Masoud Ghazikor, Zhou Ni, Morteza Hashemi

entry.summary: Develops a packet-level model of federated learning uplinks over UAV relays in unlicensed spectrum, capturing buffer overflow, delay violations, and transmission errors as a Bernoulli mask on model aggregation. A bilevel optimization jointly tunes transmission thresholds and aggregation to balance fairness and consensus under partial observability.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks: Theory, Implementations, and Applications

author.name: L\'eo Monbroussou, Maniraman Periyasamy, Viacheslav Kuzmin, Pavel Sekatski, Viktoria Patapovich, Asel Sagingalieva, Alexey Melnikov

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.01194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence has been transformed by deep neural networks, yet the search for new learning architectures continues. Quantum machine learni...

entry.title: Climate-Dyna Deep Hedging for XVAs: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning, Residual Climate HVA, and Hedge-Instrument Discovery

author.name: Xiaozhen Wang, Francois Buet-Golfouse

entry.summary: Formulates residual climate hedging valuation adjustment for a derivatives desk by comparing paired climate-on and baseline simulated worlds and re-optimizing the hedge overlay, so that instrument selection becomes a valuation question. A model-based reinforcement learning agent starts from an exact linear-Gaussian Riccati hedge and learns the nonlinear correction from world-model rollouts.

entry.title: Using Non-Lipschitz Signum-based Functions for Distributed Optimization and Machine Learning: Trade-off Between Con-vergence Rate and Optimality Gap

author.name: Mohammadreza Doostmohammadian, Amir Ahmad Ghods, Alireza Aghasi, Zulfiya R. Gabidullina, Hamid R. Rabiee

entry.summary: Analyzes signum-based non-Lipschitz distributed optimization algorithms that achieve fast, prescribed-time convergence and robustness to noisy data, and shows they incur a residual optimality gap. The paper characterizes the trade-off between convergence speed and this steady-state error in distributed machine learning settings.

entry.title: Detecting Nonproperness of Likelihood Equations

author.name: Xiaoxian Tang, Bican Xia, Tianqi Zhao

entry.summary: Studies how to detect the nonproperness set of likelihood equations in algebraic statistical models, which characterizes data where solutions escape to infinity and the count of real critical points changes. This is a component of computing discriminant varieties for real root classification of maximum likelihood problems.

entry.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

author.name: Iaroslav Chelombitko, Ekaterina Chelombitko, Mika H\"am\"al\"ainen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.02486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-source LLMs reliably name Zeus, Jupiter, and Thor, but recover their counterparts in less-represented traditions like Finnish, Slavic, Egyptian,...

entry.title: Exploiting Intrinsic Duality for Multi-Hop Question Generation

author.name: Maodong Li, Xinyue Kang, Yuanchen Shi, Fang Kong

entry.summary: Exploits the duality between multi-hop question generation and question answering by training a unified model with bidirectional alignment constraints so generated questions must be answerable back to the target answer. Improves multi-hop question quality over generation-only baselines.

entry.title: CTRAG: An In-Context Retrieval-based Framework for Automated Compliance Checking using LLMs

author.name: Muhammad Roman, Karen Rafferty, Barry Devereux

entry.summary: CTRAG is a retrieval-augmented pipeline for automated regulatory compliance checking, including cases where compliance depends indirectly on third-party cloud vendors. It targets the inconsistency and cost of manual compliance testing in regulated sectors.

entry.title: Poplar: A Scalable Pipeline for Human-Centric Image Dataset Synthesis

author.name: Zhishan Zou

entry.summary: Poplar is a reproducible specify-render-inspect pipeline for synthesizing human-centric image datasets, sampling structured attributes under commonsense constraints and applying structured quality inspection at scale. It emphasizes coverage, plausible attribute combinations, and transparent quality control rather than single-image quality.

entry.title: WiFuse: An Attention Mechanism for Human Activity Recognition using Fused CSI Amplitude and Delay-Doppler Channel Features

author.name: Chenggong Hu, Shaoyin Ma, Yi Wang, Li Sun, Mingli Song, Jie Song

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-driven emotional talking face generation aims to synthesize realistic videos with expressive facial dynamics. However, existing methods struggle ...

author.name: Peng Zheng, Ruiqi Liu, Rui Ma, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent subject-to-image models have achieved impressive progress in personalized image generation, yet they still struggle to preserve fine-grained sub...

author.name: Wei Lu, Yi Liu, Si-Bao

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shadows in remote sensing images obscure surface appearance and disrupt radiometric continuity, reducing the reliability of visual interpretation and d...

author.name: Yihan Qiu, Xiaodong Lin, Baoquan Zhao, Hailong Jiao, Ge Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LiDAR point clouds provide explicit, deterministic physical boundaries critical for collaborative safety-critical perception. However, wireless channel...

author.name: Zhenyang Li, Zongqi He, Jia Pan, Shijie Lin, Yifan Peng

author.name: Jianfeng Qiu, Peiyuan Li, Juan Xie, Xueliang Ma, Sihang Zhou, Yanning Hou, Ke Xu

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zero-shot anomaly detection (ZSAD) aims to detect anomalies and localize defective regions in unseen target domains without target training data. Recen...

author.name: Wei Lu, Hongyuan Liu, Si-Bao Chen

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nighttime aerial image enhancement is challenged by spatially nonuniform exposure, mixed illumination, and weak structural evidence, while registered n...

author.name: Mateusz Michalkiewicz, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Guha Balakrishnan

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.00726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frozen vision foundation models are commonly evaluated through a single global image embedding, but this interface can conflate missing information wit...

entry.summary: This work improves radiology report generation by aligning local visual regions with pathology semantics, arguing that plain autoregressive supervision under-constrains image-text alignment while contrastive learning wrongly separates unpaired reports that describe compatible findings. It proposes pathology-aware alignment to fix that mismatch.

entry.title: Mapping melliferous tree species in Kenya via one-class classification with hyperspectral unsupervised domain adaptation

author.name: Zhaozhi Luo, Janne Heiskanen, Ilja Vuorinne, Ian Ocholla, Shiqi Zhang, Saana J\"arvinen, Xinyu Wang, Yanfei Zhong, Petri Pellikka

entry.summary: This study maps bee-forage tree species in Kenya using one-class classification with unsupervised domain adaptation on hyperspectral imagery, so a detector trained in one region transfers to unseen areas without labeled negatives. The application supports beekeeping-based livelihood diversification for agropastoral communities.

entry.title: Estimating SSIM from MSE for DCT-Based Compressed Images

author.name: Luc Trudeau, Maria G. Martini

entry.summary: This article shows that for DCT-compressed images, the structural similarity index can be approximated from global PSNR or MSE by redistributing global error using local statistics computed only from the reference image. Two weighting schemes based on variance or standard deviation are validated across JPEG quality levels on standard datasets.

entry.title: OmniAI: A Surface-Adaptive Aerial Projection Interface for Human--Drone Interaction

author.name: Nikita Kuzmin, Yuhua Jin, Georgii Demianchuk, Mariya Lezina, Fawad Mehboob, Ivan Valuev, Nikolai Lutsenko, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: OmniAI is a drone that communicates by projecting LLM-generated text and images either on an onboard screen or onto nearby surfaces detected online with RGB-D sensing and plane fitting, with voice and gesture control for both flight and content. It demonstrates a mobile spatial augmented reality interface for human-drone interaction.

entry.title: III. Anthropic reasoning has issues with infinite worlds; D-SIA can fix this

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Third post in a series on anthropic probability, arguing that the self-indication assumption breaks down in worlds with infinitely many agents through divergent and degenerate reweighting. The author proposes distributional SIA as a repair that resolves most infinite-world pathologies at the cost of no longer favoring infinite worlds.

entry.title: II. Anthropic reasoning with duplication is not consistent with probability properties

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: The second post in the anthropics series presents an impossibility result: no probability theory can remain consistent across an agent-duplication event without violating either Bayesian updating in non-anthropic cases or the martingale condition. The author argues duplication specifically, not the mere existence of copies, is the breaking point.

entry.title: Transformer Geometry Observatory TGO-III: Semantic Geometry Observatory

author.name: Kaustubh Kapil, Kishor P. Upla

entry.summary: An analysis framework that tracks how covariance structure and class separability evolve across layers and training of a small vision transformer. Positioned as an observatory for semantic geometry rather than a new model.

entry.title: RPL-UIE: Reliable Prior Learning for Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Yifan Chen, Jiaming Liu, Ye Zheng, Zhe Sun, Tao Chen

entry.summary: RPL-UIE is a teacher-student framework for underwater image enhancement in which a teacher learns spatial appearance and photometric priors from paired degraded and clean images, and a student learns to reproduce those priors from degraded input alone. The aim is to prevent semantic drift that generative restoration methods introduce under severe information loss.

entry.title: Optimization and Constraint Modeling using LLMs with a Retrieval Augmented Generation Process

author.name: Prateek Roy, Akash Singirikonda

entry.summary: Tests whether a retrieval-augmented pipeline over 500 synthetically generated optimization problems improves LLM ability to write correct constraint and optimization models. Uses Text2Zinc seeds and persona-based problem synthesis.

entry.title: Ekova: A Personality-Support Agent for Self-Discovery Dialogue

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces personality support as a paradigm distinct from emotional support, aiming at self-understanding rather than distress relief, with a Chinese dataset of 8,590 longitudinal samples across five interaction personas and a multi-persona system trained with a style-tailored tuning method. Positioned explicitly as non-clinical.

entry.title: Neuro-Evolved Heuristics for Variable Gapped Common Subsequence Identification

author.name: Marko Djukanovi\'c, Christian Blum, Aleksandar Kartelj, Saso Dzeroski, Ziga Zebec

entry.summary: Automatically designs heuristics for the multi-sequence variable-gapped longest common subsequence problem by optimizing a fixed-architecture neural network's weights with a genetic algorithm, replacing hand-crafted beam search guidance. Targets robustness limitations of manual heuristic design.

entry.title: Multimodal Wearable-Based Olfactory-Induced Emotion Recognition in Arousal-Valence Dimensions

author.name: Chen-Yang Xu, Lan Zhang, Fei-Yi Fan, Bin Hu, Qing-Hao Meng

entry.summary: Builds a large multimodal dataset of 111 subjects with synchronized central and peripheral physiological signals under odor stimuli, labeling both arousal and valence rather than valence alone. Proposes recognition models for olfactory-induced emotion in the arousal-valence space.

entry.title: SymNet: A Multi-Task Network for Joint Radio Map Reconstruction and Transmitter Localization

author.name: Lyuzhou Ye, Thanh Dat Le, Yan Huang

entry.summary: SymNet is a multi-task neural network that jointly reconstructs directional radio propagation maps and localizes transmitters from sparse measurements, arguing that in directional settings the peak-signal location no longer coincides with the transmitter. It matters for wireless network planning where angular effects, reflections and building occlusion break the assumptions of prior omnidirectional methods.

entry.title: Entity-Aware Sequence Transduction for Player-Centric Ball Action Spotting

author.name: Ruifeng Wang, Di Yang, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: ME-DST keeps a per-player role-slot dimension throughout encoding for ball action spotting in sports video, using temporal attention within each slot and spatial attention across slots. The factorized design improves the inductive bias for attributing precise events to specific players.

entry.title: X-KGRank: A Knowledge Graph RAG Framework for Explainable Recommendations via Pattern Mining and LLM Re-Ranking

author.name: Meenakshi Rajpurohit, Jainish Patel

entry.summary: X-KGRank builds a heterogeneous knowledge graph from MovieLens interactions, mines structural patterns for candidate generation, and uses an LLM to re-rank and explain recommendations. The design aims to combine collaborative-filtering grounding with fluent, less hallucinated explanations.

entry.title: Agentic Self-Healing for Data and AI Pipelines: An Affordable Vendor-Agnostic Architecture using Open-Source Software

author.name: Solomon Eshun, Dennis Murage, Sharleen Muoki, Chih-Chun Chen, Stephen Adjignon, Matteo Staar, Oliver Ang\'elil

entry.summary: This paper compares commercial AIOps and observability platforms and then presents a vendor-agnostic, open-source agentic architecture that detects, diagnoses, and repairs failures in data and machine learning pipelines. It targets smaller teams priced out of proprietary self-healing tooling.

entry.title: TBSG-Net: Temporal Bipartite Scene Graph Network for Fine-Grained Video Moment Retrieval

author.name: Ji Huang, Yongsheng Dai, Tianyu Ren, Barry Devereux, Hui Wang

entry.summary: TBSG-Net adds temporal dynamics and explicit relationship-duration encoding to scene-graph representations for proposal-free video moment retrieval, addressing the static nature of frame-level scene graphs. The bipartite temporal design aims to improve fine-grained localization.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Crossmodal Fusion for Classification of Animal Behavior

author.name: Ehsan Yaghoubi, Florian Haselbeck

entry.summary: This work fuses raw waveform and spectrogram representations for animal vocalization classification with uncertainty awareness, since the two representations degrade differently under clipping, reverberation, and sensor faults common in field and farm recordings. The application spans livestock welfare and wildlife monitoring.

entry.title: Assessing the Impacts of Imperfect Datasets on Client Selections in Federated Learning

author.name: Yuan-Heng Tsai, Li-Hsing Yen, Yan-Wei Chen

entry.summary: This study experimentally measures how non-IID data quantity and label skew, noisy datasets, and fairness constraints in client selection jointly affect federated learning accuracy and convergence latency. The findings inform when excluding low-quality clients helps versus when selection bias itself degrades learning.

entry.title: Context-Aware Mixture of Domain Experts for Bodily Expression of Emotion in the Wild

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Dehshibi, David Masip

entry.summary: CA-MoDE recognizes bodily emotion in the wild by treating scene and object cues as structured priors, with dedicated experts producing soft emotion distributions that modulate the body expert's prediction at the distributional rather than feature level. This reflects that identical postures convey different emotions in different contexts.

entry.title: Ensemble of Unsupervised Deep Learning for Clustering Imbalanced Tabular Data

author.name: Pulock Das, Yina Hou, Md. Kamrozzaman Bhuiyan, Manar D. Samad

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates modern deep clustering methods on imbalanced tabular data and proposes two cluster-ensemble strategies that aggregate assignments across embedding dimensions or by majority voting. Argues label-free clustering can sidestep majority-class bias that plagues supervised classifiers.

entry.title: Generic Vision and Cross-Attention for Reaction Yield Prediction

author.name: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou

entry.summary: Predicts chemical reaction yields by fusing tabular physical-organic descriptors with 2D molecular skeleton images through cross-attention, reporting that a generic vision backbone on drawings alone beats quantum-descriptor baselines. Mechanistic probing suggests the image branch handles steric information.

entry.title: Adaptive Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Differential Equations with Applications to Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Fabio Pereira dos Santos, Renato Portugal, J\'ulio de Castro Vargas Fernandes, Lucas Timotheo Sanches

entry.summary: Enhances quantum physics-informed neural networks with adaptive collocation sampling and loss-aware attention that concentrate effort where PDE residuals or gradients are large. Argues the bottleneck for such hybrid models is sampling and optimization rather than only quantum-circuit expressivity, with fluid dynamics demonstrations.

entry.title: Cluster-Aware Over-the-Air Federated Learning with Energy-Harvesting Devices: From Global Training to Model Personalization

author.name: Furkan Bagci, Busra Tegin, Mohammad Kazemi, Tolga M. Duman

entry.summary: Studies over-the-air federated learning where energy-harvesting mobile devices have stochastic power availability and heterogeneous data, forming natural clusters of users with shared model objectives. Compares global training against cluster-level personalization under joint communication and energy constraints.

entry.title: Stochastic Sequential Search in Very-High-Dimensional Feature Selection

author.name: Petr Somol, Ji\v{r}\'{\i} Grim

entry.summary: Makes sequential feature selection with floating backtracking tractable in very high dimensions by replacing exhaustive candidate sweeps with a fixed budget of sampled evaluations. Candidates are drawn by temperature-controlled softmax sampling from dependency-aware statistics learned online during the search, with uniform exploration as a guard.

entry.title: Retrieval-Based Cross-Domain Generalization in Optical Networks via Global Features

author.name: Ali Al Housseini, Carlos Natalino, Paolo Monti, Omran Ayoub

entry.summary: Proposes retrieval-based quality-of-transmission estimation for optical networks that reuses transferable global feature representations instead of source-domain decision boundaries, supporting zero-shot and few-shot cross-domain adaptation without retraining. Reports gains over conventional and contrastive baselines.

entry.title: Uncertainty-guided active learning for surrogate prediction of stream-finishing wear fields

author.name: Anand Kumar, Puli Saikiran, Vineet Dawara, Koushik Viswanathan

entry.summary: Builds an uncertainty-guided active learning surrogate that predicts impact velocity and flux fields on a workpiece directly from geometry, replacing expensive discrete element simulations of abrasive stream finishing. The predicted fields feed a wear model to identify orientations that produce uniform material removal.

entry.title: A Sequence-to-Sequence ConvLSTM Approach for Leaf Area Index Forecasting over the South-Central United States

author.name: Zhixing Ruan, Lixin Lu

entry.summary: Presents a sequence-to-sequence convolutional LSTM that forecasts daily one-kilometer leaf area index up to 30 days ahead from past vegetation states and meteorological forcing over the south-central United States. The aim is a gridded prognostic vegetation forecast usable in subseasonal land surface and climate models.

entry.title: Finite-Probe Total-Variation Certificates for Finite-Basis Drifting Models

author.name: Sam Andersson, Ricky Mol\'en

entry.summary: Derives a posteriori total variation confidence bounds for comparing a target and model distribution when only a finite set of noisy vector-field probes is available, under a declared finite density basis. The bounds account for measurement noise, operator estimation error, and residual approximation radii, and return no conclusion when observability is insufficient.

entry.title: Learning-Based Collaborative MEC for LLM Inference with Soft-Deadline Awareness via Transformer-Enhanced PPO

author.name: Ngoc Hung Nguyen, Bjorn Landfeldt

entry.summary: Schedules LLM inference across collaborative mobile edge servers under soft deadlines, introducing a mechanism that allows a limited number of deadline extensions while accounting for dependencies between subtasks of a request. A transformer-enhanced PPO agent learns the offloading and extension policy.

entry.title: Cardiovascular Digital Twins from Physics Based to Data Driven Approaches

author.name: Emmanuel Lwele, Francis Chikweto

entry.summary: A review of cardiovascular digital twin modelling, contrasting mechanistic physics-based models with data-driven and hybrid physics-informed graph approaches. Summarizes data assimilation, validation gaps, and paths to clinical deployment.

entry.title: Domain-Specific Evaluation of Text-to-Speech Systems: A Multi-Metric Benchmarking Study

author.name: Ali Jafar, Amal Sarmad, Shifa Yousaf, Maryam Bashir

entry.summary: Presents a reproducible multi-metric framework for evaluating text-to-speech systems that jointly measures perceptual quality, speaker similarity, and acoustic fidelity across speech domains, demonstrated on a low-resource language. Aims to fill a gap in standardized TTS evaluation outside English.

entry.title: Extended Field of View Analysis for VideoGAN-based Trajectory Generation

author.name: Annajoyce Mariani, Kira Maag, Hanno Gottschalk

entry.summary: Extends a GAN-based generator of bird's-eye-view traffic scenes with better semantic representation, graph-based trajectory extraction, and systematically larger fields of view. Introduces quantitative measures for the realism and diversity of generated driving trajectories.

entry.title: Evaluating VLMs on Multimodal Aristotelian Persuasion Tasks

author.name: Khondoker Ittehadul Islam

entry.summary: Evaluates vision-language models on detecting Aristotelian persuasion appeals of logos, ethos, and pathos in multimodal argument datasets. Finds Qwen-family models perform relatively well, with ethos remaining hardest.

entry.title: An Evidence-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Transformer Framework for Health Misinformation Verification

author.name: Isah M. Bukar, Bala Mairiga Abduljalil, Bashir Saleh Maina, Abdulbasit Hassan

entry.summary: Builds a retrieval-augmented transformer pipeline that verifies health claims against WHO and Nigerian public health sources, targeting the gap where global biomedical resources miss local context. Aimed at faster verification during outbreaks in developing-country settings.

entry.title: Beyond Edge Maps: Wavelet-Domain Conditioning for Multi-Adapter Map-to-Satellite Diffusion

author.name: Arisha Prasain

entry.summary: Synthesizes satellite imagery conditioned only on independently maintained cartographic data plus wavelet-domain structure, avoiding the circularity of prior methods that condition on features extracted from the target image. The motivation is refreshing basemaps in regions without commercial mapping partnerships.

entry.title: The 1st AI Children Challenge

author.name: Boyi Li, Yifan Shen, Houze Yang, Xu Cao, Guojun Yun, Li Gao, Turong Chen, Long Xu, Jianguo Cao, Meihuan Huang

entry.summary: Report on a first challenge track for fine-grained analysis of children's gait from keypoint sequences, spanning ages three to sixteen, aimed at pediatric and child-health applications of computer vision. It positions children-focused vision as an underserved domain where clinicians can perceive distinctions current models cannot.

entry.title: Quaternion Tensor Modeling for Joint Color-Polarization Demosaicking

author.name: Yanqing Song, Jifei Miao, Chaoqian Li, Rui Mei, Kit Ian Kou, Liqiao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a quaternion-tensor model with Stokes-domain total variation regularization for jointly demosaicking color and polarization from snapshot division-of-focal-plane camera mosaics. Exploits the finding that polarization channels correlate more strongly than color channels.

entry.title: Calibrated Similarity and Graph Clustering for Open-Set Animal Re-Identification

author.name: Mohamed ElBassat, Seifeldin Elkerdany, Mohamed ElBialy, Gamal Abouelhamd, Jana Ghoneim, Assem Elkady, Mohamed Elboraay, Nelly Semenova

entry.summary: This is a competition-style pipeline for open-set animal re-identification across four species, combining segmentation, species-specific preprocessing, calibrated similarity fusion of multiple descriptors, and graph clustering to both match known individuals and discover new ones. It targets the AnimalCLEF26 discovery-oriented benchmark.

entry.title: A Robotic System for Automated Manufacturing of Dielectric Elastomer Actuators

author.name: Van Remenar, Anatol Gogoj, Ang Li, Tomas Verardi, Matei Mandoiu, Victor Jimenez Santiago, Mihai Duduta

entry.summary: This letter describes an automated robotic line for fabricating multilayer dielectric elastomer actuators, focusing on spin-coated dielectric layers and stamped carbon nanotube electrodes. Twenty twelve-layer devices were produced with reported thickness consistency, a 14 percent process time reduction, and removal of the human operator from most of the process.

entry.title: VespaSeg: A Resource-Aware Ground-then-Segment Pipeline for Referring Expression Segmentation

author.name: Savindu Dilshan Wickramasinghe (University of Moratuwa)
